title: Optimize Conductor 2.0 - Release Notes and Migration Guide
content:
Optimize Conductor 2.0 - Release Notes and Migration Guide

Summary

This document describes the Redwood Optimize Conductor 2.0 release: what changed, why it matters, SLO and billing impacts, rollout and migration steps, and operational notes for customers and internal teams. Optimize Conductor 2.0 introduces workload-aware multi-pass optimization, a pluggable estimator for hybrid deployments, and default telemetry schemas for per-route cost attribution. The release is focused on reducing per-token inference cost for conversational workloads while preserving quality SLAs.

Highlights

- Workload-aware multi-pass optimization: a new orchestration layer that simulates alternate batching, quantization, and cache policies across historical traces and recommends per-route profiles.
- Hybrid estimator plugin: customers running Dedicated + Private topologies can use the new estimator to predict cross-environment cost tradeoffs and warm-capacity benefits.
- Observability schema v2: standardized telemetry fields for capture of per-variant latency, KV cache hit rates, and token-level cost estimates (see Telemetry changes section).
- Migration assistant CLI: a guided CLI and UI assistant that validates a tenant’s usage traces, runs a sandboxed simulation, and produces recommended policy bundles with confidence bands.
- Compatibility and fallbacks: automatic fallback rules to Produce Conductor 1.x profiles when runtime compatibility or regression risks are detected.

Why this release?

Customers have asked for more deterministic cost reductions without manual tuning. Optimize Conductor 2.0 is intended to:

- reduce average per-token serving cost for chat-like flows by 8–22% in early benchmarks,
- shorten time-to-safe-rollout (canary → A/B → 100%) via integrated simulation-driven confidence scores, and
- provide clearer observability to map cost changes to specific configuration deltas.

What’s changed (detailed)

1) Multi-pass optimization engine
- Runs a sequence of optimizers (batch sizing, prefix caching, quantization profile selection, KV eviction policy) against a tenant’s trace in a sandbox.
- Produces an ordered set of recommended policy bundles with: expected cost delta, expected latency delta (p50/p95), and a confidence score derived from simulation variance.
- Output format (JSON example):

  {
    "bundle_id": "optc-202612-sandbox-01",
    "candidate_policies": ["batch-128","q8_2","prefix-kv-enabled"],
    "estimated_cost_change_pct": "-12.4",
    "estimated_latency_p95_ms": "210",
    "confidence": "0.87"
  }

2) Hybrid estimator plugin
- Extensible plugin API that accepts per-region capacity profiles and returns cross-topology allocations.
- Useful for customers who split traffic between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Sample CLI call: redwood-optimize simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --plugin hybrid-estimator --trace traces/2026-11-01.json

3) Observability schema v2
- New required telemetry fields: optimize.bundle_id, optimize.simulation_confidence, optimize.estimated_cost_usd, optimize.kv_hit_rate, optimize.batch_shape.
- Backwards compatibility: the ingestion pipeline will accept v1 telemetry but only the new dashboards and reports will show v2 fields.

4) Migration assistant CLI/UI
- Provides an automated sequence: validate traces → run sandbox sim → produce recommended bundles → run offline regression evals → generate rollout plan.
- CLI example (high level):

  # validate traces and run simulation\  redwood-optimize migrate validate --tenant TENANT_ID --trace s3://bucket/trace-2026-10-15.json\  redwood-optimize migrate simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --policy-bounds "{\"min_batch\":32,\"max_batch\":256}"

- The UI exposes an interactive confidence slider for selecting more conservative vs aggressive bundles.

SLO and billing impacts

- Expected unit economics: Early benchmarks across 6 representative tenants show mean cost reduction 12% (range 8–22%) with p95 latency change within +/- 10% of baseline for the chosen conservative bundles.
- Billing: There is no immediate change to billing metrics or pricing SKUs. Cost savings are realized through optimization of runtime configuration and will show up as lower consumption in token/cpu/GPU usage reports.
- SLA considerations: Teams must validate per-tenant latency/p95 and function-call integrity. Optimize Conductor 2.0 includes a safety gate that will not permit an automatic rollout if p95 regression > 15% in the sandbox regression evals.

Upgrade and migration plan (for customers)

Recommended staged migration (small-to-large tenants):

1) Prepare (owner: customer success / solutions engineering)
- Gather a 7–14 day usage trace covering representative traffic (session length distribution, model variants, peak windows).\- Ensure trace contains at least 50k inference requests or the migration assistant will flag low-confidence recommendations.
- Confirm tenant has a staging route (non-production) that can proxy 5–10% of live traffic for A/B tests.

2) Simulate and validate (owner: customer success + tenant engineering)
- Run the migration assistant simulate command to generate candidate bundles.
- Review recommended bundles and associated confidence scores.
- Run offline regression evals against a fixed prompt set to verify functional parity (owner provides known-good prompts for critical flows).

3) Canary rollout (owner: tenant engineering + Redwood SRE)
- Apply conservative bundle to 1–2 production routes at 1–5% traffic.
- Monitor optimize.simulation_confidence, optimize.estimated_cost_usd, request.latency_p95, model.output_consistency metrics for 24–72 hours.
- If p95 regression remains < 10% and no functional regressions detected, proceed to A/B.

4) A/B and ramp (owner: customer success + Redwood product)
- Ramp to 25–50% traffic, compare endpoint KPIs, and collect user-facing error rates.
- Typical ramp cadence: double traffic every 12 hours if all checks pass.

5) Full rollout and post-rollout audit (owner: customer success + finance)
- Ramp to 100% when confidence remains high.
- Generate a 7-day post-rollout audit report showing realized cost delta and latency impact.

Rollback criteria

Immediate rollback triggers:
- p95 latency regression > 15% vs baseline for the route during the canary or A/B.
- Any functional regression detected by the offline regression evals (semantic inconsistency, hallucination increase measured by test oracle).
- KV/cache hit rate drop > 30% causing unexpected cost increases.

Operational runbook (SRE)

Owner: eng-sre

Monitoring checklist (alerts to configure):
- optimize.simulation_confidence < 0.5 for a recently applied bundle → alert to product/sre.
- optimize.estimated_cost_usd increases > 10% over rolling 24h → alert to billing-ops.
- request.latency_p95 increases > 12% over baseline → page oncall.
- optimize.kv_hit_rate falls below configured threshold for a route → run cache debug runbook.

Quick debug steps:
1) Identify affected routes using optimize.bundle_id in logs.
2) Use the simulation sandbox to replay a representative subset of traffic.
3) If rollback is required: redwood-optimize migrate rollback --tenant TENANT_ID --bundle BUNDLE_ID
4) Open an incident and follow standard oncall postmortem cadence if the cause is not apparent.

Compatibility and fallbacks

- Compatibility matrix: Conductor 2.0 supports runtime agent versions >= 3.2.2. If a route uses agent < 3.2.2, the migration assistant will recommend a v1-compatible bundle and include an upgrade path.
- Fallback behavior: If a live trial detects functional regressions, the platform will automatically apply the last-known-good bundle for that route and create a high-visibility ticket to the product owner.

Telemetry and dashboard changes (what product teams should know)

- New Optimize dashboards (Console):
  - Per-tenant Optimization Summary (shows realized vs estimated cost deltas, per-route confidence scores).
  - Bundle Explorer (lists applied bundles, simulation metadata, and rollback events).
  - Regression surface map (maps prompts/paths that failed offline regressions).

- Telemetry ingestion notes: SDKs and ingestion pipelines must emit the optimize.* v2 fields. Agents older than 3.2.2 will continue to emit v1 fields; the ingestion layer will backfill where possible but v2-only reports require agent upgrade.

Administrative and billing notes

- There is no separate paid SKU for Optimize Conductor 2.0 during the initial preview period. Usage of the migration assistant sandbox is metered and shown as an internal optimization run in the tenant’s console.
- Finance ops will track realized savings as part of monthly consumption reports. For enterprise customers on committed Dedicated plans, Optimize-driven savings will be reconciled as operational improvements and reflected in future commit discussions.

Known limitations and gotchas

- Small tenants (fewer than 50k requests in the trace window) should expect lower-confidence recommendations; consider a longer trace window.
- Extremely bursty traffic patterns can reduce optimizer confidence; the migration assistant offers a conservative bundle option for these tenants.
- The sandbox simulation assumes identical model weights and versioning; if a tenant uses rapidly changing model variants, freeze model rollouts during sandbox runs.

Support and escalation

- Primary contact: customer-success-optimize@redwood.ai (for migration coordination)
- SRE escalation: oncall-sre@redwood.ai (pager contacts in internal roster)
- Engineering bug reports: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/issues (label: conductor-2.0)

Owners and contacts

- Product manager: Ava Nguyen (owner)
- Engineering lead: Diego Martinez
- Customer success lead: Maya Patel
- SRE lead: Liam O'Connor

Appendices

A — Example recommended bundle (full JSON)
{
  "bundle_id": "optc-202612-conservative-001",
  "policies": {
    "batch": 64,
    "quantization": "q8_2",
    "prefix_kv_enabled": true,
    "kv_eviction_policy": "lru_time_based_1h"
  },
  "estimated_cost_change_pct": "-9.8",
  "estimated_latency_p95_ms": "195",
  "confidence": "0.78"
}

B — CLI checklist for migration assistants
- Ensure trace is complete and covers peak windows.
- Run redwood-optimize migrate validate --tenant TENANT_ID --trace s3://...
- If validation passes, run redwood-optimize migrate simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --plugin hybrid-estimator
- Review candidate bundles and run offline regression evals
- Execute canary rollback plan if any regression triggers occur

C — Release timeline
- 2026-11-15: internal alpha completed
- 2026-11-22: customer preview starts (select tenants)
- 2026-12-01: general availability (GA) and documentation published

D — Links (internal)
- Migration assistant repo: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/migration-assistant
- Telemetry schema v2 reference: /product-docs/design-specs/optimize-telemetry-schema-v2

title: Usage Insights (Console) — UX Spec (IA, Breakdown Tables, Drilldowns, Export, Share Links, A11y)
content:
Usage Insights (Console) — UX Spec (IA, Breakdown Tables, Drilldowns, Export, Share Links, A11y)

## 1. Overview
This spec defines the Redwood Console UX for **Usage Insights**: cost + usage breakdowns by **API route** and **model**, including drilldowns, “Top cost drivers” insights, CSV export, shareable report links, and accessibility requirements.

Primary goals:
- Help developers understand **where spend is coming from** (route + model) and **why** (tokens in/out, cache, retries, fallbacks, context length, latency-correlated spend).
- Support engineering + finance workflows with **exportable and shareable** reports.
- Ensure the Console totals remain consistent with Billing (within tolerance; see PRD + correctness checks).

Non-goals (initial):
- Automated optimization actions (we only surface recommendations/links).
- Scheduled email reports.

## 2. Personas & permissions
### Personas
- **Engineering lead / platform engineer:** wants hotspots by route/model and actionable drivers.
- **FinOps / finance partner:** wants consistent totals vs billing, exports, and stable definitions.
- **Support / solutions engineer:** wants to troubleshoot customer “why did it spike?” questions.

### Permissions (RBAC)
The UI must be fully functional under different workspace settings.
- **View cost**: gated by workspace role/permission. Users lacking permission can still view *non-cost usage metrics* where allowed (e.g., requests/tokens) depending on workspace settings.
- **Export**: separate permission (often narrower than view).
- **Share links**: creation requires share permission; viewing a shared link still requires standard RBAC checks at access time.

Permission-driven UI states are specified in Section 9.

## 3. Information Architecture (IA)
### Primary navigation placement
**Console → Usage & Cost → Usage Insights (Beta)**
- Left-nav group: **Usage & Cost**
  - Usage Overview
  - Billing (invoices, payment, plans)
  - **Usage Insights (Beta)** (new)

### Page structure
**Usage Insights landing page** is a tabbed page with persistent global filters.
Tabs:
1) **Breakdown** (default)
2) **Top cost drivers**
3) **What changed?**
4) **Exports & Reports** (history + share links)

Rationale:
- “Breakdown” is the core table-first workflow.
- “Top cost drivers” is interpretive, anchored to the same filters.
- “What changed?” answers delta questions without forcing users to export.
- “Exports & Reports” prevents export actions from being hidden behind a single table CTA and supports governance/audit.

## 4. Global filter bar (applies to all tabs)
### Filter controls
The filter bar is sticky at the top of the content area.

Controls (left to right):
1) **Time range**
   - Presets: Last 24h, 7d (default), 14d, 30d
   - Custom range (calendar)
   - Timezone: use user profile timezone for display; queries use UTC with explicit boundaries.
2) **Workspace/Project selector**
   - Workspace always required.
   - Project optional; defaults to “All projects.”
3) **Environment** (if enabled): Prod / Staging / Dev / All
4) Optional dimensions (feature-flagged per workspace / readiness):
   - Deployment mode: Hosted / Dedicated / Private / All
   - Region: multi-select
5) **Route**
   - Search + select
   - Display name: canonical route templates (per ADR)
   - Option: “All routes”
6) **Model**
   - Search + select
   - Grouped display: Model family → versions/aliases
   - Option: “All models”

### Filter interaction rules
- Any change triggers a new query and updates the URL query params.
- The UI must show a **loading skeleton** for table/chart regions, but keep filters interactive.
- Multi-select controls should show “N selected” with a clear remove-all action.

### Applied filters chip row
Below the filter bar, show chips for applied filters (excluding workspace).
- Chips are removable.
- Long values truncate with tooltip on hover/focus.

### Defaults & guardrails
- Default time range: **Last 7 days**.
- Interactive mode max: **30 days**. For longer ranges, user must use export flow (Section 7) with “Async export recommended” messaging.

## 5. Breakdown tab (core experience)
### Layout
- Header: “Usage Insights (Beta)” + short description + “Learn more” link to docs.
- Freshness indicator (right side): “Data updated X minutes ago” with warning state.
- Primary content: **Breakdown table** with optional summary row.

### Breakdown table: grouping & rows
User-selectable grouping control above the table:
- Group by: 
  - **Route → Model** (default)
  - **Model → Route**
  - Route only
  - Model only

Behavior:
- If grouped (Route → Model), top-level rows are routes with expandable caret.
- Expanded rows show models under that route, sorted by cost by default.

### Columns (default)
Columns are configurable (column picker) but start with a stable default.

Default columns:
- Route / Model (depending on grouping)
- **Cost** (currency)
- Requests
- Tokens in
- Tokens out
- Cache hit rate
- Retries
- Fallbacks
- p95 latency

Column definitions (tooltip text required):
- **Cost**: computed from metered usage aligned to billing hooks; may lag.
- **Cache hit rate**: cache hits / eligible requests.
- **Retries**: count of retried requests (as defined in attribution ADR).
- **Fallbacks**: count of requests served by fallback model/region policy.

### Sorting
- Default sort: Cost (desc).
- Sorting available on all numeric columns.
- Sorting must apply within each hierarchy level (route-level rows sort independently from nested model rows).

### Pagination
- Page size: 25 rows (top-level). Options: 25 / 50 / 100.
- Expanded children: virtualized list within row expansion; “Show more” if needed.

### Row interactions
- Clicking a row opens drilldown (Section 6).
- Expand/collapse uses caret; clicking caret does not navigate.
- Right-click / kebab menu options:
  - “Open in new tab” (drilldown)
  - “Copy link to this view” (deep link with filters + row key)
  - “Export this selection” (pre-fills export with current grouping/filter)

### Summary & consistency messaging
Above the table, show a single-line summary:
- “Total cost (filtered): $X,XXX — Requests: N — Tokens out: N”
- When filtered totals differ from Billing due to freshness/lag, show an info tooltip:
  - “Totals may differ from invoices for the selected range until all events are processed. See freshness details.”

## 6. Drilldown behavior (route/model detail)
### Entry points
- From Breakdown tab row click.
- From “Top cost drivers” cards via “View details.”
- From shared link.

### Drilldown URL & breadcrumbs
- URL includes stable identifiers (workspace + project + route_template + model_family + model_version_bucket).
- Breadcrumbs:
  - Usage & Cost → Usage Insights → Breakdown → [Route] → [Model]

### Drilldown page sections
1) **Header**
   - Title: “/v1/chat/completions · llama-3.1-70b (bucketed)”
   - Chips: applied filters (time range, env, deployment mode, region)
   - Actions: Export, Share, Copy link

2) **KPI strip** (4–6 tiles)
   - Cost
   - Requests
   - Tokens out (and in)
   - Cache hit rate
   - Retries
   - Fallback rate

3) **Trends (time series)**
   - Cost over time
   - Tokens out over time
   - Requests over time
   - Toggle to compare previous period (for “What changed?” style view)

4) **Drivers breakdown (explainable)**
   - “Tokens out” distribution (p50/p90/p99)
   - Context length distribution (prompt tokens)
   - Cache eligible vs not eligible
   - Retry reasons (if available)
   - Fallback destinations (model/region)

5) **Recommendations module (non-automated)**
   - Contextual links (Docs + Console areas) based on observed drivers:
     - Low cache hit rate → link to caching docs
     - High tokens out → link to response-length controls/structured outputs
     - High fallbacks → link to routing policy docs
     - High retries → link to reliability troubleshooting

### Loading & error states
- Use skeleton for KPI strip and charts.
- If charts cannot load but table data exists, show partial data message and keep KPIs.

## 7. Export interactions (CSV)
### Entry points
- Primary CTA in Breakdown tab header: “Export CSV”
- Secondary CTA in drilldown header: “Export”
- Table row kebab: “Export this selection”

### Export modal (single flow)
Modal sections:
1) **What to export**
   - Export type:
     - “Current breakdown (grouped table)”
     - “Current selection only” (if invoked from a row)
     - “Raw daily buckets (advanced)” (if enabled)
2) **Time range** (pre-filled from global filters)
3) **Dimensions** (read-only preview derived from current grouping/filter)
4) **Format options**
   - Currency display: USD (or workspace billing currency) with consistent rounding rules.
   - Include columns: checkbox list.
5) **Delivery**
   - Download now (if small)
   - Generate export (async)

### Sync vs async decision
- If estimated rows ≤ 50k and estimated size ≤ 25MB: allow “Download now” (still implemented via short-lived generated file).
- Otherwise default to async:
  - Show message: “This export may take a few minutes. We’ll generate a file and keep it available for 7 days.”

### Export progress & completion
- After “Generate export,” show a non-blocking toast + navigate user to **Exports & Reports** tab.
- In Exports & Reports:
  - Status: Queued / Running / Completed / Failed / Expired
  - Actions: Download, Copy share link (if permitted), View parameters

### File naming
Use deterministic naming to simplify finance workflows:
- `usage-insights_<workspace>_<project-or-all>_<YYYY-MM-DD_to_YYYY-MM-DD>_<grouping>_<generatedAtUTC>.csv`

### Limits & messaging
- Show explicit limits in the modal:
  - Max range for export (e.g., 90 days) if enforced
  - Max exports per hour per user/workspace
- On limit hit: inline error with “Try smaller range” guidance.

## 8. Shareable link behavior (reports)
### What “Share” means
A share link is a **saved report view** (filters + tab + optional focused row/drilldown context). It is not a public link.

### Share creation
- “Share” button available on Breakdown and Drilldown headers.
- Opens Share modal:
  - Name (optional): “Jan 2026 cost spike investigation”
  - Scope: “Current view” (default) or “This drilldown”
  - Access note: “Only users with access to this workspace and cost permissions can view.”
- On create:
  - Generate link and copy-to-clipboard
  - Create audit log entry (handled by backend; UI references that auditing occurs)

### Share viewing
- If user has RBAC: open the view with filters pre-applied.
- If user lacks cost permission: show permission empty state (Section 9) and hide cost fields.
- If report includes restricted dimension (e.g., certain regions for Private): enforce the strictest policy.

### Share management
In **Exports & Reports** tab:
- List “Shared reports” created by user (and optionally those shared with them if supported).
- Actions: Copy link, Rename, Delete
- Deleting invalidates link.

## 9. Empty states & edge cases
### A) No data for selection
Condition: query returns zero rows.
UI:
- Title: “No usage data for this selection.”
- Suggestions:
  - Expand time range
  - Switch to “All projects”
  - Check environment filter
- Show a small help link: “How Usage Insights is computed.”

### B) Partial data / freshness lag
Condition: backend indicates lag > threshold or partitions incomplete.
UI:
- Banner (warning): “Usage Insights is still processing recent events. Some totals may be incomplete.”
- Include:
  - “Last complete hour/day: …”
  - Link: “View freshness details” (opens popover with timestamp + guidance)

### C) Permission denied (view cost)
Condition: user lacks cost permission but can access Console.
UI:
- Banner (neutral): “You don’t have permission to view cost for this workspace.”
- Table behavior:
  - Hide cost column entirely (do not show $0).
  - Keep usage columns if allowed.
- CTA: “Request access” (links to internal workflow/help article or opens support contact for workspace admins).

### D) Permission denied (export/share)
Condition: user can view but cannot export/share.
UI:
- Disable Export/Share buttons with tooltip: “You don’t have permission to export usage insights.”

### E) Query too large / timeouts
Condition: backend responds with “query complexity exceeded” or timeout.
UI:
- Error state with clear next steps:
  - Reduce time range (recommend ≤ 14 days)
  - Filter by project/route/model
  - Use export for longer ranges
- Provide “Try again” button.

### F) Route or model normalization changes
Condition: historical rows were bucketed differently (post-migration).
UI:
- Info tooltip: “Some routes/models may be grouped differently due to normalization updates. See definitions.”

## 10. Top cost drivers tab
### Purpose
A ranked view that answers “What are the biggest contributors right now?” with explainability text.

### Layout
- Ranked cards/table with:
  - Entity: Route + Model (or Route-only if model not applicable)
  - Cost contribution (%, $)
  - Primary driver label (e.g., “Tokens out ↑”, “Cache hit rate ↓”, “Retries ↑”)
  - Short explanation (2 lines)
  - CTA: “View details” (drilldown)

### Guardrails
- Always include a “Why am I seeing this?” link that explains heuristics are directional.
- Avoid implying causation when it’s correlation (copy must use “associated with” language).

## 11. What changed? tab
### Purpose
Compare current period vs previous period to find deltas by route/model.

### Controls
- Toggle: “Compare to previous period” (default on)
- Metric selector: Cost, tokens out, requests

### Table behavior
- Rows: Route + Model
- Columns:
  - Current value
  - Previous value
  - Delta (absolute)
  - Delta (%)
- Sort default: Delta cost (desc)
- Row click → drilldown with compare mode pre-enabled.

## 12. Exports & Reports tab
### Content
Two sections:
1) **Exports**
   - Table: Created at, Created by, Parameters summary, Status, Actions
   - Actions: Download (if completed), Copy download link (if permitted), View parameters
2) **Shared reports**
   - Table: Name, Created by, Last viewed (if available), Link, Actions

### Retention UX
- Show expiration date for each export.
- When expired: status “Expired” + CTA “Regenerate” (pre-fills modal).

## 13. Accessibility (A11y) requirements
Must meet WCAG 2.1 AA for the Console.

### Keyboard navigation
- All filter controls reachable via Tab; dropdowns usable with arrow keys and Enter.
- Table:
  - Row expansion via keyboard (Enter/Space on caret)
  - Row navigation does not trap focus
  - Kebab menu accessible via keyboard with visible focus

### Screen reader semantics
- Filters have explicit labels (not placeholder-only).
- Table uses semantic headers with `scope="col"` and consistent column order.
- Expandable rows announce expanded/collapsed state.
- Charts provide an accessible summary (text alternative) for key values.

### Color & contrast
- Ensure banners (warning/info) meet contrast.
- Do not rely on color alone to convey “up/down” deltas; include arrows/icons + text.

### Motion & loading
- Skeleton loading should respect reduced-motion preferences.
- Progress states for exports must be announced (aria-live region for status changes).

## 14. Telemetry (product analytics)
Track to validate adoption and identify confusion points:
- Page view: Usage Insights landing + each tab.
- Filter interactions: time range changes, route/model selection.
- Drilldown open events.
- Export created (sync vs async), export failed, download clicked.
- Share link created, share link opened.
- Permission denied impressions (view cost / export).

## 15. Open questions (to resolve before Beta)
1) Terminology: do we label “Route” as “Endpoint (Route)” in the UI to reduce confusion (DevEx feedback)?
2) Default columns: include p95 latency by default or behind column picker?
3) Compare mode: should “What changed?” be a separate tab at beta or a toggle inside Breakdown?
4) Max interactive time range: confirm 30 days vs 14 days based on query performance.
5) Private deployments: confirm any additional copy/controls required for restricted workspaces (export/share constraints).

## 16. Acceptance criteria (UX)
- Users can find the page under Usage & Cost and understand the core workflow within 60 seconds.
- Breakdown table supports grouping, sorting, pagination, row drilldown, and deep links.
- Exports work end-to-end with clear status and retained history.
- Share links reproduce the same view and always enforce RBAC.
- Empty states are actionable and do not mislead (no silent $0s).
- Accessibility requirements are met for filters, tables, modals, and status changes.

title: Capacity Signal Denoising and SLO Guardrail Runbook
content:
Capacity Signal Denoising and SLO Guardrail Runbook

Overview

Purpose: provide a repeatable, tool-agnostic runbook for converting noisy capacity and SLO telemetry into reliable decision signals used by autoscaling, error-budget orchestration, and incident detection. This document codifies: denoising algorithms, sampling and aggregation policies, thresholds for automated actions, verification checks, ownership, and a staged rollout plan.

Why this exists

- Model inference workloads generate high-cardinality, bursty telemetry (token-level latencies, KV cache/hit rates, GPU utilization by batch size). Raw telemetry often produces false positives for SLO regressions and leads to unnecessary capacity changes.
- This runbook reduces operational churn by: (1) converting raw telemetry into robust signals, (2) providing action matrices tied to error-budget burn, and (3) validating those signals before automated remediation.

Scope

- Applies to all inference-facing services managed by eng-sre (hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments).
- Focus metrics: request latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99), request success rate (HTTP 2xx-%), per-tenant request rate, GPU utilization (device), model hot-pool hit rate, KV cache hit ratio.
- Out-of-scope: per-development environment experiments (use telemetry-sandbox for that).

Key concepts and definitions

- Denoised signal: metric after smoothing, outlier filtering, and seasonal decomposition.
- Burst: short-lived spike where request rate > 3x local moving median for the same hour-of-week.
- Stable window: rolling 30-minute window used for operational decisions unless otherwise noted.
- Actionable event: denoised signal crossing a configured threshold for >= two consecutive stable windows.

Signal processing pipeline (recommended implementation)

1) Collection and raw retention

- Collect raw events at full fidelity (token-level traces) but primarily route to hot storage for 72 hours and cold storage for 90 days.
- Sampling guideline: store 100% of aggregate request/latency metrics; sample token-level traces at 2% baseline, up to 20% during anomalous periods triggered by a preliminary detector.

2) Preprocessing

- Tag normalization: ensure every telemetry row includes service, cluster, region, model-version, tenant-id, route, and request-type. Missing tags -> forward to telemetry-quality channel for remediation.
- Clock alignment: metrics must be aligned to the cluster-local minute; apply server-time skew correction if >250ms.

3) Denoising steps (applied in order)

A. Outlier trimming (short tail suppression)
- Remove top 0.1% sample values per minute per metric to limit measurement noise from instrumentation spikes.
- Rationale: instrumentation or transient host scheduling can produce extreme latencies that should not immediately drive autoscale.

B. Median absolute deviation (MAD) filter
- Compute median M and MAD over the last 30 minutes. Mark samples outside M ± 6*MAD as transient; downweight them by 90% in the aggregation.

C. Seasonal-trend decomposition (STL)
- If the metric exhibits clear periodicity (hour-of-day or day-of-week), decompose using STL with seasonal period = 60 (minutes) or 1440 (minutes) depending on dataset. Use the trend component for autoscale decisions and the seasonal residual to avoid reacting to predictable load cycles.

D. Robust exponential smoothing for trend (RTS)
- Apply an alpha tuned to the metric class: latency quantiles: alpha=0.12; request rate: alpha=0.25; GPU util: alpha=0.08. Maintain both smoothed and raw percentiles for drift detection.

E. Burst-aware gating
- When an increase in request rate qualifies as a burst (see definition), require at least two conditions to be true before autoscale: smoothed request rate > 1.3x baseline AND p95 latency smoothed > threshold. This prevents scale-up on short spiky traffic that current model-serving pool can absorb.

Telemetry queries (examples)

- Baseline p95 (ClickHouse-style):

SELECT toStartOfMinute(timestamp) AS minute, quantileExact(0.95)(latency_ms) AS p95
FROM inference_requests
WHERE service = 'redwood-api' AND model_version = 'rwd-v2' AND region = 'us-west-2'
  AND timestamp BETWEEN now() - INTERVAL 2 HOUR AND now()
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute DESC

- Denosing pipeline (pseudocode):

# pseudocode
raw = query(metric, window=60min)
trimmed = trim_top_percent(raw, 0.1)
median, mad = stats(trimmed)
filtered = downweight_outliers(trimmed, median, mad, threshold=6)
seasonal, trend = stl_decompose(filtered, period=60)
smoothed = rts(trend, alpha=0.12)
return smoothed

Action matrix (automated vs. human-in-loop)

- Inputs: denoised p95 latency, denoised request rate, GPU util, error budget burn rate (24h and 1h).

| Condition | 1h burn | 24h burn | Action | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Minor latency rise: p95 > SLO*1.05 for 30m | <2x | <1.5x | Annotate signal, create async ticket to platform, no autoscale | Platform Oncall |
| Sustained latency regression: p95 > SLO*1.1 for 2 windows | >2x | <3x | Open incident, human approval for scale-up, runbook: manual pool add | Oncall + Platform Eng |
| Rapid high burn: 1h burn > 4x and p95 > SLO*1.15 | >4x | >6x | Automated pre-approved scale-up of +20% capacity, notify SRE, begin throttling policies if capacity not provisioned in 10m | SRE Autopilot |
| Resource saturation: GPU util > 92% for 15m + queue growth | - | - | Immediate scale up limited by quota; trigger priority routing & error-budget admission control | Oncall + Capacity team |
Note: SLO multipliers are tied to product tier (free-tier tenants use stricter admission control). See governance section for per-tenant policy.

SLO and error-budget integration

- Canonical SLOs to drive the pipeline: availability (successful requests >= 99.95% monthly), latency p95 <= 120ms for 'short' requests, p95 <= 500ms for 'long' requests. These are the baseline; product teams may define stricter SLOs per feature.
- Error budget burn detection: compute burn rate as (observed bad / expected bad) over a lookback. Trigger levels defined at 1h, 6h, 24h.
- Linkage: denoised signals feed the error-budget dashboard. Only actionable events as defined above should decrement automated budget allowances (to avoid punishing teams for instrumentation noise).

Operational verification checklist (pre-automation)

1) Synthetic canary: deploy synthetic generator at 1% of traffic with configured steady patterns. Verify denoised trend matches canary within +/- 3% over 6 hours.
2) Replay test: run pipeline on archived 48-hour trace with known incidents; confirm detection precision >= 0.92 and false positive rate <= 0.06.
3) Shadow autoscaling: run the autoscale decisions in shadow mode for 48 hours and compare to baseline operator decisions.
4) Safety net: automated scale-up rate-limited to 20% per 10 minutes; require manual approval for >50% changes.

Incident review and evidence requirements

- For any incident where the denoised signal triggered an automated action, incident owners must provide: link to raw telemetry bucket, the denoising assertion (median/MAD summary), the STL decomposition visuals, and the synthetic canary comparison. Use template: IncidentEvidenceID-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>.
- Post-incident questions to answer: Did denoising mask a real regression? Were thresholds misconfigured? Was sampling rate adequate? Each answer must be documented in the postmortem.

Ownership and governance

- Owner: SRE Telemetry Squad (primary), Capacity team (secondary).
- Review cadence: monthly review of thresholds and denoising parameters; quarterly run replay tests across representative model families.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1) Detection: Alert fires on "denoised-p95-crossing" with tags {service, cluster, tenant}.
2) Triage (first 10 minutes):
   a) Verify the denoised signal dashboard.
   b) Cross-check raw minute-level p95 and sampled token traces.
   c) Check for correlated signals: GPU util, queue length, cache hit rate.
3) If actionable event (see Action Matrix):
   a) For automated actions, confirm change in ticketing system and observe for 10 minutes.
   b) For manual actions, escalate to platform oncall and follow manual pool add/runbook steps.
4) Post-action (within 1 hour):
   a) Verify SLO status and error-budget burn.
   b) If automated action did not reduce latency, begin rollback sequence and open incident.
5) Postmortem and parameter tuning: run replay and update denoising parameters if necessary.

Rollback safety and throttles

- Every automated scale operation includes an automatic rollback hook if:
  - latency p95 does not improve by at least 7% within 15 minutes, OR
  - queue growth continues for 20 minutes after scale-up.
- Throttle policy: when error budget < 20% remaining and 24h burn > 2x, admit new low-priority tokens at 70% rate and redirect bulk-batch jobs to deferred queue.

Example configs (YAML)

---
denoising:
  outlier_trim_percent: 0.1
  mad_threshold: 6
  smoothing:
    latency_alpha: 0.12
    rate_alpha: 0.25
    gpu_alpha: 0.08
  seasonal_period_minutes: 60
actions:
  max_auto_scale_pct_per_10m: 20
  auto_scale_notify: true
  require_manual_over_pct: 50
thresholds:
  p95_short_request_ms: 120
  p95_long_request_ms: 500
  gpu_saturation_pct: 92
  burst_multiplier: 3.0
---

Rollout plan

1) Pilot (2 weeks): enable denoising in shadow for a single service (recommendation: embeddings route) with sampling increased to 5%.
2) Evaluate: run replay tests and shadow autoscale. Review metrics with Platform Eng.
3) Gradual enable: enable for 25% of clusters for 1 week, then 50% for 1 week, then full for non-critical regions.
4) Hardening: after 30 days of full traffic with autopilot, remove shadow-mode rate limits for autoscaling and incorporate into SRE runbook triggers.

Related pages and templates

- SLO contract template: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-contract-template
- Incident evidence template: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-review/evidence-template
- Telemetry-sandbox guide: /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/telemetry-sandbox

Appendix A: Troubleshooting snippets

- Quick query to compare raw vs denoised p95 (ClickHouse):
SELECT minute, quantileExact(0.95)(latency_ms) AS raw_p95, smoothed_p95
FROM (
  SELECT toStartOfMinute(timestamp) AS minute, latency_ms, -- smoothed_p95 computed offline by pipeline
  FROM inference_requests
  WHERE service = 'redwood-api' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 2 HOUR
)
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute DESC

- If denoised signal suppressed a true regression: check sampling rate (increase to 20%), verify raw-top-0.1% values, and re-run replay with lower MAD threshold.

Revision history

- 2025-03-12 (Priya Nambiar): initial draft and pilot config.
- 2025-05-04 (Maya Chen): added burst gating logic and YAML defaults.
- 2026-11-02 (Ethan Ruiz): tuned alpha parameters after model-family replay testing; publish.

Contact and escalation

- Primary: SRE Telemetry Squad (pager: #sre-telemetry)
- Secondary: Capacity Team (pager: #capacity-ops)

End of runbook.

title: Capacity surge decision matrix and telemetry playbook
content:
Capacity surge decision matrix and telemetry playbook

Summary

This playbook codifies a decision matrix for rapid, repeatable responses to capacity surges across our inference and control-plane services. It defines telemetry signals, automated actions that can be taken without human intervention, and clear handoffs for on-call and capacity teams when escalation is required. The intent is to reduce time-to-decision during transient and sustained surges while protecting SLOs and error budget health.

Goals

- Provide a deterministic decision matrix mapping telemetry signals to actions.
- Differentiate between automated mitigations and manual interventions.
- Ensure ownership and communication paths are explicit.
- Capture instrumentation queries, thresholds, and post-action validation steps.

Scope and applicability

Applies to: Redwood public inference API, dedicated routing plane, autoscaler controller, and request-queueing components. Does not replace service-specific runbooks for data-plane hardware faults (GPU ECC, host offline). Use this playbook for traffic-driven capacity incidents and degraded latency/availability attributable to load.

Key telemetry signals

Primary signals (real-time — used in decision matrix):
- p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile upstream request latency (30s window).
- p99_9_latency_ms: 99.9th percentile (1m window) — failure early warning.
- error_rate_5m: 5-minute rolling request error rate (4xx/5xx split).
- queue_depth: average request queue length across the front-end pool.
- batch_fill_rate: fraction of batched requests meeting min_batch_size.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: model KV-cache prefix hit ratio.
- gpu_util: per-host GPU utilization (90th percentile).
- instance_provision_rate: new instance create rate (1m window).

Secondary signals (correlate before escalation):
- infra_restarts: host/container restart rate.
- disk_io_wait_ms: storage latency impacting model loads.
- model_load_failures: model pull errors from registry.

Representative Prometheus queries (implement exactly in Alerts/Playbook snippets)

- p95 latency (30s):
  - query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[30s])) by (le, service))
- p99.9 latency (1m):
  - query: histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, service))
- queue depth:
  - query: avg_over_time(request_queue_depth[30s])
- error rate (5m):
  - query: sum(rate(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))

Decision matrix (automatic -> guarded -> manual)

Table: telemetry -> error budget / SLO band -> immediate automated action -> on-call action if persists

| Signal | Error budget band | Automated action (0–15 min) | If persists (15–60 min) | Owner |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------------|-------|
| p95_latency > SLO * 1.25 | Minor consumption (<= 30% of budget/month) | Activate short-burst autoscale; increase batch-window up to configured max; enable fast-batch policy | Page primary on-call; run latency isolation playbook; consider rollback of recent rollout | service oncall / platform-autoscaler |
| p99_9_latency > SLO * 1.5 OR error_rate > 2% | Major consumption (> 30% of budget/month) | Immediately reduce max-concurrency per instance by 20%; route 20% traffic to warm fallback model (lower-cost variant) | Escalate to SRE war room; throttle non-critical routes; open capacity ticket for Dedicated pools | service oncall + capacity team |
| queue_depth > 2x baseline AND gpu_util < 85% | Potential batching saturation | Increase batch fill wait timeout by 50ms; enable KV-cache-prefetch optimization | Investigate slow downstream (disk/model load) and schedule controlled draining of affected hosts | service oncall / runtime team |
| gpu_util > 97% AND instance_provision_rate low | Sustained capacity saturation | Trigger preemptible burst pool (if available); mark capacity request for urgent allocation | Page capacity lead; evaluate resizing node pools; prepare emergency procurement/priority uplift | capacity team / infra |

Notes on bands and thresholds

- SLO baseline values are in the SLO catalog. The multiplier (1.25x / 1.5x) is conservative; teams may adjust for service-specific traffic shapes with approval from SRE.
- Error budget banding:
  - Minor: <= 30% monthly consumption
  - Major: 30% - 70%
  - Critical: > 70% or projected burn rate to full in < 24h

Automated mitigation design patterns

1) Safe autoscaling: ephemeral scale-up of stateless front-ends with circuit-breakers and cooldowns (max 2x baseline, 10-minute TTL).
2) Graceful degradation: selectively route to a lower-cost model variant; preserve correctness for critical routes.
3) Batching adjustments: increase/decrease wait window and preferred batch size with max-latency guardrails.
4) Prefetching and cache warming: kick off background KV-cache prefetch for hot prefixes when p95 jumps but GPU utilization is low.

Implementation snippet: sample policy (YAML)

- name: surge-short-burst
  trigger:
    p95_latency_margin: 0.25
    min_duration: 30s
  actions:
    - type: autoscale
      target: frontends
      factor: 1.5
      ttl: 600s
    - type: batch-tune
      new_wait_ms: 120
      max_increase_ms: 80

Runbook: step-by-step (who/what/when)

1) Detection (0-2 min)
   - On-call receives PagerDuty alert channel: #sre-alerts and a phone page if Major band.
   - Confirm signal by cross-checking p99_9 and queue_depth dashboards.

2) Automated mitigation verification (2-10 min)
   - Verify automation executed via /playbooks/actions log in Observability Console.
   - Check impact: p95 and queue metrics should start trending down within 1-3 minutes for transient events.

3) Initial human decision (10-20 min)
   - If automated actions reduced impact: declare incident level = Mitigated; continue monitoring and close after 60m stable.
   - If not: elevate to SRE on-call for deeper triage (open incident in incident-management tool).

4) Escalation and sustained response (20-60 min)
   - Execute manual mitigations (traffic throttles, targeted route blackholing to failover model).
   - Capacity team evaluates immediate pool resizing and preemption requests.
   - Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Capacity Lead, Runtime Triage.

5) Recovery and validation (60-180 min)
   - Confirm SLOs returning to normal and error budget burn rate reduced below critical threshold.
   - Run synthetic canary traffic through affected routes to validate behavior at target qps.

6) Post-incident (within 72h)
   - Run an incident review with the template in incident-review standards.
   - Update this playbook if any decision points were ambiguous.

Ownership and responsibility matrix

- Service on-call: initial triage, execute immediate safe actions, own incident timeline.
- Platform autoscaler: owns automated short-burst policies and their telemetry.
- Capacity team: handles pool resizing, priority allocation, cloud quota requests.
- Runtime team: investigates batching/kernel issues and KV-cache behavior.
- Observability: maintains and validates alerts, PromQL snippets, and dashboard correctness.

Communication templates

Slack incident header (use for initial page):
- [INCIDENT] <service> high latency — p95 at <value>ms — automated mitigations triggered.
- Current action: <autoscale / batch-tune / fallback>.
- IC: @<name> | Capacity lead: @<name> | Estimated next update: 10 min.

Pager message (for Major band):
- Rule: p99.9 > SLO*1.5 OR error_rate > 2% for 1m.
- Escalation path: service oncall -> capacity -> runtime -> infra

Observability checklist (post-action verification)

- Verify automated action executed: /playbooks/actions logs show success.
- Run these queries:
  - avg_over_time(request_duration_seconds[5m])
  - sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (route) to confirm load shift.
  - avg_over_time(gpu_util[1m]) by (pool) to confirm headroom.

Simulation and runbook drills

- Quarterly chaos drills: simulate 30% sustained qps increase for 30m on a canary region.
- Run tabletop exercises for the decision matrix with SRE + capacity + runtime.
- Measure time-to-decision and time-to-stable; target median time-to-decision < 12 minutes.

Metrics for playbook effectiveness

- Median time from alert to automated action: target < 90s.
- Fraction of surges resolved by automation: target >= 60%.
- Median time from detection to SLO recovery: target < 30 minutes.
- False-positive throttle/scale events (< 1% of actions).

Change control and review cadence

- Any change to automated thresholds requires a runbook change request and approval from SRE lead and Platform Autoscaler owner.
- Annual review of matrix and quarterly review after every drill.

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands and scripts

- Check queue depth across region:
  - curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/query?expr=avg_over_time(request_queue_depth{region=\"us-west-2\"}[30s])" | jq
- Manually trigger safe-burst autoscale (CLI):
  - rdx autoscale trigger --policy surge-short-burst --reason "oncall manual override" --ttl 600
- Example alert definition (YAML fragment):
  - alert: HighP95Latency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, service)) > (service_slo_seconds * 1.25)
    for: 30s
    labels:
      severity: warning
    annotations:
      runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/capacity-surge-decision-matrix-and-telemetry-playbook-2026

End of document.

title: Runtime Scheduler Decision Fabric and Telemetry Playbook
content:
Runtime Scheduler Decision Fabric and Telemetry Playbook

Summary

This document defines the "Decision Fabric" concept for the runtime scheduler: a structured set of decision points, the telemetry signals required to make those decisions, and a practical playbook for evaluating, rolling out, and debugging scheduler policy changes. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and owners of scheduling policy components.

Goals

- Make scheduling decisions auditable and reproducible.
- Ensure telemetry is sufficient to explain why any request took the path it did.
- Provide safe rollout and rollback steps for scheduler changes.
- Define incident triage and escalation steps when scheduling misbehavior impacts SLOs.

Scope

Covers: kernel scheduling policy decision points, admission controllers, priority tags, preemption windows, kernel selection hints, and the telemetry & alerts that validate these decisions.
Does not cover: low-level GPU kernel source code changes or vendor driver instrumentation (those belong to kernel-and-scheduling code docs).

1. Decision Fabric: concepts and nodes

The Decision Fabric is a logical DAG of discrete decision nodes that operate on enriched request context and produce actions or routing hints. Nodes are micro-decision units intended to be small and testable. Example nodes:

- Request Classification: maps incoming request attributes to a class (e.g., interactive, batch, background).
- Admission Gate: enforces concurrency & slot availability budget for class and tenant.
- Priority Arbiter: resolves conflicts between competing requests (SLA, customer tier, emerging emergency).
- Kernel Selector: picks the kernel variant and quantization profile.
- Prefetch/KV Hint: decides whether to fetch KV cache for a session.
- Fallback Router: chooses alternate model variant/region on capacity or error.

Each node emits a standardized Decision Event (see Telemetry section). Nodes are composed into runtime pipelines.

2. Decision Event schema (telemetry contract)

All scheduler decision nodes MUST emit a Decision Event at the moment a decision is made. This makes decisions traceable end-to-end. The near-term schema (text representation):

Example Decision Event (single-line JSON text for logs; the runtime also emits structured proto for the tracing pipeline):
{
  "request_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-15T14:12:03Z",
  "node": "PriorityArbiter:v2",
  "input_signals": ["tenancy_tier:standard","seq_len_estimate:32","recent_error_rate:0.002"],
  "decision": "grant:slot-id=slot-42, kernel_hint=gptq-4bit-fp16",
  "reason_codes": ["tenancy_quota_ok","latency_target_50ms"],
  "latency_ms": 0.42,
  "cost_weight": 1.0
}

- Note: Events should be JSON-encoded when landing in structured logging systems; they must also exist as compact binary in the tracing pipeline for high-cardinality sampling.

Required fields (text form): request_id, timestamp (ISO8601), node (string), decision (string), reason_codes (list), latency_ms (number), cost_weight (number), input_signals (list).
Optional but recommended: model_version, kernel_revision, tenant_id, route, sampled_trace_id.

3. Minimal telemetry to support common investigations

To triage scheduling issues within 5–15 minutes, the following telemetry streams are required:

- Decision Events (high cardinality, sampled): ~1 per decision; sample strategy below.
- Request Timeline Trace (distributed trace spanning API -> admission -> kernel dispatch).
- Per-kernel execution metrics: queue_time_ms, kernel_exec_ms, retry_count.
- Admission & slot pool stats: available_slots, inflight_by_tier, eviction_count.
- Request classification histogram: seq_len, token_budget, request_surface_type.

Suggested retention and sampling:

| Stream | Sampling | Hot retention | Cold retention |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|Decision Events|100% for tier=enterprise; 5% for standard/free|7d|180d|
|Request Traces|100% for p99+ tail traces, 1% baseline|14d|90d|
|Kernel exec metrics|Aggregate per-min buckets 100%|30d|365d|

4. Reason-coding taxonomy (short list)

Decision nodes should attach reason codes. We maintain a canonical set to avoid free-form strings. Examples:

- quota_exhausted
- latency_slo_risk
- high_seq_len
- emergency_preemption
- kernel_incompatible
- kvcache_miss
- model_swap_fallback

5. Playbook: safe rollout of scheduler changes

This is the sequential process you must follow when deploying a scheduler policy change (e.g., new PriorityArbiter logic, admission thresholds, kernel selector rules):

1) Design review and unit tests
- Create an ADR (link to decision record). Include decision fabric impact map (which nodes change).
- Unit tests: determinism tests for decision nodes and reason_code coverage matrix.

2) Local and integration testing
- Run deterministic replay of representative request corpus (use the operational workload simulator) and compare Decision Event diffs.
- Validate no new reason codes introduced unintentionally.

3) Canary rollout (safety gates)
- Canary cohort: 0.5% baseline requests or a narrow tenant set of non-critical accounts.
- Observability checks (automated):
  - p50/p95 request latency for canary <= baseline + 5%
  - decision_event.reason_code change rate <= 2x baseline for any single reason code
  - admission.rejection_rate <= baseline + 0.1% absolute
  - kernel_exec_ms median unchanged or improved

4) Gradual ramp and policy checks
- Ramp to 5% after 30m if canary signals pass for 15m rolling windows.
- Run the differential tracer extractor to verify decision path similarity (expectation: >95% of canary decisions match legacy for non-experimental paths).

5) Full rollout and post-mortem observation
- After 24 hours at 100% observe metrics for 72 hours.
- If any SLO regressions occur, trigger automatic rollback and open a postmortem.

6. Incident triage checklist (scheduling-related)

When customers observe increased latency or error rates that trace to scheduler behavior:

1. Confirm alert and scope: check SLO dashboards for elevated p99 and per-route errors.
2. Correlate with Decision Event spike: query decision_event.node aggregated by reason_code in last 15m.
3. Inspect admission pool state: available_slots, pool_eviction_count, queue_time_ms.
4. Query kernel health: dispatch_fail_rate, nvlink_errors, watchdog_restarts.
5. If decision nodes show a sudden change in reason_code distribution (e.g., quota_exhausted spikes), identify the upstream change (policy, config, traffic surge).
6. If root cause is policy regression, execute rollback (see Rollback snippet).

Rollback CLI snippet (example):

# Roll back to last stable policy bundle
redwood-schedctl rollback --bundle-id=rb-2026-0007 --reason="p99-latency-regression"

Wait for slot metrics and decision_event reason_code to normalize, then annotate the incident.

7. Debug recipes and quick checks

- "Why did my request get preempted?"
  1) Search Decision Events by request_id -> look at PriorityArbiter and Admission Gate nodes.
  2) Check reason_codes: if emergency_preemption present, check active incident tags and owner.

- "Why was kernel_variant X chosen?"
  1) Inspect KernelSelector decision event; cross-check input_signals for sequence length and model_version.
  2) Look at kernel_revision compatibility table (see table below).

Kernel compatibility table (text):
| kernel_revision | model_family | quant_profile | notes |
| kv1.4 | gpt-j | 8bit | legacy; higher latency for long seqs |
| gq-2025-4b | llama-family | gptq-4bit-fp16 | low cost; prefer for background tasks |
| vbench-rc2 | opt | int8 | experimental; disable for enterprise tenants |

8. Metric and alert definitions (examples)

- sched.decision.rate (counter): decision events per second. Alert: sustained drop >30% over 5m -> scheduler stall investigation.
- sched.admission.rejection_rate (gauge %): Alert if >0.5% absolute above baseline for 10m.
- sched.kernel.queue_time_p99 (ms): Alert if >250ms for 5m.
- sched.reasoncode.quotas_exhausted.rate (counter): Alert if sudden spike (>5x expected) during deployment windows.

9. Sampling and storage plan for Decision Events

We recommend a two-path approach:
1) High-fidelity path (tracing infra) stores sampled full traces and Decision Events for a narrow sample of requests and all p99 tail traces.
2) Low-cost aggregated path stores per-minute aggregated counters and histograms for long-term analytics.

Sampling knobs (examples):
- sample_by_tier: {enterprise: 100%, standard: 5%, free: 1%}
- tail_capture: p99+ of request_latency || error_rate -> force sample.

10. Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: runtime-scheduler team (oncall rota: runtime-scheduler@pagerduty).
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (for capacity, node-level issues).
- Incident severity mapping:
  - Sev-1: customer-facing outage (SLO > 30m breach) -> notify exec-oncall, start incident bridge.
  - Sev-2: p99 latency spikes without complete outage (SRE & scheduler oncall).

11. Compatibility and migration notes

- When changing reason codes or Decision Event schema, include a compatibility shim for 60 days. Update the schema registry and add transformers in the analytics pipeline.

12. Appendix: example decision event query patterns

- Find the decision path for a request id (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT * FROM decision_events WHERE request_id = 'req-123' ORDER BY timestamp ASC;

- Aggregate reason code rate by node:
  SELECT node, reason_code, count(*) FROM decision_events WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '15m' GROUP BY node, reason_code ORDER BY count DESC;

13. Change log

- 2024-09-12: initial draft by Riley Chen.
- 2025-03-02: added kernel compatibility table and rollout gates (Aisha Patel review).
- 2026-01-15: updated Decision Event schema and sampling defaults (Marco Silva).

Related material and references

- Scheduler policy language spec (see related pages).
- Request classification and telemetry contract (team-wiki).

Contact

For questions or to request changes to the decision fabric, open a PR against the runtime-scheduler repo and add runtime-scheduler@team as reviewers.

title: Platform Observability & SLI Onboarding Playbook
content:
Platform Observability & SLI Onboarding Playbook

Overview:
This playbook standardizes how platform services are onboarded into Redwood's observability stack, how SLIs/SLOs are defined and registered, and what dashboard/alert templates are required before a service is considered production-ready. It is targeted at platform engineers, service owners, and SREs.

Why this exists:
- Reduce time-to-observable for new services while enforcing consistent SLI definitions.
- Protect product teams from noisy alerts and under-instrumentation.
- Provide a repeatable checklist for production readiness reviews and SLO registration.

Quick summary (one-line):
All platform services must implement the onboarding checklist below, publish SLIs to the SLO library, and deploy a standardized Grafana dashboard and Prometheus alerts prior to enrollment in error-budget policies.

Scope:
- Applies to: services owned by eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, and core infra teams that expose HTTP/gRPC endpoints, async job processors, or stream processors.
- Exempts: ephemeral experimentation sandboxes and single-run jobs (document exceptions with owner and retention policy).

Ownership and escalation:
- Playbook owner: Platform Observability Guild (contact: platform-observability@redwood.ai)
- Service owner: listed in the service manifest (see onboarding checklist step 1).
- SRE reviewer: assigned during PR review for onboarding (rotation in eng-sre team).

Required artifacts before "production-ready" badge is granted:
1) Service manifest updated in infra repo with contact, component tag, and SLIs.
2) Instrumentation: metrics, structured logs, and traces (see instrumentation section).
3) Grafana dashboard using the platform template (see panels below).
4) Prometheus alert rules committed and linted.
5) SLO registered in SLO library with owner and review cadence.
6) Runbook entry with playbook steps, recovery commands, and rollback guidance.
7) Cost and retention guardrails validated with infra costing tool.

SLI / SLO standardization:
- Default SLI set (apply to HTTP/gRPC services):
  - Availability (success rate): requests with 2xx/3xx over total requests — window=30d, daily burn back.
  - Latency P95: request duration (ms) — window=30d.
  - Latency P99 (for high-priority routes): request duration (ms) — window=7d.
  - Queue depth / backlog for async processors: 99th percentile of queue_length over 1d.
  - Error rate by class: 5xx and client-expected-errors measured separately.

- Default SLO targets (suggested baseline):
  - Availability: 99.95% (soft default for latency-sensitive platform endpoints)
  - Latency P95: <= 200ms for API routes; <= 1s for heavy batch endpoints
  - Latency P99: <= 1s for API routes; <= 5s for batch
  - Queue depth: target mean below 10 items for normal load

- Error budget policy:
  - Burn alerts at 25%, 50%, and 75% of daily error budget consumptions.
  - At 100% consumption trigger immediate on-call page and canary rollback recommendation.

Instrumentation guidelines:
- Metrics: use open-metrics naming conventions. Prefix: redwood_<component>_<metric>. Example: redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket
- Labels: service, env, region, route, team, pod (avoid freeform user ids).
- Tracing: include a distributed trace id in logs. Sample at 5% globally; increase to 100% for Canary environments. Use W3C Trace Context.
- Logs: JSON structured logs with level, service, shard, trace_id. Sensitive data must be redacted at the emitter.
- Exporters: Prometheus for metrics, Grafana Tempo for traces, Loki/Datadog native for logs (depending on environment).

Dashboard template (minimum panels):
- Overview row: Success rate (30d), Requests per second (last 1h), Error budget remaining
- Latency row: P50/P95/P99 latency heatmap, latency by route table
- Capacity row: Pod counts, CPU/Memory by pod, OOM rate
- Backpressure row: Queue length, inflight requests, DB pool saturation
- Cost row: estimated GPU/VM-hours consumed (if applicable)

Example table (panel -> query -> suggested thresholds):
| Panel | PromQL example | Alert threshold | Notes |
| Overview: success_rate | (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\",code!~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m]))) * 100 | < 99.9% for 5m | Service-level availability |
| Latency p95 | histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m])) by (le)) | p95 > 0.2 for 10m | Use per-route override |
| Queue depth | max(queue_length{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}) | > 50 for 15m | Backpressure sign |

Prometheus alert rule examples (paste into alerts/prometheus/%SERVICE%.rules.yaml):
---
- alert: ServiceAvailabilityDegraded
  expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\",code!~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m]))) * 100 < 99.9
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
    team: %TEAM%
  annotations:
    summary: "%SERVICE% availability below 99.9%"
    runbook: "link_to_runbook/%SERVICE%"

- alert: ServiceLatencyP95High
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.2
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
    team: %TEAM%
  annotations:
    summary: "%SERVICE% p95 latency > 200ms"

Alert categorization and routing:
- severity: page (P0-P1): immediate paging to on-call, include runbook and rollback link.
- severity: ticket (P2): create tracking ticket in PagerDuty/ServiceNow; notify team Slack channel.
- severity: info (P3): create quiet incident in tracking board.

On-call runbook (first-response):
1) Acknowledge the page within 5 minutes.
2) Check the dashboard overview: success rate, requests/s, p95.
3) Determine scope: single route / region / global. Use query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\",route=~\"%ROUTE%\"}[5m])) by (region)
4) If error budget > 25% consumed: begin mitigation. If 100%: escalate to incident.
5) Mitigation steps (in order):
   a) Trigger traffic-shift to canary (kubectl -n %NS% set image deploy/%DEPLOY% %CONTAINER%=%BACKUP_IMAGE%) or toggle edge routing to fallback model.
   b) Scale up pods: kubectl -n %NS% scale deploy/%DEPLOY% --replicas=<replica-count>
   c) Rollback last release: kubectl -n %NS% rollout undo deploy/%DEPLOY% --to-revision=<rev>
   d) If database-related, fail-fast: reduce write traffic via feature-flagging or turn on queueing layer.
6) Record mitigation and update incident ticket with root cause hypotheses.

Post-incident actions and SLO review:
- Run a focused retrospective within 3 business days.
- Update SLO if cadence or traffic patterns change.
- Add synthetic check for failing route if missing.
- If root cause is instrumentation blindspot, update the instrumentation checklist and re-review all services in the component.

Automation and CI gates:
- PRs to production manifests must pass: prometheus-rule-lint, grafana-dashboard-validator, and slo-linter.
- A CI job generates a preview dashboard and a preview PrometheusRule in staging for verification.
- A pre-merge hook rejects alerts with severity:page that lack a runbook link.

Cost and retention guardrails:
- Default metric scrape interval: 15s for infra-critical metrics, 60s for app-level metrics.
- Minimize high-cardinality labels. Use cardinality budget: 100k series per service as starting limit.
- Logs: 30d hot retention, 90d warm depending on service SLAs. Traces: 7d by default; 30d for high-priority customer-facing flows (approve via data governance).

Onboarding checklist (detailed steps):
1) Create service manifest entry in infra/services/ with owner, team, contact, and tags.
2) Implement metrics + export to Prometheus (include example metrics: request_count, request_duration_seconds_bucket, error_count).
3) Add tracing headers and wire into Tempo; verify end-to-end trace in staging.
4) Add Grafana dashboard: use template import ID: 1089 (platform-service-overview). Replace %SERVICE% variables.
5) Add Prometheus rule: commit to alerts/%SERVICE%.rules.yaml and run lint.
6) Register SLO: open a PR against eng-sre/slo-library with SLI queries, SLO target, owner, and review cadence.
7) Create runbook page: copy template and fill recovery steps and CNAs.
8) Schedule a production readiness brief with SRE reviewer and platform guild.
9) After successful verification in staging for 72h under normal load, tag PR with "ready-for-prod" for merge.

Template snippets and helpful links:
- Dashboard template: grafana://dashboard/1089
- SLO library PR template: https://git.internal.redwood.ai/eng-sre/slo-library/templates/slo-pr.md
- Prometheus lint: ./tools/prom-lint --path alerts/%SERVICE%.rules.yaml
- Grafana validator: ./tools/grafana-validate --file dashboards/%SERVICE%.json

Common pitfalls and remediation:
- Missing route labels: leads to noisy aggregate alerts. Remedy: require per-route label in instrumentation.
- High-cardinality metrics from user_id tags: block in code review; suggest using hashed_user_bucket instead.
- Over-aggressive tracing: high cost; use adaptive sampling and increase only for canaries.

Retrospective prompts (post-onboarding, 30d):
- Were the SLO targets appropriate?
- Did dashboards surface the root cause quickly?
- Any alert noise that needs suppression or reclassification?
- Cost impacts of retention and scrape frequency — can we tune?

Change log:
- 2025-08-12: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2025-11-03: Added error budget policy and alert thresholds (Arjun Patel).
- 2026-01-10: Updated dashboard template ID and added CI gate requirements (Lina Gómez).

Appendix: sample CLI checks (copy into runbook):
- Check p95 in last 15m:
  curl -s -G 'https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m])) by (le))' | jq -r '.data.result'
- Verify alert presence:
  kubectl -n monitoring get prometheusrules -o yaml | grep -A3 "%SERVICE%"
- Preview dashboard locally:
  ./tools/grafana-preview dashboards/%SERVICE%.json

End of playbook. For onboarding support, contact platform-observability@redwood.ai or open a PR in infra/services for review.

title: Usage Insights API Contract (v1)
content:
Usage Insights API Contract (v1)

h1. Overview

This document defines the v1 API contract for *Usage Insights* in Redwood Console.

The API provides:
* Cost/usage breakdowns attributed by *route + model* (and optional dimensions: project, env, deployment mode, region).
* “Top cost drivers” and “What changed?” insights.
* CSV export job lifecycle (async generation + signed downloads).

This is an *API standards* contract. Service-specific implementation details (warehouse tables, cache strategy, dependencies) live in the system doc.

h2. Goals

* Provide stable, predictable request/response shapes for console and external tooling.
* Support cursor-based pagination and consistent filter semantics.
* Ensure time bucket boundaries are deterministic and well-defined with time zone handling.
* Provide a robust export job model (create → poll → download) with RBAC and audit logging.
* Maintain consistent totals vs billing, with documented rounding/tolerance.

h2. Non-goals

* Fully automated optimization actions (API may include recommendations as links only).
* Arbitrary customer-defined dimensions beyond the fixed allowlist.

h2. Versioning and compatibility

* All endpoints are under */v1/*.
* Backwards compatibility policy:
  * Additive changes (new fields) are allowed without version bump.
  * Renames/removals require a new major version.
  * Enums may gain new values; clients must handle unknown enum values.

h1. Authentication and authorization

h2. AuthN

* Standard Redwood API auth: *Authorization: Bearer <token>*.
* Requests must include *X-Request-Id* (client-generated UUID) when possible; otherwise the server will generate one.

h2. AuthZ (RBAC)

Usage Insights contains cost data and must be gated.

* Read breakdowns:
  * Requires permission: *insights.cost:read* (or workspace setting that allows cost visibility).
* Create/download exports:
  * Requires permission: *insights.cost:export*.
* Shareable links (if enabled) are governed by the same permission checks at time of access.

If a workspace is configured to *Hide cost data*, endpoints return 403 even if the user can view non-cost usage metrics elsewhere.

h1. Common conventions

h2. Content types

* Requests: JSON
  * Content-Type: application/json
* Responses: JSON
  * Content-Type: application/json
* Export downloads: text/csv (via signed URL)

h2. Time handling

* All timestamps in responses are RFC 3339 in UTC (e.g., 2026-02-16T18:42:11Z).
* Requests accept a *tz* parameter (IANA time zone, e.g., America/Los_Angeles) used only to compute *bucket boundaries* and to interpret *date-only* ranges.
* If *tz* is omitted:
  * Default tz = UTC.

h3. Range semantics

Requests can specify either:
* Explicit timestamps (*start_at*, *end_at*) in RFC 3339, OR
* A relative window (*lookback*) like 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d.

Rules:
* *start_at* is inclusive.
* *end_at* is exclusive.
* If both explicit and lookback are provided, the server returns 400.

h2. Freshness semantics

Most responses include:
* *as_of*: the latest event timestamp fully included.
* *data_lag_seconds*: estimated lag from “now” to *as_of*.

Clients should render warnings when data_lag_seconds is above the UI threshold.

h2. Cardinality and filter allowlist

To keep query latency predictable, only the following dimensions are queryable and/or groupable:
* workspace_id (required)
* project_id (optional)
* environment (optional; enum: prod | staging | dev | unknown)
* deployment_mode (optional; enum: hosted | dedicated | private | unknown)
* region (optional; Redwood region string)
* route (optional; *normalized* route, see ADR)
* model (optional; stable model identifier)
* model_family (optional)
* model_version (optional; reporting bucket)

Route normalization and model bucketing MUST follow:
* ADR: *Route normalization and attribution*

h2. Standard error format

All non-2xx responses return:

{code}
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_argument",
    "message": "end_at must be after start_at",
    "request_id": "3f8b3a2a-9e1f-4e6b-8c2a-3fd0fbfe7e0d"
  }
}
{code}

Common error codes:
* invalid_argument (400)
* unauthorized (401)
* forbidden (403)
* not_found (404)
* conflict (409)
* too_many_requests (429)
* internal (500)

h1. Endpoint summary

* GET /v1/usage-insights/breakdown
* GET /v1/usage-insights/top-drivers
* POST /v1/usage-insights/exports
* GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}
* POST /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}/cancel

Notes:
* Export download is via a signed URL returned by GET export status when ready.
* Some installations may additionally support: GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}/download-url (alias) for clarity.

h1. GET /v1/usage-insights/breakdown

Returns a paginated breakdown table grouped by one or more dimensions, with per-group cost and usage metrics.

h2. Query parameters

Required:
* workspace_id (string)

Time window (choose one):
* start_at (RFC3339)
* end_at (RFC3339)
* lookback (string: 1h | 24h | 7d | 30d)

Optional filters:
* project_id (string)
* environment (prod | staging | dev | unknown)
* deployment_mode (hosted | dedicated | private | unknown)
* region (string)
* route (string; normalized)
* model (string)
* model_family (string)
* model_version (string)

Grouping:
* group_by (repeatable query param; allowed values: route, model, model_family, model_version, region, deployment_mode, environment, project_id)
  * Default: group_by=route&group_by=model

Bucketing:
* granularity (string; enum: hour | day)
  * Default: day
* tz (IANA time zone)
  * Default: UTC

Sorting/pagination:
* order_by (string; enum: total_cost | tokens_in | tokens_out | requests | p95_latency_ms)
  * Default: total_cost
* order (asc | desc)
  * Default: desc
* page_size (int; 1–500)
  * Default: 100
* cursor (opaque string)

h2. Response shape

{code}
{
  "as_of": "2026-02-16T18:00:00Z",
  "data_lag_seconds": 420,
  "currency": "USD",
  "granularity": "day",
  "tz": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "range": {
    "start_at": "2026-02-09T08:00:00Z",
    "end_at": "2026-02-16T08:00:00Z"
  },
  "group_by": ["route", "model"],
  "rows": [
    {
      "dimensions": {
        "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
        "model": "llama-3.1-70b"
      },
      "metrics": {
        "requests": 182341,
        "successful_requests": 181902,
        "errored_requests": 439,
        "retries": 1203,
        "fallback_requests": 881,
        "streaming_requests": 176210,
        "tokens_in": 934820112,
        "tokens_out": 1120938812,
        "cache_hit_tokens": 402881920,
        "cache_miss_tokens": 1532877004,
        "total_cost": 28432.17,
        "avg_latency_ms": 812.4,
        "p50_latency_ms": 691,
        "p95_latency_ms": 1612
      }
    }
  ],
  "page": {
    "next_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMH0=",
    "has_more": true
  },
  "totals": {
    "requests": 401223,
    "tokens_in": 1900012211,
    "tokens_out": 2219001123,
    "total_cost": 51210.44
  }
}
{code}

h2. Notes on fields

* dimensions: Only includes keys specified by group_by.
* retries: Count of server-side retry attempts attributable to the request lifecycle.
* fallback_requests: Number of requests that were served by a fallback policy/model after the originally selected model could not serve.
* cache_*_tokens: Token attribution follows the metering pipeline definition; for prefix/KV cache, token accounting is based on “billed tokens avoided” vs “billed tokens processed” as standardized in telemetry.

h2. Billing consistency and rounding

* total_cost is returned as a decimal number in the workspace billing currency.
* Totals are expected to reconcile with billing within tolerance:
  * Daily range: <= 0.5%
  * Hourly range: <= 1.0% (more sensitive to late events)
* The API returns *unrounded* values to 1/10000 currency unit internally; clients should display with 2 decimal places.

h1. GET /v1/usage-insights/top-drivers

Returns top cost drivers and “what changed” explanations for the selected window compared to a prior period.

h2. Query parameters

Required:
* workspace_id

Time window (choose one):
* start_at + end_at OR lookback

Optional:
* project_id, environment, deployment_mode, region
* route (if set, provides drivers within a route)
* model/model_family/model_version (if set, provides drivers within a model bucket)

Comparison:
* compare_to (string; enum: previous_period | previous_week)
  * Default: previous_period
* tz (IANA time zone; default UTC)

Pagination:
* page_size (1–200; default 50)
* cursor

h2. Response shape

{code}
{
  "as_of": "2026-02-16T18:00:00Z",
  "data_lag_seconds": 420,
  "currency": "USD",
  "range": {
    "start_at": "2026-02-09T08:00:00Z",
    "end_at": "2026-02-16T08:00:00Z"
  },
  "compare_to": {
    "mode": "previous_period",
    "start_at": "2026-02-02T08:00:00Z",
    "end_at": "2026-02-09T08:00:00Z"
  },
  "drivers": [
    {
      "scope": {
        "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
        "model": "llama-3.1-70b"
      },
      "rank": 1,
      "headline": "Token out increased +35% WoW",
      "impact": {
        "cost_delta": 8120.55,
        "percent_of_total_delta": 0.41
      },
      "signals": [
        {
          "name": "tokens_out",
          "delta_percent": 35.2,
          "delta_absolute": 221990112,
          "explain": "More output tokens per request increased cost; median output length shifted from 410 → 540 tokens."
        },
        {
          "name": "cache_hit_rate",
          "delta_percent": -12.1,
          "explain": "Cache hit rate decreased; more tokens were processed by the model instead of served from cache."
        }
      ],
      "recommended_actions": [
        {
          "title": "Add response length guardrails",
          "url": "https://docs.redwood.example/optimize/response-length"
        },
        {
          "title": "Review caching configuration for this route",
          "url": "https://docs.redwood.example/console/usage-insights#cache"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "page": {
    "next_cursor": null,
    "has_more": false
  }
}
{code}

h2. Explainability requirements

Top drivers MUST:
* Include a plain-language headline.
* Provide at least one measurable signal (delta) tied to user-visible metrics.
* Avoid causal claims that cannot be supported (use “correlates with” when appropriate).

h1. POST /v1/usage-insights/exports

Creates an async export job for a breakdown dataset (CSV). Exports are used for engineering and finance workflows (chargeback, BI ingestion).

h2. Request body

{code}
{
  "workspace_id": "ws_123",
  "project_id": "proj_456",
  "filters": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
    "model_family": "llama-3.1",
    "model_version": "2026-01"
  },
  "range": {
    "start_at": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_at": "2026-02-16T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "tz": "UTC",
  "granularity": "day",
  "group_by": ["route", "model"],
  "format": "csv",
  "columns": "default"
}
{code}

Notes:
* filters keys are optional; unknown keys return 400.
* columns may be:
  * "default" (server-defined stable default set)
  * "all" (includes extended metrics)

h2. Response (201)

{code}
{
  "export_id": "exp_01HTY5Q7K2Y0A0N6ZK3Z0K9P0M",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2026-02-16T18:10:00Z",
