- Hybrid: base session fee + per-token on overage (best for unpredictable long sessions).
- Tiered fidelity bundles: customers buy bundles of sessions at different fidelity presets with discounts on committed volume.

Recommended baseline presets (example):
- low-fidelity (L1): gpt-like-2s-quant, max_input 512 tokens, max_output 256 tokens, 10 ms tail-latency SLO, recommended for high-volume low-complexity tasks. Price: $0.003 per session.
- medium-fidelity (M1): open-xlarge-1, max_input 2048 tokens, max_output 512 tokens, 30 ms tail-latency SLO, Price: $0.01 per session.
- high-fidelity (H1): open-xxl, max_input 4096 tokens, max_output 1024 tokens, 100 ms tail-latency SLO, Price: $0.04 per session.
(Prices are illustrative; final contract pricing is adjusted by region, commitment, and Dedicated capacity mix.)

Economics calculation (example table):
| Metric | low-fidelity | medium-fidelity | high-fidelity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| avg tokens per session (input+output) | 150 | 600 | 1800 |
| tokens processed per session (incl. caching) | 120 | 420 | 1300 |
| GPU-second equivalent | 0.02 | 0.08 | 0.35 |
| incremental infra cost estimate | $0.0006 | $0.0024 | $0.0105 |
| suggested session price | $0.003 | $0.01 | $0.04 |

Notes on calculation: use 90-day rolling medians for tokens/session, prefix-cache hit-rate, and model-level throughput to avoid over-indexing on spikes. For Dedicated customers, base infra cost should use committed capacity marginal cost rather than public hosted rates.

Telemetry & KPIs to publish in Console:
- sessions.created per minute, sessions.active, median & 95th percentile tokens per session
- session_fidelity_applied metric (enum: L1/M1/H1)
- session_warmup_seconds and session_warmup_success (boolean)
- billing_effective_cost_per_session (derived)
- fidelity_overage_events and fallback_reasons

Customer onboarding checklist (sales & CSM):
1. Collect expected session profile: avg length, peak concurrency, expected monthly sessions, required SLOs.
2. Recommend fidelity presets and simulate economics using the simulator (see Appendix A).
3. Agree on warm-capacity reservation level for peak concurrency and any burst credits.
4. Define rollback trigger thresholds: e.g., cost drift >15% or user-visible latency > target for 24h.

Internal rollout runbook (engineering + product):
1. Feature toggle: enable session-pricing per tenant (console flag: session_pricing_enabled).
2. Implement meter: attach session_id label to telemetry & billing pipeline.
3. Acceptance tests: synthetic traffic generator with 3 session profiles (short, medium, long) and assert billing matches simulator within 5%.
4. Canary: release to <5 customers with auto-rollback if billing_mismatch_rate > 2% or fidelity_fallback_rate > 1%.
5. Scale: open to broader beta after 2-week stability and sign-off from Finance.

Customer-facing docs and UX notes:
- Console should show per-session cost estimate with sliders to alter avg tokens and fidelity preset.
- Provide an exportable simulation report (CSV) with expected monthly cost, peak concurrency recommendation, and recommended commitment tier.
- Show fallback transparency: if a session falls back (quantized variant or lower fidelity) record and expose reason and cost delta.

Rollback and incident playbook (SRE):
1. Detect: alert if billing_effective_cost_per_session drift > 20% vs expected for >1h (PAGE S1).
2. Triage: check recent model variant changes, quantization rollouts, and autoscaler events.
3. Immediate mitigation: switch impacted tenants to hybrid mode (base fee + per-token) and cap session concurrency to last-known-safe level.
4. Postmortem: include cost delta, root cause, customer impact, and required product changes.

Rollout timeline (recommended):
- Q1 2027: Internal alpha (engineering + product) with simulator and console mockups.
- Q2 2027: Beta with up to 10 customers (hosted + dedicated pilot).
- Q3 2027: Public launch with SDK updates, console features, and billing integration.

Ownership and contacts:
- Product lead: Priya Menon
- Engineering owner: Daniel Wu (runtime billing integration)
- Finance steward: Mariana Costa
- SRE contact: Luca Moretti

Appendix A — Quick simulator examples (CLI):
1) Local simulation (example):
$ redwood-sim sessions --preset M1 --avg-input 400 --avg-output 200 --monthly-sessions 250000 --out report.csv
2) Draft JSON payload for pricing API (example):
{
  "tenant_id": "T-12345",
  "pricing_mode": "hybrid",
  "base_session_fee": "0.01",
  "overage_per_token": "0.000002",
  "fidelity_presets": ["M1"]
}

Appendix B — Done criteria for public launch:
- Telemetry shows accurate session attribution for 30 days with <1% unmapped events.
- Finance validates margin model across hosted & dedicated customers with sample contracts.
- Console UX passes accessibility and clarity heuristics with customer testing.

Document history:
- 2026-11-15: Draft created by Priya Menon.
- 2026-12-08: Internal review with Runtime and Finance; updated fidelity presets.
- 2027-01-12: Updated rollout timeline and approval for Beta cohort.

Related links:
- Design spec: /confluence/product-docs/design-specs/elastic-session-crediting-and-migration-playbook-2026-01-15
- PRD: /confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-session-resilience-and-fallback-contract-2026-08-03

Questions or feedback: contact priya.menon@redwood.com

title: Optimize 1.3 release notes — Performance Profiles & Cost Telemetry
content:
Optimize 1.3 release notes — Performance Profiles & Cost Telemetry

Summary
-------
This document summarizes the Redwood Optimize 1.3 release (GA: 2026-02-20). Optimize 1.3 introduces Performance Profiles, Telemetry-based Cost Estimator, latency-tier presets for the Console, and several SDK/CLI usability improvements. The release targets customers using Redwood Optimize to tune Dedicated and Hosted inference for predictable unit economics and simplified rollout of quantization/batching recommendations.

Highlights
----------
- Performance Profiles (feature flag: optimize.performance_profiles): per-model, per-workload profiles that capture measured latency/throughput/cost at multiple sequence-length distributions. Profiles power auto-suggestion rules and the new cost estimator.
- Telemetry-based Cost Estimator: end-to-end estimator that uses historical request shape telemetry (prefix length, tokens-per-request, hit rates) to produce monthly cost projections and sensitivity analyses.
- Latency-tier Presets in Console: new predefined profiles (S0: <50ms p95, S1: <120ms p95, S2: <250ms p95) that automatically tune batching and cache TTL recommendations.
- SDK v0.18.0: new Optimize client with async estimate_cost() and get_performance_profile() helpers; breaking rename of estimate() -> estimate_cost().
- CLI: redwood optimize export-profile <model> -> writes a reproducible YAML profile used for Dedicated scheduling.
- Migration & compatibility: recommended default quantization profiles unchanged; deprecated optimize.legacy_hint removed (see Migration notes).

What’s new (detailed)
---------------------
1) Performance Profiles
   - Description: Profiles record observed stat distributions for: sequence_length, tokens_generated, request_rate (qps), prefix_cache_hit_rate. Each profile stores measured p50/p95 latencies and per-token GPU time across representative buckets (short/medium/long).
   - Storage: profiles are stored in the customer namespace (s3-backed), versioned, and visible via Console and API.
   - API preview: POST /v1/optimize/profiles {"model":"redwood-7b-v1","workload":"chat-short"} -> returns profile id and recommendations.
   - Owner: Optimize team (owner: Deepa Nair).

2) Telemetry-based Cost Estimator
   - Inputs: time window (default 30d), model(s), deployment mode (hosted/dedicated), commitment tier, sequence-length histogram.
   - Output: month-over-month projection (USD), token breakdown (input/system/output), sensitivity table (how cost changes if average tokens/request increases by +10/25/50%).
   - Accuracy caveats: estimator factors in measured batching efficiency and prefix cache hit rate; for cold-start or sparse telemetry customers, the estimator uses conservative defaults (see config below).
   - Console: new "Cost Projection" panel on Optimize pages with download CSV button.

3) Latency-tier Presets
   - Presets: S0 (ultra-low latency), S1 (balanced), S2 (cost-efficient). Each preset maps to batching window targets, max batch size, and prefix_cache_TTL suggestions.
   - Implementation: presets are applied as heuristics on top of Performance Profiles and can be overridden by route-level policy.

4) SDK & CLI changes
   - SDK v0.18.0: function rename estimate() -> estimate_cost(); new async wrapper; returns structured CostEstimate object. See SDK guide for migration snippet.
   - CLI: new export-profile command produces a YAML suitable for Dedicated scheduler. Example: redwood optimize export-profile redwood-13b-v2 --window 7d --out profile.yaml

Migration notes and breaking changes
----------------------------------
- Deprecated field removed: optimize.legacy_hint (previously used for heuristic-only recommendations). Action: remove any usages in saved route configs. Failure to remove will return 400 in API calls that include the field.
- SDK rename: update code references estimate() -> estimate_cost(). Simple search-and-replace sufficient for most codebases.
- Profile format changes: profile v1 -> v2 adds buckets for "prefix_cache_hit_rate". Dedicated scheduler accepts both v1 and v2, but v1 profiles will be automatically converted on import with a best-effort fill (read-only). We recommend re-exporting profiles after conversion.

Configuration snippets and examples
----------------------------------
- Console: Toggle Performance Profiles via Admin -> Optimize feature flags -> optimize.performance_profiles (default: off for existing tenants; on for new tenants).

- Example API request (cost estimate):
  POST /v1/optimize/estimate_cost
  Content-Type: application/json

  {
    "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
    "deployment_mode": "dedicated",
    "window_days": 30,
    "sequence_histogram": {"short": 0.7, "medium": 0.25, "long": 0.05},
    "commitment_tier": "std-monthly-1"
  }

  Response (truncated):
  {
    "monthly_cost_usd": 11500.32,
    "cost_per_1k_output_tokens": 2.87,
    "sensitivity": {"+10%_tokens_per_request": 12650.35}
  }

- SDK migration example (Python):
  # before
  cost = optimize_client.estimate(model="redwood-7b-v1", window_days=30)
  # after
  cost = await optimize_client.estimate_cost(model="redwood-7b-v1", window_days=30)

Rollout plan
------------
- Canary: 2026-02-18 -> enable Performance Profiles for 10 pilot tenants (selection criteria: medium-sized Dedicated customers with diverse request shapes). Monitor p95 latency impact and console correctness.
- Gradual rollout: 2026-02-20 -> enable for new tenants and opt-in for existing tenants via Console.
- Full enforcement: 2026-03-10 -> deprecate legacy_hint on route configs (400 returned if present).

SLOs and observability
----------------------
- Optimize service SLO unaffected: 99.9% availability for API endpoints.
- Cost estimator-specific: 99% of estimates generated within 2s for inputs with cached Performance Profiles; 95% within 5s for uncached inputs.
- Telemetry metrics exposed: optimize.profile_generation.count, optimize.estimate_latency_ms.p95, optimize.estimate_cache_hit_rate. Dashboards: /dashboards/optimize/1-3-release-estimates

How to opt-in / try it today
---------------------------
1) Console: Admin -> Feature flags -> toggle optimize.performance_profiles -> follow "Enable" flow to accept data-sharing for profile generation.
2) API: POST /v1/optimize/profiles?action=generate with model + window_days.
3) CLI: redwood optimize export-profile --generate redwood-7b-v1 --window 7d --out my-profile.yaml

Owner and support
-----------------
- Product owner: Deepa Nair (Optimize)
- Engineering lead: Samir Gupta (Optimize infra)
- Support: support@redwood.ai (use tag: optimize-1.3)
- Runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/optimize-profile-generation-runbook

Known issues and limitations
---------------------------
- Cold telemetry causes conservative cost projections (noted in UI). We plan a future release (1.4) to add synthetic workload injection to reduce conservatism.
- Some legacy Dedicated accounts with strict region restrictions may see profile import failures due to S3 path policies; workaround: use CLI export/import via local file.

Full changelog (selected)
------------------------
- 1.3.0 (2026-02-20): GA release. Added Performance Profiles, Cost Estimator, Console presets, SDK 0.18.0, CLI export-profile.
- 1.3.0-rc1 (2026-02-10): Canary with 10 tenants; fixed profile-merge race leading to duplicate buckets.

Feedback and next steps
-----------------------
- We're actively collecting feedback via the Optimize workspace channel and customer QBRs. Priorities for 1.4: synthetic workload generation, improved estimator calculus for multi-model ensembles, and automated rollback suggestions when recommendations cause SLA regressions.

Appendix: reproducible profile YAML example
-----------------------------------------
name: redwood-13b-v2-chat-short
version: 2
model: redwood-13b-v2
workload: chat-short
buckets:
  - name: short
    pct: 70
    p95_latency_ms: 42
    tokens_per_request: 28
  - name: medium
    pct: 25
    p95_latency_ms: 120
    tokens_per_request: 160
  - name: long
    pct: 5
    p95_latency_ms: 420
    tokens_per_request: 1024
prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.34
recommendations:
  batching: {max_batch_size: 128, target_window_ms: 8}
  quantization: {profile: qc-2-8bit, expected_cpu_savings_pct: 18}

If you need help migrating or want the Optimize team to run a custom projection for your account, contact Deepa or open a ticket with support (tag: optimize-1.3).

title: Deployment Conformance Crosswalk and Checklist
content:
Deployment Conformance Crosswalk and Checklist

Overview

This document provides a cross-functional conformance crosswalk and operational checklist for Redwood Private Deployments that maps common regulatory and customer data-classification requirements to specific deployment controls, packaging expectations, VPC design constraints, day-2 operational practices, and upgrade/rollback guardrails. Use this page during pre-sales technical validation, onboarding acceptance tests, and quarterly compliance reviews.

Scope

- Applies to: VPC-based private deployments, air-gapped on-prem packages, and hybrid control-plane deployments delivered to customers.
- Not covered: hosted API tenant operations, internal SRE-only playbooks (see eng-sre runbooks).

Audience

- Solutions Engineers, Field Engineering, Private Deployments PMs, Security & Compliance, Customer Ops.

How to use this doc

1. Select the customer's regulatory/data profile from the left column of the Conformance Matrix.
2. Apply the mapped controls and validate with the acceptance checklist at the end of this doc.
3. Capture evidence artifacts (audit logs, signed image digests, KMS policy snippets) and link into the customer folder.

Conformance Matrix (high level)

| Requirement / Profile | Network & VPC Controls | Data-at-rest | KMS & Key Management | Runtime Packaging | Day-2 Ops & Telemetry | Upgrade/Rollback Constraint | Acceptance Artifact Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low-sensitivity (internal dev) | Isolated VPC, optional public egress | AES-256 on disk | Redwood-managed key optional | Standard container image | Default telemetry on | Rolling upgrade allowed | Image digest, smoke test logs |
| Regulated PII (EU) | Private subnets, no public egress, egress via customer proxy | Encryption with customer-managed keys | Customer KMS recommended (Cloud KMS/HSM) | Signed images, attestation required | Telemetry sampling limit; PII redaction | Canary first; manual approval for global rollout | KMS policy, attestation report, telemetry config |
| HIPAA / PHI | VPC with strict ACLs, no third-party egress, dedicated subnet for inference | Customer KMS + HSM-backed keys | HSM-backed keys, rotation cadence defined | Air-gapped packaging option | Minimal telemetry; S3-level access logs only | Blue/green with automatic data-plane rollback | Signed SBOM, attestation, access logs |
| Classified / Highly Restricted | On-prem with FIPS-validated components, isolated build & deploy pipeline | FIPS-validated encryption, no external key exchange | HSM + internal KMS with strict split access | Ephemeral boot images, measured boot, attestation | No telemetry off-box; local observability only | Manual, documented upgrade window; rollback appendix required | Firmware attestation, measured boot report |

Notes:
- The rows map common profiles to minimal controls; customer-specific contracts may impose stronger controls.
- For hybrid control-plane deployments, apply control-plane telemetry except where restricted by contract.

Detailed Controls (selected fields)

1) Network & VPC controls

- VPC design must include: dedicated management subnet, tenant inference subnet, and optional shared services subnet.
- Mandatory NSG / ACLs: allow only ports 443 (control plane TLS), 2202 (optional SSH bastion restricted by allowlist), 50051 (gRPC internal), and custom health ports described in service manifest.
- Egress: either blocked or routed through customer-managed proxy/inspection appliance. No direct internet egress for regulated workloads.
- BGP / Cross-region failover: maintain pairwise BGP sessions with route targets documented in network runbook.

Example VPC policy (excerpt):

```
# Minimal security group rules (YAML snippet)
control_plane_sg:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 443
    src: customer_mgmt_cidr
bastion_sg:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 2202
    src: operator_allowlist
inference_sg:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 50051
    src: control_plane_sg
```

2) Data-at-rest and Key Management

- Storage must be encrypted with AES-256 at minimum. For regulated profiles use customer-managed keys (CMKs) in cloud KMS or HSM.
- Key rotation cadence: default 90 days; for PHI/HIPAA recommend 30–60 days depending on contract.
- KMS access control: require separation of duties — CI/CD service accounts must not have unilateral key create/delete permissions.

KMS policy checklist:

- CMK present and validated
- Key rotation policy documented
- Key usage logging enabled and exported to customer audit store

3) Packaging & Image Signing

- All images shipped for private deployments must be signed with our supply-chain signing keys and produce an SBOM. For air-gapped environments produce an offline signed bundle and provide verification steps.
- Image digest must be provided to customer in onboarding artifact.
- Reproducible builds: include exact build recipe and OS package list.

Packaging checklist:

- [ ] Image signed by Redwood CI signature
- [ ] SBOM included (CycloneDX or SPDX)
- [ ] Offline bundle includes signed tarball + verification script

4) Telemetry and Observability

- Default telemetry includes: health pings, model inference latency histograms, error rates, and token counts. For restricted deployments, provide a minimal local-only observability bundle.
- Telemetry must support filtering/sampling at customer request and remove PII at source.

Telemetry options matrix:

- Full (hosted): metrics + traces + logs to Redwood observability (default)
- Filtered (private): metrics to customer endpoint only; traces retained locally
- Local-only (restricted): file-based logs and on-host metrics; periodic collection by ops under customer agreement

5) Day-2 Operations (operational runbook highlights)

- Routine checks (daily): pod health, KV cache hit-rate, GPU utilization, node disk pressure.
- Weekly: snapshot KV caches, verify KMS access logs, run full smoke test via customer API gateway.
- Incident escalation path: SRE on-call -> Private Deployments on-call -> Customer NOC; include runbook link and escalation matrix.

Key day-2 playbook entries:

1. Capacity pressure (GPU contention):
   a. Evaluate batch targets and throttle non-critical routes
   b. Temporarily scale dedicated pool if autoscale enabled
   c. If scale fails, enact model-fallback policy (route to quantized variant)
2. KV cache corruption detected:
   a. Drain traffic from affected replicas
   b. Restore latest consistent snapshot from object store
   c. Reprime caches with warmup traffic using safe prompts
3. Telemetry spike with error rates >5% sustained for 10 minutes:
   a. Switch to degraded model variant
   b. Open incident and run guided debug checklist

Upgrade & Rollback Guidance

Principles:
- Minimize data-plane exposure during upgrades. Prefer canary or blue/green when stateful components are involved.
- Automate preflight checks; require manual approval for production if new packaging changes (e.g., kernel, firmware, FIPS components) are included.

Recommended workflow:

1. Preflight (automated):
   - Validate image signature and SBOM
   - Run integration smoke tests in staging that mirror customer routing (rate-limited)
   - Run KV cache migration dry-run (no write)
2. Canary deployment (1–5% traffic):
   - Monitor latency and error SLO (latency P99 <= baseline + 15% and error rate < 1%) for minimum 30 minutes
3. Gradual rollout (25%, 50%, 100%) with automated health gates

Rollback triggers (examples):
- P99 latency degradation > 50% for 10m AND CPU/GPU saturating beyond expected profile
- Error rate > 5% sustained for 10m on canary group
- Data plane inconsistency (KV mismatch, stateful restore failures)

Rollback procedure (stateful focus):

1. Pause traffic to rolling set
2. Re-deploy previous signed image(s) and rehydrate caches from last successful snapshot
3. Run acceptance smoke tests tied to customer API (see Acceptance Checklist)
4. If rollback fails, escalate to engineering incident + customer war room and enact warm standby (route to hosted/dedicated fallback)

Acceptance Checklist (pre-delivery & post-upgrade)

- Identity & Access
  - [ ] Admin user provisioning completed and tested
  - [ ] Operator allowlist configured for SSH/bastion
- Network & Egress
  - [ ] Private subnets created and verified
  - [ ] Egress path validated (proxy inspection / no direct internet)
- Cryptography & Keys
  - [ ] CMK present (or HSM) and policy attached
  - [ ] Key rotation schedule agreed and documented
- Packaging & Supply Chain
  - [ ] Image digest provided & signature validated by customer
  - [ ] SBOM and build recipe delivered
- Observability
  - [ ] Telemetry mode and sampling configured per contract
  - [ ] Audit logging exported and verified
- Functional Acceptance
  - [ ] Latency P95/P99 and error SLOs validated under capped load (see Test Plan below)
  - [ ] KV cache priming validated and persistence verified

Test Plan (minimal smoke load)

- Run 10-minute capped load at 10 RPS with mixed prompt sizes (short/medium/long). Validate:
  - P95 latency within contract SLA (document SLA value in delivery notes)
  - Error rate < 0.5%
  - Token accounting matches expected limits

Evidence artifacts to collect and hand to customer

- Signed image digest and SBOM (file, path)
- KMS policy snippet and rotation proof (screenshot or policy JSON)
- Attestation report for offline bundle (if applicable)
- Telemetry config manifest showing sampling/filters
- Smoke test logs and SLO graphs

Owner and escalation

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (Priya Shah)
- Delivery owner: Field Engineering lead (assigned per customer)
- On-call: Private Deployments SRE rotation (see eng-sre oncall roster)

Appendices

A. Minimal SLO examples (for acceptance tests)

- Availability: 99.9% (monthly) for dedicated pools; aim for 99.5% for small private installs
- Latency: baseline P95 as observed in staging + 20% allowed during first 24h after rollout
- Error budget: 0.5% monthly for non-critical routes

B. Example rollout command snippets

```
# canary deploy (example)
redwoodctl deploy --image=redwood/private-runtime@sha256:<digest> --canary-percent=5 --health-check=/healthz
```

C. Common customer questions (FAQ)

Q: Can we disable all telemetry?
A: Yes, for the most restricted profiles we provide a local-only observability bundle and a documented process for on-site collection under customer control.

Q: Do you provide HSM integrations?
A: Yes; we support Cloud HSM offerings and on-prem HSMs for classified workloads. Integration verification and acceptance tests are part of onboarding.

D. Change log

- 2026-01-10: Created by Priya Shah (initial crosswalk)
- 2026-02-05: Added FIPS and measured boot notes per security review (Lena Fischer)
- 2026-03-02: Expanded acceptance checklist and telemetry matrix (Miguel Ortega)

If you have questions or need this crosswalk adapted to a specific regulation or customer contract, contact eng-private-deployments@redwood.com or open a request in the Private Deployments backlog.

title: Operator feedback playback and cost-debt reconciliation
content:
Operator feedback playback and cost-debt reconciliation

Summary

This page defines the operator feedback-playback process and the linked cost-debt reconciliation workflow for platform services. The goal is to create a reproducible cadence that converts operator observations and incident playback notes into prioritized, tracked work to reduce recurring cost and reliability debt. This doc covers signals, dashboard ownership, alert thresholds, an operator runbook for playback, the cost-debt triage process, metrics used for prioritization, and a 6-month roadmap for adoption.

Goals
- Close the loop between operations (oncall/platform-ops) and engineering teams so runbook learnings produce measurable debt reduction.
- Track and reduce recurring token/cost debt and wasteful patterns by 30% for target services within 6 months.
- Standardize playback artifacts so retrospective insights are actionable and schedulable.

Scope
- Applies to platform-managed LLM inference services, caching layers (KV prefix cache), batching subsystems, and tenant-routing controllers.
- Not in scope: customer-managed private deployments (those follow customer-specific SOWs) and billing/legal reconciliation.

Background and Rationale
Operators frequently observe recurring cost spikes, repeated fallbacks, and cache-miss storms that indicate systemic design debt rather than isolated incidents. Historically, playback notes lived in ad-hoc folders or Slack threads, delaying remediation. This process aims to formalize "operator playback" (a short, structured debrief) and create a connected cost-debt ticket lifecycle from observation -> triage -> fix -> validation.

Key Definitions
- Operator Playback: a 30–60 minute structured debrief performed by the operator team after a noteworthy event or synthesis of recurring alerts.
- Cost debt: any measurable recurring or avoidable expense driven by platform behavior (e.g., excessive cold starts, token leaks, inefficient model routing, misconfigured batching).
- Reconciliation ticket: an engineering task with a defined acceptance test and metric target aimed at eliminating the root cause of cost debt.

Ownership and Roles
- Platform Oncall (primary): capture playback, raise triage tickets, and assign preliminary impact estimates.
- Service Owner (secondary/assignee): engineers responsible for the affected service; own implementation and verification.
- Cost Steward (finance-eng): validates cost-savings estimates and provides historical cost data for prioritization.
- Platform Program Manager: runs the quarterly review and ensures SLAs for reconciliation.

Signals and Dashboards
The operator playback must reference a standard dashboard snapshot. Below are required widgets and who owns them.

Required dashboard widgets (table)
| Widget | Description | Owner | Notes |
| Runtime token cost by tenant | 7d and 30d rolling token spend, P50/P95 cost-per-request | cost-steering | Show top 20 tenants and trailing 7d spike annotations |
| KV cache hit/miss by prefix | Per-prefix hit-rate, eviction rate, and TTL distribution | caching-team | Correlate with request sequence-lengths |
| Model-routing fallbacks | Count of requests routed to fallback variants per region | routing-service | Include last 24h timeline and per-region heatmap |
| Cold-start latency vs warm | Warm-up success ratio and average cold start penalty (ms) | runtime-team | 1h & 24h views, grouped by instance flavor |
| Batching efficiency | Effective batching window utilization and average tokens per batch | batching-team | Include coalescing latency percentiles |
| Synthetic cost regressions | Synthetic job that runs the canonical prompt suite and reports delta cost/latency | eval-infra | Synthetic baseline and rolling regression line |

Alert thresholds and routing
- Token-cost anomaly alert: trig when top-3 tenants combined 24h spend increases > 40% vs baseline and absolute spend > $X/day for that tenant class. Route to oncall and Cost Steward.
- Cache-eviction storm: trig when global eviction rate > 0.5% of cache size per hour for 30 minutes. Route to caching-team and oncall.
- Fallback surge: >10x increase in fallback routing rate for region-tier and >1000 events in 10 minutes. Route to routing-service and platform oncall.
- Cold-start epidemic: 20% of warmup attempts failing across pool for >15 minutes. Route to runtime-team and SRE.

Operator playback runbook (30–60m)
1. Gather artifacts (5m): take the dashboard snapshot links (use the "Playback snapshot" button), collect relevant alert IDs, and attach the synthetic regression run.
2. Quick impact estimate (5m): estimate customer-facing impact (users affected, latency degradation, cost delta). Use the impact checklist below.
3. Root-cause hypothesis (10–15m): walk through recent deploys, config changes, model swaps, and any capacity events. Add a hypothesis with supporting evidence.
4. Temporary mitigations (5–10m): if a mitigation exists (traffic steering, throttles, emergency model swap), note it and owner.
5. Create a reconciliation ticket (10m): the ticket must include: summary, hypothesis, dashboard links, proposed acceptance criteria (metric and time-based), estimated cost impact, and preliminary priority tag. Assign to service owner.
6. Post-playback notification (1–2m): post a short summary in #platform-playback with ticket link and runbook snapshot.

Impact checklist (used during quick estimate)
- Visibility: whether customers will notice latency or cost changes.
- SLA exposure: any SLOs affected (percent error or latency).
- Revenue risk: potential churn or big-tenant exposure.
- Reproducibility: can we reproduce in canary or synthetic job?

Cost-debt triage lifecycle
1. Intake: Platform oncall files a reconciliation ticket tagged "cost-debt". Must include estimated $/day waste and concrete metric to be fixed.
2. Triage (weekly): Platform Program Manager and Cost Steward run through new tickets in a 1-hour triage meeting. Tickets are scored on impact, effort, and confidence.
3. Prioritization matrix: use the following scoring (each 1–5): impact (cost reduction), effort (engineering hours), confidence (likelihood of root cause). Compute a priority score = (impact * confidence) / effort.
4. Scheduling: high-priority tickets are slotted into the next sprint or into a 2-week cost-debt blitz; medium go to backlog with monthly review.
5. Implementation and verification: Service Owner implements fix and provides a validation job (synthetic + 7d retrospective).
6. Close and retro: after validation, ticket moves to "verified savings" and is discussed in the monthly cost-debt bulletin.

Acceptance criteria examples (must be included in every reconciliation ticket)
- Reduce average token cost per request by >= 18% for the target workload over 14 days.
- Improve KV prefix hit-rate from 78% to >= 92% for at least 7 consecutive days.
- Eliminate fallback events for the top-2 tenants for 30 days.

Metrics and SLOs used for prioritization
- Cost-per-inference (P50/P95) – baseline & target
- Cache hit-rate by prefix – baseline & improvement target
- Fallback rate per 10k requests – baseline & target
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) – operator efficiency metric to track process health

Example reconciliation ticket template (short)
- Title: "Reduce token cost for PDF embedding flow (tenant: acme-inc)"
- Summary: one-paragraph with link to playback snapshot
- Hypothesis: misconfigured batching window + oversized model variant -> high tokens per call
- Acceptance: P50 token cost down 25% over 14d synthetic run
- Estimated effort: 3 engineering days
- Owner: embeddings-service team

Implementation checklist for Service Owners
- [ ] Clone playback snapshot dashboard and add the fix validation widgets
- [ ] Add synthetic job and ensure it is running daily with a regression alert
- [ ] Implement change behind a feature flag or canary rollout where possible
- [ ] Run 14-day validation window, attach results to ticket
- [ ] Close ticket or escalate if criteria not met

Retrospective cadence and artifacts
- Short playback (for single incidents) -> immediate triage ticket + weekly triage meeting.
- Monthly cost-debt bulletin -> summary of closed tickets, estimated savings, and outstanding blockers. Published by Platform Program Manager.
- Quarterly 2-hour retrospective -> cross-team deep-dive into recurring patterns and roadmap adjustments. Outcomes are added to the 6-month roadmap.

Roadmap (next 6 months)
- Month 0–1: adopt standard playback snapshot button and ensure all oncall have write access to triage board.
- Month 1–2: roll out synthetic-regression standard job across 8 critical services.
- Month 2–4: pilot cost-debt blitz with 3 targeted services; aim for ~20% aggregate cost reduction in pilot group.
- Month 4–6: integrate cost-steward approvals into triage flow and automate close-on-validated-savings.

Retrospective insights (initial pilot notes)
- Common root causes found so far: batching window misconfiguration, oversized model selection by fallback policy, and stale cache TTLs after model swaps.
- Operator friction: missing snapshot links and inconsistent evidence lengthened triage. Fix: standardized snapshot export and a 6-field minimal evidence requirement.
- Cultural insight: giving small, measurable wins (e.g., one tenant 12% savings) drives adoption faster than large multi-team projects.

Open risks and mitigations
- Risk: engineering prioritization fatigue. Mitigation: timebox blitzes and require service owners to commit a level of effort in advance.
- Risk: noisy synthetic regressions producing false positives. Mitigation: tune baselines and require confirmation by manual replay before scheduling fixes.

Appendix
- Playback snapshot CLI (example):
  # take a snapshot of current playback dashboard
  rdx dashboards snapshot --dashboard platform-cost-debt --output-url

- Example alert rule (YAML snippet):
  alerts:
    - name: token_cost_anomaly
      expr: |
        increase(token_cost_total[24h]) / max(1, avg_over_time(token_cost_total[28d])) > 0.4
      for: 10m
      labels:
        severity: major
      annotations:
        runbook: "/eng-platform/systems-and-services/operator-feedback-playback-and-cost-debt-reconciliation-2026"

Related pages
- See also: /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/runtime-cost-instrumentation-and-alerting-2026 (dashboard templates)
- See also: /eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026 (mitigation primitives)

Contact and next steps
- Primary contact: Aisha Patel (platform-ops lead)
- Program owner: Priya Nair (Platform Program Manager)
- Next step: platform-ops to run a pilot playback for three services during week of 2026-02-15 and report results in the monthly bulletin.

title: Forensic Readiness: Authorization Chain & Evidence Orchestration Playbook
content:
Forensic Readiness: Authorization Chain & Evidence Orchestration Playbook

Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood's standardized approach to forensic readiness for authorization-related incidents. It focuses on traceability of authorization decisions (the "authorization chain"), automated evidence orchestration, residency- and retention-aware packaging, and SDLC controls to reduce investigation time. The guidance is intended for Security Engineers, SREs, Platform, and Incident Responders.

Goals:
- Ensure authorization events are recorded with sufficient context to reconstruct decisions end-to-end within 48 hours.
- Provide a repeatable evidence-orchestration flow that satisfies audit requests (SOX/ISO/PCI/SOC2) and legal holds.
- Minimize need for manual data collection and preserve data residency constraints during evidence packaging.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood services that perform authorization decisions (API gateway, authz service, model-serving control plane, console, admin tools).
- Includes service-to-service tokens, user sessions, feature-flag gating, and delegated/temporal access flows.
- Excludes: developer local test environments unless they touch production credentials.

Key Definitions:
- Authorization Chain: the sequence of inputs that lead to a final authorization decision (identity, token, role attributes, policy engine evaluation, cached allowances, and failover decisions).
- Evidence Bundle: a time-boxed, tamper-evident archive containing logs, snapshots, and metadata used for audit or forensic analysis.

Principles:
1) Reconstructability: every authorization decision should be reconstructable by combining event streams (authn/authz), policy evaluations, and service traces.
2) Minimum-necessary collection: collect only required fields to prove decision provenance while reducing PII exposure.
3) Residency-aware packaging: evidence bundles must honor tenant and regulatory residency constraints.
4) Automation-first: evidence orchestration must be automated to avoid variability and support legal holds.

Ownership and Roles:
- Security - Playbook owner, legal/third-party escalation, evidence integrity validation.
- SRE - Collection agent deployment, retention configuration, emergency extraction support.
- Platform/AuthN/AuthZ teams - Ensure events include required fields and maintain policy engine versioning.
- Legal/Compliance - Evidence acceptance criteria for audits and subpoenas.

Minimum Event Schema (required fields):
- timestamp (ISO 8601)
- event_id (UUID v4)
- principal_id (user_id or service_id)
- principal_type (human | service | machine-account)
- authn_method (sso | oidc | mfa | token)
- token_id (nullable)
- request_path
- request_method
- resource_identifier
- policy_version
- policy_decision (allow | deny | conditional)
- decision_reasons (list of rule ids / short text)
- cache_hit (true | false)
- fallback_variant (if any)
- request_trace_id
- tenant_id
- geometa (region / shard id)

Example audit event (JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2027-01-04T14:22:33Z",
  "event_id": "c3d2f2b4-8b1a-4a3b-9e49-2c5ef3f7a123",
  "principal_id": "svc-model-router-3",
  "principal_type": "service",
  "authn_method": "service-token",
  "token_id": "tk-4f9a",
  "request_path": "/v1/model/infer",
  "request_method": "POST",
  "resource_identifier": "model:llama-70b:prod:2027-01-02",
  "policy_version": "policy-2027-01-01",
  "policy_decision": "deny",
  "decision_reasons": ["rule-023"],
  "cache_hit": false,
  "fallback_variant": "none",
  "request_trace_id": "trace-78a9",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-acme-corp",
  "geometa": "eu-west-1"
}

Detection and Alerting Thresholds:
- High-severity: 5+ unique denied authorization chains for the same principal-resource pair in 5 minutes -> PagerDuty SEV-1.
- Medium-severity: sudden increase in fallback_variant usage (>=20% of requests against baseline) -> Email + Slack alert to Platform.
- Low-severity: missing policy_version field in >0.1% of auth events over 24h -> Create SRE ticket.

Incident Response Runbook (Authorization Incidents):
1) Triage (0-15m):
   a) Confirm alert and collect initial telemetry: request_trace_ids, event_ids, sample request payloads.
   b) Stakeholders: Security Lead, Oncall SRE, AuthZ Owner, Legal if cross-tenant or PII is suspected.
2) Containment (15-60m):
   a) If authorized decision leakage suspected, rotate affected tokens/service keys and apply scoped throttles.
   b) Apply policy fallback to strict-deny for impacted resources if safe.
3) Forensic Collection (30-240m):
   a) Trigger automated evidence bundle for the incident window (see Evidence Packaging procedure).
   b) Snapshot in-memory policy engine state and any cached KV (KV export must be written with checksums).
   c) Preserve immutable copies of audit streams (see Retention & Residency rules).
4) Root Cause & Remediation (T+4h onward):
   a) Reconstruct authorization chain: join authn logs, policy evaluation logs, trace spans, and config commit history.
   b) Implement permanent fix (policy patch, fix bug, roll out new policy_version).
   c) Run regression evals against representative prompt sets where applicable (model-serving authorization flows).
5) Post-incident (2-14 days):
   a) Evidence review with Legal/Compliance; produce signed evidence manifest.
   b) Update policy and SDLC gates to prevent recurrence.
   c) Draft postmortem with remediation timeline and risk acceptance if applicable.

Evidence Packaging Procedure (Automated):
1) Triggering: evidence generation automatically triggers on SEV-1 or by Security/Legal request.
2) Window selection: default = incident_start - 30m to incident_end + 4h (configurable).
3) Data sources collected in each bundle:
   - AuthN stream (raw)
   - AuthZ policy evaluation log (with policy_version)
   - Distributed traces for request_trace_ids (Jaeger/Tempo snapshots)
   - Service-specific logs (application and platform) for involved hosts
   - KV/cache snapshots (policy engine cache, prefix KV)
   - Git commits for policy/config (signed commit SHAs)
   - Operator actions (console audit, impersonation events)
4) Packaging format:
   - Use signed, gzipped tarball: rbw-evidence-<incident-id>-<sha256>.tar.gz.sig
   - Include manifest.json (flat key:value pairs) and chain-of-custody.txt
5) Residency enforcement:
   - For tenant data with geo constraint, collect only metadata outside tenant data center. Full data stays in-place and Legal may request a hosted review session with data access controls.
6) Integrity proofing:
   - Each file includes SHA256 and evidence bundle includes a bundle-level signature from the Security keyring (KMS/HSM-backed).

Sample manifest table (CSV-style in manifest.json):
file_name,sha256,source_system,time_range,residency, pii_flag
authn-stream-20270104.log,3b2f...,authn-stream,2027-01-04T14:00:00Z/2027-01-04T16:30:00Z,eu-west-1,false
policy-eval-20270104.log,a9d1...,policy-engine,2027-01-04T14:00:00Z/2027-01-04T16:30:00Z,global,false
trace-snapshot-20270104.jaeger,7ac0...,tempo,2027-01-04T14:20:00Z/2027-01-04T14:25:00Z,eu-west-1,false

Retention & Residency Guidance:
- Default retention for authz events: 2 years for tenant-scoped audit events; 5 years for platform-level policy change history required for compliance.
- PII minimization: do not store full request payloads in long-term audit logs. Use redaction pipelines with hashed placeholders for sensitive fields.
- Legal Hold: evidence bundle TTL is extended and immutable copies are placed in an escrow bucket flagged for legal. Escrow buckets have separate access controls and multi-party approvers.

SDLC Integration (prevention and verification):
- Policy-as-code: all policy changes must be PR-reviewed in Git and include a policy-impact test (unit + behavioral tests).
- CI Gate: failing to include policy_version or unit tests prevents merge to main.
- Release-time traceability: CI artifacts must record signed artifacts and policy_version that maps to runtime metadata.
- Canary rollout: policy_version rollouts use canary windows with authorization telemetry sampling and rollback metrics.

Risk & Exception Handling:
- Risk classification matrix: Low (single-tenant, no PII, transient), Medium (multi-tenant exposure, PII), High (exfiltration, cross-border data exposure).
- Exception process: temporary exceptions to retention/residency require Risk Board approval and produce an automatic evidence trail (requestor, approver, window, justification).
- Expedited exception: for emergency remediation where data must leave a region for analysis, a 2-of-3 approval (Security, Legal, CTO) is required and must be appended to the evidence bundle.

Operational Playnotes and Checklists:
- Daily health job: validate policy_version tagging in auth events; alert if coverage <99.9%.
- Weekly supply: ensure signature keys used for evidence bundles are rotated per key-management policy.
- Game day: simulate an authorization incident quarterly with at least one cross-team extraction to validate end-to-end bundling and residency requirements.

Appendix A — Quick CLI snippets:
# Trigger evidence bundle from admin tooling (example)
redwood-cli evidence create --incident-id rwd-20270104-01 --start 2027-01-04T13:30:00Z --end 2027-01-04T17:00:00Z --scope authz --encrypt --residency eu-west-1

# Validate bundle signature
redwood-cli evidence verify --bundle /tmp/rbw-evidence-rwd-20270104-01.tar.gz.sig --keyring security-evidence-keyring

Appendix B — Related pages and links:
- /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025
- /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-provenance-and-retention-framework-2026

Revision history:
- 2026-11-02: Drafted by Anjali Rao.
- 2026-12-10: Added packaging integrity controls (Marcus Chen review).
- 2027-01-15: Finalized residency exception approval flow and published.

Contact:
Security oncall: security-oncall@redwood.example.com
Playbook owner: Anjali Rao (anjali@redwood.example.com)

title: Evidence Pack v1: Hosted Data Residency Enforcement (Region Pinning) — Security & Compliance Foundation
content:
Evidence Pack v1: Hosted Data Residency Enforcement (Region Pinning) — Security & Compliance Foundation

## 1. Purpose
This evidence pack provides auditor-ready artifacts for Redwood Inference’s **Hosted data residency enforcement** capability (“region pinning”). It is designed for:
- SOC 2 Type II evidence requests (Security, Availability, Confidentiality)
- ISO 27001 / ISO 27701 evidence requests where applicable
- Enterprise customer security questionnaires (data location, geo-fencing, auditability)

This pack focuses on **Hosted API** enforcement and notes alignment for **Dedicated** where behavior differs.

## 2. Control objective (plain language)
Redwood Inference ensures that when a customer configures an allowed set of regions for Hosted API (and a primary region), Redwood:
1) Evaluates residency policy deterministically at request time.
2) Routes and processes customer content only within the configured allowed region set.
3) Blocks requests that would violate policy using a consistent public error contract.
4) Records auditable events for residency policy configuration changes.
5) Provides monitoring and operational controls to detect and respond to enforcement issues (e.g., false positives).

## 3. Scope, system boundaries, and definitions
### 3.1 In-scope systems (Hosted)
- API Gateway (request validation, standardized error responses)
- Smart Routing layer (region selection + fallback constraints)
- Residency Policy Service (control plane configuration: org/project/key-level)
- Logging/telemetry related to residency decisions (decision context, enforcement reason codes)
- Audit Logging pipeline (create/update/delete policy events; admin overrides)
- Console / Admin UX (policy configuration and history view)

### 3.2 Out-of-scope / explicit exclusions (v1)
- Automatic multi-region replication of customer content
- Customer-defined geo-fencing rules for every internal subsystem (handled via phased hardening)
- Customer-managed encryption key residency requirements (KMS/HSM integrations covered under separate controls)

### 3.3 Definitions
- **Customer content:** request payloads (prompts/messages), uploaded files for inference where supported, and model outputs.
- **Residency policy:** configuration describing allowed region(s) and a primary region at org/project and optionally API key scope.
- **Allowed regions:** list/set of regions where customer content may be processed.
- **Cross-region fallback:** routing from primary region to another region due to capacity/health events.

## 4. Control mapping (SOC 2 / ISO crosswalk)
This section maps evidence to common auditor language. Exact SOC 2 criteria mappings may vary by audit firm.

### 4.1 Control statement DR-01 — Residency policy configuration is authorized and auditable
**Control intent:** Only authorized administrators can configure residency policies; all changes are logged.

**Key mechanisms**
- Residency Policy Service requires authenticated admin context for create/update/delete.
- Audit log events emitted for policy lifecycle changes (create/update/delete) and for admin overrides.
- Console provides configuration history for self-service review.

**Primary evidence**
- Audit log event samples (see Section 6.2)
- Console screenshots showing configuration history (see Section 6.3)
- Change management artifacts for enabling residency enforcement (see Section 7)

**Owners**
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin
- GRC: Olga Petrov
- Platform: Ethan Park


### 4.2 Control statement DR-02 — Residency is enforced at request time with deterministic checks
**Control intent:** Requests are processed only in allowed regions; violations are blocked.

**Key mechanisms**
- API gateway validates residency policy context and returns standardized policy violation errors.
- Routing layer selects region from allowed set; cross-region fallback disabled by default unless explicitly allowed.
- Residency decision context is propagated downstream for observability and auditability.

**Primary evidence**
- ADRs documenting boundaries and error contract (see Section 5)
- End-to-end test results and CI gating artifacts (see Section 8)
- Blocked request metrics and dashboards (see Section 6.1)

**Owners**
- Routing: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Gateway: Amara Diallo
- SRE: Sean Gallagher


### 4.3 Control statement DR-03 — Security monitoring detects enforcement failures and abnormal block rates
**Control intent:** Redwood monitors enforcement health and investigates anomalies.

**Key mechanisms**
- Dashboards for blocked requests, evaluation latency, and cross-region routing attempts.
- Alerts for abnormal block-rate changes and policy evaluation failures.
- On-call runbook for false positives and rollback/feature-flag mitigation.

**Primary evidence**
- Monitoring spec + dashboard screenshots (see Section 6.1)
- Alert definitions and paging thresholds (see Section 6.1)
- Runbook and sample incident timeline (see Section 9)

**Owners**
- SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Observability: Allison Grant


### 4.4 Control statement DR-04 — Customer-facing error responses are consistent and actionable
**Control intent:** Customers receive clear, machine-readable errors that facilitate remediation.

**Key mechanisms**
- Standardized HTTP status, error_code, request_id, and help_url.
- Same contract for streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
- SDK surfaces dedicated exception type for residency violations.

**Primary evidence**
- ADR-022 (error contract) and sample responses (Section 5)
- Gateway behavior validation tests (Section 8)
- Support tickets / fixes confirming streaming path correctness (Section 9.3)

**Owners**
- Product: Naomi Feldman
- Gateway: Brian Murphy / Amara Diallo


## 5. Design and policy documentation references (auditor context)
Provide these documents for narrative evidence and boundary clarity.

1) **Hosted Data Residency Policy and Controls (internal policy)**
- Location: `security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/hosted-data-residency-policy-and-controls`
- What it answers: what is guaranteed, what is excluded, how it maps to SOC2/ISO narratives.

2) **ADR-021: Region Pinning Enforcement Boundaries**
- Location: `architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-region-pinning-enforcement-boundaries`
- What it answers: definition of customer content; what subsystems are in-scope; explicit allowed cross-region metadata (non-content).

3) **ADR-022: Error Contract for Residency Violations**
- Location: `architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-error-contract-for-residency-violations`
- What it answers: HTTP status, error codes, message template requirements, request-id linkage, and SDK expectations.

4) **Residency Policy Service (system documentation)**
- Location: `eng-platform/systems-and-services/residency-policy-service`
- What it answers: schema, endpoints, auth model, validation, and integration points.


## 6. Operational evidence (monitoring, logs, audit events)
### 6.1 Monitoring dashboards and alerts
**Dashboard set name:** “Data Residency Enforcement”

**Required screenshots / exports (attach for audit package)**
- Dashboard overview (last 30 days):
  - `residency.blocked_requests.count` (by region, by org tier)
  - `residency.policy_eval.latency_ms.p95` (by region)
  - `routing.cross_region_attempts.count` (should be 0 unless explicitly allowed)
  - `gateway.residency_violations.count` (streaming vs non-streaming)
- Alert definitions page:
  - “Residency enforcement evaluation failures > 0 for 5m” (page)
  - “Blocked request rate delta > 3x baseline for 15m (per region)” (page)
  - “Cross-region attempt detected for pinned org” (page)

**Evidence notes for auditors**
- We provide dashboard screenshots for the audit period and can export raw metric time series upon request.
- For customer-sensitive data, we sanitize org identifiers in screenshots unless auditor has NDA and scoping includes customer names.


### 6.2 Audit log events (configuration changes)
**Event categories (expected)**
- `residency_policy.created`
- `residency_policy.updated`
- `residency_policy.deleted`
- `residency_policy.override_enabled` (admin-only, break-glass)
- `residency_policy.override_disabled`

**Fields auditors typically request**
- actor (user/service principal), actor_type
- org_id / project_id
- policy_id
- before/after summary (allowed_regions, primary_region)
- timestamp
- request_id / correlation_id

**Sample redacted event (format illustration)**
- event_type: `residency_policy.updated`
- timestamp: 2025-04-08T17:22:11Z
- actor_type: `user`
- actor: `admin@redwoodinference.com` (redacted in external exports)
- org_id: `org_8f3...`
- project_id: `proj_19c...`
- policy_id: `rp_2d1...`
- change_summary: `allowed_regions: [eu-central-1] -> [eu-central-1, eu-west-1]; primary_region: eu-central-1`
- correlation_id: `req_01HR...`

**How to produce evidence**
- Export from Audit Log Exporter: “Compliance Exports → Data Residency (Policy Changes)”
- Retention: per enterprise audit-log retention policy; minimum 1 year for enterprise tenants (see Security Logging & Monitoring policy).


### 6.3 Console/admin UX screenshots
Provide screenshots showing:
- Residency settings page (org-level and project-level)
- Allowed regions selector + primary region selector
- Confirmation modal and warning copy for restrictive policies
- Configuration history / “recent changes” view (timestamps and actor)
- “Blocked requests” troubleshooting view (shows error_code, request_id, block reason)

Redaction guidance:
- Mask customer org name if not in audit scope.
- Leave region names, error_code, and timestamps visible.


## 7. Change management artifacts (release governance)
Auditors frequently request proof that changes were reviewed, tested, and approved.

### 7.1 Architecture and security reviews
Provide:
- Threat model review summary (security sign-off). Include:
  - threats considered: cross-region content leakage via fallback, logging/tracing leakage, background tasks
  - mitigations and owners
  - acceptance notes for v1 exclusions
- Link to Security Engineering review thread (internal reference) and final approval date.

### 7.2 Implementation tracking and approvals
Provide:
- Launch checklist and rollout gates (staging → dogfood → allowlist customers → progressive rollout)
- List of feature flags used and who can toggle them
- Approvals:
  - Product sign-off (Naomi Feldman)
  - Security sign-off (Marcus Lin / CISO delegate)
  - SRE readiness sign-off (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes)

### 7.3 Code review evidence
Provide references to:
- Control plane schema + validation PR (reviewers and merge date)
- Routing enforcement PR (reviewers and merge date)
- Gateway error contract PR (reviewers and merge date)
- Audit event emission PR (reviewers and merge date)
- Observability pack PR (dashboard creation)

Evidence format:
- PR links with merge commit hashes and “Approved by” screenshots, if required by auditor.


## 8. Test evidence (design validation and operating effectiveness)
### 8.1 Test plan overview
**Test categories**
- Unit tests: residency policy evaluation logic, schema validation, precedence rules
- Integration tests: gateway-to-routing propagation of residency context
- E2E tests (CI gated): pinned EU org hitting US endpoint; streaming behavior; fallback scenarios
- Negative tests: invalid region IDs, empty allowed set, mismatched primary region

### 8.2 Required test artifacts
Attach/export for audit:
- Test suite execution report for audit period sample (e.g., one run per release)
- CI job logs showing pass/fail and commit SHA
- E2E test cases list with expected results

### 8.3 Example E2E test cases (for auditor readability)
1) **Pinned EU-only, request arrives at US edge**
- Given: allowed_regions = [EU], primary = EU
- When: request enters via US edge POP
- Then: request is routed to EU region; no cross-region fallback; logs show residency_selected_region in EU

2) **Pinned EU-only, EU capacity constrained**
- Given: allowed_regions = [EU], primary = EU
- When: EU region is degraded
- Then: request is blocked (no fallback outside allowed set)
- And: response matches standardized error contract

3) **Streaming endpoint residency violation**
- Given: allowed_regions excludes selected region
- When: streaming chat completion requested
- Then: initial stream frame returns standardized error structure and terminates stream cleanly


## 9. Operational readiness evidence (runbooks, incidents, support learnings)
### 9.1 Runbook: residency enforcement false positives
Provide:
- Runbook link and screenshots of key sections:
  - triage steps: confirm policy config, check routing attempt metrics, validate evaluation latency
  - mitigations: temporary allowlist expansion, feature-flag override (break-glass), rollback
  - customer comms template guidance

### 9.2 Incident evidence (if applicable in audit period)
If a relevant incident occurred during the audit window, provide:
- incident ticket ID
- timeline summary
- customer impact summary
- corrective actions and verification steps

### 9.3 Support case evidence (quality and consistency of enforcement)
Provide at least one redacted support ticket showing:
- the problem (e.g., confusing error or unexpected fallback attempt)
- investigation notes referencing residency decision context
- resolution (bug fix or config guidance)


## 10. Evidence index (what to attach / provide on request)
Use this as a checklist when assembling the final audit packet.

### 10.1 Governance / policy
- Hosted Data Residency Policy and Controls (internal policy doc)
- ADR-021 (enforcement boundaries)
- ADR-022 (error contract)

### 10.2 Technical controls (system and code)
- Residency Policy Service system doc
- PR references (schema/validation, routing enforcement, gateway errors, audit events)
- Configuration validation rules documentation (allowed_regions, primary_region constraints)

### 10.3 Monitoring and detection
- Dashboard screenshots (30-day view, by region)
- Alert definitions and recent alert history (redacted if needed)
- Sample queries used to detect cross-region routing attempts

### 10.4 Auditability
- Audit log export samples for policy create/update/delete
- Evidence of retention configuration for audit logs

### 10.5 Testing
- CI job logs for E2E suite (commit SHA + timestamp)
- Test case list and results summary
- Evidence that streaming endpoints return standardized residency errors

### 10.6 Operational readiness
- Runbook(s)
- On-call training note or readiness sign-off (if maintained)
- Incident postmortem(s), if any within audit scope


## 11. Redaction and data handling for audit submissions
- Default: redact customer names, org IDs, and API keys.
- Leave: region names, error_code, policy logic descriptions, timestamps, and aggregated metrics.
- For auditors under NDA requesting raw logs: provide time-bounded exports with minimized fields and approval from Security (Marcus Lin) and GRC (Olga Petrov).


## 12. Point of contact and evidence production workflow
**Primary GRC contact:** Olga Petrov (evidence coordination, auditor Q&A)
**Security Engineering:** Marcus Lin (technical control narrative, threat model)
**SRE:** Sean Gallagher (monitoring/alerts, operational effectiveness)
**Product:** Naomi Feldman (customer-facing scope, error messaging commitments)

**Standard turnaround targets**
- Initial evidence packet: 3–5 business days
- Follow-up samples/exports: 5–10 business days (depending on redaction and approvals)


## 13. Appendix: Standardized residency violation error (public contract excerpt)
(Include as a readability aid; authoritative source is ADR-022.)

- HTTP status: 409 (Policy conflict) for residency violations
- error_code: `RESIDENCY_POLICY_VIOLATION`
- Required fields: `message`, `request_id`, `help_url`
- Optional fields (subject to final policy): `policy_scope` (org/project/key), `allowed_regions`, `selected_region`

Example (redacted):
- status: 409
- error_code: RESIDENCY_POLICY_VIOLATION
- message: "Request blocked by data residency policy. Configure an allowed region that includes the target region, or send requests to your pinned primary region."
- request_id: req_01HRXXXX
- help_url: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/security/data-residency#region-pinning-troubleshooting


---
Document history
- 2025-03-10: v1 outline created (Olga Petrov)
- 2025-04-22: updated audit log event list, monitoring checklist, and redaction guidance (Olga Petrov)
