title: POC scoping: sensitive flow retention & redaction - BlueHarbor Analytics
content:
POC scoping: sensitive flow retention & redaction - BlueHarbor Analytics

Discovery + POC scoping for handling PII in prompts and logs. Discussed redaction, retention windows, scope of data stored for telemetry, benchmarking plan (replay vs synthetic), success criteria (latency SLOs, quality parity, auditability), and a two-week pilot timeline. Agreed to run a 7-day benchmark and provide security docs and a draft quote.
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO), Priya (MLOps), Samir (Security)

Summary: quick scoping call focused on how BlueHarbor routes sensitive prompts through Redwood for a 2-week pilot. Main concerns: PII leakage in logs, configurable retention, redaction automation, and benchmark sizing.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros and then jump in. We're budgeting 45–60 minutes.
[00:12] Carlos: Hi, Carlos here. CTO. We're looking to test Redwood for our customer support summarization workflow which touches PHI/PII.
[00:20] Priya: Priya — lead on MLOps. We run approx 100k support interactions per month, average prompt length around 120 tokens, peaks are spikier. We're mostly worried about what gets stored and how to prove deletion.
[00:35] Ethan: thanks, yeah so from the platform side we support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For POC we usually start on Hosted with strict retention + redaction rules, or a Private control-plane if you need full network isolation.
[00:47] Samir: Quick — are you SOC 2 Type II? And what about key management, do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?
[00:55] Maya: Yes we are SOC2 and have an ISO pack. KMS integration is supported, HSM via our Private deployment — we'll send the docs.
[01:08] Carlos: Good. For the POC success criteria: 1) no raw PII in logs, 2) 95th pct latency under 200ms for the main route, 3) output quality parity with current pipeline — we'll use a fixed eval set.
[01:22] Priya: Also need audit logs that show retention and deletion events for prompt IDs. Right to Erasure is a blocker for us.
[01:33] Ethan: Understood. For redaction we have two approaches: automated inline redaction at ingestion (regex + ML PII classifier), or store hashed prompts and redact the stored copy on write. Both have tradeoffs — inline redaction reduces fidelity for debugging, hashed storage preserves raw tokens off of the main store but is irreversible unless you keep separate vaults.
[01:56] Carlos: Can you walk through an example? Say a prompt contains a SSN and a credit card number. What gets stored?
[02:04] Ethan: Sure. Option A (inline redaction): we scrub and replace detected tokens with <REDACTED> before logging; Option B (hash + ephemeral): we hash the prompt text (sha256) and store only the hash + derived metadata, while routing the raw prompt ephemeral directly to the model but not persisted past X seconds — this helps debugging if you keep ephemeral snapshots guarded by KMS, but it's more operational overhead.
[02:32] Priya: How good is the PII classifier? FPs/ FNs matter to us — a missed SSN is bad.
[02:39] Ethan: The built-in classifier is tuned for common PII types; we recommend a two-stage check: regex for high-confidence patterns (SSN/CC) and ML detector for contextual leaks. We can ship the classifier config used in the POC and you can fine-tune thresholds.
[02:58] Maya: On retention, we expose per-route retention windows: 0 days (no storage), 7 days, 30, 90, 365. You can also mark certain routes as ephemeral: logs are deleted after processing.
[03:12] Carlos: Do deletions provide proof? Audit trail?
[03:15] Ethan: Yes, deletions are recorded in audit logs with event IDs, timestamps, and the requesting principal. Those logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3.
[03:26] Samir: We need proofs for GDPR erasure — is the deletion immediate across all backups?
[03:30] Maya: For Hosted we provide logical deletion and scrub copies in standard backup windows; for legal-level guarantees we recommend Private where backups are customer-managed — we can detail RTO/RPO semantics in the security pack.
[03:44] Priya: Benchmarking — we want to understand latency and cost tradeoffs. Our target is approx 95th percentile <200ms and steady-state throughput ~30 requests/sec for the route.
[03:56] Ethan: For throughput/latency sizing we'll run two benchmarks: replay of your sample set (best) and synthetic traffic that simulates bursts. For replay we need ~2–5k representative prompts and target concurrency. We'll also test with quantized model variants to estimate cost delta.
[04:14] Carlos: What's the expected delta when using int8/quantized models vs full precision in terms of quality? We can't accept >3% drop in summary quality.
[04:22] Ethan: Quality delta depends on model family; for many Llama-based variants we've seen <2% drop on summarization tasks with 8-bit quantization if you tune temperature and sampling. We'll include a small human evaluation on your eval set.
[04:38] Priya: Can Redwood do prefix/KV cache so we get lower tail latency on repeated contexts? Our workflow reuses multiple customer context templates.
[04:46] Ethan: Yes, our runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching per route. That can cut median latency significantly for repeated tokens. We'll include that in the benchmark config.
[05:00] Carlos: For the pilot length — we prefer a 2-week pilot but operationally ok with a 7-day intensive benchmark followed by a 7-day softer integration run. Can Redwood support that timeline in early Jan?
[05:12] Maya: Yes, tentatively Jan 4th start for the 7-day benchmark, Jan 11–18 soft integration. We'll confirm.
[05:20] Samir: Can you also show redaction false positive logs? We need to see examples of when PII is redacted but it wasn't PII.
[05:28] Ethan: We'll capture FP/FN counts and example cases and surface them in the evaluation report.
[05:35] Priya: What about prompt storage for debugging — hashing means we can't replay exact prompts to reproduce issues. Any middle ground?
[05:42] Ethan: Middle ground is encrypted vaults: store raw prompts encrypted with your KMS key and access via RBAC only to approved engineers; deletion still triggers KMS-based wiping procedures. This gives replayability but increases compliance burden.
[06:00] Carlos: Procurement — quote needed. For POC we'd likely want a short-term reserved capacity with burst to Hosted. Any rough estimate for 100k monthly interactions?
[06:10] Maya: We'll run a back-of-envelope after we get sample prompts (token distribution) — Ethan will do an estimate and give a per-1M token estimate and possible Dedicated delta if you choose reserved capacity.
[06:22] Priya: Also, can we configure route-level retention to zero for certain user-facing routes (e.g., password reset flow)?
[06:30] Ethan: Yes, route-level policies are supported. You can attach policy tags like PII:HIGH -> retention=0 and logging=redact.
[06:38] Samir: Audit requirements — we need immutable logs, event signatures?
[06:42] Maya: Audit logs are append-only, stored with event signatures, and exported to your S3 or SIEM. For highest assurance we recommend Private so you manage storage retention end-to-end.
[06:55] Carlos: Ok let's align on success criteria again — latency <200ms 95p, FP/FN PII detection thresholds below 1%/2% respectively, evidence of deletion/audits, and a cost estimate under our target.
[07:12] Priya: We'll provide an eval set of 500 labelled examples for quality checks and 2–5k unlabeled prompts for replay.
[07:20] Maya: Great, here's what we'll do next — send security pack, benchmark plan, and a preliminary quote. We'll also include instructions for uploading prompts securely.
[07:32] Ethan: I'll prepare the synthetic workload template: concurrency, token distribution, KV-cache on/off scenarios, and quantization flags.
[07:40] Carlos: Thanks all — anything else?
[07:42] Priya: One more — can we get SLA terms for Dedicated if we scale?
[07:46] Maya: We'll include Dedicated SLA language in the quote addendum.
[07:50] Samir: Sounds good. End of call.

Meeting close.

title: Lexana POC: model shortlist & workload scoping
content:
Lexana POC: model shortlist & workload scoping

Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Connor (Redwood); Sofia, Omar, Elena (Lexana)
---
Summary:
Sofia wants a 6-week POC to validate open-model options for multilingual contract clause extraction and risk scoring. Primary constraints: legal-grade accuracy, low hallucination, Spanish/Portuguese/Russian support, and on-prem/VPC options for sensitive files. Redwood to propose 3-model shortlist (+quantized variants), run small hosted benchmark, and provide cost/latency projections and security docs.
Topics covered:
- Workload sizing: tokens per contract, QPS, concurrency, retention policy
- Success criteria: precision/recall targets for clause extraction, acceptable latency, failure modes
- Model shortlist: candidate open models and size tradeoffs
- Benchmarks: dataset, metrics, evaluation cadence
- Timeline & next steps
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Sofia (Lexana): hi hi, Sofia here. Head of ML.
[00:09] Omar: Omar, lead counsel. i'll mostly listen but will flag legal constraints.
[00:12] Elena: Elena, PM. focusing on scope and timelines.
[00:15] Connor (Redwood): Connor, infra/SE. i'll run the bench and the hosting setup.
[00:20] Maya: Cool. high level — Lexana wants to run a POC to compare model options for clause extraction and risk scoring across english, spanish, portuguese, and russian. Is that right, Sofia?
[00:29] Sofia: Yes, exact. we also want to measure hallucination rates when models are asked to synthesize missing clauses, and false positives on liability clauses.
[00:35] Omar: also data residency — some contracts from EU clients require data remain in our VPC or an on-prem instance. SOC 2 is baseline, but some customers ask for ISO or audit logs and HSM/KMS.
[00:45] Maya: that's helpful. we can do Hosted for initial runs but will propose Dedicated / Private for production. Redwood has audit logs and KMS integrations; we'll send the security brief. sorry — our security deck.
[00:53] Elena: timeline constraint: we want results before the legal review cycle in mid July, so roughly a six-week window.
[01:00] Connor: noted. to scope infra: can you give rough workload numbers — average contract length, number of docs per day, peak concurrent reviewers?
[01:08] Sofia: average contract is ~3,500 tokens, some long ones up to 12k. we'll pilot with 200 anonymized contracts (mix of standard NDAs, SOWs, supplier contracts). Daily throughput target for POC ~500 documents, peak concurrent users maybe 40.
[01:20] Connor: ok that maps to qps and token throughput. for early bench we can simulate 50 QPS with batching. production expectations?
[01:27] Sofia: production could be 2k docs/day, but POC should demonstrate we can meet ~500/day with sub-second-ish latency per clause extraction call.
[01:35] Maya: let's talk success criteria — what metrics will you use to decide go/no-go?
[01:40] Elena: primary: clause extraction F1 >= 0.85 for key clause types (termination, indemnity, liability). secondary: hallucination rate < 2% on generative answers, latency < 800 ms for single-document extract endpoint, and cost per document under $0.05 for hosted.
[01:55] Sofia: and multilingual performance: for Spanish/Portuguese we want within 5 percentage points of English performance; russian is lower priority but should not be catastrophic.
[02:05] Omar: compliance: all PII must be redacted and logs should be configurable to avoid storing full text in Redwood logs.
[02:12] Connor: we support redaction and KV/prefix cache controls; will note retention config and masking.
[02:17] Maya: model shortlist — based on your domain we recommend testing a small, medium, and a larger open model variant. initial candidates: 1) LlamaX-13B (quantized 4-bit), 2) Orion-33B (unoptimized), 3) JurisGPT-70B-open (if available) — plus distilled / quantized variants. any concerns?
[02:36] Sofia: JurisGPT — is that an external community model? i've heard inconsistent results.
[02:40] Maya: yes community-sourced, tends to be best-in-class for legal prompts but can be less stable on hallucinations. that's why we'll include a medium-sized generalist model as a control.
[02:49] Connor: tradeoffs — 13B quantized will be cheapest and fast with decent accuracy; 33B is a middle ground; 70B likely best accuracy but higher cost and may need Dedicated or higher GPU to meet latency. we can also test smart rerouting: run extractors on 13B and fallback to 70B for low-confidence cases.
[03:05] Elena: fallback policy sounds promising. can we measure reroute latency?
[03:08] Connor: yes we'll instrument trace — expected extra latency if fallback is invoked, but only for small percent of requests.
[03:14] Sofia: what's Redwood's approach to model quantization? are we losing crucial legal nuance?
[03:18] Connor: quantization degrades some subtlety but with instruction-tuning and careful prompt engineering it's often acceptable for extraction tasks. for scoring/risk we might need the larger model. we'll include a quality delta table in the bench.
[03:29] [crosstalk] Omar: and what about fine-tuning vs prompt engineering?
[03:32] Maya: for POC we recommend prompt & eval-first to avoid long fine-tune cycles. If results plateau, we can do a small instruction-tune or RLHF later — which would change timeline.
[03:41] Elena: budget? we have limited budget for this quarter. can you give rough cost brackets?
[03:45] Maya: ballpark for 2-week hosted bench: small model runs maybe $800-$1.2k, mid model $2k-$3k, large $6k+. Production cost depends on tokens and model—we'll provide per-doc estimates.
[03:58] Sofia: ok that's fine as a preliminary.
[04:00] Connor: benchmark plan:
- Week 0: ingest and sanitize 200 contracts (Sofia)
- Week 1: run smoke tests on 13B quantized and 33B baseline (hosted) for extraction metrics
- Week 2: run larger 70B test and fallback policy sim
- Week 3: stress tests for throughput (simulate 500/day, peak 40 concurrent)
- Week 4: compile results, meeting to review and recommend production config
[04:25] Elena: that fits the 6-week window if we start asap.
[04:28] Maya: security items — we'll send SOC 2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, SAML SSO, and KMS docs. any extra certs?
[04:36] Omar: for certain clients we may need on-prem or private deployment and HSM integration. also legal wants to see data deletion audit trail.
[04:44] Connor: Private deployment is supported; scheduling and hardware planning would add ~4–6 weeks after POC if you choose that route.
[04:52] Sofia: can Redwood provide a sample evaluation script so we can reproduce metrics?
[04:55] Connor: yes we'll share our benchmark harness and a reproducible notebook (will include tokenization, metrics, and conf intervals).
[05:01] Maya: any competitors or internal constraints we should be aware of?
[05:04] Sofia: we did preliminary tests with Bedrock and OpenAI; Bedrock was cheaper but we had trouble with fine-grained extraction, OpenAI had best out-of-the-box but cost is a worry.
[05:15] Omar: legal also flagged vendor lock-in risk.
[05:18] Maya: that's a good point — Redwood's exportable prompts and pinned model versions help reduce lock-in. we'll document the model artifacts and configs.
[05:25] Elena: final recap and next steps?
[05:27] Maya: recap: Lexana provides 200 anonymized contracts + label set by 2026-05-18. Redwood shares benchmark spreadsheet, security brief, and sample notebook by 2026-05-16. Connor to provision hosted trial and run initial 13B/33B smoke by 2026-05-20. We'll target a POC kickoff run week of 2026-05-25.
[05:45] Sofia: sounds good. Omar — any final?
[05:48] Omar: just please include deletion audit detail in the security brief.
[05:52] Maya: will do. thanks all.
[05:55] End of call.
---
References & shared artifacts mentioned:
- Deck: drive.lexana/POC/lexana-poc-deck.pdf
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (notebook link to be provided)
- Security brief: redwood.com/security/lexana-brief.pdf
---
Recorded with moderate transcription fidelity; speaker turns accurate but some technical names may be mis-transcribed.

title: LucentGrid POC acceptance criteria + security alignment
content:
LucentGrid POC acceptance criteria + security alignment

Kickoff to align on POC acceptance criteria, sizing for expected workloads (inference qps / concurrency), security gating (SOC 2 + ISO checklist), SSO/SAML integration and required RBAC, and audit log retention/KMS expectations. Agreed next steps include sending a concise security playbook, a baseline benchmark plan, and scheduling a short on-prem/VPC install walkthrough.
Owner: Maya Patel - Send SOC 2 + ISO executive summary and Redwood private deployment checklist - Due: 2027-02-16
Owner: Ethan Cole - Draft benchmark plan (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cold vs warm cache) and sample test harness scripts - Due: 2027-02-18
Owner: Priya Menon - Provide representative workload (sample prompts + expected concurrency patterns, token lengths) and synthetic dataset - Due: 2027-02-15

Redwood to send security pack + short private deployment notes

Schedule 60-min benchkick (shared spreadsheet) for the week of 2027-02-22
Confirm procurement timeline and PO trigger (Tom)
Meeting: 2027-02-11 16:00 UTC - Duration 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rina (CSM) -- Nina (VP Eng), Omar (SecOps), Priya (ML Eng), Tom (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros and then we'll jump to acceptance criteria. Uh, Nina are you leading on the success criteria side?
[00:12] Nina: Yeah thanks, hi all, hi Maya, Ethan. So for LucentGrid we need to validate three things in the pilot: first functional parity for routing and prompt handling, second performance under our 250 concurrent sessions peak, and third security and auditability - SOC 2 style controls and SSO integration.
[00:30] Ethan: Great, can I ask a quick clarifying q, when you say 250 concurrent, is that hard concurrency or sessions with long polling? Like are these streaming sessions?
[00:40] Priya: Mostly short-turn chat like 60-120 token responses, some longer 600-800 token generation for summarization, and yes streaming is important for UX. Concurrency is around 250 active connections, QPS about 120 sustained, bursts to 300 for a minute or two.
[01:01] Maya: good, that's helpful. We'll propose a baseline benchmark that includes p50/p95 latency, and throughput targets. Our typical private deployment config for that footprint is-- sorry Rina interjects--
[01:12] Rina: and just to note we have autoscale + burst on Dedicated but for Private VPC it depends on infra.
[01:18] Omar: security front, a few must-haves: SOC 2 type II equivalence, ISO 27001 evidence preferred, SSO with SAML2.0 and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC scoped to environment and model, and full audit logs with immutable retention for at least 1 year. Also KMS integration for envelope encryption.
[01:36] Ethan: Understood. For SOC 2 / ISO we can provide our audit artifacts and an executive summary. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments and can outline key rotation flow.
[01:48] Omar: How granular are your audit logs? We need token-level attribution back to the user identity and model version, plus tamper-evidence.
[01:55] Ethan: We capture request id, caller identity (via token claims or SSO subject), model id/version, full request/metadata and, depending on config, truncated payloads. We can retain logs on the customer's S3/GCS bucket with lifecycle policies. There may be redaction options for PII in transit though that's part of the workload design.
[02:14] Nina: retention - we can't keep raw content beyond 90 days in some markets, but audit metadata must stay 1 year. Is redaction configurable so we can keep logs for auditing but redact text?
[02:25] Maya: Yes, we typically separate audit metadata from payload. We can discuss a configuration where full payloads are off by default, metadata retained longer; also we can support routed copies to customer-owned bucket for retention policies.
[02:38] Tom: procurement question, timeline - we need an internal security review first before a PO. What's a realistic pilot start date if we move quickly?
[02:45] Maya: If all artifacts are shared promptly, we can start benchkick in ~2 weeks and have a 4-week pilot. So start date target week of 2027-02-22 and wrap by mid-March.
[02:56] Priya: on benchmarks can you lay out cold vs warm cache numbers? Our models are GPT-style decoder models, KV cache matters for warm starts.
[03:07] Ethan: Absolutely. Bench plan will include cold start latency (first token), warm cached latency (p50/p95), and throughput tests with continuous batching. We'll also test prefix caching for repeated prompts. We'll attach scripts - note sometimes transcribe as redwood runtime does continuous batching which lowers per-token cost.
[03:26] Nina: about environment isolation - we want a VPC-deployed private control plane. Is there a lightweight control plane that still gives us RBAC and tracing hooks?
[03:35] Ethan: The Private offering runs a control plane that can be customer-hosted in your VPC. It exposes RBAC, per-model routes, and tracing hooks (trace id injected). We can provide SSO mapping to Azure AD or Okta and SCIM provisioning.
[03:49] Omar: any third-party pen test or do you provide SOC 2 report only? We might require a pen test summary for the specific setup.
[03:57] Maya: We have a SOC 2 Type II report and can share redacted pen test summaries. For on-prem/private deployments we offer assistance during our onboarding pen test window and can coordinate a scoped test with your team.
[04:12] Priya: data residency — we have EU customers; for this pilot data must stay in eu-west-1. Can Private run in their region?
[04:20] Ethan: Yes we can deploy in customer VPC in eu-west-1 region or on-prem; we'll note network egress requirements in the checklist.
[04:27] Tom: SLAs - during pilot we don't need a formal SLA but need reliability targets for acceptance.
[04:33] Maya: Acceptance criteria doc will include uptime thresholds (>=99% over bench window), p95 latency <= 500ms for short responses, and throughput targets per your sample workload. We'll put those into the success criteria spreadsheet.
[04:46] Nina: Can you also capture cost estimate per 1M tokens and per-hour reserved capacity so we can budget?
[04:53] Maya: Yes, we'll provide rough unit economics for both hosted and private (GPU-backed) configurations and show sensitivity to batching and quantization.
[05:02] Omar: SSO integration detail - we need SAML metadata and SCIM for group sync into RBAC. Also, audit trail must show which group made changes to model versions.
[05:12] Ethan: We'll map SAML attributes to RBAC and log admin actions with subject and group info. Model rollouts are logged as events with before/after model ids.
[05:21] Priya: any gotchas with HSM/KMS in private - rotation frequency and access patterns?
[05:28] Ethan: Customer KMS supports envelope keys, we don't hold plaintext root keys. Rotation is handled per your KMS policy; we document the handshake and access control. If you require HSM-backed keys in your HSM we can integrate via standard KMS providers.
[05:42] Rina: quick note, we'll share a short 1-pager that maps compliance asks to artifacts we can provide.
[05:48] Maya: Okay to recap - Redwood sends security pack (SOC2/ISO exec summary + private deployment notes), Ethan sends bench plan and test scripts, LucentGrid sends workload samples and IdP metadata, Omar sends retention/KMS specifics. We aim to kick bench the week of 2/22.
[06:04] Tom: sounds good, I'll start procurement gating and let you know PO timeline.
[06:09] Nina: thanks, one last question, competitors - we're also testing a Bedrock path and an internal inference stack. How do you help compare cost/perf?
[06:18] Maya: We'll include a short comparison matrix and run the same benchmark harness so apples-to-apples. We'll also highlight where our routing and caching gives unit cost benefits.
[06:28] Maya: Alright we'll follow up with the pack and schedule the benchkick. Thanks everyone.
[06:33] End meeting

title: AurumX Systems - Implementation Kickoff & Onboarding
content:
AurumX Systems - Implementation Kickoff & Onboarding

Kickoff to align on onboarding runbook, network/VPC intake, security checklist (SOC2/SAML), pilot scope and initial rollouts. Agreed next steps: share runbook, schedule infra deep dive, grant staging access, and propose pilot SLOs.
Redwood to send onboarding runbook + staging access instructions (Maya) by 2026-07-02
Schedule infra deep-dive with AurumX platform team (Liam) week of 2026-07-06
AurumX to share sample workload shape + token profile (Jared) by 2026-07-05
Security team to review SOC2 and SAML docs; Redwood to provide redacted audit logs sample (Priya) by 2026-07-07
Maya Chen: Send onboarding runbook, staging cluster invite, and quickstart scripts (2026-07-02)
Liam O'Connor: Book infra deep-dive and prepare KV-cache/batching notes (2026-07-06)
Jared Kim: Provide token distribution CSV and 3 sample prompts for eval (2026-07-05)
Eliot Cho: Send current compliance posture doc + list of required controls (2026-07-07)
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01 15:00 PT | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Priya Rao (CSM) - Redwood; Jared Kim (Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Platform), Eliot Cho (Security), Mina Park (PM) - AurumX

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then we ll jump into the onboarding runbook and what the first two weeks look like. Uh, quick note, recording is on.
[00:18] Jared: Cool, thanks Maya. We re excited to get this moving; we have a tight Q3 goal to ship inference for our customer support assistant. Main blockers are network + compliance.
[00:33] Priya: Great, high level agenda: run through the onboarding steps, VPC/network intake, security checklist, sample workload and pilot definition, then next steps.
[00:47] Liam: I'll cover the infra bits — how staging works, typical batching and KV cache patterns, and what we need from you for a smooth pilot.
[01:05] Sofia: On the platform side we use k8s with an internal ingress and egress rules; we re prefer private connectivity. We d like to understand Redwood Private options and if we need an on prem box.
[01:24] Maya: For private, we have a few patterns — VPC peering, private link, and on-prem package. Most customers start with VPC peering to our private control plane; if you need full air-gap we can talk about the on-prem bundle. For your use-case, VPC peering sounds right.
[01:45] Eliot: From security, can you share SOC 2 Type II artifacts, SAML SSO support, and encryption key management? Also curious about audit logs retention and redaction capabilities.
[02:03] Priya: Absolutely, we will share SOC2 certificate and our security pack. We can provide sample audit log output; note that logs sometimes have obfuscated ids — we ll show format. SAML and SSO are supported. KMS integration for customer keys is available for Private deployments.
[02:26] Jared: For perf, our latency budget is 200ms p95 for single-turn queries. Is that realistic on hosted or do we need Dedicated GPUs?
[02:40] Liam: 200ms p95 is tight depending on model size. For smaller quantized models and good batching we can be sub-200ms on Dedicated capacity. Hosted can hit that for some smaller models and with prefix caching but it's less predictable during bursts. There's tradeoff between cost and latency.
[03:02] Mina: Can you say more about caching? We re concerned about cold-starts.
[03:10] Liam: Sure — we have prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. If your workload has repeat prompts (like templated support replies), cache helps a lot. Also we can tune batch windows to balance latency/cost per token.
[03:27] Jared: We'll send a token distribution and sample conversations so you can suggest batching and quantization configs.
[03:33] Maya: Perfect.
[03:36] [04:00] — brief cross talk about calendars —
[04:15] Eliot: On compliance — do you support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS)? We need all PII encrypted with our keys while at rest.
[04:27] Priya: Yes for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and can work on dedicated keys for enterprise plans.
[04:41] Sofia: Network wise: what do you need for route tables and egress? We have restricted internet egress.
[04:51] Liam: We'll need a few IP ranges for the staging endpoints and ephemeral ports for model updates. If you re doing strict egress, VPC peering eliminates most egress needs; we'll share a minimal whitelist.
[05:06] Jared: Pilot scope — we re thinking two-week PoC with 10k daily requests, ramp to 50k by end of quarter. Success is meet 200ms p95 and maintain <=0.5% error rate.
[05:22] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose a pilot plan: week 1 instrument + baseline tests in staging; week 2 run ramp and ops handoff. We'll provide dashboards and cost projections.
[05:35] Mina: Who will be the primary contacts during the pilot?
[05:39] Maya: Priya will be your CSM, Liam handles infra/benchmarks, and I ll coordinate commercial and rollout.
[05:48] [06:00] — 6 minutes in —
[06:05] Liam: On metrics, we ll instrument token-level cost, p50/p95 latencies, and per-route error breakdown. We can also attach traces to specific requests if you provide sample ids.
[06:20] Sofia: For staging access, how do we authenticate? SSO or API keys?
[06:26] Priya: We can support SAML SSO for team access; for programmatic onboarding we'll issue scoped API keys and can lock them to an IP range.
[06:37] Jared: Any gotchas with data residency? We need EU-only data residency for a subset of customers.
[06:44] Maya: We have region pinning; we can route EU traffic to EU-hosted clusters and keep data in-region. For Private, that's configurable.
[06:55] Eliot: Can we get an example of your rollback/fallback policy if a model deploy causes quality regression?
[07:03] Liam: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variant. Also Redwood Optimize can monitor evals and trigger alerts on regressions against a prompt set.
[07:15] Mina: What's the typical time to onboard to staging?
[07:19] Priya: For simple VPC peering and a small pilot, 3-5 business days once we have the network info and a point of contact. On-prem takes longer.
[07:30] Jared: We're leaning VPC peering. I'll have networking send the route table and firewall rules.
[07:36] Maya: Great. We'll send a checklist today.
[07:39] [08:02] — discussion of pricing high-level —
[08:12] Maya: For pilot we'll give a temporary eval credit; once we move to Dedicated we ll provide commit options and a cost/latency tradeoff matrix.
[08:25] Jared: Competitor question — we did an internal eval vs VendorX and our own stack; curious how Redwood handles multitenant isolation.
[08:34] Liam: Dedicated pools with tenant isolation and per-tenant quotas are standard; for extra isolation we do single-tenant Dedicated clusters.
[08:43] Eliot: About logs — need them in our SIEM; can you push audit logs or do we need to pull?
[08:50] Priya: We can push to your SIEM or provide S3 delivery. The logs are in standard JSON; sometimes product names are abbreviated in auto transcriptions — but the fields are stable.
[08:59] Mina: Is there a recommended eval set or tooling?
[09:03] Maya: We'll share our eval harness and a sample prompt set; Redwood Optimize can run periodic checks and surface regressions.
[09:12] Jared: Okay next steps — we ll send token profile and sample prompts; please send runbook and staging access. Also want the SOC2 and SAML schema.
[09:23] Maya: Confirmed. We'll attach a short SLO template for pilot and a suggested monitoring dashboard.
[09:31] Eliot: One more thing — vulnerability scanning, do you allow us to scan the staging endpoints?
[09:37] Priya: Yes, we allow authenticated scanning in staging; we'll coordinate scope.
[09:43] [10:00] — closing recap by Maya —
[10:05] Maya: Quick recap: 1) Redwood sends onboarding runbook, SOC2 pack, example logs, and SSO integration notes; 2) AurumX shares workload tokens, prompts, and network rules; 3) schedule infra deep dive with Liam; 4) set pilot dates and SLOs. Action owners in the notes. Any final Qs?
[10:26] Jared: Nope, all clear. Thanks team.
[10:29] Maya: Thanks everyone, we ll follow up with the packet.
[10:33] Meeting ends.

title: Summerset platform activation sync-up
content:
Summerset platform activation sync-up

Initial implementation kickoff to align on activation runway, security constraints, and pilot benchmarks. Customer prefers dedicated/private deployment but needs cost scenarios and VPC design details. Immediate deliverables: pricing scenarios, security pack, and pilot test matrix.
Onboarding runbook and permissions
Dedicated vs hosted deployment tradeoffs
Pilot benchmark scope and metrics
Networking and VPC peering
SAML/SSO, KMS, and audit logging
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-07-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE); Priya Reddy (Redwood CSM); Jasper Liu (Redwood SE); Marina Cole (Summerset Eng Mgr); Omar Aziz (Summerset Cloud Architect); Lena Park (Summerset Security)

Summary: quick kick off to align ops, security, and pilot. Capture next steps for pricing and pilot setup.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. We'll do quick intros then dive into the activation runway. Priya and Jasper will handle the onboarding timeline and technical plan.
[00:18] Marina: Hi all, thanks, excited. We want to get clear on the timeline - Q4 launch target and a pilot in late July, maybe early August.
[00:35] Priya (CSM): Great. Quick question on success criteria — are you primarily looking at latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, or both?
[00:50] Marina: Both, but latency for customer-facing chat is highest priority. Cost matters for scale - we're forecasting 10M tokens/month in steady state.
[01:12] Jasper (SE): Okay, latency SLOs—are you targeting p95 under 300ms? Also, do you have a preference for dedicated vs hosted? Dedicated gives more predictable latency but requires networking.
[01:33] Omar: We prefer dedicated because of data residency and egress controls; also want VPC peering to our GCP project. Security will be a showstopper if we can't do private deployments.
[01:50] Lena (Security): Yep, SOC 2 and audit logs are required. We also need SSO via SAML, role-based access, and KMS integration for key rotation.
[02:10] Alex: That's all supported—Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, and we have audit logs. Jasper will follow up on the specific KMS providers supported. I'll also link the security pack after the call.
[02:40] Jasper: Quick note - we will need an IP allowlist and a short window for peering setup. For benchmarks, do you have a staging VPC with sample traffic patterns we can run against?
[03:05] Marina: We don't yet, but we can spin up a small staging cluster. We'll share estimated QPS and traffic bursts.
[03:22] Alex: Excellent. For the pilot, we usually do a 2-week benchmark: baseline hosted test, then dedicated run, capture p50/p95/p99, token costs, and steady-state throughput. Does that align?
[03:44] Omar: Yes. Also can you simulate prefix caching and session affinity? Our chat workloads keep long context windows.
[04:01] Jasper: We'll include a KV cache warmup and typical session lengths. We'll instrument token-level costs in the report.
[04:18] Marina: What's the expected timeline to get dedicated capacity up? We have compliance review in mid-August.
[04:30] Alex: With our standard process, dedicated can be provisioned in 10-14 business days after contract. If you need faster, there's a priority onboarding add-on.
[04:49] Lena: Pricing—can you provide reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go scenarios? We need budget sign-off.
[05:03] Alex: Absolutely. I'll share a pricing scenarios spreadsheet with reserved commitments, burst rates, and an estimated unit cost. We'll include cost comparisons to hosted.
[05:18] Marina: Any competitors we should consider? We looked at Anthropic's enterprise offering and also evaluated Vertex managed endpoints.
[05:30] Priya: Noted. We'll highlight where Redwood's routing and caching reduce per-token cost compared to standard endpoints.
[05:48] Jasper: A couple technical clarifications: what quantization profiles do you support for the model variants, and can we pin model versions during rollout?
[06:05] Alex: Yes—model pinning and rollout policies are supported. Quantization recommendations will be part of Redwood Optimize suggestions; Jasper will run a quick compatibility check during the pilot.

--- Transcript continues with timestamped back-and-forth ---
[12:10] Marina: We have an internal requirement that any external logs be redacted of PII before leaving our VPC, is that possible?
[12:28] Jasper: By default, log forwarding can be configured to redact fields. We can also route logs to your Splunk via secure collector. We'll document the redaction patterns.
[18:05] Omar: For networking, does Redwood require dedicated peering or is NAT gateway sufficient for private deployments?
[18:22] Alex: We can support both; peering gives lower variance. For regulatory workloads, peering + private deployment is recommended.
[21:03] Lena: About KMS—we use Cloud KMS with customer-managed keys, can Redwood integrate with that or do we need HSM?
[21:18] Jasper: Cloud KMS is supported; we also support HSM integrations for extra assurance. We'll capture the exact cipher suites in the security pack.
[28:40] Marina: Ok, let's talk runbook and roles. Priya, will you own the onboarding runbook?
[28:51] Priya: Yes, I'll own runbook updates. We'll need a primary contact for network and a separate contact for security.
[29:10] Marina: Omar will own networking, Lena will own security. I'll be overall program lead.
[31:55] Jasper: For pilot metrics—what thresholds should we consider pass/fail? E.g., p95 < 400ms and cost delta under 20% versus hosted?
[32:11] Marina: p95 < 350ms would be ideal, but we can be flexible to 400ms for pilot. Cost target: < 25% higher than hosted if latency gains are evident.
[35:00] Alex: Good. We'll provide an initial proposal listing two pilot scenarios: conservative (lower capacity) and full-scale (higher capacity). The conservative plan aims for speed to results.
[39:14] Marina: Regarding SSO and user access—do you require SCIM for user provisioning or can we do manual RBAC?
[39:29] Priya: We support SCIM and manual invites. For enterprise rollouts we recommend SCIM to sync groups.
[42:40] Omar: One more item—data residency. Some tenant data must be kept in EU regions. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[42:55] Alex: Yes we have region pinning for model serving and data at rest. We'll note the available regions for Private deployments in the follow-up.
[46:10] Marina: This is helpful, thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[46:20] Priya: Recap: Alex sends pricing scenarios; Jasper schedules the pilot and shares the test matrix; Marina/Omar will provide traffic samples and provision staging VPC; Priya sends onboarding runbook and permissions checklist.
[46:40] Marina: Agreed. Also please share the security pack and SOC 2 evidence link.
[46:55] Alex: Will do. I'll drop links: security pack (https://redwood-internal.docs/security-pack.pdf), onboarding runbook (https://redwood-internal.docs/onboarding-runbook), pricing gsheet (link will be shared). We'll also create a pilot workspace in Slack.
[47:20] Omar: Expect traffic patterns by 2026-07-20. We want pilot to start week of 2026-07-27 if possible.
[47:40] Jasper: We'll aim to have the benchmark plan by 2026-07-24 and the pilot runbook by 2026-07-26.
[48:05] Lena: I'll follow up with any compliance questions; otherwise we can proceed.
[48:30] Alex: Great thanks — we'll follow up via email and Slack and set the pilot kickoff calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
[48:45] Meeting ends.

Questions captured:
- Do you need HSM or Cloud KMS? (answered)
- Can you do VPC peering or NAT? (answered)

Action items noted above.

References:
- Security pack link (shared post-call)
- Pricing scenarios gsheet (to be shared)
- Pilot benchmark template (Jasper to attach)

Alex to share estimated capacity pricing sheet by 2026-07-18
Jasper to schedule pilot benchmark run with customer infra team week of 2026-07-27
Priya to send onboarding runbook and permissions checklist
Alex - Pricing + reserved capacity scenarios (due 2026-07-18)
Jasper - Pilot benchmark plan + test matrix (due 2026-07-24)
Marina - Provide sample traffic patterns and SSO contacts (due 2026-07-20)

title: Weekly POC bench readout & routing decision - Windfall Health
content:
Weekly POC bench readout & routing decision - Windfall Health

Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-04 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Tao Nguyen (Redwood SE), Dana Morris (Windfall Head of ML), Ravi Kaur (Windfall Platform), Marta Silva (Windfall CTO)

Auto-summary:
Windfall ran the week-3 bench against their incumbent (CurrentVendor AIServ). Redwood showed head-to-head numbers with lower median and 95th latency for the short chat path but slightly higher 99th under heavy burst. Throughput (tokens/sec) looked favorable with Redwood's batching + prefix cache when QPS steady. Customer asked about VPC private deploy latency, KMS encryption overhead, and fallback to smaller model to preserve tail SLOs. Actionables: share detailed per-route percentiles, routing playbook, and schedule in-lab head-to-head.

Topics:
- Week 3 benchmark: median/95/99 latency vs incumbent
- Throughput and unit cost per token estimate
- Routing decision: primary->redwood, fallback->incumbent or smaller quantized variant
- Security/Private deployment constraints (V P C, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and in-lab head-to-head run scheduling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. can we do quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana (Windfall): Dana here, ravi and marta with me as well.
[00:12] Ravi (Windfall): morning, yeah we got the week 3 runs in, excited to walk through.
[00:16] Samir: great. Elena will run through the numbers and tao will cover routing playbook.
[00:24] Elena (Redwood): ok, so quick context — we re-ran the same workload you sent last week, matching prompt distribution and 95th token lengths. baseline is CurrentVendor AIServ v3.1, we ran 10k requests over two sessions to capture warm and cold tails.
[00:40] Elena: median latency on the chat path was 54 ms on redwood vs 78 ms baseline, 95th was 210 ms vs 310 ms. 99th we saw 780 ms vs 640 ms — so tail is higher for us in that particular burst window, likely queueing under continuous batching.
[01:05] Dana: ok that's interesting — median better, 99th worse, that 99th discrepancy is concerning for us because our SLO is 800 ms 99th.
[01:12] Elena: totally, yep we noticed that and dug into the KV cache behavior — the cold prefixes and a couple of long-request spikes caused a backlog. our fix options: 1) aggressive per-model slot reservation (dedicated), 2) fallback routing to a smaller quantized variant for long tails, or 3) change batching window to prefer latency (lower batch size at cost per-token).
[01:33] Ravi: what's the quantized variant trade? does output quality drop a lot?
[01:36] Elena: slight truncation on nuanced completions, we recommend running a small eval set — we can attach eval diffs. for many instruction prompts the difference is minimal.
[01:46] Marta: are we able to do VPC private deployment for the dedicated slot? security wants the control plane in our V P C and keys in our K M S.
[01:53] Samir: yes, we support private deployments. control plane can be customer-managed. KMS integration is supported, full audit logs. we'll share SOC2 + architecture diagram after.
[02:03] Dana: overhead? any latency hit when KMS rotates or we use H S M?
[02:08] Tao (Redwood): small on initial handshake for key unwrap, negligible per-request if we cache the data key locally. typical numbers are 2-5 ms once keys are cached; cold rotation adds a spike but not per-token.
[02:22] Dana: ok that sounds fine.
[02:25] Elena: on throughput, redwood showed 1.8x tokens/sec under steady QPS vs baseline for the large model, mainly due to continuous batching and our prefix cache. unit cost estimate after quantization and batching suggestions drops ~30% vs baseline for your workload.
[02:44] Ravi: can you share the config we used for the run — batch size, sequence length assumptions, warmup steps?
[02:49] Elena: yes, we'll attach the runner config and the CSV. note we intentionally left burst policy permissive which inflated 99th.
[02:56] Dana: can you explain the burst policy? our traffic is spiky, like 200 to 1200 RPS for minutes.
[03:03] Tao: burst policy determines how much we accept above reserved capacity before routing fallback. if you set strict reserved capacity with small burst, you'll avoid queueing but see throttling; if you allow larger bursts, we handle via short queues and batching which improves median but can hurt tail.
[03:18] Ravi: could we run a variant that pins dedicated slots for peak windows and uses hosted for base?
[03:23] Samir: yes — hybrid: reserved slots for base SLO, autoscale for peaks + graceful fallback to quantized variant for tails. that's what the routing playbook proposes.
[03:32] Marta: what's the fallback latency delta if routed to quantized variant?
[03:36] Elena: median goes down to ~40 ms, 95th to 160 ms, 99th ~420 ms, and quality drop is minor on short instructions.
[03:47] Dana: how about fallback to incumbent instead of quantized variant?
[03:50] Elena: we can fallback to any compatible model including your incumbent merchant; downside is egress/handshake overhead and possible auth/token rotation to another vendor. also, you'd pay two vendors during failover windows.
[04:05] Ravi: cost question — you said unit cost down 30% with quantize + batching. what's absolute cost per 1M tokens?
[04:11] Samir: rough sketch: baseline vendor is ~ $1,400 per 1M tokens in your run; with redwood optimized profile we estimate ~$980 per 1M after batching & quantization. dedicated contracts change the math — we can run committed slot numbers.
[04:28] Dana: please send an example committed slot math.
[04:31] Samir: will do.
[04:33] Elena: one more datapoint — while median improved, we saw sensitivity to request size variance. when token length spikes above 1.8x median, batching groups fewer requests and queueing increases. causes a tail.
[04:47] Ravi: could we change client to send truncated prefix or use token budget?
[04:51] Elena: yes, truncating non-critical context helps, or you can leverage our prefix/K V cache so repeated context doesn't count towards seq length after warm cache.
[05:02] Marta: ok. security wise, can we get the full audit logs and an ingestion timeline?
[05:07] Tao: yes audit logs available, can forward retention SLAs. note for private deployment we can store logs in your S3 with export TTL you control.

title: Lighthouse alignment - radical transparency & Q3 priorities
content:
Lighthouse alignment - radical transparency & Q3 priorities

Company all-hands focused on Q3 operational priorities, transparency on hiring and budget, product performance investments (latency/cost tradeoffs), and security/compliance updates. Leadership introduced a new "Lighthouse" initiative to centralize strategic bets and clarified canary rollout rules. Open Q&A covered SOC2 timeline, Dedicated vs Hosted guidance for large customers, and planned changes to on-call rotation and observability dashboards.
1) Lighthouse initiative + definition of success
2) Q3 priority areas: performance, reliability, go-to-market enablement, hiring cadence
3) Budget & hiring: tradeoffs and runway considerations
4) Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
5) Observability improvements and developer ergonomics
6) Open Q&A
[00:00] Ava: okay hi everyone, welcome to the all hands, thanks for joining. I'm Ava. Uh today we want to be a little bit shorter than usual, 70-ish minutes, got a tight agenda.
[00:16] Marcus: hey folks, Marcus here, quick heads up — we'll go through tech highlights first then product then q&a.
[00:30] Priya: hi, team — quick update from eng: we've been dogfooding the continuous batching improvements, seeing about 12 to 18% token cost reduction on average for web traffic but — uh — not uniformly across long-form bursts. so there is more tuning to do.
[00:55] Jamal: quick context, the "Lighthouse" idea is basically to pick three strategic bets for Q3 where we concentrate product, infra, and GTM so we don't spread thin. the bets are: 1) extreme latency SLOs for interactive apps, 2) Dedicated capacity for mid-market enterprise, 3) verticalized solutions for search & customer support.
[01:18] Ava: i want to emphasize transparency — we'll publish a dashboard that shows progress on each lighthouse bet weekly. not the whole payroll but high level metrics.
[01:34] Lena: also want to call out changes to how we prioritize hiring requests — there will be a short rubric, it's about impact on lighthouse bets and critical operational risk.
[01:50] Diego: from sales, customers keep asking about dedicated vs hosted overhead and what signals should push a POC into a Reserved capacity conversation. we'll share a decision tree.
[02:08] Nora: security quick — SOC2 phase 2 kickoff is next month, KMS integration for private deployments is in design, and we will publish an FAQ for Sales and SEs.
[02:27] Samir: observability — rolling out token-level tracing in staging this week, which should make it easier to correlate latency spikes to model/version.
[02:40] Audience (mic): applause / cheers (brief)
[03:00] Ava: ok now demo highlight — Marcus, you want to show the latency profile?
[03:08] Marcus: sure; so we ran a 1,024 token tail experiment across our 80/20 load split and found that the new kernel selection reduces p95 by around 30ms for small seqs but adds about 10ms for some quantized paths. there's a trade — cost decreases, sometimes latency edges up.
[03:38] Priya: yeah there's a tradeoff matrix in the doc. the key is we can make profile-based routing pick the lower-latency path at the cost of some throughput.
[03:50] Audience question: any updates on private/on-prem customers and air-gapped installs?
[03:57] Nora: yes, we have two pilot customers for private on-prem and both have unique networking needs. the package will include a local control-plane option and KMS hooks. still early.
[04:18] Jamal: product rollout policy update — canaries will default to 10% for major model switches, with automatic fallback to previous variant on error spikes. we'll add a warmup period for KV cache priming to reduce cold-start regressions.
[04:45] Diego: on pricing, we will not change public hosted pricing this quarter but for Dedicated we are looking at more granular bundles to match mid-market patterns.
[05:00] Audience comment (murmur): "how will this affect current pilots?"
[05:05] Ava: good question — pilots shouldn't be negatively impacted; SEs will get recommended settings per pilot.
[05:12] [05:12] Marcus: quick note about kernels — some model families still show instability with the quantized path on A100 gen2 earlier this week; we rolled a patch but need a follow-up.
[05:30] [06:00] Priya: ops update — we will adjust on-call rotations to reduce pager fatigue, moving to 48 hour handoffs for infra owners and adding an extra backup on high-traffic days. feedback pls to people ops.
[06:22] [06:40] Lena: yes please fill the anonymous pulse if you are affected, we'll revise.
[07:00] Audience question: "what's runway and hiring status?"
[07:08] Ava: runway is healthy but we have to be deliberate; hiring will be prioritized for lighthouse bets and critical ops. teams must submit requests with clear impact statements.
[07:28] Diego: tying to GTM — we'll focus inbound motion for self-serve but allocate SEs for mid-market Dedicated POCs.
[07:44] [08:00] Nora: security Q — some folks asked about encryption at rest for hosted API. we already encrypt at rest and in transit; the KMS integration gives additional customer-managed key options for Dedicated/Private.
[08:20] Audience: "timeline for SOC2?"
[08:25] Nora: target is to complete Type II readiness audit by Q1 next year; phase 1 documents will be out mid-August.
[08:40] [09:00] Jamal: product clarifying — "verticalized solutions" means we will publish starter packs for search and support use-cases: prompts, evals, and quantization settings tuned per workload.
[09:20] Priya: engineering will deliver quantization recommendations and a lighter 8-bit runtime for small VMs by mid-Q3.
[09:36] Audience: "how do we measure success for lighthouse?"
[09:40] Ava: success metrics: latency p95 improvement, gross margin impact from cost reduction, number of customers on Dedicated, and number of closed-loop regressions detected by our evals.
[09:58] [10:15] Samir: observability will expose a weekly lighthouse dashboard: traffic share, p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, rollback events.
[10:30] Audience follow-up: "can we see the dashboard before public release?"
[10:35] Ava: yes leaders will get access and we'll ask for feedback.
[10:45] [11:00] Diego: sales playbook update — we'll publish a one-pager for AEs on when to recommend Dedicated and a checklist for procurement items.
[11:16] Audience question: "Any change to compensation or headcount?"
[11:22] Lena: compensation stable; headcount prioritized; we will not hire across the board.
[11:35] [12:00] Open Q&A (rapidfire):
[12:05] Employee 1: will we extend free credits for startups?
[12:08] Diego: probably yes, but with tighter qualifying signals.
[12:12] Employee 2: will the new batching change affect latency-sensitive customers?
[12:15] Marcus: we'll allow per-route overrides so sensitive customers can opt out of aggressive batching.
[12:28] Employee 3: can we have more clarity on regional capacity?
[12:32] Ava: we're expanding EU and APAC regions; details in the infra update next week.
[12:44] Employee 4 (mumble): requests for more async docs and runbooks.
[12:48] Priya: noted. docs team — we'll add sprint to backlog.
[13:05] [13:30] Final recap by Ava: recap: lighthouse bets, hiring rubric, SOC2 timeline, observability dashboard, canary policy. next steps: leadership doc next week, team leads submit resource asks, security FAQ. thanks all, meeting adjourned.
[13:50] (end)
Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts: model names and kernel terms sometimes transcribed incorrectly; timestamps approximate. Action items captured in metadata above. Deck and detailed lighthouse doc linked in the follow-up email (internal doc link).

title: 2026-05-22-rate-fencing-and-tenant-split-patterns-livestream-demo-tidewave-systems
content:
2026-05-22-rate-fencing-and-tenant-split-patterns-livestream-demo-tidewave-systems

Intro demo focused on multi-tenant rate fencing, org/project key strategies and handling bursty payments-like traffic. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated with strong security requirements. SE showed console flows for org keys, burst quotas, fairshare, and sticky routing; discussed fallback to lower-cost variants and KV/prefix caching implications. Agreed to run a scoped POC to validate 99th latency under mixed traffic and to share pricing options.
[00:00] Maya (AE): okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference. we got Jonah our systems engineer and Priya on product, um we'll run through rate-fencing patterns and then open for Q&A.
[00:14] Aisha: afternoon, thanks. traffic is kinda spiky for us, we have a payments notifications pipeline that has big bursts during settlement windows. we're trying to figure out how to prevent noisy tenants from chewing up our tokens.
[00:28] Jonah (SE): yeah and that's exactly where org/project keying helps. we'll show two topologies: single org key with per-project metadata, and dedicated project keys mapped to quotas. each has tradeoffs for billing and routing.
[00:41] Luis (SRE): quick Q, is the billing then per-project key? we want per-customer chargeback.
[00:47] Maya: yes you can map billing to project keys so accounting is clean. if you use org-wildcard keys you can still do tag-based usage but it's trickier for invoice line-iteming.
[01:02] Jonah: starting demo, pulling up Console -> Governance -> Key topology. this view shows active tokens, associated projects, and current concurrency slices. note that the console has a live QPS heatmap, and you can set soft/hard quotas.
[01:18] [screen share noise] Jonah: here I'm configuring a "burst fence" policy. the idea: each key gets a base rate, a burst bucket, and a cooldown window. when a key hits hard limit we can either queue, drop, or route to a cheaper model variant as a fallback.
[01:33] Ben (Security): about the fallback to cheaper variants — are we sure that's safe for PII? we can't degrade to a public model for regulated traffic.
[01:43] Priya (Product): great point. policies can be annotated with data classification. you can configure policy rules to never fallback for keys marked PHI, and those keys can be pinned to Dedicated or Private deployments.
[01:57] Nora (CTO): timeline question — our procurement needs to know if Dedicated is required for compliant PII handling or if hosted with VPC+KMS will suffice.
[02:08] Maya: depends on control plane expectations. many customers use Hosted + VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and are SOC2 happy, but some prefer Dedicated for stronger tenancy isolation. we'll add a comparison doc.
[02:22] Jonah: back to live traffic — here's a sample rule I'm simulating: fairshare across projects, with a reservation of 20% capacity for gold tenants then best-effort for others. see the graph — under heavy spike, gold stays within SLO, others throttle.
[02:40] Aisha: can we set preemptive throttles for a tenant before they cross the threshold? like soft limits that warn then hard limit?
[02:47] Jonah: yes soft alerts, then automated throttling. soft is metric-based alert with webhook, and the system supports gradual ramp-down policies so you don't see sharp failures.
[02:58] Luis: what about backpressure to our clients? any recommended client-side patterns?
[03:03] Jonah: yes recommended patterns: client should implement exponential retry with jitter, observe Retry-After header, and use sticky routing keys to maintain KV cache locality. KV caching reduces per-token compute for repeated contexts.
[03:20] Aisha: sticky routing, can you expand? is that per-project key pinned to a pool?
[03:25] Jonah: exactly. when you pin a project key to a pool, subsequent requests hit the same serving nodes which preserves KV cache and lowers p95/p99 latency. downside is less global load balance and possible hotspots; we expose pool-level autoscaling to mitigate.
[03:42] Priya: and we have a sticky-aware scheduler that moves warm state proactively during planned outages.
[03:49] [small crosstalk, typing]
[04:02] Maya: let's talk about unit economics quickly — batching, prefix KV caching and quantization all reduce per-token cost. Jonah did a quick numbers calc for a chat workload — enabling KV cache cut per-token cost by ~18% in our last benchmark.
[04:18] Jonah: the catch is cold starts for new routing keys — first request pays warmup. so our burst buckets and warmup TTL settings are important.
[04:28] Nora: curious about SLO verification — can you run a benchmark that simulates our peaks and show 99th latency?
[04:35] Jonah: yes we can. that's one of the POC items — we'll run a simulated arrival model with your traffic curves. please share the curves.
[04:44] Aisha: we'll export a week with per-minute QPS and 95th/99th token lengths.
[04:49] Ben: security — how are audit logs produced, retention, and encryption? also SSO and RBAC?
[04:56] Priya: audit logs are streamed to your S3 or GCS with AES-256 and tie into customer KMS; retention is configurable. we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC roles at org/project levels.
[05:09] Ben: any certifications for the hosted environment?
[05:12] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we can share the report under NDA. Dedicated/private deployments have additional contractual controls.
[05:22] Luis: what about multiregion failover for low-latency routing? we can't tolerate 200ms spikes for EU customers.
[05:28] Jonah: routing policies support region preference and geo-failover. you can define latency SLOs per customer and the smart router will pick nearest healthy pool.
[05:40] Aisha: okay demo makes sense, show me one more: how do we quickly revoke a compromised key and re-route traffic?
[05:46] Jonah: revocation is a one-click in Console -> Keys -> Revoke; you can also rotate keys via API. after revocation, you can optionally create a temporary fallback key mapped to a different pool to drain state.
[05:59] [sound of a message ping]
[06:05] Nora (joined): sorry, timezone mix up, jumped in. quick Q: if a tenant is on Dedicated but occasionally wants to burst to Hosted, do you support hybrid routing?
[06:15] Maya: yes hybrid is supported via policy-based routing; you can allow overflow to a hosted pool when dedicated is saturated with data-compliance annotations preventing PHI from overflowing.
[06:29] Maya: recap: we showed topologies, burst fences, sticky routing, and fallback policies; action items are benchmark run, pricing deck, and security pack.
[06:38] Aisha: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side?
[06:41] Maya: we need your traffic curves and list of keys that will be PHI-bound. Jonah will draft the benchmark plan.
[06:48] Luis: one last question on observability — can we get token-level tracing and costs per trace?
[06:54] Priya: yep token-level cost breakdown per request is available, plus trace IDs you can join to your APM, and per-route dashboards.
[07:05] Maya: excellent okay we'll follow up with the POC scoping invite for 06/02 and share the docs. thanks all.
[07:12] [meeting ends]

title: Mariner Retail - Renewal + EU Edge Capacity Onboarding Sync
content:
Mariner Retail - Renewal + EU Edge Capacity Onboarding Sync

Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Clarke (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Lena Morales (Mariner - Head of ML), Tom Briggs (Mariner - Platform), Ibrahim Khan (Mariner - Procurement), Asha Patel (Mariner - Security)

Summary: Quick renewal + expansion check-in. Customer is mid-contract, seeking 20% capacity uplift, EU-edge nodes for EU shopfronts, and a one-year contract extension with predictable pricing. Discussed dedicated pool sizing, burst capacity, SLOs for EU region, KMS integration, and next steps to finalize commercials and run a short benchmark.

Topics: renewal/pricing, capacity bump (20%), EU-edge onboarding, private data residency concerns, security docs, benchmark timeline, contract redlines.

Transcript body:
[15:00] Sophie Clarke: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — we wanted to align on the renewal and the EU-edge ask. How's the week, Lena?
[15:12] Lena Morales: Good, thanks. Sorry, running a little behind this morning. Appreciate you pulling this together. We got budget approval on the core renewal but we need clarity on the EU-edge pricing and the burst behavior for Black Friday-like peaks.
[15:27] Sophie Clarke: Understood. Ravi, do you want to run through the proposed dedicated pool config and how burst works?
[15:33] Ravi Patel: Yeah, sure. So from a runtime side, we recommend a baseline dedicated pool sized to handle steady-state spiky TPS, in Mariner's case looks like 120 concurrent generation streams during peak, so we suggested a 20% headroom bump on top of current reserved. Bursts are handled by short-lived shared capacity — that's the default fallback — but for EU-edge we can configure a local warm pool for much faster cold-starts.
[15:56] Tom Briggs: Wait, by "shared capacity" do you mean the hosted multi-tenant tiers? We have data residency constraints, so we need the EU-edge requests to stay in eu-west unless overflow is explicit and encrypted.
[16:09] Ravi Patel: Right, good call. For EU-edge we can route by region and policy. Overflow can be set to fall back to EU-dedicated, or if the dedicated is saturated we can route to a fallthrough hosted instance that also pins to eu-west. There is an additional cost for pinned eu-west hosted capacity; Sophie will detail that in pricing.
[16:28] Ibrahim Khan: From procurement perspective we also want the renewal to lock pricing for 12 months and have a clear SLA for latency 95th percentile. Can you commit to that?
[16:38] Sophie Clarke: Yeah, we can do a 12-month fixed pricing for the reserved capacity component. For SLAs we have standard latency SLOs for Dedicated — we can add a 95th percentile target in the contract for the dedicated pool. The hosted fallback has different SLOs; we'll flag that in the document.
[16:58] Asha Patel: Also, encryption questions. We use a customer-managed KMS in AWS for keys. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM? And how do audit logs look for private EU-edge traffic?
[17:10] Ravi Patel: Yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS via IAM roles, and for on-prem or VPC options we can support HSM/KMS through our Private offering. Audit logs for inference calls are available — token-level logs are redacted by default but we can enable full request/response logging for customers with appropriate controls. There is an extra retention fee for longer audit retention.
[17:34] Lena Morales: Hmm ok. What's the timeline to have the EU-edge nodes live if we greenlight now?
[17:41] Sophie Clarke: For a standard EU-edge onboarding with reserved capacity and basic networking (VPC peering), we usually see 3-4 weeks. If you want HSM integration and longer audit retention, add 1-2 weeks to accommodate security reviews and cert provisioning.
[17:56] Tom Briggs: We also want to validate throughput for our 6k tokens average requests — do you have a quick bench we can run?
[18:05] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll run a 5k-6k token throughput run with quantized model paths to mimic your workload. I'll use staging region eu-west-1 and share results and traces. Expect to see per-token p50/p95 numbers and cost-impact for quant vs fp16.
[18:20] Lena Morales: That would be great. Also a note — we've been testing the new reranking flow and saw some variability after last month's rollout. Curious about how Redwood handles model rollouts across regions.
[18:33] Jordan Kim: On rollouts: we provide canary and A/B rollout controls in the console; you can pin traffic percentages by model version and region. If you prefer, we can do an automatic fallback to last-known-good model under regressions. We also surface regression alerts tied to evals.
[18:52] Tom Briggs: Nice. On the pricing side, Sophie, can you share a line item for the dedicated pool, EU-edge premium, and hosted fallback? We need it split by monthly committed and overage/burst rates.
[19:04] Sophie Clarke: Absolutely. I'll send a detailed quote. For transparency, we'll show per-token unit economics, reserved flat fee, dedicated instance hourly, and overage/burst multipliers. i'm going to include an optional 15% discount for a 12-month commitment if you sign by end of the month.
[19:21] Ibrahim Khan: Procurement will need NET30 terms and a PO. Also, can you include a clause about data residency and KMS in the SOW?
[19:29] Sophie Clarke: We'll include explicit SOW language and KMS appendix. Legal usually wants the redline session — propose next Thurs?
[19:36] Ibrahim Khan: That works. 2027-02-25?
[19:38] Sophie Clarke: I'll set it up.
[19:40] Asha Patel: One more security thing — do you have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO certs? We need to store them in our vendor portal.
[19:48] Jordan Kim: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. I'll upload the latest artifacts to your portal and share direct links as well.
[19:58] Lena Morales: ok great. circling back to the capacity numbers: we said 20% bump — is that on top of current reserved, or total?
[20:08] Ravi Patel: It's additive on top of current reserved. But Sophie and I will model two variants: a conservative 12% uplift and a more comfortable 20% uplift with a small burst buffer. We'll show cost delta for both.
[20:21] Tom Briggs: For the benchmark, can you include KV cache warmup patterns? Our live traffic has a high repetition rate for product descriptions.
[20:31] Ravi Patel: Yep, I'll simulate prefix caching and include tests with and without prefix/KV cache to showcase cost savings and latency improvements.
[20:41] Lena Morales: Perfect. That helps our budget case. Also heads up, MegaCloud AI procurement flagged a discounted comparison — don't want to be surprised if they bring a competing price.
[20:51] Sophie Clarke: Noted — we'll make the value vs price explicit: per-token latency, regional guarantees, and observability differences.
[20:58] Ibrahim Khan: Anything else?
[21:02] Sophie Clarke: Quick recap: Action items — I'll send quote with EU-edge line item and optional discount, Ravi will run the benchmark and share results, Jordan will upload security docs and prepare onboarding checklist. We'll schedule legal redline for 2027-02-25. If that works we'll aim to sign and start provisioning by early March.
[21:18] Lena Morales: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[21:21] Sophie Clarke: Thanks all — we'll follow up by email with the materials.

End of call.

title: Pilot weekly triage: performance contrast - AxiomHealth
content:
Pilot weekly triage: performance contrast - AxiomHealth

Weekly POC sync to triage throughput/latency deltas vs incumbent provider. Team reviewed tail latency incidents, KV/prefix cache priming, routing decisions, and next tuning steps (dedicated slot request + 100k synthetic run). Agreed owner for follow-ups and schedule for final mid-pilot benchmark next Tuesday.
tail latency and p95/p99 deltas
prefix/KV cache priming
routing playbook and fallbacks
dedicated slots vs hosted bursts
quantization tradeoffs
Priya Raman: produce updated routing config (include fallback to small-quant variant) and share link to config repo by 2026-04-16
Dana Liu: run 100k synthetic traffic run on incumbent and attach raw CSV results to the shared bench spreadsheet by 2026-04-15
Ravi Kapoor: provision a dedicated 4-slot pool for two hours on 2026-04-18 for side-by-side run (Jordan to send order form)
Jordan Hayes: share security checklist and short explainer doc on prefix caching and KV priming by 2026-04-14
Evan Cho: schedule mid-pilot readout meeting for 2026-04-21
Send dedicated slot order and booking window
Run side-by-side 2 hour throughput test with KV cache primed vs cold
Compare p50/p95/p99 and unit token cost with incumbent across same test corpus
SE to propose adjusted batching config and recommend quantization profile
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 42 minutes, quick agenda--look at last week's bench, triage a couple of tail latency spikes, agree next run.
[00:18] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good, Jordan. We saw the big p99 blip at 3pm on Monday, that killed a few user flows. We want to understand root cause and whether that's routing or model cold starts.
[00:35] Priya Raman: Right, looking at traces we saw a pattern where long prefix sequences produced larger KV cache misses, plus one of the routing hops send traffic to the smaller GPU class which added 60-80ms.
[00:50] Dana Liu: To add, the incumbent is using a pinned smaller context model for short prompts which reduced cost but helped our 95th. We're trying to see if Redwood's batching + prefix cache can match p95 without doubling token cost.
[01:12] Ravi Kapoor: Also note our SRE saw CPU throttling on the proxy during burst 10k qps window, might be client side issue too.
[01:28] Priya Raman: Good call, Ravi. For today's triage I pulled the traced requests, annotated where prefix cache was cold. There's a shared spreadsheet link in the chat: https://redwood.share/axh-bench-2026 (note: link may be mis-typed by transcriber).
[01:45] Mel: Quick ask — can you remind us the difference between Redwood Dedicated slot behavior vs hosted burst? Our security team leaning hosted but we need predictable latency.
[02:03] Jordan Hayes: Sure — hosted is the fast path but multi-tenant, bursts are best-effort. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU slots and isolation; we can also schedule short dedicated windows for apples-to-apples runs. We'll send the order form after this call.
[02:25] Dana Liu: When you ran the 50k bench last week, how was KV priming handled? We primed with warm prefixes but saw cold tails.
[02:40] Priya Raman: The bench did a naive primer; we didn't prime every active prefix. For the next run we suggest targeted priming for top-10 prefixes and a background priming worker to reduce cold miss rate. That should knock down some p99s.
[03:05] Carlos Mendez: Is that expensive though? More tokens to prime maybe increases cost.
[03:12] Priya Raman: There's a tradeoff: a short priming phase reduces tail latency and can actually lower overall unit cost because retries/timeouts are costly. We'll model that for your corpus.
[03:29] Dana Liu: Could quantization help? Incumbent uses an 8-bit profile; What's Redwood's quant recommendation?
[03:40] Priya Raman: We have quant profiles — 4-bit and 8-bit. For this workload 8-bit with selective KV layout tends to hit the best latency/cost balance; 4-bit can introduce small quality diffs for longer contexts. We'll recommend a profile after one more eval.
[04:05] Ravi Kapoor: Any weird network hops? We saw one request route through eu-west even though client origin is us-west, which added 70ms.
[04:16] Jordan Hayes: That was from our routing policy test where traffic steered by cost; looks like a mis-config in the canary rules. Priya will include routing policy that pins by region for the next run.
[04:33] Priya Raman: I'll fold that into the routing config and add explicit region pin for steady-state. Also adding a fallback to a lower-cost model variant to avoid errors when dedicated slots are saturated.
[04:49] Mel: On security, our infosec asked about audit logs retention and KMS integration for private deployment. Is that separate?
[04:58] Evan Cho: I captured that. We sent a compliance pack earlier but Jordan will re-share the short security checklist tonight. For any private/prem deployments we support KMS and audit exports.
[05:15] Carlos Mendez: Great. Let's talk numbers — last week's baseline vs Redwood: p50 similar, p95 about +22ms, p99 about +120ms. Cost per 1k tokens was slightly lower on Redwood but variance hurts UX.
[05:34] Jordan Hayes: Exactly. Our hypothesis — tail is from cold KV + cross-region routing + a few requests hitting smaller GPU class during bursts. If we eliminate those factors we expect p99 to approach incumbent.
[05:50] Dana Liu: For the dedicated run, can we replicate exact token distribution and request concurrency? Incumbent used a 2k concurrency window and a heavy tail.
[06:04] Priya Raman: Yes, when you run the synthetic we need the CSV of request lengths and concurrency schedule. Dana, can you attach that?
[06:13] Dana Liu: I'll do that after the call, yes.
[06:20] Priya Raman: Also note that batching config was conservative — we can increase batch max tokens for short prompts to get better throughput without hurting median latency. I'll propose new batch settings in the config.
[06:35] Ravi Kapoor: Side question — does Redwood have a way to pre-warm the KV cache on deploys? We see p99 spikes after model swaps.
[06:46] Priya Raman: There's a prefix priming hook in the runtime; we can run a controlled warm-up before traffic cutover. We'll document recommended priming sequences for model rollouts.
[07:02] Jordan Hayes: Ok let's go through the action owners quickly. Priya will update routing + batching + fallback. Dana will run the 100k synthetic on incumbent and share results. Ravi will provision dedicated slot. Jordan will share order/security docs. Evan will schedule the mid-pilot readout.
[07:22] Mel: Can you put the expected ROI numbers in the routing doc? Our CFO needs a unit-cost delta with assumptions.
[07:31] Jordan Hayes: We'll include token unit cost delta, expected savings with batching and quantization assumptions.
[07:40] Carlos Mendez: On the prior bench, we also noticed a handful of 5xxs during the 8k spike. Are those timeouts or OOMs?
[07:52] Priya Raman: The traces show timeouts at the proxy layer due to backpressure; not OOMs in the model. We'll add backpressure metrics to the shared dashboard and propose a soft-fail fallback to a lower-latency model to keep user flows alive.
[08:12] Dana Liu: That fallback idea is critical for UX. If the fallback changes output a lot we can't use it, need to test.
[08:22] Priya Raman: Totally — we can A/B the fallback variant on a small percent and run a quality check against your evaluation set.
[08:33] Jordan Hayes: Quick note — we'll also try a KV cache heuristic change: evict larger prefix items sooner to favor hot short prefixes. Might improve p95.
[08:46] Ravi Kapoor: Any instrument changes we need to make on our side?
[08:52] Priya Raman: Add the trace-id header to all synthetic runs and ensure timestamps are synced to NTP. That helps correlate.
[09:02] Carlos Mendez: Ok, timeline? We want the mid-pilot readout next Tuesday.
[09:08] Evan Cho: We'll aim for 2026-04-21 for the readout; Jordan will send invite once the dedicated slot is booked.
[09:16] Mel: One last ask — include the incumbent config we used so it's apples-to-apples.

[09:30] Priya Raman: Great, I'll follow up with routing config and batch proposal. Also including a short explainer about quant profiles.
