Omar El-Sayed: One more: how does this interact with the fix in PR-18428 (stream retries double counting)? Any chance we’re reintroducing a retry path that counts twice because the same segment is retried?
Samir Qureshi (author): I audited the retry path. Retries now carry a new logical attempt_id but the same request_id; however, segment_index is assigned per attempt. In the retry case we want to count attempted_tokens (because we actually did work again) but we must avoid counting reused_tokens as a “hit” when the retry is due to transport. The existing guard from PR-18428 ensures we don’t treat retry-prefill as cache-hit attribution unless the cache layer explicitly reports reuse. I also ensured segment_index increments on a new prefill compute, so metrics reflect real work while staying consistent with hit semantics.
Sofia Ivanova: Can we add a note in the description that this is expected to lower hit-rate in workloads with big batches? SRE will get nervous if graphs change.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added to rollout section + pinged Allison/Sean to expect correction in canary dashboards.
Omar El-Sayed: Approved after test coverage + explanation. Thanks for the detailed breakdown.
Nadia Rahman: Approved. Please make sure downstream dashboards use attempted/reused tokens, not request counts, for hit-rate; otherwise this won’t fix their graphs.
Samir Qureshi (author): Ack. I linked this PR in the dashboard ticket notes and added a short note to the internal metrics README follow-up PR.

title: Private observability: add preflight checks + post-install validation for Prometheus scrapes and Grafana dashboards
content:
Private observability: add preflight checks + post-install validation for Prometheus scrapes and Grafana dashboards

## Summary This PR adds installer-level observability guardrails for Redwood Private installs (VPC + on-prem), focused on the “Private observability minimum pack” rollout. It introduces (1) preflight checks to catch the most common misconfigurations that lead to blank dashboards / missing alerts (storage class, PVC sizing, NetworkPolicy restrictions, resource requests) and (2) a post-install validation step that verifies Prometheus scrapes and Grafana dashboard import succeeded. The goal is to make installs more deterministic for customer platform teams and reduce Support escalations like SUP-49210.

## Motivation / context We’ve seen repeated failures where the installer completes successfully but the observability pack is effectively broken: Prometheus can’t scrape due to restrictive NetworkPolicies, Prometheus/Grafana PVCs can’t bind in customer clusters, or Grafana dashboards never import because the sidecar/loader can’t reach the API. In hosted environments we have stronger environmental guarantees; in Private, the installer should surface actionable guidance before and immediately after install.

## What’s included Preflight checks (new `installer preflight observability` stage, also runs as part of `install` when enabled): - Storage: confirm a writable StorageClass exists (or user supplied `observability.storageClassName`), validate PVC access mode compatibility, validate requested sizes are >= minimums. - Resources: sanity check requests/limits for Prometheus + Grafana + log collector against node allocatable (best-effort; warns if cluster appears undersized). - Networking: detect whether NetworkPolicies are present in the target namespace and (if enabled) validate egress/ingress needed for Prometheus to scrape Redwood services (TCP/metrics ports) and for Grafana to reach Prometheus datasource. - DNS/service reachability: verify Service DNS names resolve from an in-cluster ephemeral pod.

Post-install validation (new `installer validate observability` stage, automatically invoked after successful install when `observability.validation.enabled=true`): - Prometheus: query `/api/v1/targets` and confirm expected jobs are present and up (gateway, control plane services, runtime/serving pods). If Prometheus is not installed/managed by Redwood, validation can be pointed at the customer Prometheus URL (or skipped). - Grafana: verify datasource exists and is healthy; confirm Redwood dashboards are present (by UID prefix) and have non-empty panel queries (basic check). - Output: installer prints a short “what we checked / what failed / what to do next” summary and writes a JSON artifact to the installer workdir for Support attachments.

## Configuration / flags - `observability.preflight.enabled` (default: true when `observability.enabled=true`) - `observability.preflight.mode` = `warn` | `block` (default: `warn`; we block only on missing StorageClass / unbound PVC prereqs when the installer is responsible for provisioning them) - `observability.validation.enabled` (default: true) - `observability.validation.prometheus.url` (optional; for customer-managed Prometheus) - `observability.validation.grafana.url` (optional; for customer-managed Grafana) - `observability.validation.timeoutSeconds` (default: 120)

## Implementation notes - Adds a small in-cluster “validator” Job (`redwood-observability-validator`) that runs with a minimal serviceAccount and uses K8s DNS to reach Prometheus/Grafana Services; avoids requiring the installer host to have network access into the cluster. - Prometheus checks are tolerant to slow startup: we poll targets until timeout and show the set of down targets with `lastError` where available. - Grafana checks use the internal service endpoint + admin creds from the existing secret (when Grafana is installer-managed). For customer-managed Grafana, we require an API token via values and skip dashboard validation if not provided.

## Security / privacy - No request payloads are logged. Validator output is limited to: target/job names, scrape health, HTTP status codes, and high-level errors. - Secrets are not printed; we redact URLs containing credentials and avoid dumping K8s Secret contents. - Added allowlist validation for external URLs to reduce accidental SSRF from misconfiguration.

## Tests - Unit tests for preflight rule evaluation + formatter for failure messages. - Integration test in CI: spins up kind cluster, installs with observability enabled, applies a restrictive NetworkPolicy to reproduce scrape failure, and asserts installer reports the expected actionable message (ENG-19156). - Manual: validated on an internal VPC reference cluster + simulated “customer-managed Prometheus” mode.

## Screenshots / example output (text) - Preflight warn example: `WARN observability/networkpolicy: NetworkPolicies detected in namespace redwood-private; Prometheus may be unable to scrape gateway:9090/metrics. Suggested fix: allow ingress from prometheus to pods with label app=redwood-gateway on port 9090.` - Post-install fail example: `FAIL observability/targets: 3/12 scrape targets down (redwood-runtime, redwood-router, redwood-policy). First error: context deadline exceeded. Suggested fix: verify NetworkPolicy allows prometheus->pods and that metrics port is exposed.`

## Rollout plan - Land behind defaults that are safe: warn-only preflight, post-install validation on by default but non-blocking (installer exit code remains 0; we surface a “validation failed” summary and write artifact). - After a couple of releases + noise review, consider switching specific checks to block in “supported minimum pack” mode.

## Related - Linear: ENG-19153 (preflight), ENG-19156 (smoke tests), PM-842 (minimum pack definition) - Support: SUP-49210 (missing dashboards after install), INT-11804 (CI failing smoke tests)

## Checklist - [x] Adds preflight checks for storage/network/resources - [x] Adds post-install validation for Prometheus scrapes and Grafana dashboards - [x] Safe logging / redaction - [x] CI coverage + kind-based integration test - [x] Docs stub added to installer `--help` + values schema

---

### Commits (squash summary) 1. `installer: add observability preflight framework + rules` 2. `installer: add in-cluster observability validator job` 3. `installer: implement prometheus targets validation` 4. `installer: implement grafana datasource + dashboard validation` 5. `ci: add kind test for networkpolicy scrape failures` 6. `docs: expose new observability preflight/validation flags`

### Changed areas / files (high level) - `cmd/redwood-private-installer/main.go` (wire new stages + flags) - `pkg/preflight/observability/*.go` (storage/network/resources rules) - `pkg/validate/observability/*.go` (prometheus/grafana validators) - `charts/private-installer/templates/validator-job.yaml` (new Job + RBAC) - `charts/private-installer/values.yaml` + `values.schema.json` (new config) - `ci/kind/private_observability_validation_test.sh` (integration coverage)

---

## Review conversation (highlights) **Allison Grant (requested changes):** The network preflight reads like it will block installs when NetworkPolicies exist. We need to be explicit that this is warn-only by default and avoid false positives (some customers pre-allow via namespace selectors). Also please align wording with our alert severity taxonomy (warn/block). **Diego Santos (author):** Updated defaults to `mode=warn`, added a note that we only block on definite provisioning prerequisites (StorageClass/PVC binding) when installer-managed. Also adjusted messaging to “detected NetworkPolicies; cannot determine allow rules reliably; here are common required allowances” and linked to the runbook stub.

**Rafael Mendes:** Post-install validation should not fail the whole install. Support wants an artifact they can ask customers for. Can we always write a JSON summary? **Diego Santos:** Yep — added `observability-validation-report.json` written to the installer workdir + referenced in stdout. Installer exits 0 unless core install failed.

**Marcus Lin:** Please ensure we don’t allow arbitrary URLs for customer-managed Prometheus/Grafana without guardrails (SSRF risk if installer runs with elevated network access). **Diego Santos:** Added URL allowlist (scheme must be http/https, no userinfo, no link-local IPs, no RFC1918 bypass unless explicitly allowed via `observability.validation.allowPrivateCIDRs=true`). Also validation is in-cluster by default so blast radius is limited to the cluster network.

**Logan Wright:** Target matching: relying on job names might drift as we refactor metrics. Prefer label-based matching or a small set of stable job names. **Diego Santos:** Switched to a two-step approach: (1) assert Prometheus is reachable and has any targets, (2) check that targets exist for a stable list of `app.kubernetes.io/part-of=redwood-private` scrape endpoints, and treat missing component targets as WARN unless `supportedMinimum=true`.

**Dylan Brooks:** Grafana dashboard validation shouldn’t require panel evaluation; it’s expensive and fragile. Just confirm dashboards are present + datasource is healthy. **Diego Santos:** Agreed; reduced panel query checks to a lightweight “dashboard JSON contains datasource ref” sanity check; removed render/panel eval.

Approvals: - Allison Grant: Approved after messaging/defaults changes - Rafael Mendes: Approved (requested artifact + non-blocking) - Marcus Lin: Approved after SSRF guardrails - Dylan Brooks: Approved

---

## CI - `build` ✅ - `unit-tests` ✅ - `lint` ✅ - `kind-private-install` ✅ - `kind-private-observability-validation` ✅ (added)

Merge: Squash merged by Diego Santos into `main`.

title: Add SLO→Customer Impact Classifier & Remediation Workflow doc (v2 scoring + updated comms)
content:
Add SLO→Customer Impact Classifier & Remediation Workflow doc (v2 scoring + updated comms)

Context
We have an internal Confluence page describing the SLO→customer impact tier classifier and the remediation workflow. That page is being referenced during incidents, but the operational details have drifted since the enrichment pipeline shipped score weighting changes (v2) and CS escalation timing was tightened after SUP-19344.

This PR adds the canonical doc to the slo-toolkit repo so it can be versioned alongside the classifier code and reviewed via normal PR workflows. The majority of the content mirrors the Confluence page, but includes the v2 scoring thresholds and updated templates.

What changed (summary)
- Keep: tier definitions (1–4), overall workflow (alert→enrich→score→tier→remediate), evidence retention requirements, and post-incident/error budget reconciliation flow.
- Update: score mapping thresholds (v2), add confidence gating and a human-review fallback, update Tier 1 comms SLA (10 min), and reduce Tier 4 auto-escalation window (4 hours).
- Update: SLO catalog excerpt targets to match current baselines; add explicit note that targets are examples and owners must use the live SLO registry as source of truth.
- Update: capacity knobs table to reflect current CLI commands and pool naming.

Doc content (added under docs/incident-response/)

Title: SLO to Customer Impact Classifier and Remediation Workflow

Overview
This document defines a reproducible classifier that maps SLO signals to a customer-impact tier and a prescriptive remediation workflow. It is intended to: align SRE, Product, and Customer Success during SLO degradations; minimize time-to-customer-remediation; and create consistent inputs for post-incident reviews and error-budget decisions.

Audience
- On-call SREs
- SRE leads and managers
- Incident commanders (ICs)
- Customer Success (CS) and Support for high-impact incidents

Principles
1) Tie every SLO alert to an explicit customer-impact tier (1–4).
2) Automate low-friction routing and remediation for common degradations.
3) Escalate proactively for any Tier 1/2 customer impact.
4) Preserve evidence for postmortems and error-budget reconciliations.

Definitions
- SLO: Service Level Objective (e.g., request_latency_p95 <= 250ms).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO target over the defined rolling window.
- Customer-impact tier: a 1–4 classification used to route and prioritize incident response.

Customer-impact tiers (quick guide)
| Tier | User-visible symptoms | Business effect | Escalation urgency | Owner to notify |
|------|----------------------|-----------------|-------------------|----------------|
| 1 | Multi-region outage OR widespread request failures OR sustained elevated error rate affecting a large portion of traffic | Severe revenue/customer retention impact | Immediate (page) | SRE lead + Product PM + CS Director |
| 2 | Single-region outage, or large subset of customers impacted (major tenants) or major feature down | Significant business disruption for key customers | High (page + slack) | SRE oncall + Product owner + CS manager |
| 3 | Localized errors, degraded latency for non-critical endpoints | Minor customer annoyance, limited support tickets | Medium (slack alert) | On-call SRE + Feature owner |
| 4 | Minor latency increase or transient errors with no customer tickets | No immediate business impact | Low (ticket) | On-call SRE |

SLO catalog excerpt (example mapping; owners must confirm in live SLO registry)
| SLO name | Metric | Target | Error-budget window | Default customer-impact tier |
|----------|--------|--------|--------------------|--------------------------|
| request_latency_p95_public | request_latency_p95{route=~"/v1/.*"} | <= 250ms | 30d | 2 |
| api_error_rate_5m | sum(rate(api_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) | <= 0.5% | 7d | 1 |
| embedding_throughput_tail | embedding_infer_latency_p99 | < 1.4s | 14d | 3 |
| console_ui_availability | synthetic_check(console_login) | 99.7% monthly | 30d | 3 |

Classification algorithm (operational)
1) Alert receives telemetry: detector alerts on SLI breach or error-budget burn (alerting config).
2) Metrics enrichment: pull impact signals (affected tenant count, region distribution, top N tenants by RPS, open support tickets matching pattern).
3) Heuristics engine evaluates scores (0–100): failure-scope, severity, customer-exposure.
4) Confidence gating (v2): compute confidence (0–100) based on completeness/consistency of enrichment inputs. If confidence < 50, do not auto-upgrade beyond Tier 3; route to on-call for manual triage and re-run enrichment after 5 minutes.
5) Combined score maps to Tier (v2 thresholds): Score >= 85 -> Tier 1; 70–84 -> Tier 2; 35–69 -> Tier 3; < 35 -> Tier 4.
6) Attach classification + confidence to incident and follow the tiered remediation workflow below.

Heuristics inputs (examples)
- affected_tenant_ratio: percent of total tenant RPS impacted.
- p95_latency_delta: percent change vs baseline.
- error_rate_delta: absolute change in error rate vs baseline (preferred over p99_error_spike for API).
- active_cs_tickets: number of open tickets tagged /inference or /api.
- region_blast_radius: number of regions with concurrent impact.

Operational remediations by tier
Tier 1 (Immediate response)
- Page the SRE oncall and SRE lead (PagerDuty service: customer-impact).
- Open an incident in the incident-management system using template tag=CUSTOMER_IMPACT_TIER_1 (auto-created if classifier confidence >= 70).
- Run mitigation playbook: fallback-to-compatible-model-variant.
- If capacity-related: trigger immediate capacity burst policy (see CLI below).
- Notify CS and Product leadership within 10 minutes with templated Slack/Jira.

Tier 2 (High-priority)
- Page on-call (high urgency) and post to #incidents.
- Execute targeted throttles or tenant fair-share configuration.
- Begin canary rollback of recent model or config changes (if correlated).

Tier 3 (Operational handling)
- Create ticket and schedule on-call investigation within 30–60 minutes.
- Apply mitigations from the runbook: restart worker pool, clear KV cache, or disable newly-deployed feature flag.

Tier 4 (Monitoring)
- Monitor metrics and let automated remediation run. If unresolved after SLA window (4 hours), escalate to Tier 3.

Sample alert rule (Prometheus-style YAML)
alert: HighAPIErrorRate
expr: sum(rate(api_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) > 0.005
for: 2m
labels: severity: page impact: "possible-customer-impact"
annotations: summary: "API error rate >0.5% over 5m" runbook: "https://confluence.internal/s/reliability/runbooks/api-error-rate-mitigation"

Enrichment query examples (pseudo-SQL / analytics)
- Tenants affected in last 10m: SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 50;
- Support ticket correlation: count tickets where created_at >= now()-10m AND tags IN ('api','inference')

Capacity escalation knobs (examples)
| Trigger | Condition | Automated action | Escalation threshold |
|---------|-----------|------------------|----------------------|
| headroom_exhausted | available_gpu_slots < 7% | trigger-burst-alloc --pool=shared-burst-v2 | immediate (Tier1) |
| model_warm_pool_empty | warm_pool_size < configured_min | scale warm pool by +2 nodes | Tier2 |
| p95_latency_spike | p95 > baseline*1.6 for 10m | enable-prefetch-kv-cache=true | Tier2 |

CLI examples
- Trigger burst capacity (operators only): rcmd infra capacity burst apply --pool shared-burst-v2 --reason "Tier1 SLO breach" --expires 30m
- Re-route traffic to fallback models: rcmd infra routing promote --from model-xyz-v2 --to model-xyz-v1 --weight 100

Communication templates
Slack template (Tier1)
- Channel: #incidents
- Message: [Tier 1 SLO breach] api_error_rate_5m at 1.2% impacting ~32% of tenant RPS across 2 regions. IC: @oncall. Mitigation in progress: promoting fallback routing. Please notify CS lead @renee.zhao. Incident: <INCIDENT_URL>

Jira template fields
- Priority: P0 for Tier1, P1 for Tier2, P2 for Tier3/4
- Components: runtime, routing, capacity, product-feature
- Labels: slo-breach, customer-impact-tier-<n>, automated-enrichment, classifier-v2

Post-incident / Error-budget reconciliation
1) Add classification evidence (metrics, tenant list, tickets) to the incident story.
2) Compute error-budget consumption attributable to the incident window.
3) For Tier1/Tier2 incidents: schedule a joint SRE/Product/CS triage within 72 hours. The triage determines whether to take a governance action (e.g., customer credits, temporary throttle, emergency capacity commit).
4) Document remediation plan and assign owners with due dates.

Postmortem checklist (to include in incident review)
- Summary of classifier result (tier + confidence) and whether the initial tier matched customer reports.
- Timeline of detection -> mitigation -> recovery.
- Root cause and contributing factors including capacity and SLO misconfigurations.
- Action items (owner + due date) and follow-up on error-budget policy.
- Evidence attachments: metrics, logs, enrichment query results.

Automation and operational tooling notes
- The classifier runs in the telemetry enrichment pipeline (owner: telemetry-team). Inputs are Prometheus alerts, request traces, and support ticket API.
- All automated classification decisions must be auditable: store computed scores, confidence, and input summaries in incident metadata.
- Confidence gating exists to prevent false Tier 1/2 upgrades when enrichment is degraded (e.g., ticket API latency, tenant-mapping lag).

Ownership and governance
- SLO owner: Each SLO must list a primary owner (SRE or Product) and a secondary owner. Owners are responsible for maintaining mapping in the SLO registry and ensuring this doc stays consistent.

title: Introduce consensus-backed migration lock + operator pauser for safe in-place schema transforms
content:
Introduce consensus-backed migration lock + operator pauser for safe in-place schema transforms

Problem: Private deployments performing in-place schema changes or operator-driven upgrades can race (multiple CI/CD runs, manual operator actions, or automated patchers) which leads to partially-applied migrations and mismatched tenant state. We need a robust guard that: 1) prevents concurrent migrations across controller replicas and automation runs, 2) provides an operator-level pause to quiesce requests for targeted tenants during a migration window, and 3) verifies that pre-upgrade backups are intact and restorable before allowing schema application.

This PR introduces a consensus-backed migration lock (based on the cluster's etcd/consensus layer where available, falling back to a tenant-scoped leader election CRD) and an operator pauser that quiesces inbound tenant traffic during schema transforms. It also wires a preflight backup verifier that computes and records checksum manifests for logical PostgreSQL dumps before migrations proceed. The goal is safe in-place schema transforms with deterministic, reversible steps and clear operator controls.

Changes: single continuous description of what was done (checklist): 
- implement a MigrationLock CRD and controller that acquires a cluster-scoped consensus lease with retry/backoff and TTL metadata
- add a TenantQuiesce subcontroller that annotates ingress proxies (helm chart hook) and toggles a feature-flag on the operator to pause new requests for a tenant during the migration window
- add a migration preflight command to the installer CLI: `installer migrate --tenant <id> --dry-run/--apply --backup-checksum <auto|path>`
- wire automatic logical backup creation (pg_dump) into the migrate flow and record checksum + object path in BackupManifest CRD
- add a `migration.dry_run=true` path that executes schema transformations in a sandbox (helm test job) and reports a rollout readiness score
- introduce terraform module inputs for `migration_lock_ttl` and `operator_pause_grace_seconds` and document defaults
- Helm chart: add pre-upgrade hook that waits for MigrationLock and runs the backup verifier, and a post-failure hook that triggers an automatic unlock with a diagnostic bundle
- add metrics (migration_lock_acquired_total, backup_verification_status) and tracing spans for the lock lifecycle
- tests: unit tests for lock backoff, e2e test using a two-controller race scenario, and a restore smoke test that validates checksum match after a simulated restore

Commits: [summaries] 
- feat(migration): add MigrationLock CRD + controller with TTL and renewals
- feat(operator): add TenantQuiesce controller and operator pause flag
- feat(installer): add `migrate` CLI flow, backup verifier and checksum manifest wiring
- feat(helm): helm hooks for pre-upgrade backup-check and post-failure diagnostics
- tf(migration): terraform inputs and docs for migration lock config
- test(e2e): race-condition e2e harness and restore smoke test
- chore: docs and README updates for private-installer migration flow

Files changed (high level):
- chart/private-installer/templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-backup-check.yaml (new helm pre-upgrade hook that blocks until backup verification passes)
- api/v1/migrationlock_types.go, controllers/migrationlock_controller.go (CRD + controller)
- controllers/tenantquiesce_controller.go (operator-pauser logic)
- cli/installer/cmd/migrate.go (installer migrate CLI + flags)
- docs/migration-runbook.md (runbook for operators + rollback steps)
- terraform/modules/installer/variables.tf (migration_lock_ttl, operator_pause_grace_seconds)
- tests/e2e/migration_race_test.go, tests/e2e/restore_smoke_test.go

Migration flow and rollback plan (operator runbook summary):
1) Run `installer migrate --tenant T123 --dry-run` to exercise the dry-run path. The dry-run creates a namespaced sandbox job in the cluster and reports schema diffs and a readiness score.
2) Create a pre-upgrade backup via `installer migrate --tenant T123 --run-backup` (this is automatic if `--run-backup` not suppressed). The BackupManifest CRD will contain checksum and signed metadata (GPG optional).
3) Acquire the MigrationLock (controller will attempt consensus lease). If lock acquisition fails, operator may retry or abort; UI surfaces owner and TTL.
4) Operator toggles TenantQuiesce; ingress will start returning 503 for new session requests for the target tenant while allowing inflight requests to drain within `operator_pause_grace_seconds`.
5) Apply schema transforms. The helm pre-upgrade hook ensures the backup-check passed before hitting migrations.
6) On success, release MigrationLock and unquiesce the tenant.
7) On failure or timeout, the post-failure hook collects diagnostics, performs an automatic unlock (with TTL), and can optionally trigger a restore job using the BackupManifest. The runbook includes steps for manual failback when automatic restore is insufficient.

Testing and verification notes: 
- e2e race test simulates two parallel migrators and asserts that only one succeeds and the other receives a clear backoff error + owner metadata.
- restore_smoke_test verifies that BackupManifest checksum can be fetched and used to validate a restored dump; smoke test runs pg_restore in a sandbox and compares row counts for a sample table.
- Unit tests cover TTL expiry, renewals, and operator pause grace period.
- CI: initial runs failed on a flaky race in the e2e harness (timing assumptions around controller leader election). I adjusted the harness backoff and added a deterministic latch; rerun passed (CI status: pass).

Review conversation (summary): 
- Jonah Keene: "This general approach looks good. Two asks: 1) show how we avoid lockholder loss on controller restart (lease renewal semantics), 2) ensure BackupManifest is immutable once created to avoid TOCTOU on restore."
- Ava (author): "Added deterministic renewals and a manifest immutability controller check that rejects updates after creation. See controller tests in migrationlock_controller_test.go and backupmanifest_immutability_test.go."
- Priya Desai: "Operator pauser is needed but we should make the ingress quiesce pluggable for on-prem customers who use different proxies."
- Ava: "Pauser is implemented as an interface with a default implementation for our nginx/ambassador overlays; added a `QuiesceProvider` interface and docs for implementing custom providers."
- Luca Moretti: "Terraform defaults look sane; recommend exposing `migration_lock_namespace` for constrained clusters."
- Ava: "Added `migration_lock_namespace` with default `redwood-system` and documented implications for multi-tenant clusters."
- Jonah: "Approve after a small nits patch to improve logging on lock acquisition failure."
- Ava: "Addressed logging nits in the last commit."

CI and gating: 
- Unit: pass
- Integration: pass
- E2E: initially fail, rerun pass
- Lint/docs: pass

Release notes: "Add consensus-backed MigrationLock and TenantQuiesce operator to improve safety for in-place schema changes. Adds installer `migrate` flow with automatic backups and checksum verification, a Helm pre-upgrade backup check hook, and Terraform knobs for migration tuning."

Notes for operators/upgrade owners: 
- This change is additive and opt-in; `migrate` is only invoked by operator action or explicit installer CLI. Default config will not quiesce tenants unless `--quiesce`/`operator_pause` is enabled.
- Recommended rollout: apply helm chart update to a staging cluster, exercise `--dry-run` for a representative tenant, validate BackupManifest and restore smoke test, then flip to `--apply` on production tenants during a low-traffic window.
- Observability: migration_lock_acquired_total and backup_verification_status show up in the operator metrics group; dashboard and alert playbooks added to docs/migration-runbook.md.

Related work: ENG-3421 (migration safety redesign), ENG-3498 (installer CLI improvements), SUPPORT ticket SUP-1182 (customer reported partial migration during previous hotfix).
Jonah Keene: 'This general approach looks good. Two asks: show how we avoid lockholder loss on controller restart and ensure BackupManifest is immutable.'
Ava Martinez: 'Added deterministic renewals and a manifest immutability controller check; tests added.'
Priya Desai: 'Make ingress quiesce pluggable for on-prem customers.'
Ava Martinez: 'QuiesceProvider interface added with docs for custom providers.'
Luca Moretti: 'Recommend exposing migration_lock_namespace for constrained clusters.'
Ava Martinez: 'Added migration_lock_namespace; updated terraform docs.'
Jonah Keene: 'Approve after logging nits.'
Ava Martinez: 'Addressed nits in final commit.'
CI: 'E2E failed on first run due to harness timing; rerun passed.'
Add consensus-backed MigrationLock and TenantQuiesce operator for safer in-place schema changes; installer migrate flow with automatic backup+checksum verification; Helm pre-upgrade hook to block until backup is verified; Terraform knobs for migration tuning.
This PR is intentionally conservative: default behavior is opt-in. Operators should exercise dry-run flow and the restore smoke test before enabling auto-apply in production. The MigrationLock falls back to a namespaced leader election when a cluster consensus store is unavailable.

title: Turnstile safety lane with snapshot quarantine and synthetic-smoke bridge for incremental ABs
content:
Turnstile safety lane with snapshot quarantine and synthetic-smoke bridge for incremental ABs

Context: Teams asked for a lightweight, auditable safety lane to introduce tiny A/B fractions and shadow rehearsals without risking full commit traffic. This PR implements a 'turnstile' safety lane: an opt-in side-path in the rollout runtime that holds traffic in a quarantine snapshot, runs synthetic-smoke rehearsals and an observation-driven gate before any traffic is promoted. Motivation: existing staged rollouts either fully shadow (no live validation) or promote trivially; we needed a middle ground that provides deterministic snapshotting, reproducible replays, and automated backout hooks when smoke or live metrics diverge. High level: 1) snapshot-quarantine: capture deterministic request slice and KV snapshot at rollout start and keep it isolated for replay/smoke; 2) synthetic-smoke-bridge: exercise the candidate model with engineered synthetic prompts representative of targeted cohorts plus a small randomized sampling of live traffic to surface regressions early; 3) incremental-ab-toggle: support fractional AB toggles driven by telemetry confidence rather than fixed timers; 4) auto-backout-agent: automated rollback when metric envelopes exceed configured thresholds or when smoke-run asserts fail. Implementation details: added a new TurnstileController in rollout/orchestrator that coordinates snapshot creation and lease-based quarantine; stores snapshot metadata in /orchestrator/snapshots service; integrates with the existing telemetry scorer to compute a confidence score (weighted latency + reply-coherence + safety-checks). The synthetic-smoke-bridge is implemented as a lightweight harness that can run in parallel to live shadowing; it supports custom smoke sets per-Linear task and records diffs to the smoke ledger. The incremental AB toggle uses a token-fraction allocator that permits deterministic seeding for reproducible experiments. Rollback hooks include an idempotent revert plan that triggers a graceful drain of promoted lanes and promotes an observational rollback snapshot for offline analysis. Testing: unit tests for TurnstileController lease logic and snapshot lifecycle; integration tests that simulate snapshot capture, smoke bridge runs, and automated backout flow; e2e rehearsal on staging with a 0.5% AB using the redwood/bench harness. Performance: isolated smoke runs target sub-10ms wall time per synthetic prompt in the harness; added opt-out feature to bypass smoke bridge for emergency hotfixes. Migration and config: new rolloutPolicy.turnstile object in deployment manifests with fields: snapshotWindowMs, smokeSetRef, initialFraction, confidenceThresholds, maxGraceRevertSecs. Defaults are conservative. Backwards compatibility: feature is opt-in; existing rollouts unchanged. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag rollout.turnstile.enabled; pilot with internal infra and one customer on Dedicated for two weeks; monitor the telemetry confidence trace and SLO alerts. Related Linear: ENG-12890 (turnstile design), ENG-12912 (smoke bridge harness), PM-457 (customer pilot). Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by infra and SRE - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] staged e2e rehearsal completed on staging - [x] telemetry dashboards updated - [x] runbook and rollback playbook authored in /docs/runbooks/turnstile.md Commits summary: 1) add TurnstileController skeleton and snapshot APIs 2) implement synthetic-smoke-harness and smoke ledger 3) integrate telemetry confidence scorer and fractional allocator 4) add migration docs and rolloutPolicy schema 5) test and fix lease race conditions 6) add runbook and dashboards. Files changed (high level): ["orchestrator/turnstile_controller.go","orchestrator/snapshots/store.go","telemetry/confidence_scorer.go","tools/smoke/harness.go","api/rollouts/schema.yaml","docs/runbooks/turnstile.md","test/integration/turnstile_replay_test.go","charts/values-rollout.yaml"]. CI summary: initial lint failed due to schema validation; fixed, reran, full test matrix green. Review conversation summary: - Evan Cole: "Nice separation between snapshot lifecycle and promotion. Two nits: make snapshot metadata non-blocking for long requests, and add metrics for snapshot size." Author reply: "Addressed: metadata write is now async, added snapshot.size_bytes and snapshot.request_count gauges." - Rita Singh: "Concern about synthetic smoke coverage vs cost; can we cap per-minute smoke tokens?" Author reply: "Added smokeRateLimiter and default of 100 tokens/min, configurable via smokeSetRef." - Jasper Li: "Approval pending CI green and runbook link." Author reply: "CI green, runbook link added at docs/runbooks/turnstile.md, ready for squash merge." CI Checks: ["golangci-lint: pass","unit-tests: pass","integration-tests: pass","e2e-staging: pass","schema-check: pass"]. Merge: merged by Rita Singh via squash and merge. Merge details: "Squash merge into main with PR title preserved; generated merge commit includes compacted changelog and runbook link." Merged at: "2026-02-18" Release notes: "Introduces an opt-in 'Turnstile' safety lane for rollouts that provides snapshot quarantine, synthetic smoke rehearsals, and automated rollback triggers. Enabled via rolloutPolicy.turnstile config. Intended for teams that need reproducible pre-promotion validation and deterministic replay. Requires feature flag rollout.turnstile.enabled."

title: Audit log pipeline dashboards + alerts (ingestion latency, drop rate) with runbook links
content:
Audit log pipeline dashboards + alerts (ingestion latency, drop rate) with runbook links

Context: As part of the audit logging standardization effort we’re tightening operational visibility for the audit event ingestion/export path. We’ve had a couple of near-misses where ingestion lag spiked without a clear on-call landing page, and early alert drafts lacked enough context to triage quickly.

This PR adds:
- A Grafana dashboard for the audit-log ingestion pipeline (end-to-end delivery latency, ingest backlog, drop rate, retry/429/5xx, DLQ growth).
- Alert rules for delivery latency and drop rate with sane defaults + per-environment routing.
- Runbook links embedded in alert annotations and dashboard panel descriptions.

Key signals / definitions:
- delivery_latency_seconds: time from event emission at producer to ack at ingestion sink (measured via audit-ingest gateway metrics + exporter timestamps).
- drop_rate: fraction of events not successfully delivered after retry budget (from ingest and exporter counters).
- backlog: queued events in buffer (when enabled) + ingestion consumer lag.

Alert thresholds (initial):
- AuditLogDeliveryLatencyP99High: p99(delivery_latency_seconds) > 60s for 10m (page: enterprise tiers; ticket: others).
- AuditLogDropRateHigh: drop_rate > 0.10% for 5m (page; includes per-region breakdown).
- AuditLogIngestBacklogGrowing: backlog > 50k AND increasing for 15m (ticket; pages if > 200k).

Cardinality guardrails:
- Dashboard panels group primarily by region, deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), and service. We intentionally do not group by raw tenant_id/project_id. event_type is only used in a single table panel with top-N + allow-listed types.

Runbooks:
- Incident runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/audit-log-pipeline-incident-runbook.json
- Coverage regression runbook is linked from the dashboard “Coverage” row for follow-up when events are missing but pipeline is healthy.

Testing:
- jsonnetfmt + dashboards render in CI.
- promtool rules tests added for the new alert expressions.

Notes:
- This is intended to be the “default landing page” linked from paging alerts. We can iterate thresholds after a week of production data; see INT-3984 for noise tuning follow-ups.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Thresholds look OK but we should avoid paging on backlog alone. Can we gate backlog alert on backlog increasing + delivery latency elevated?

title: Introduce onboarding heuristic ranker and summarized release creator
content:
Introduce onboarding heuristic ranker and summarized release creator

Context and motivation: model intake currently produces raw metadata and full performance profiles but lacks a lightweight, deterministic ranking that helps reviewers prioritize which model versions to certify first. When dozens of candidate variants appear (quantized, distilled, quant+distill), reviewers need a concise, evidence-backed suggestion plus an initial release blurb. This PR adds a small, pluggable heuristic ranker and a summarized release-note generator that drafts short changelog entries tied to onboarding artifacts.

Design: The ranker assigns a score computed from three weighted signals: stability_score (based on rollout probe pass rate), coverage_score (how many canonical workloads the model hit during preflight), and cost_estimate (tokens/sec and quantization hint). We expose a config object for weights so platform teams can tune heuristics per workspace. The summarizer consumes ranked artifacts and: - extracts the top-3 contributing changes (e.g. quantization, sequence-length tuning, prompt-template hints), - generates a 2-3 sentence release blurb with deterministic templates, - attaches a small Impact badge (latency delta and cost delta). The summarizer is intentionally conservative: drafts are marked "DRAFT: auto" and require human sign-off in the console.

What changed (summary of commits): commit 1: add ranker module and unit tests; commit 2: add summarizer and integration tests; commit 3: add CLI preview tool and docs; commit 4: wire into release assembler and CI workflow; commit 5: fix edge-case where coverage_score==0 and add guard rails.

Files / key diffs: registry/intake/ranker.py  (new) - core Ranker class with compute_score(metadata, perf_profile) -> float. Sample snippet: def compute_score(meta, perf):
    stability = min(meta.get('probe_pass_rate', 0.0), 1.0)
    coverage = perf.get('workload_coverage', 0) / float(MAX_WORKLOADS)
    cost = max(1e-6, perf.get('estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens', 0.0))
    score = weights['stability'] * stability + weights['coverage'] * coverage - weights['cost'] * math.log(cost + 1.0)
    return round(score, 4)

registry/release/summarizer.py (new) - small template engine with deterministic slot filling and a safety layer preventing PII or long free-text passthrough. CLI: cli/onboard_preview.py (new) - preview a model's ranked entry and summarizer blurb locally before pushing. Docs: docs/onboarding/heuristics.md - explains config knobs and when to tune weights. CI: workflow/ci.yml updated to run summarizer integration tests in the release stage.

Testing and CI: Unit tests for ranker cover corner cases (zero coverage, absent probe_metrics). Integration test simulates a small intake pipeline with two candidate variants and asserts the summarizer produces consistent drafts. CI initially failed on the e2e integration due to a mock secrets race; I added a retry in the test harness and updated the workflow to use isolated ephemeral buckets for test artifacts. Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e).

Review conversation (high-level single-string aggregation): Marco Nguyen: "Nice incremental approach. Two asks: (1) make weight config pluggable per-organization; (2) add guardrail to avoid creating a release blurb for variants with <50% probe coverage."
Aisha (author): "Both addressed: added org-level config and a coverage threshold check in summarizer that tags drafts as 'insufficient telemetry' if below threshold."
Dana Sokol: "Can we include a concise sample of the generated blurb in the docs?"
Aisha: "Added examples in docs/onboarding/heuristics.md and the CLI prints a preview sample."
Priya Raman: "Unit tests look good. Please add a changelog entry for the release assembler wiring."
Aisha: "Added a small CHANGELOG fragment and a README note; moved the release assembler step to a named hook so downstream consumers can opt-in."

Backward-compatibility and risks: There are no changes to public REST APIs. The ranker and summarizer run as part of the internal intake pipeline; teams who relied on the previous purely manual review flow will now see auto-drafts — they must opt-in to auto-publishing. The main risk is over-reliance on heuristic scores; mitigations: conservative defaults, prominently labelled drafts, and per-org weight overrides.

Operational notes: Added a feature flag onboarding.heuristic_ranker.enabled=false by default; rollout plan: enable for 25% of orgs w/ high-throughput onboarding for two weeks, gather feedback, then increase. Metrics added: onboarding.rank_score histogram, summarizer.draft_generated_count, summarizer.draft_signoff_rate. Alerts: summarizer.error_rate > 1% triggers pager.

Follow-ups (future work): (1) add ML-backed ranker trained on historical signoffs; (2) allow customizable natural-language templates per org; (3) surface draft signoff analytics in the Console.

Merge notes: this PR was squashed on merge, changelog fragment included in commit message. Merge method: squash and merge.
Adds a heuristic scoring stage to the model intake pipeline that ranks candidate onboarding artifacts by stability, telemetry coverage, and estimated cost-per-token. Produces condensed release note drafts per model version and wires them into the release assembler. No public API changes.

Highlights: heuristic scoring config (pluggable), summarized changelog autodrafts, small CLI to preview release blurbs, unit + integration tests.

title: Introduce Budget Marshal: mini-scheduler, quota-sipper, and quant-compat deprecation policy
content:
Introduce Budget Marshal: mini-scheduler, quota-sipper, and quant-compat deprecation policy

Motivation: Many tenants run with conservative batching/caching defaults that waste budget on short interactive flows. This PR introduces the Budget Marshal subsystem: a lightweight tenant-aware mini-scheduler plus a quota-sipper admission controller and a quant-compat deprecation policy to automate safe, unit-economics-driven defaults. Goals are to reduce per-token cost for interactive workloads, provide safe automated rollouts of compact quant profiles, and surface unit-econ signals for ops and product to tune tenant defaults. Summary of changes: 1) mini-scheduler service: a low-latency scheduler that runs in the prefilling path and groups short, affinity-friendly requests into micro-lanes. It supports policy knobs for max-lane-wait-ms, tenant-priority, and cost-target-per-token. 2) quota-sipper admission controller: enforces a soft quota budget per-session that preferentially routes requests into cheaper lanes (microbatch + prefix-caching) when the tenant is on a budget tier. It exposes an API for console overrides. 3) quant-compat deprecation policy: catalog metadata and rollout rules for quant profiles (q4/q8/q6) including a compatibility probe stage, safety rollback thresholds (quality regression > 2% on eval set) and automatic fallback to higher-precision variants. 4) unit-econ telemetry tags: emits token-cost-estimate, lane-type, and prefill-hit-rate tags to tracing and metrics; a new telemetry bridge aggregates per-tenant daily unit-econ snapshots. 5) CLI and defaults-as-code: add budget-marshal CLI that can dry-run tenant defaults and export recommended compact quant profiles as a policy bundle. 6) Tests and canary: synthetic microbench harness plus perf canary job to verify latency and unit-econ regression tolerances. Backwards compatibility and safety: default behavior is opt-in via tenant flag budget_marshal.enabled=false; quant deprecation requires explicit linear ticket and approval to enable for a tenant. The quota-sipper uses soft quotas with graceful degradation — requests never get dropped by the subsystem itself, only routed to non-compact lanes when budgets are exhausted. Rollout plan: staged canary on internal staging tenants, then 5% production traffic with monitoring dashboard and automated rollback if unit-econ delta or latency p95 increases beyond configured thresholds. Checklist: - [x] mini-scheduler core impl - [x] admission controller + API - [x] telemetry tags + bridge - [x] CLI + policy export - [x] unit/e2e tests and perf canary - [x] docs and console feature flag - [x] Linear tickets linked Related work: builds on ENG-1732 (prefill cache API), borrows tracer semantics from ENG-1987 (telemetry bridge), and complements ENG-2123 (tenant defaults CLI). How to test locally: run ./dev/mini_sched --simulate-profile small-interactive and run the canary harness scripts in tools/prefill-sim/ README contains sample commands and expected metrics. Small snippet of policy bundle (example): {"budget_target": "0.002/token", "preferred_quant": "q4_0", "compat_probe_percent": "10"}
Ethan Cole: Overall design looks solid. A few concerns: scheduler fairness across tenants and memory pressure when micro-lanes accumulate — please add a per-node lane-cap and eviction policy.

title: ephemeral throttle harmonizer and standby drain probe (SLO smoothing + hotfix)
content:
ephemeral throttle harmonizer and standby drain probe (SLO smoothing + hotfix)

Context and motivation:
This PR implements an SLO-focused admission smoothing layer (ephemeral throttle harmonizer) and a small but critical standby drain probe that prevents mass KV cache drains during regional failover. We shipped a small change to circuit reopen logic to stop rapid flip-flops observed under surge conditions (root cause seen in recent incident SUP-3321). Goal is: reduce tenant-level oscillation, protect downstream serving nodes from simultaneous heavy KV work, and provide richer telemetry so on-call can reason about reopen events.

What it changes (high level):
- runtime/admission/harmonizer.go: new SLO-aware harmonizer that aggregates short-term token usage and produces a smoothed per-tenant admission score. Uses exponential smoothing with configurable alpha and a soft cap window; integrates with existing admission API.
- runtime/drain/standby_probe.go: probe that runs during region-standby transitions; verifies KV cache health and delays non-critical drains until probe passes or soft timeout.
- runtime/circuit/reopen_guard.go: per-tenant cooldown (backoff multiplier + jitter) to avoid reopen flapping; records reopen_reason and reopen_attempts into telemetry.
- operator/helm/templates/configmap.yaml: new config knobs to tune harmonizer alpha, probe timeout, and reopen cooldown values.
- tools/eval/promptset_stability.yaml: test harness additions to simulate bursty tenant traffic and verify harmonizer behavior.
- docs/observability/reopen-telemetry.md: docs for the new telemetry fields and alert guidance.
- release/2026-02-hotfix/*: minimal backport for release branch with opt-in flags.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for harmonizer smoothing and timeout behavior.
- [x] Integration scenario in eval harness that reproduces incident-like oscillation and demonstrates improvement.
- [x] Added metrics/traces and dashboard snippets for reopen events.
- [x] Backported opt-in hotfix for release channel and documented escape hatch.
- [x] SRE review and oncall runbook entry drafted.

Commits (summary):
- c1a2b3f: initial harmonizer implementation and basic tests
- d4e5f6a: add standby drain probe and integrate with region state transitions
- f7a8b9c: reopen cooldown + telemetry fields; update dashboards
- a1b2c3d: helm chart knobs + backport to release branch
- b2c3d4e: test harness scenarios and flaky-test fixes

Files changed (high level list):

Review conversation (selected):
- Samir Patel (reviewer): "This addresses the production flip-flop we've seen. Two asks: 1) add a metric for harmonizer smoothing lag so SRE can detect stuck state, 2) ensure probe can't block critical KV drains during progressive rollout."

Canary on a small non-critical namespace for 24h, monitor harmonizer.smoothing_lag_gauge, reopened_circuit_count, kv_drain_duration, and request p99. If reopen rate increases unexpectedly, flip feature flag off — the harmonizer is designed as non-blocking and can be toggled without restarts.

Why this is safe as a hotfix:
- The change is opt-in by default (harmonizer.enabled=false in release hotfix), the reopen cooldown only adds a conservative backoff (no functional change unless enabled), and the standby probe defers only non-critical drains behind a soft timeout. The backported patch keeps defaults unchanged and exposes knobs so SRE can enable gradually.

This quickstart provides: 1) a minimal file layout with a staged prompt pipeline, 2) a watch-mode devserver that hot-reloads prompt stage files and runs fast contract checks, 3) TypeScript and Go example adapters that show tool-calling guard rails, 4) an opinionated structured-output linter (StrucLint) with example contracts and fixes, 5) devcontainer + docker-compose for reproducible local runs, and 6) lightweight telemetry presets for the Console (span tags and step timing) so teams can instrument authoring iterations. title: correlated-load-generator-with-e2e-telemetry-export
content:
correlated-load-generator-with-e2e-telemetry-export

Motivation: existing workload runners cover independent request streams (single-sequence throughput, sequence-mix) but do not model correlated cross-stream load spikes that occur in production (e.g., user action fanout, background sync overlapping with foreground traffic). This PR introduces a correlated-load generator harness plus an end-to-end telemetry export pipeline to capture cross-stream latency, queue-growth, and synchronization metrics so that downstream analysis and reporting can reason about tail behavior caused by inter-stream contention. Key deliverables: 1) bench/correlated_runner.py - a new runner that models N interdependent streams with configurable correlation matrices, jitter, and fanout; 2) telemetry/otel_exporter.py - lightweight OTel exporter that emits per-request attributes, cross-stream correlation IDs, and histogram buckets; 3) reporting/cross_stream_reporter.py - post-run aggregator that computes cross_stream_p50/p95/p99, queue_peak_avg, backlog_area (integral of queue length over time), and produces CSV + NDJSON outputs for the existing reporting pipeline; 4) integration test harness (tests/integration/test_correlated_end_to_end.py) that runs the runner against the model stub and asserts telemetry invariants; 5) CI workflow update to run the correlated workload in a short smoke mode on PRs. Design notes: the runner uses event-driven scheduling (asyncio) with a central correlation controller that injects synthetic causality between streams; correlation is parameterized as a matrix of probabilities (float in [0,1]) that governs whether an event in stream A triggers related events in stream B within a time window. Telemetry uses OpenTelemetry traces + custom metric instruments; to avoid high cardinality, correlation IDs are hashed to a bounded dimension and we export representative sample traces at a 1/100 sampling rate in CI mode. Backwards compatibility: the runner is opt-in for the lab (not enabled by default), uses existing bench runner interfaces, and integrates with current reporting consumers. Checklist: [x] add correlated runner and unit tests; [x] add OTel exporter with config; [x] add reporting aggregator and CSV/NDJSON writer; [x] add integration smoke test; [x] update CI workflow; [x] document config knobs (README). Known limitations and future work: higher-fidelity user models (session state), long-running persistence of correlation IDs to simulate multi-minute flows, and a telemetry ingest sidecar for high-throughput on-prem runs. Impact: enables reproducible stress tests for cross-stream tail behavior and provides structured outputs for the dashboarding team to add cross-stream charts.

Add correlated workload runner and end-to-end telemetry exporter for cross-stream tail analysis. Includes reporting aggregator and CI smoke tests. This enables reproducible correlated spike tests and CSV/NDJSON outputs for dashboards.
Testing guidance: run `python -m bench.correlated_runner --config examples/correlated_small.yaml --ci-fast-sample` for a quick smoke run.
Backward compatibility: default behavior unchanged for existing runners; correlated runner is opt-in.
Follow-ups: add a Jupyter notebook that visualizes backlog_area over time and integrate with perf-canary dashboards.

title: Introduce conditional lint router and release-window coordinator to reduce noisy presubmit and protect releases
content:
Introduce conditional lint router and release-window coordinator to reduce noisy presubmit and protect releases

Context: Our presubmit lanes run the same full lint/test matrix for all PRs which causes noisy queues and slow feedback for trivial changes. Separately, release automation has tripped twice during externally scheduled maintenance windows. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a conditional lint router (routes PRs to lightweight vs full lint lanes based on path heuristics, diff size, and opt-in labels) and a release-window coordinator (centralized gate that prevents automated release merges/rollouts during configured blackout windows and retries with backoff). Motivation: speed up developer feedback on small changes, reduce CI cost, and avoid accidental releases during scheduled infra work. Changes in this PR: 1) New presubmit router service (lightweight Go lambda + GH Actions composite) that evaluates changed paths, owned modules, and heuristics (third-party locks, build files) to pick one of: quick-lint, staged-lint, full-lint. 2) Lightweight lint lane implemented as composite actions for fast JS/py style checks and type stubs only. 3) Staged-lint lane for medium changes: run targeted tests and a limited subset of integration tests. 4) Release-window coordinator: central job that reads release windows from repo config (.release-windows.yml) and annotates release PRs to block merge if window active; includes a safe retry/backoff and escalation label. 5) Dep-pruner helper: small script that scans devDependencies in package manifests and flags stale transitive devdeps (optional run as repo-hygiene job). Migration notes and checklist: - [x] Add .release-windows.yml schema and default window (Sundays 02:00-05:00 UTC) - [x] Add `presubmit: lightweight` label and opt-in docs - [x] Add feature flag `CI_ROUTER_ENABLED` (enabled for redwood/* repos by default) - [x] Add monitoring dashboards (console: presubmit-latency, presubmit-cost, release-blocks) Testing performed: unit tests for router heuristics, integration test against a mock GH API, canary rollout of router to 10% of PRs across redwood repo for 48 hours, and a dry-run for release coordinator. Related tickets: ENG-3245 (presubmit refactor), ENG-3301 (release safety improvements). Rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 100% in 3 days with rollback via feature flag. Links: Linear ENG-3245: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3245/conditional-lint-router and support ticket SUP-1124 for release blackout incidents.

Author reply: added allowlist config and regen of default in .github/allowlists.json.
Lina Park requested more granular test-shard mapping for staged-lint; suggested we reuse the path->shard mapping from the test-orchestrator. Response: implemented mapping and added unit tests.

Added conditional presubmit routing to speed feedback for small PRs; added release-window coordinator to block automated merges during configured blackout windows; included a devdep pruner job to flag stale dev dependencies. See docs/dev/presubmit.md for usage and configuration.

title: introduce-targeted-presubmit-slimline-and-dep-pruner-operator
content:
introduce-targeted-presubmit-slimline-and-dep-pruner-operator

Motivation: our presubmit CI has grown noisy and slow due to monolithic lint/test lanes that run across the entire monorepo for non-impactful changes. At the same time, transitive dev-dependencies and stale tooling in package manifests cause intermittent CI cache churn and unnecessary build costs. This PR implements two complementary improvements: (1) a targeted presubmit strategy that runs only lightweight checks and narrowly scoped lint/test shards based on path-aware change detection, and (2) a new dep-pruner operator (action + small CLI) that detects and suggests removal of unused dev-deps and flags version instabilities. The intent is to preserve strong correctness guarantees while giving fast feedback for small changes and surfacing dependency debt for maintainers to triage. Highlights/what changed: - Introduce .github/actions/dep-pruner (composite action) and a minimal Go CLI (tools/dep-pruner) that computes unused dev-deps across package.json / pyproject.toml roots. The action runs in a dry-run by default and posts PR comments with suggested edits. - Add path-aware presubmit runner: .github/workflows/presubmit-slimline.yml. The workflow contains three lanes: quick (fast lint + unit smoke), targeted (pattern-driven test shards), and full (fallback that runs full integration on release branches). Quick runs on push for small changes; targeted is triggered when changed files exceed patterns for a module. - Move heavy lint rules behind a staged lint gate; add 'lint-shadow' job that only runs full lint when more than N files touched or explicit label is set. - Add a lightweight test selector script (scripts/select-tests-by-diff.py) that maps changed files to Jest/Pytest shards via a simple config under ci/test-mapping.yaml. - Introduce dep-stability-probe: a periodic job (weekly) that detects transitive version drift and files an issue with a report. - Add infra docs: docs/ci/presubmit-strategy.md and docs/ci/dep-pruner.md. Checklist: - [x] design doc and implementation for presubmit lanes - [x] composite action + CLI with unit tests - [x] workflow templates and mapping file - [x] docs and contributor guide updates - [x] initial integration tests against a lightweight staging runner - [x] staged rollout plan (canary on selected repos) Rollout plan: 1) Deploy workflows in dry-run mode for 48 hours to gather metrics (CI time, jobs avoided). 2) Enable auto PR comments from dep-pruner for contributors with opt-in flag. 3) After one week of metrics, enable lint-shadow gate for all repos. Backwards compatibility and safety: - Presubmit workflows default to conservative thresholds; full workflow is still the default for release/* branches. - dep-pruner never mutates files automatically; suggestions are comments and draft PRs behind a toggled flag. Related tickets: ENG-7721 (presubmit redesign), ENG-7818 (dep hygiene initiative), SUP-501 (customer-incurred CI cost spike).

title: unified-orbit-rollout-runtime-with-early-safety-cutpoints
content:
unified-orbit-rollout-runtime-with-early-safety-cutpoints

Context: We need a single runtime path that unifies canary, A/B, and shadow traffic workflows so operators can declare multi-mode rollouts in one policy without wiring custom controllers. This PR implements the "Orbit" rollout runtime: a declarative execution graph, early safety cutpoints, and a lightweight playbook-based rollback adapter.

Motivation: Current rollout logic is scattered across multiple controllers and ad-hoc scripts. Teams running hybrid experiments (shadow + canary) must coordinate manually. Orbit aims to reduce operator cognitive load, enable reproducible safeguards, and surface actionable telemetry for automated rollback decisions.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a declarative rollout graph schema (api/rollout_graph.proto) that supports nodes for shadow, canary, multi-arm A/B splits, and stop/fallback hooks.
- Implements a runtime executor (pkg/rollout/orbit) that evaluates node predicates, applies traffic transforms (split/mirror), and enforces early safety cutpoints (latency, error-rate, fidelity diff).
- Introduces a rollback playbook adapter (pkg/rollout/playbook) that composes audit-safe rollback steps (drain, snapshot-promote, quota-unbind) to run automatically when gates fail.
- Adds a compact simulator (cmd/rollout-sim) for local testing of rollout policies against synthetic traces.
- Exposes new telemetry: rollout_epoch, gate_evaluation:pass|fail, fidelity_delta; surfaced into Console and trace spans.

Migration notes: Existing rollout policies remain supported. A one-line conversion script (tools/rollout-migrate) translates older YAML to the new graph schema. Customers on Dedicated with custom controllers will see no behavioral change until they opt in.

Testing and validation: Included unit tests for the executor logic, integration tests that run simulated clusters in CI, and a canary runbook used to validate on staging (see docs/playbooks/orbit-canary.md).

Checklist: 
- [x] api design review (ENG-2742)
- [x] telemetry integration (SLO team)
- [x] docs/console updates (docs/playbooks)

Related work: Linear ENG-2742, design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2742/unified-orbit-rollout-proposal.

title: add-phasewise-token-latency-matrix-and-cost-cascade-playback
content:
add-phasewise-token-latency-matrix-and-cost-cascade-playback

Motivation: We've been seeing unexplained long-tail token latency spikes across multi-stage model pipelines. Existing dashboards show aggregate p95/p99 but lack phase-separation (tokenization, encoder, kv-lookup, attention, decode) and a way to replay cost impact over time. This PR introduces a phasewise token latency matrix collector, a compact cost-cascade visualizer for the Console, and lightweight trace enrichment so sampled spans include token-phase breakpoints. Changes include: new prometheus/OTel metrics (phase_duration_ms{phase,model,variant,route}), an internal compact histogram rollup for UI tiling, a dashboard JSON with interactive playback slider, and an alert tuning guide to reduce noisy p99 alerts by gating on phase-contributed proportion. Implementation notes: collector implemented as a thin runtime hook (serving/runtime/phase_collector.cc) with guarded sampling to avoid alloc overhead in hot paths; trace decorator adds a small token-phase array to span tags when trace sampling is active. UI: Console dashboard panels added under Observability -> Token Cost & Latency -> Phase Matrix. Rollout plan: staged flag (observability.phase_matrix.enabled) default off; enable first for staging customers, opt-in for high-volume tenants. title: Introduce stability windows, anchor snapshots, and automated rollback playbook
content:
Introduce stability windows, anchor snapshots, and automated rollback playbook

Context: Model onboarding churn and noisy changelogs make it hard for SREs and product engineers to determine whether a new model profile change is genuinely material or an artifact of sampling. Small profile deltas frequently trigger downstream rollouts and manual reviews even when signals are within the expected instability of the dataset.

Goal: Provide a deterministic, time-bounded mechanism (StabilityWindow) to anchor profile snapshots, produce compact signatures for snapshots, compute reproducible micro-deltas with seeded sampling, and ship an automated rollback/rollforward playbook that can be executed by the curator CLI or surfaced in incident runbooks. This reduces surprise rollouts, makes changelogs more actionable, and shortens troubleshooting time for regressions.

What this PR contains: Adds a StabilityWindow abstraction to the model registry metadata (start_ts, end_ts, seed, snapshot_id), an anchor snapshot generator that emits a compact signature (SHA256 of canonicalized profile + seed) and deterministic sample indices, and a changelog micro-delta algorithm that computes diffs relative to the nearest anchor snapshot using seeded sampling to ensure reproducible summaries. The PR also adds a rollback_playbook generator which synthesizes step-by-step actions (rollback candidate, validation prompt sets, fast compare commands) and wires it into registryctl and the curator alert hook. Includes a backfill script to generate anchors for historical profiles and a small scheduler chart for creating periodic stability windows for high-traffic models.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (internal RFC): /docs/rfcs/2024-09-stability-windows.md
- [x] Unit tests for snapshot signing and seeded sampling (pkg/onboard/*_test.go)
- [x] Integration test (tests/integration/snapshot_seeded_test.go)

title: scalable-reserve-droplet-and-tenant-saturation-detector
content:
scalable-reserve-droplet-and-tenant-saturation-detector

Motivation: production tenants with bursty traffic patterns occasionally drive node-level saturation that triggers aggressive autoscaler decisions and SLO violations for adjacent tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight per-tenant saturation detection signal and a small, bounded 'reserve droplet' allocation mechanism that provides short-lived, spillover capacity to tenants that are about to hit sustained saturation. The goal is to reduce noisy-neighbor-induced autoscale churn, protect tail latency, and improve utilization signals used by downstream accounting. Design summary: 1) Saturation detector: a new sampler that computes a tenant_saturation_score by combining per-pool occupancy, queue-depth percentiles (P90/P99), and recent scheduling rejections. The detector emits a short TTL score (30s window) and a smoothed score for admission logic. 2) Reserve droplet allocator: small reserved allocations (1-3 slot droplets depending on tenant tier) that are liquid — they are granted for short intervals (default 45s), charged to tenant allocation, and reclaimed aggressively on preemption. Allocation decisions are conservative: total droplets per pool capped at 8% of pool capacity and subject to headroom budget. 3) Autoscaler/Admission integration: the admission controller consults the tenant_saturation_score to prefer droplet granting over immediate scale-up when a tenant shows transient saturation but the cluster still has headroom. When cluster-wide pressure persists, the fallback is the regular autoscaler path. 4) Telemetry and reporting: exports tenant_saturation_score, droplet_allocated{tenant,pool}, droplet_preempt_count, and a derived tenant_saturation_class (OK/WARM/CRITICAL). These feed the utilization rollup and a new tenant-level heatmap in Console. Rollout plan and safety: staged rollout toggled by feature flag fleet.reserve-droplet.enabled. Canary on two non-critical us-west pools for 48h, then expand to 25% of pools with increased sampling. Safety knobs: hard cap on droplets per pool, per-tenant max-droplet-per-minute, and opt-out via tenant config. Backwards-compatible: if the feature flag is off, no control path changes. Linear/Jira: relates to ENG-3419 (reduce autoscale churn), PM-4128 (tenant latency regressions), and SUP-1221 (customer incident follow-up). Checklist: - [x] unit tests for detector scoring and edge cases - [x] integration test with admission controller sim in bench-lab - [x] telemetry metrics + Grafana dashboards (draft) - [x] migration docs and tenant opt-out documented - [x] e2e dry-run in canary region - [x] rollout feature flag and safe defaults Known limitations: detection window tuned conservatively; may under-react to extremely short microbursts (sub-100ms). Future work: adaptive droplet sizing, budget-aware droplet pooling across zones.
Marco Ruiz (2026-02-14): Nice incremental design. Two asks: add a metric for droplet-request-latency and ensure the droplet reclaim path cannot starve node-level evictions.
Aisha Kumar (2026-02-15): Added droplet_request_latency metric and tightened reclaim window; added additional unit test for eviction safety.

title: Stripe prefetcher and per-CPU pin highways for block manager
content:
Stripe prefetcher and per-CPU pin highways for block manager

Motivation: Reduce early-warmup p99 tails and allocator contention in the paged KV block manager for mixed small/large request patterns. Current freelist grabs and opportunistic prefetch lead to head-of-line contention on high core counts and bursty workloads. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: a stripe-based prefetcher that issues clustered prefetch ahead-of-use, and a light-weight per-CPU pin highway that serializes pin/unpin bookkeeping per core to avoid global freelist races.

Design summary: stripe-prefetcher: maintains short-lived 'stripes' (small contiguous sets of blocks) discovered by scanning hot prefixes and allocation traces. Prefetch issues are batched into a vector-friendly path that emits contiguous async IO/KV-loads to warm the cache and prime KV block pin state. Prefetch budget is adjustable per-tenant and per-route; aggressive mode is disabled by default.

per-CPU pin highways: instead of a single freelist hot path with atomic handoffs, pins/unpins are shuttled through a per-CPU ring (highway) which batches releases and performs coalesced freelist returns. This reduces CAS storms on the global freelist and keeps hot allocations local to the CPU that consumed them. A global slowpath remains for cross-core steals.

Kernel-friendly hints: prefetcher emits 'kernel hints' that are consumed by the serving runtime path to select a vectorized copy kernel when contiguous stripes are available; this reduces per-block bookkeeping overhead when moving KV payloads into GPU-visible memory. The runtime selects the hint-aware kernel only when contiguous runs exceed a threshold to avoid fragmentation penalties.

Backward compatibility and safety: no on-disk format changes. Feature gated behind two runtime flags (kv.stripe_prefetcher.enabled, kv.percpu_pin.highways_enabled) and a dynamic prefetch_budget param. If either flag is disabled, behavior falls back to the existing allocator. We added a runtime guard to disable prefetch on constrained memory nodes and a throttler for background prefetch work to preserve latency SLOs.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on a 32-vCPU canary with 4 A100s show: +12% aggregate throughput for mixed small/med gen workloads, p99 latency down 18% on short-response chat-style requests, and a 22% reduction in CAS contention observed on the global freelist counter. End-to-end cost-per-token reduced ~6% under synthetic steady-state due to fewer reissued cache misses. Detailed numbers and methodology are in docs/ops/prefetcher.md.

Testing and rollout: unit and integration tests added; bench harness extended with a 'stripe' scenario. Rollout plan: gated canary -> region grayscale -> global enable with telemetry thresholds. Feature flags are on by default only for internal dev clusters.

- [x] Implementation of stripe prefetcher and per-CPU pin highways
- [x] Unit tests for allocator fastpath and slowpath
- [x] Integration tests covering prefetch budget and disable guards
- [x] Bench harness scenario and raw results attached
- [x] Telemetry (contention, prefetch hits/misses, highway occupancy)
- [x] Docs: ops guide and rollout notes

title: Introduce contextual-entropy-indexer and alert heuristics for prefetch paths
content:
Introduce contextual-entropy-indexer and alert heuristics for prefetch paths

Adds a lightweight contextual entropy indexer and heuristic alert weighting for prefetch/pipeline paths. Improves observability of token-level prefetch effects and reduces noisy alerts for transient warmups.
Motivation: We see recurring noisy alerts and high-cardinality telemetry around prefetch and prefix-warmup activity that obscures real regressions. This PR introduces a compact "contextual entropy indexer" to fingerprint invocation prompt-contexts, attaches entropy deltas to token-phase spans, and layers a heuristic alert-weighting engine so alerts triggered by prefetch/warmup churn are de-emphasized. The change is explicitly scoped to observability: no runtime behavior changes beyond additional light instrumentation and a configurable sampling hook.

What changed (summary):
- Added an entropy indexing library (pkg/observability/entropy_index) that computes a compact 64-bit context sketch and streaming delta per invocation. The index is intentionally small to avoid metric cardinality explosion.
- Instrumented token-phase spans to emit entropy_delta and prefetch_hint tags when a request used the prefetch path. These are exposed as OTEL attributes and as metric labels for rollups.
- Introduced an alert heuristics layer (services/alerting/heuristics) that consumes token-phase histograms + entropy deltas and applies noise attenuation for alerts matching prefetch signatures. Heuristics are configurable via experiments/heuristics.yaml.
- Dashboard: added observability/dashboards/prefetch-entropy-panel.json — a focused dashboard showing "prefetch rate", "entropy-delta distribution per-route", "token-latency split by prefetch_hint", and a time-series of heuristics attenuations applied.
- Tests and sim harness: added prefetched-invocation synthetic traces to eval-harness/prefetch-sim to validate alert dampening under warmup bursts.

Why this is safe: The entropy index is deterministic and uses only hashed context summary (no PII). Instrumentation is additive and sampled by default (5% global, adjustable per-tenant). Heuristics only change alert scoring; they do not suppress telemetry or modify request routing.

Checklist: 
- [x] pkg/observability/entropy_index: go implementation + docs (see README in package)
- [x] Instrumentation added to runtime span emitter (runtime/telemetry/token_phase_emitter.go)
- [x] Alert heuristics engine and configuration (services/alerting/heuristics/*)
- [x] Prefetch dashboard JSON and dashboard setup script
- [x] Unit + integration tests for indexer and heuristics
- [x] Performance sanity run (prefetch-sim) and spike replay tested on staging

Testing results (high level):
- Synthetic warmup burst (1000 prefetched traces/min for 10 minutes) in prefetched-sim: baseline alerts reduced by 72% after heuristics compared to control, true-positive regression alerts preserved.
- End-to-end telemetry CPU impact: +0.6% median on telemetry-ingest workers at 5% sampling; estimated p50 overhead per-request for the indexer is ~120µs when enabled unsampled.

- runtime/telemetry/token_phase_emitter.go (added attributes entropy_delta, prefetch_hint)

If legitimate alerts are being suppressed, set heuristics.override=true for the affected route and escalate. The playbook includes a quick query to surface suppressed alerts for the last 15m.
