2026-02-02 15:09 (Dana Lo): TS SDK: node fetch streaming loses access to headers after consumption in some paths; but we can capture request_id early and attach to a typed error when ReadableStream errors. Also clarifying cancellation semantics vs network disconnect in docs/examples.
2026-02-03 13:27 (Mateusz Zielinski): Go SDK: we can wrap scanner/decoder errors and include request_id captured from initial response. Will also document recommended retry pattern and that retries are caller-controlled for streams.
2026-02-05 09:40 (Owen Phillips): Sent interim workaround to customer:
- If possible, configure proxy to allow long-lived SSE and disable response buffering for the Redwood domain.
- Increase overall timeout and keep connection alive (TCP keepalive) where supported.
- For best reliability behind strict proxies, consider non-streaming mode for long outputs.
- For retries: avoid automatic retry on streaming disconnect; if retrying, log request_id and use idempotency keys for any side-effecting workflows; treat partial output as best-effort display only.
Customer acknowledged and will test proxy policy changes.
2026-02-07 16:12 (Owen Phillips): Internal: linked this issue to INT-1182 (request_id visibility in SDK errors). Also flagged as a concrete driver for SDK parity initiative (streaming edge cases + typed errors).
2026-02-10 12:33 (Wei Chen): Drafted doc updates for Streaming guide: new section "Behind proxies" + "What to do on disconnect" including sample code to log request_id and capture partial output. Will align wording across Python/TS/Go pages and add explicit warning that streaming retries are not automatic.
2026-02-14 10:50 (Owen Phillips): Engineering updates in flight:
- Python: add typed StreamingDisconnectError w/ request_id and partial output semantics.
- TS: attach request_id and normalize error shape on stream failure.
- Go: wrap unexpected EOF with typed error + request_id.
Docs + examples to include idempotency guidance and consistent logging fields.
Keeping ticket in progress until customer confirms improvements or docs are published.
2026-02-18 09:07 (Customer - Acorn Financial): Proxy team applied allowlist + disabled buffering for Redwood streaming endpoint; disconnect rate reduced significantly but not eliminated. They still want request_id in errors to speed up escalation and want clear guidance on when to retry.
2026-02-19 17:28 (Owen Phillips): Docs PR and SDK PRs merged/queued for release per parity rollout. Provided customer with preview link and recommended pattern:
- Always log request_id at stream start.
- On disconnect: show partial output (if acceptable) and present a "Regenerate" action rather than silent automatic retry.
- For background jobs: prefer non-streaming with idempotency key and standard retry policy.
Customer satisfied with plan; will upgrade SDKs when releases land.
2026-02-20 11:02 (Dev Patel): Closing as resolved via docs guidance + upcoming SDK changes (typed errors w/ request_id, clarified partial output + retry guidance). Follow-ups tracked in SDK parity epic and INT-1182. If customer sees ongoing high disconnect rate after proxy changes, we will re-open for deeper platform/proxy analysis.
Resolved via (1) published streaming docs guidance for enterprise proxies and safe retry patterns, and (2) SDK parity work to surface typed streaming disconnect errors including request_id and consistent semantics for partial output/cancellation. Customer implemented proxy allowlist/buffering changes as a mitigation and will upgrade SDKs to pick up improved error surfaces.

title: Preventing duplicate external-tool invocations when orchestrating streaming responses across Python, Go, and TS SDKs (chunk-level acks)
content:
Preventing duplicate external-tool invocations when orchestrating streaming responses across Python, Go, and TS SDKs (chunk-level acks)

Issue summary:
Customer ScribeAI is orchestrating streamed model responses from Redwood across a Python orchestration service, a Go sidecar that invokes external tools (webhooks/3rd-party APIs), and a Typescript frontend that re-connects to the stream. They observe duplicated external tool calls when the frontend reconnects mid-stream and when the Go sidecar retries on transient HTTP 5xx.

Impact:
- External tools (billing-critical third-party APIs) are invoked multiple times for the same logical user request, causing duplicate charges and inconsistent downstream state.
- Customer has an SLA with their downstream provider; duplicates cause financial and operational risk.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API, dedicated capacity (prod-us-east)
- Orchestration: python-orch v1.3.4 (async generator streaming to clients)
- Sidecar: go-tool-proxy v0.9.1 (performs tool.call webhooks and returns call confirmation)
- Client: ts-web reconnects with resume token support

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Client sends a streaming request to Python orchestrator via Redwood API (streaming).
2) Orchestrator emits partial tokens/chunks; at chunk N the orchestrator issues a tool.call to the Go sidecar and forwards an interim acknowledgement object to the client that contains a partial "ack_token" (not a final confirmation).
3) Client disconnects and reconnects before receiving final tool confirmation. On reconnect the client replays the stream state; the orchestrator re-issues the tool.call (or the Go sidecar retries due to ambiguous response), resulting in duplicate external webhook calls.

Expected behavior:
- A single external-tool invocation per logical tool request regardless of client reconnects or sidecar retries.

Actual behavior:
- Duplicated tool calls when: a) client reconnects during in-flight tool call, b) sidecar retries without dedup key, or c) orchestrator replays chunk-level messages lacking end-of-call confirmation.

Logs / snippets provided by customer:
- Python orchestrator logs show "tool_call_sent nonce=abc123 chunk=12" and later "replay: replaying chunk=12 nonce=abc123" which triggers another HTTP POST to the sidecar.
- Go sidecar logs show two POSTs within 2s with identical payloads but different request IDs; the third-party API charged twice.

Customer request:
- Guidance on a robust cross-language pattern to avoid duplicates while preserving low-latency partial streaming and client reconnect semantics. Practical SDK-level and server-side changes they'd need to implement.

Temporary workaround suggested by customer:
- Disable automatic replay on reconnect (client-level) and force full restart of the request. This reduces duplicates but loses resume UX.

Notes:
- This is different from a simple idempotency key because the request lifecycle includes partial streaming acknowledgements (chunk-level) and the final tool result arrives asynchronously. The orchestration needs a pattern for partial acks vs final confirmation.

Request: Please provide a recommended pattern we can implement with minimal API/runtime changes and sample pseudo-code for Python and Go sidecar.

2026-03-10 09:32 - Support (Ava Roberts): Received initial report from ScribeAI CS. Marking P1 due to financial duplicate charges. Assigned to Liam for triage.
2026-03-10 13:18 - Liam Chen: Reproduced in staging with synthetic client. Confirmed duplicates when orchestrator replays chunk-level messages without a final 'tool_result' marker. Will reach out to runtime team for dedup store options.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Runtime Eng (Diego Morales): Noted serving-runtime currently supports per-request idempotency token but assumes single final tool invocation. Streaming partial-ack tokens aren't deduped. Suggested a lightweight server-side dedup cache keyed by (customer_id, invocation_nonce) with TTL equal to request lifetime.
2026-03-11 12:02 - ScribeAI (Elena Novak): Happy to implement client-side changes if you can provide concrete patterns and minimal changes to the Go sidecar. Currently sidecar does exponential retries on 5xx without checking any idempotency header.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Liam Chen: Drafting guidance — adding to ticket as investigation notes and sample patterns. Leaving open for follow-up on SDK exposures.
Findings summary:
1) Root cause is orchestration-level ambiguity about what constitutes a confirmed tool invocation vs an in-flight partial ack.
2) Three failure modes: client reconnect replay, sidecar retry on 5xx, orchestrator re-emitting chunk during replay.
3) Existing SDKs expose a generic "idempotency_key" but customers are concerned about assigning and persisting keys across partial-stream lifecycles.

Engineering constraints:
- Minimal change preferred to avoid broad SDK churn across Python/Go/TS.
- Workload is latency-sensitive; any synchronous call to central dedup store must be low-latency or optional.

Proposed multi-pronged pattern (recommended):
- Invocation identity: generate a stable invocation_id at the start of a logical tool request. Format: <session_id>::<invocation_nonce> (session_id persisted across reconnects). SDKs should expose an optional "invocation_id" parameter on tool.call.
- Chunk markers vs final confirmation: streaming messages should include one of: "partial_ack: invocation_id, chunk_index, interim_token" or "final_ack: invocation_id, tool_run_id, status". Only the final_ack marks the call as completed.
- Sidecar dedup header: sidecar must forward an Idempotency-Key header derived from invocation_id to external webhook. The sidecar should be updated to check and set Idempotency-Key header and to skip retrying if the response indicates a non-idempotent success (or query local cache).
- Lightweight dedup store: runtime or sidecar keeps a small in-memory dedup cache keyed by invocation_id -> tool_run_id with TTL=5m (configurable). Cache should be checked before issuing webhook POSTs. If cache hit and tool_run_id present, treat as already-invoked and return stored result to orchestrator. This avoids cross-process duplicate calls without heavy central infra.
- Replay semantics: On client reconnect, orchestrator must replay partial chunks that are idempotent (non-invocation) but must not re-emit tool.call if the chunk already had invocation_id and the dedup record exists. Instead it should re-send the last-known partial_ack and the orchestration state including invocation_id and interim_token.

Pseudo-code (Python orchestrator) suggestion (plain text):
- Before invoking tool: invocation_id = session_id + '::' + uuid4()
- Send partial chunk to client: {"chunk": ..., "partial_ack": {"invocation_id": invocation_id, "chunk": n, "interim_token": token}}
- Sidecar call: POST /invoke with body {"invocation_id": invocation_id, "payload": ...} and header "Idempotency-Key: invocation_id"
- On final tool result: send final_ack {"invocation_id": invocation_id, "tool_run_id": run-xyz, "status": "ok"}

Go sidecar changes (plain text):
- On POST /invoke: if invocation_id missing -> reject with 400 (recommendation to customer)
- Check in-memory cache: if cache[invocation_id] exists -> return cached result (200 + cached response) to orchestrator
- Otherwise perform external POST with header Idempotency-Key: invocation_id
- On success store cache[invocation_id] = external_response (TTL)
- Retry policy: do not retry blindly on 5xx if you already have cache hit or if external API supports idempotency keys. Use exponential backoff but consult cache before each retry.

SDK exposure suggestions (minimal):
- Expose optional invocation_id on tooling APIs for Python/Go/TS SDKs.
- Provide helper to derive invocation_id from session token so clients can persist session across reconnects.
- Add example patterns in SDK docs for "streaming tool call with chunk-level ack".

Compatibility notes:
- This pattern is compatible with customers who already use per-request idempotency keys; it merely scopes keys to logical invocation lifecycle and formalizes partial vs final ack semantics.

Workarounds and next steps:
1) Short term: ScribeAI to add invocation_id generation in python-orch and update Go sidecar to set/check Idempotency-Key and a small in-memory cache. This reduces duplicates immediately with minimal infra.
2) Medium term: SDK change to accept invocation_id and helper to derive it from session; add docs and patterns. Target: SDK patch releases in two sprints.
3) Long term: runtime feature to optionally provide a dedup API (centralized store) for cross-process dedup if customers need multi-replica guarantees.

Action items assigned:
- Liam Chen: provide sample python/go snippets and a reference sidecar change set (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Runtime Eng (Diego Morales): spike on lightweight per-customer dedup cache across replicas and performance implications (ETA 2026-03-20).
- ScribeAI: implement invocation_id client change in staging and report results (ETA 2026-03-18).

Ticket remains open pending customer validation in staging and a small SDK docs update.

title: Unexpected spike in 429s after upgrading SDK (quota mismatch vs rate-limit headers)
content:
Unexpected spike in 429s after upgrading SDK (quota mismatch vs rate-limit headers)

Customer reports a noticeable increase in HTTP 429 responses immediately after upgrading Redwood SDK (Python -> latest minor). Customer believes they are under their purchased quota and that prior to upgrade they did not see sustained throttling.

Issue Summary
- Symptom: Increased 429s ("Too Many Requests") with inconsistent/misleading rate limit headers across endpoints.
- Trigger: SDK upgrade + switching more traffic to streaming + increased concurrency.
- Suspected: Edge-case in quota enforcement / header classification (429 returned with headers that do not reflect actual enforcement window), plus SDK retry behavior amplifying bursts.

Impact
- Customer-facing impact: Elevated request failures; customer implemented aggressive retries, causing additional burst traffic and more 429s.
- Scope: Primarily hosted API traffic; reported across us-east and eu-west.
- Business impact: Customer escalated due to downstream search latency and perceived platform instability.

Customer Environment
- Tier: self_serve (high-usage hosted account)
- SDK: Redwood Python SDK (upgraded within last 24 hours). Customer also has a TS service calling embeddings.
- Workload pattern: mixture of chat completions (streaming) + embeddings batch jobs.
- Concurrency: increased by customer during rollout.

What we need from customer (requested)
- Approx time range (UTC) for the spike
- Request IDs for sample 429s (5-10)
- Endpoint breakdown (chat vs embeddings)
- SDK version + language, and whether retries/backoff are enabled

Observed / Provided Examples
- Sample response indicated 429 with headers suggesting remaining=0 while dashboard usage looked below hourly quota.
- Some 429s appear to be rate-limit (burst) while others appear to be quota enforcement, but both surface as 429 and sometimes share the same error message.

Initial Hypotheses
1) Quota enforcement edge-case incorrectly classifies (or caches) limit state, leading to 429s even when token/quota counters look below the contracted limit.
2) Rate-limit headers inconsistent across endpoints and/or under fallback routing, confusing customer-side logic that keys on headers.
3) SDK upgrade changed default retry semantics or timeouts, causing higher effective RPS bursts (especially with streaming reconnect patterns).

Immediate Mitigation Guidance (Support)
- Reduce concurrency temporarily (cap worker pool)
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries; do not retry immediately on 429
- If using streaming, avoid reconnect loops without a backoff; log request IDs per attempt
- Use server-provided Retry-After (if present) over custom fixed delays

Engineering Follow-up
- Linked ENG-4825 to address rate-limit/quota mismatch and header consistency; request confirmation on whether fallback can affect header calculation.
- Track for known-issues sprint article: workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers (draft already in progress).
2026-02-04 17:12 UTC — Dev Patel (Support Ops): Created ticket from Aurora Search escalation. Assigning to Priya Shah for triage. Please follow intake checklist: region/model/sdk version + request IDs. Customer claims quota available but gets 429s post-SDK upgrade.
2026-02-04 17:28 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Reached out to customer for: (1) time window, (2) 5–10 request IDs, (3) SDK version, (4) endpoint mix and concurrency, (5) whether they added retries after the upgrade. Also asked for a sample of response headers (RateLimit-* and Retry-After).
2026-02-04 18:05 UTC — Rachel Kim (Enterprise CS): Aurora is not enterprise, but is a high-usage account evaluating Dedicated. Please keep comms crisp and provide a practical mitigation they can deploy today (retry/backoff + concurrency cap).
2026-02-04 18:44 UTC — Customer (Aurora Search, via Support portal): Time range: 2026-02-04 15:00–18:30 UTC. SDK: redwood-sdk-python 1.9.x (upgraded from 1.8.x). We added retries (3 attempts) with fixed 200ms delay. Seeing 429s on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings. Regions: mostly us-east, some eu-west failover. Providing request IDs in a separate message.
2026-02-04 19:02 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Noted fixed 200ms retry is likely amplifying burst. Asked them to switch to exponential backoff w/ jitter and honor Retry-After if present. Also requested whether they key retry logic off RateLimit-Remaining (some clients do).
2026-02-04 19:20 UTC — Mina Haddad (Platform, Routing): Under fallback, some headers may reflect the gateway limiter rather than the downstream quota service. We should verify header source-of-truth and ensure consistent behavior across endpoints. This sounds consistent with the ongoing header consistency bug report.
2026-02-04 19:31 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Created ENG-4825 and linked it here. Added note: customer reads RateLimit-* headers for adaptive concurrency; inconsistent headers can cause them to increase load at the wrong time.
2026-02-05 00:16 UTC — Ethan Park (Platform): We have at least one known issue where quota enforcement and rate-limit headers can diverge in edge cases. Likely impact: misleading remaining/reset values; 429 classification can be ambiguous. Please collect raw headers + request IDs; we can trace through gateway logs. Recommend customer uses Retry-After and backs off more aggressively.
2026-02-05 10:41 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Customer shared 10 request IDs (stored in internal-only note in the ticket UI) and header snapshots. Pattern: RateLimit-Remaining=0 while account usage dashboard shows well below hourly limit. Retry-After is sometimes absent. 429 body message varies between "quota exceeded" and "rate limit exceeded" for similar traffic.
2026-02-05 12:09 UTC — Sean Gallagher (SRE): This does not meet paging threshold (no platform-wide signal). Treat as customer-impacting bug. Please keep the customer on a stable mitigation: reduce concurrency + exponential backoff w/ jitter. If they continue to see 429s with low traffic, share request IDs and we’ll trace quota service counters vs gateway limiter state.
2026-02-06 09:22 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Sent customer a workaround summary + a copy/paste backoff snippet and asked them to deploy: max retries=2, base delay=500ms, max delay=8s, jitter, and respect Retry-After. Also asked them to stop using RateLimit-Remaining as a signal until we confirm header correctness.
2026-02-07 16:40 UTC — Customer (Aurora Search): After adjusting backoff and reducing concurrency, 429 rate dropped ~70% but still seeing occasional bursts where headers look wrong. We can operate with this for now, but want confirmation whether headers are reliable.
2026-02-08 11:05 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Updating: Engineering is working on header consistency fix (ENG-4825). In the interim: treat 429 as a backpressure signal; rely on Retry-After when present; otherwise exponential backoff. Drafting a Known Issue article for consistent guidance.
2026-02-10 14:12 UTC — Platform (via Ethan Park): Fix in progress; we’re making RateLimit headers consistent and ensuring 429 classification matches enforcement source. Will roll out behind a flag, then ramp. Please point customer to KB draft once published.
2026-02-11 18:03 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): KB article drafted: workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers. Requested Docs review to ensure we avoid customer-specific details and keep guidance generic. Added 'When to escalate' section: sustained 429s at low RPS, missing Retry-After, or RateLimit-Reset > 10 minutes unexpectedly.
2026-02-12 09:37 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Engineering fix merged (PR-19322) and scheduled for rollout. Customer stable with mitigations. Marking ticket Resolved; leaving open follow-up to confirm rollout completion + link final KB article when published.
2026-02-12 10:05 UTC — Dev Patel (Support Ops): Confirmed this aligns with known-issues sprint focus. Please ensure SUP-1855 references this ticket for header inconsistency tracking and that macros include backoff guidance + request ID collection.
Resolved with customer-side mitigation while Engineering fix proceeded.

Customer Mitigation (immediate)
- Reduced concurrency and removed fixed 200ms retry.
- Implemented exponential backoff with jitter for 429s and respected Retry-After when present.
- Temporarily stopped using RateLimit-Remaining as an adaptive concurrency signal due to header inconsistency risk.

Engineering Outcome (tracked separately)
- Linked ENG-4825: quota enforcement edge-case + rate-limit header consistency.
- Related code change: PR-19322 (header consistency + regression tests) merged and queued for rollout.

Docs / Known Issue
- Added/updated draft guidance in workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers with clear 'When to escalate' criteria.

Next Steps
- Support to follow up post-rollout to confirm header behavior is consistent for customer and close the loop with final KB link.

title: Noisy-neighbor tail latency increase for non-burst Dedicated tenant during another tenant’s burst window (us-east / H100)
content:
Noisy-neighbor tail latency increase for non-burst Dedicated tenant during another tenant’s burst window (us-east / H100)

Issue summary
- Northpeak Search (Dedicated, burst NOT enabled) reported elevated p99 latency and intermittent request timeouts during a 35–45 min window on 2025-05-16.
- Correlation observed between Northpeak’s latency spike and a separate tenant’s burst activity against the shared us-east H100 burst pool.

Impact
- Customer-reported: p99 latency increased from ~2.2s baseline to 6–9s for chat completion requests; a subset of requests hit client timeout (30s) and were retried.
- Redwood telemetry: elevated tail latency (p95/p99) on Northpeak’s dedicated route, plus increased queueing time at router/scheduler boundary.
- Duration: ~14:05–14:47 UTC (approx; see investigation notes).

Customer expectations / concern
- Customer is explicitly not opted into burst and expects neighbor activity not to affect their SLOs.
- Asked whether Dedicated implies strict isolation and whether Redwood is prioritizing burst traffic over reserved baseline traffic.

Environment
- prod / us-east
- Hardware class: H100
- Northpeak Dedicated baseline capacity: 8x H100 (reserved)
- Burst pool: shared managed pool, us-east H100

Initial hypotheses
1) Smart routing fallback or capacity spillover incorrectly sending burst traffic into non-burst dedicated pools.
2) Shared upstream bottleneck (router CPU, rate limiter, admission controller latency, shared KV cache service, or network) causing head-of-line blocking.
3) Fleet safety cap not engaging quickly enough; burst pool saturation caused global contention in the serving runtime / scheduler on the same cluster.
4) Telemetry lag causing the admission controller to admit too many burst requests temporarily.

What we need to answer
- Confirm whether Northpeak traffic ever ran on burst GPUs (it should not) vs. whether the impact was an upstream shared component.
- Identify the guardrail that failed (or was missing) and put a mitigation in place before continuing beta burst testing in us-east.

Customer-visible request
- Provide written explanation of root cause, assurances on isolation, and what changes were made to prevent recurrence.

Attachments / references
- Slack: #incidents thread 1739649912 (beta burst test latency event)
- Dashboards: Burst Saturation (us-east/H100), Dedicated Tenant Latency (Northpeak), Router Queue Depth (us-east)
- Runbook: Burst pool overload mitigation
2025-05-16 14:18 UTC — Miguel Santos (Reporter)
Customer (Northpeak) escalation via CS: “Our p99 jumped to ~8s starting around 14:05 UTC. We do not have burst enabled. Did you move us onto shared capacity?” Customer provided request IDs and noted spike coincided with their internal batch job, but request rate is within normal envelope (+10%).

Asks: please confirm isolation, and whether an incident is in progress. Tagging SRE due to potential neighbor impact + beta burst testing today.
2025-05-16 14:23 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Acknowledged. Treating as Sev2 until confirmed. Pulling dedicated tenant latency dashboard + burst pool panels. Also pinging #incidents and #eng-sre.

Immediate checks:
- Any failover/fallback routing toggles?
- Any evidence Northpeak ran on burst pool nodes?
- Burst pool saturation and admission rate in us-east/H100.
2025-05-16 14:31 UTC — Allison Grant (Observability)
Dashboard notes:
- us-east/H100 burst pool utilization hits ~92–96% between 14:06–14:41 UTC.
- burst_admission_denied_total spikes after 14:20 UTC, but only after saturation was already high.
- Router queue depth increased ~3x during that window across multiple tenants (not only burst-enabled).
- Northpeak p99 latency tracks router queue depth more closely than GPU busy time.

Hypothesis: shared router/scheduler bottleneck rather than Northpeak running on burst GPUs.
2025-05-16 14:36 UTC — Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
Routing check: Northpeak tenant policy still pins to dedicated pool, burst disabled. No policy change events. No evidence of fallback into burst pool either.

However, we do see increased “admission decision latency” in routing logs during that time. If routing calls admission controller synchronously for burst-enabled tenants, and that service is overloaded, it could increase latency for unrelated routing paths depending on how shared the threadpools are.
2025-05-16 14:44 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE Manager)
Suggest applying runbook step 1: reduce max burst ratio and/or enable global circuit breaker for us-east/H100 while we confirm blast radius.

Also: check if we are sharing the same ingress/Envoy cluster for both dedicated and burst traffic. If yes, we may be CPU-saturated on ingress which would explain cross-tenant impact.
2025-05-16 14:51 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Mitigation applied at 14:49 UTC:
- Reduced burst pool safety cap (us-east/H100) from 0.30 to 0.15 of regional headroom.
- Temporarily disabled burst allow-list for the one tenant driving sustained burst (per Product-approved beta controls).

Result: router queue depth trending down within ~3–5 minutes; Northpeak p99 started recovering by ~14:55 UTC. Continuing to monitor for 30 minutes before telling customer we’re stable.
2025-05-16 15:05 UTC — Miguel Santos (CS)
Updated customer: We are investigating a suspected interaction with ongoing burst beta activity in the region. Confirmed no intentional changes were made to Northpeak’s Dedicated configuration. Provided status: mitigation in place and metrics recovering. Customer asked for RCA within 48 hours.
2025-05-16 16:12 UTC — Ethan Park (Control Plane)
Checked audit events for Northpeak burst settings: no changes in last 14 days; burst_enabled=false; no admin overrides.

Admission controller metrics:
- P99 admission decision latency rose from ~12ms to ~180–250ms during 14:10–14:35 UTC.
- CPU throttling observed on admission controller pods.

This supports the theory that a shared dependency (admission controller) increased request processing time. Action item: make admission checks async/isolated per routing path, or ensure non-burst traffic doesn’t wait on burst admission control.
2025-05-17 09:02 UTC — Ravi Menon (Routing)
Deep dive:
- Dedicated traffic path SHOULD bypass burst admission entirely, but current routing implementation still performs a “capability fetch” call that hits the same policy evaluation service used by burst admission (shared client + shared circuit breaker).
- Under load, the shared client pool backs up and impacts non-burst tenants.

Fix direction:
1) Split routing clients: non-burst path must not depend on admission controller/policy engine latency.
2) Add strict timeouts + fail-open for non-burst capability fetch (do not block request).
3) SLO gate: if non-burst p95/p99 degrades, automatically hard-disable burst in region/hardware.

Tracking to ENG-4902 / PR-23988.
2025-05-18 13:40 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Status update:
- No evidence Northpeak requests ran on burst GPUs (confirmed by capacity attribution logs and per-node tenant tags).
- Root cause is shared routing dependency coupling: burst admission / policy evaluation latency bled into non-burst routing due to shared client pools and insufficient isolation.
- Mitigations still active: lowered us-east/H100 burst cap + tenant-level burst paused.

Requesting approval to re-enable burst only after PR-23988 SLO gating is deployed to prod us-east.
2025-05-19 18:22 UTC — Keiko Yamamoto (Autoscaling/Guardrails)
Added an additional guardrail on the burst pool autoscaler to avoid pushing admission controller and router into CPU contention:
- If router CPU > 75% for 5m OR admission decision p99 > 100ms for 5m, freeze burst scale-up and progressively tighten burst token bucket rate.

This is a short-term safety valve until routing decoupling lands.
2025-05-20 10:11 UTC — Miguel Santos (CS)
Customer-facing summary sent to Northpeak:
- Confirmed: Northpeak traffic remained on reserved dedicated capacity (no spillover onto shared burst pool).
- What happened: during a burst beta test in us-east/H100, the burst admission/policy evaluation path experienced elevated latency. A shared routing dependency caused increased queueing that affected some non-burst tenants’ tail latency.
- What we changed immediately: tightened burst caps and paused sustained burst activity in the region; latency returned to baseline.
- Preventing recurrence: shipping an SLO regression gate + additional isolation in routing; adding alerts that page SRE before non-burst SLOs degrade.

Customer satisfied with explanation; requested notification once burst is re-enabled in region so they can watch their own dashboards.
2025-05-20 10:27 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Closing as resolved.

Resolution criteria met:
- Northpeak p99 back to baseline for 72 hours.
- Guardrail tightened in us-east/H100.
- Engineering work tracked and prioritized (SLO gate + routing decoupling).

Follow-ups:
- Ensure SLO gate (PR-23988) is enabled for us-east before resuming beta bursts.
- Add explicit runbook step: verify non-burst routing path does not hit admission controller under load.
- Link this incident in burst beta retro notes.
Mitigated by tightening us-east/H100 burst safety caps and pausing sustained burst activity for the burst-enabled tenant. Investigation confirmed no spillover of non-burst Dedicated traffic onto burst GPUs; tail latency increase was caused by a shared routing dependency on the burst admission/policy evaluation path, leading to queueing under admission controller load. Preventative work tracked: routing decoupling, stricter timeouts/fail-open for non-burst paths, and SLO-based burst gating (auto-disable burst when non-burst latency regresses).
Deploy and enable SLO regression gate for burst in us-east/H100 (PR-23988) and verify rollback behavior.
Routing: split client pools / remove non-burst dependency on admission controller and policy evaluation latency (owner: Smart Routing).
Add alert on admission decision p99 and router CPU that pages before non-burst SLO impact (owner: SRE/Observability).
Update CS enablement: how to explain that Dedicated does not run on burst GPUs, and what ‘shared dependencies’ are (owner: CS + Docs).

title: Jira automation: SLA reminders + triage required-field validation + known-issues index prompt
content:
Jira automation: SLA reminders + triage required-field validation + known-issues index prompt

Goal: Reduce time-to-triage + prevent avoidable back-and-forth by enforcing minimum triage context and keeping SLA timers visible/acted on.

This ticket implements Jira Automation rules for the Customer Support project (SUP-*) and light-touch prompts to link customers/workflows to the Known Issues hub.

Scope
1) SLA reminders
- Automated reminders when first response or next update cadence is at-risk or breached.
- Reminders should be Support-friendly (actionable, not noisy) and aligned to the new SLA policy by tier.

2) Required field validation at triage
- When a SUP ticket transitions into Triage (or In Progress), validate a small set of required fields needed for effective escalation to SRE/Eng.
- If fields are missing, block progression (or immediately bounce back to New with a clear comment) and tag the reporter/assignee with what’s missing.

3) Known-issues index prompt (auto-link suggestion)
- When a SUP ticket matches common recurring categories (streaming disconnects, 429/quota confusion, autoscaling oscillation, private installer upgrade stuck, audit log lag), prompt the agent to check/link the Known Issues Index and applicable workaround article.
- This is a prompt only (no forced auto-resolution), to avoid misclassifying novel incidents.

Non-goals
- Changing Support SLA policy language (tracked elsewhere).
- Building new fields beyond what’s already in the guidelines (we should start with validation + reminders first).
SLA reminders
- A1: For SUP tickets in status New/Triage/In Progress (excluding Waiting on Customer/Resolved/Closed), post an internal comment and send a notification to #support-ops when first-response timer is within 15 minutes of due OR overdue.
- A2: For P0/P1 SUP tickets, send an additional reminder if no public update is logged within the expected cadence (per tier policy) after the last public update timestamp.
- A3: Reminders are de-duped (no more than 1 reminder per ticket per hour) to avoid alert fatigue.

Required field validation at triage
- B1: On transition to Triage, validate: customer tier, affected region(s), model (or endpoint type), impact summary, and at least one of (request IDs / timestamps window / reproduction steps).
- B2: If missing fields, automation posts a checklist-style comment with exactly what’s missing and how to get it (link to Support intake checklist).
- B3: If missing fields, ticket cannot move to In Progress (either block transition or auto-revert with comment).

Known-issues index prompt
- C1: When agent sets Component/Label consistent with a known-issue category OR sets priority P2+ with matching summary keywords, automation comments with: (1) link to Known Issues Index, (2) the most likely workaround article(s), and (3) reminder to add the KB link in the customer reply if applicable.
- C2: Prompt is suppressed for tickets labeled security-sensitive or customer-sensitive.

Operational
- D1: All rules have clear owner (Support Ops + Tooling) and are documented in the Jira field guidelines page.
- D2: Rollout starts with a 48-hour dry run (comment-only, no transition blocking) before enabling hard enforcement.
Proposed Jira Automation rules (draft)

Rule 1 — Triage required fields (dry run)
- Trigger: Issue transitioned -> To status = Triage
- Condition: Project = customer-support (SUP)
- Condition: Labels does not contain security-sensitive
- Action: IF any missing required fields THEN
  - Add internal comment:
    "Triage checklist missing: <fields>. Please update before moving forward. Intake checklist: <link>"
  - Add label: triage-missing-context
  - Notify channel: #support-ops (via Slack automation / email)
- No transition blocking in dry run mode.

Rule 2 — Triage required fields (enforcement)
- Same as Rule 1, but add action to revert status to New OR prevent transition to In Progress by reverting when status changes to In Progress and missing fields.
- Prefer pattern: allow transition to Triage but prevent transition to In Progress (less disruptive during initial intake).

Rule 3 — SLA first-response at-risk reminder
- Trigger: Scheduled (every 10 minutes)
- JQL (approx): project = SUP AND status in (New, Triage) AND "First Response Due" <= now() + 15m AND labels not in (sla-reminded)
- Action:
  - Internal comment: "First response due soon (<timestamp>). If awaiting customer info, set status=Waiting on Customer." 
  - Add label: sla-reminded
  - Send Slack notification to #support-ops with key + assignee + priority.
- De-dupe: set an entity property or label with timestamp (preferred) OR remove/expire label via a second scheduled rule after 60m.

Rule 4 — Update cadence reminder (P0/P1)
- Trigger: Scheduled (every 15 minutes)
- Condition: priority in (P0, P1) AND status in (Triage, In Progress) AND status != Waiting on Customer
- Condition: last public comment/customer update older than threshold (tier-aware)
- Action: comment + notify #support-ops

Rule 5 — Known-issues prompt
- Trigger: Field value changed (Component, Labels, Priority) OR Issue created
- If summary/labels/components match patterns:
  - streaming: "stream", "disconnect", "reset", "truncated"
  - quota: "429", "rate limit", "quota", "headers"
  - dedicated scaling: "autoscaling", "oscillation", "churn", "replicas"
  - private upgrade: "installer", "migrations", "upgrade stuck"
  - audit logs: "audit log", "delivery lag", "delayed"
- Action: internal comment with links:
  - Known issues index
  - Specific workaround page(s)
  - Reminder: "If this matches, paste workaround and include ‘when to escalate’ guidance."
- Suppress if labels include: security-sensitive, customer-sensitive, legal

Open questions
- Where is the canonical field for ‘public update timestamp’? If we don’t have one, we may need to start by using last customer-visible comment OR add a simple checkbox/field later.
- Tier-aware thresholds: do we encode tier table in automation (hardcoded) or use lookup via a Jira field (Customer Tier)? Start hardcoded for enterprise/dedicated/private/self_serve based on SLA policy page.

Dependencies
- INT-332: Slack automation for support bridges (channel + template). If Slack notification method changes, coordinate.
- Jira fields used must match the published guidelines page to avoid drift.
Phase 0 (today): Implement rules in disabled state, validate JQL matches ~expected volume using audit log.

Phase 1 (48h dry run): Enable Rule 1 (triage checklist comment only) + Rule 3 (first-response at-risk) as comment-only (no transitions). Monitor noise in #support-ops.

Phase 2 (enforce): Enable prevention/revert for missing triage fields when transitioning to In Progress.

Phase 3 (known-issues prompts): Enable Rule 5 and tune keyword/component matching based on false positives.

Phase 4 (update cadence): Enable P0/P1 update reminders once we confirm a reliable signal for public updates.
Primary risk is notification fatigue (too many reminders) leading to ignored automation. Secondary risk is over-enforcement causing tickets to bounce during high-volume incidents. We mitigate via dry run, de-dupe, and narrowing enforcement to the In Progress transition.
2026-02-10 (Dev Patel): This is the #1 tooling gap coming out of the escalation playbook refresh. On-call asked for consistent context before pages; we can’t rely on training alone. Please start with dry-run comments so we can tune the required fields list.
2026-02-11 (Dylan Brooks): Drafted Rule 1 + Rule 3 in Jira Automation (disabled). Need confirmation on exact field names:
- Customer Tier (single select)
- Affected Region(s) (multi)
- Model / Endpoint (text vs select)
- Impact Summary (textarea)
- Request IDs (textarea)
If any of these don’t exist consistently, I’ll align to the Jira field guidelines page and update it with exact names.
2026-02-12 (Owen Phillips): +1 on blocking only at In Progress. During active incidents we triage quickly and fill fields while we investigate. If we block earlier, we’ll end up fighting the workflow. Required: region, model/endpoint, impact summary, and request IDs/timestamps window.
2026-02-13 (Rachel Kim): For enterprise accounts, make sure reminders don’t imply we owe 30-min updates 24/7. Language should reference coverage windows (business hours vs after-hours) and say “per tier policy”.
2026-02-14 (Dylan Brooks): Implemented dry-run required-fields comment. Added suppression for labels security-sensitive/customer-sensitive. Next: set up scheduled JQL for first-response ‘at risk’ reminders. Need a Slack destination: #support-ops vs #support. Preference?
2026-02-14 (Dev Patel): Use #support-ops for reminders. #support is too noisy and will get ignored. For P0/P1 only, also @mention on-call coordinator in the comment (we can manually tune later).
2026-02-15 (Chris Osei): Please add a lightweight metric: count of tickets hitting triage-missing-context label and median time from New -> Triage. We want to show impact in the post-sprint metrics review.
2026-02-16 (Dylan Brooks): Known-issues prompt rule draft is ready but I’m holding it until we confirm keyword mapping to avoid spamming. I’ll ship SLA first-response reminders + triage dry run first, then enable known-issues prompts with limited categories (streaming + 429) as a pilot.
1) Confirm exact Jira field IDs/names with Support (Dev/PRiya Shah) and reconcile with Jira field guidelines page.
2) Enable Phase 1 dry run and monitor reminder volume + false positives for 48 hours.
3) Add de-dupe mechanism (label timestamp or entity property) before enabling scheduled reminders broadly.
4) Pilot known-issues prompt for streaming + 429 categories, then expand to Dedicated/Private/audit logs.

title: Burst p99 latency spikes on Dedicated chat traffic (suspected KV cache fragmentation / allocator churn)
content:
Burst p99 latency spikes on Dedicated chat traffic (suspected KV cache fragmentation / allocator churn)

Issue summary
- Customer reports burst-driven p99 latency spikes (10–30s) on Dedicated capacity in us-east during mixed-length chat traffic. Median latency stable, but tail degrades sharply during bursts and high request churn.

Customer impact
- Production user-facing chat product experiences timeouts + retries when bursts happen (customer sees elevated 5xx from their upstream due to timeouts).
- Customer SLO target: p99 < 2.5s for streaming-first response; currently p99 intermittently 12–28s during bursts.

Customer environment
- Customer: Northwind Analytics
- Tier: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Workload: chat completions, mixed prompt lengths (short prompts + occasional long context ~8k tokens), sustained decode with bursty arrival
- Runtime: runtime-1.21.x (customer pool) at time of initial report
- Client behavior: retries after 12s; concurrency spikes at top-of-hour batch jobs

Symptoms observed (initial)
- Tail latency spikes correlate with GPU memory pressure events, allocator stalls, and opportunistic KV evictions.
- No evidence of network/TLS issues; primarily runtime scheduling/allocator behavior.

Reproduction hints provided by customer
- Burst traffic: 4–6x baseline QPS for 2–4 minutes, repeated 1–3 times/hour
- Mixed sequence lengths: ~70% short, ~25% medium, ~5% long contexts

Diagnostics requested
1) Request IDs + timestamps for worst spikes
2) Response headers (x-redwood-request-id / model / region)
3) Any client-side timeouts / retry counts

Internal investigation notes
- Suspected KV arena fragmentation due to long-lived allocations + churn.
- Next steps: enable fragmentation/compaction metrics, capture allocator snapshots, and evaluate canary runtime-1.22 compaction feature behind flag.

Links / escalations
- Slack escalation: sources/slack/support/1768159022.json
- Runtime discussion: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1767311205.json, sources/slack/eng-runtime/1767394021.json
- Canary incident thread (later): sources/slack/incidents/1767735109.json
- Oncall procedures draft: sources/slack/eng-oncall/1767660044.json

Relevant logs (excerpt)
- 2026-01-29T19:42:11Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A model=rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct phase=decode msg="decode step stalled waiting for kv page" stall_ms=1640 kv_free_pages=12 kv_frag_ratio=0.61
- 2026-01-29T19:42:13Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A msg="kv eviction triggered" reason="alloc_fail" evicted_sequences=3 tier="dedicated" pinned_skipped=1
- 2026-01-29T19:42:18Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A msg="oom_avoided_shedding" shed_requests=2 pool=northwind-us-east-03

Dashboards (internal)
- Dedicated pool latency: Grafana > Dedicated / Pool / Request latency (p50/p95/p99) (northwind-us-east-03)
- GPU memory + allocator: Grafana > Serving runtime / KV cache health (fragmentation, free pages, evictions)
- Traces: Tracing > request exemplars filtered by request_id(s) from customer

Hypothesis
- KV cache allocator fragmentation rises during bursts; compaction/eviction currently happens at poor times, causing decode stalls and p99 spikes. Feature work in progress (runtime-1.22) expected to reduce fragmentation via budgeted compaction + tier-aware eviction.

2026-01-29 20:03 (Paula Mendes - Support): Created ticket from customer escalation. Customer reports p99 spikes up to 28s during burst windows; baseline p99 ~1.8s. Asked for 10 request IDs and approximate timestamps + confirmation of client timeouts.
2026-01-29 20:26 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Looking at northwind-us-east-03. Confirm tail spikes align with GPU memory pressure + allocator churn. Not seeing gateway 5xx first; latency originates in runtime. Recommend enabling new kv fragmentation counters if available in their current runtime build; otherwise need a canary upgrade.
2026-01-29 21:10 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Pulled logs around 19:40–19:50Z. Seeing repeated "decode stalled waiting for kv page" and "alloc_fail" bursts. Flagging Runtime team. Linking #support thread sources/slack/support/1768159022.json.
2026-01-29 22:04 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): This looks consistent with fragmentation + poor-timing evictions. We have fragmentation metrics landing (PR-19342) and budgeted compaction in runtime-1.22 behind flag. Propose: 1) get metrics in their pool; 2) run canary on a subset of traffic; 3) keep kill-switch ready.
2026-01-30 09:18 (Allison Grant - Observability): If we can roll the metrics build, please ensure we wire: kv_frag_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_compaction_time_ms, kv_evictions_total, and decode_stall_ms. Standard naming in Confluence page linked in ticket.
2026-01-30 13:37 (Paula Mendes - Support): Customer provided sample request IDs + confirmed top-of-hour batch causes 5–6x burst. They see client timeouts at 12s; retries amplify traffic. Customer asked if there is a near-term mitigation besides increasing capacity.
2026-01-30 14:05 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Short-term mitigation: raise prefill/decode concurrency caps slightly to reduce queueing, but may worsen memory pressure. Prefer to avoid. Suggest temporary traffic smoothing (customer-side) + we proceed with runtime canary w/ metrics and compaction flag off first.
2026-01-31 10:22 (Connor O’Brien - Release): We can cut a dedicated-pool canary build of runtime-1.22.0-rc2 for northwind-us-east-03. Default compaction flag OFF; metrics ON. Target: 5% traffic via router policy. ETA 2–3 hours after approval.
2026-01-31 12:11 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Approval granted with guardrails: rollback if p99 worsens >20% for 10 min OR if kv_bytes_moved spikes correlate with decode stalls. See incident playbook thread sources/slack/eng-oncall/1767660044.json.
2026-01-31 16:02 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Canary deployed (5% traffic) runtime-1.22.0-rc2 with metrics enabled, compaction OFF. Observing kv_frag_ratio rising to ~0.58 during bursts (baseline ~0.25). Evictions also spike (alloc_fail). Confirms fragmentation hypothesis.
2026-02-01 09:44 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): Next step: enable compaction flag with conservative budget (bytes/time) on canary only. Recommendation: compaction_budget_ms_per_tick=0.3ms, max_bytes_moved_per_s=256MB, trigger_frag_ratio=0.45. Ensure kill-switch config propagation is verified first (PR-19422).
2026-02-01 11:20 (Benji Okafor - Rollout/Flags): Kill-switch propagation validated in us-east (config commit -> runtime acknowledged in ~35s). Safe-disable semantics: stops scheduling new compaction steps; in-flight relocation completes per-step then halts. (See platform thread sources/slack/eng-platform/1768080411.json.)
2026-02-01 13:08 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Enabled compaction on canary (5%). Immediate effect: kv_frag_ratio peaks lower (~0.42) and returns to baseline faster post-burst. p99 improved during 14:00Z burst window (canary cohort p99 3.1s vs control 11.6s). No throughput drop detected at p50. Logging exemplar traces added (PR-19405) for correlation.
2026-02-02 08:57 (Paula Mendes - Support): Updated customer: we identified root cause as allocator fragmentation under bursty mixed-length traffic; we have mitigation in canary that is improving p99 materially. Customer agrees to keep current capacity and retest after we expand canary.
2026-02-03 17:31 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Hit an edge case during higher churn test (cancelled requests) causing transient allocator leak suspicion. Runtime patched via PR-19440. We paused canary expansion pending patch; compaction remained ON for 5% cohort with no customer-visible incident.
2026-02-04 12:26 (Connor O’Brien - Release): runtime-1.22.1 hotfix with cancellation fix is ready for dedicated canary. Plan: upgrade canary nodes, keep compaction ON w/ conservative budgets, expand to 25% if stable for 24h.
2026-02-05 15:18 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): After 24h on 25%: p99 improved ~55–70% during bursts; no OOM/forced shedding. Eviction rate down; decode stalls reduced. Proceeding to 100% within Northwind pool with rollback window open. Alert tuning notes tracked separately in sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/kv-compaction-alert-tuning-notes.json.
2026-02-06 10:42 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Rolled to 100% of northwind-us-east-03. Observed top-of-hour burst: p99 2.7s (prev 12–28s). kv_frag_ratio stays <0.45 with compaction. No capacity changes needed.
2026-02-07 09:10 (Paula Mendes - Support): Customer confirms p99 stable across three burst windows; remaining issue is occasional client-side timeout at 12s on rare long-context requests (expected). Customer requested a summary + plan for making this default for Dedicated tiers.
2026-02-08 14:30 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): Summarized internally: compaction + tier-aware eviction will roll out broadly in runtime-1.22 with staged guardrails. This ticket can be resolved; follow-ups tracked in SUP-28472 for canary regression handling and INT-11904 for dashboard defaults.
Root cause confirmed as KV cache allocator fragmentation under bursty mixed-length workloads causing allocation stalls + poorly-timed evictions, leading to decode stalls and p99 spikes. Mitigation deployed by upgrading Northwind’s dedicated pool to runtime-1.22.1 (canary -> 100%) with fragmentation metrics enabled and budgeted KV compaction turned on (conservative budget/thresholds) plus cancellation edge-case fix. Post-rollout: burst p99 reduced from 12–28s to ~2.7–3.5s; forced shedding/OOM-avoid events eliminated during observed bursts.
Keep compaction enabled for Northwind dedicated pool; maintain kill-switch readiness during first 2 weeks post-rollout.
Share customer-facing summary + guidance on client timeout expectations for rare long-context outliers (PM-611 link tracked outside Jira).
Ensure dashboards include kv_frag_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_evictions_total, and decode_stall_ms panels by default (tracked in INT-11904).
Continue staged rollout of runtime-1.22 compaction defaults across other dedicated pools; watch for regressions (SUP-28472).

title: TypeScript SDK retries on HTTP 400 responses, causing duplicate request + billing concern
content:
TypeScript SDK retries on HTTP 400 responses, causing duplicate request + billing concern

Issue summary:
Northwind AI reports that the Redwood TypeScript SDK is retrying requests that return HTTP 400 (Bad Request). They observed multiple request IDs for what they believe is a single client call, and raised concern about duplicate billing and/or duplicated side effects in their application.

Impact:
- Customer observed 2–3 identical requests sent for a single application action when the API responds with 400.
- Customer concerned this could lead to duplicate charges and/or duplicated downstream actions (they log each attempt and tie it to billing / user-visible behavior).
- Support + on-call had difficulty triaging because TS error surface did not clearly indicate whether the error was retryable and what triggered the retry.

Customer report (from email + support portal):
- SDK: @redwood-ai/sdk (TypeScript) v2.8.0 (customer-reported)
- Runtime: Node 18
- Pattern: calling chat.completions.create() with a request that sometimes returns 400 (validation failure). SDK appears to retry anyway.
- Evidence: logs show 3 request_id values within ~2 seconds, all 400, same payload.

Environment:
- Region: us-east-1
- Endpoint: api.redwoodinference.com

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use TS SDK v2.8.0.
2) Send an invalid request that triggers a gateway/service 400 (e.g., missing required field or invalid parameter type).
3) Observe SDK retry loop (backoff) and multiple requests emitted.

Expected behavior:
- 400s should not be retried by default.
- The SDK should return a non-retryable, typed error and include request_id if present.

Actual behavior:
- In certain 400 responses, the retry middleware treats the failure as retryable and retries up to the default max attempts.
- Customer sees multiple request IDs (one per attempt).

Notes / hypotheses:
- The retry middleware appears to misclassify some 400 responses as “network errors” due to an exception during error body parsing (e.g., non-JSON error body or unexpected content-type). When parse fails, status is not propagated to the retry classifier.
- This is aligned with other parity findings: different SDKs handle “error parsing failure” differently; TS path can drop status_code and request_id.

Billing clarification (preliminary):
- Platform billing is token-based for successful generations/embeddings. 400 responses should not bill tokens; however, the customer may still see request counts and/or gateway logs that look like “multiple attempts”, and they may have internal metering tied to request volume.
- Independently of billing, duplicate attempts can create duplicate application side effects if the customer couples the API call to a non-idempotent operation.

Request IDs provided by customer (example set):
- rw_req_01HNTW9VZ9J2R3… (400)
- rw_req_01HNTW9W1P8K5A… (400)
- rw_req_01HNTW9W3F0M2C… (400)
(These were within one client action window; exact IDs stored in the private Zendesk attachment, not reproduced here.)

Ask:
- Confirm whether TS SDK is retrying 400s and under what conditions.
- Provide workaround to customer ASAP.
- Align with SDK parity initiative: retryable codes + typed error taxonomy + conformance tests to prevent regressions.
2026-01-29 09:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Acknowledged customer escalation. Asked for: TS SDK version, snippet showing retry config (if any), and 3 request_ids + approximate timestamps. Noted that SDK retries are expected on 429/5xx, but not on 400. Opened as P1 due to billing concern.

Shared immediate workaround: set maxRetries: 0 in client config until we confirm behavior.
2026-01-29 10:02 PT — Customer (Northwind AI) via support portal
Confirmed @redwood-ai/sdk 2.8.0, Node 18, running behind a corporate proxy. They see 3 attempts on a single call when the error is 400. They associate retries with possible double-charging because their internal cost dashboard counts requests. They asked whether Redwood bills for failed requests.

They provided logs showing three request IDs and identical payload hash.
2026-01-29 10:30 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalation Eng)
Pulled gateway logs for the provided request_id set. Confirmed: all three requests returned HTTP 400 with ~5–20 ms service time. No streaming involved. Response size small. Error body for at least one attempt was not JSON (content-type text/plain) due to an upstream validation error path.

Conclusion: the client truly sent 3 requests. Not a duplicate server-side processing artifact.
2026-01-29 11:15 PT — Ibrahim Khan (SDK TL) (internal note)
This matches a known parity issue: TS retry middleware can treat “failed to parse error response” as retryable because it throws before constructing the HttpError with status_code. If the retry classifier sees a generic error without status, it goes down the network-retry path. Need to ensure status is captured even if body parsing fails, and never retry 400.

Flagging Dana Lo to investigate in TS repo; also aligns with ENG-5126 error taxonomy work.
2026-01-29 13:05 PT — Dana Lo (TS SDK Owner)
Reproduced locally with v2.8.0:
- When error response is JSON, status=400 is preserved and shouldRetry=false.
- When error response is text/plain (or JSON parse throws), the SDK throws a generic error prior to wrapping it, so our retry middleware sees “unknown error” and retries.

Plan:
1) Refactor error parsing so we always preserve HTTP status + headers and build a typed error even when body parsing fails.
2) Tighten shouldRetry to require an explicit retryable classification (429/5xx/408/504 + network timeouts) rather than defaulting unknown errors to retry.
3) Add conformance coverage: 400 with non-JSON body must not retry.

ETA: patch release within a week; will link PR.
2026-01-29 14:10 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Responded to customer with billing clarification:
- Redwood does not bill tokens for requests that fail with 4xx before generation.
- They may see multiple request records because the client retried.

Provided mitigation until fix is released:
- Configure client retries off (maxRetries: 0) or restrict retryableStatusCodes to [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
- Log request_id + retry_count for correlation.

Asked whether they rely on any side-effectful behavior tied to request submission; recommended idempotency keys where applicable (even though chat/embeddings are typically safe, their surrounding workflow might not be).
2026-01-31 16:42 PT — Dana Lo
Opened fix PR and requested review: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1298-unify-retry-middleware-and-error-shapes.json
Key changes:
- Ensure HttpError is constructed even when response body parse fails.
- Attach status_code, request_id (if present), and retryable flag.
- Update retry classifier: do not retry when status_code is 400–499 (except 408/429), regardless of parse failures.

Also added tests for non-JSON 400 response body.
2026-02-02 09:05 PT — Allison Grant (SRE/Standards)
Reviewed retry classification against standard. Confirmed retryable defaults should include 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 + network errors/timeouts, and must not include 400. Requested one additional guard: if Retry-After is present on a 4xx that is not 429, ignore it for retries.

Suggested adding telemetry fields (retry_count, status_code, request_id) to align with the parity logging plan.
2026-02-03 11:20 PT — Dana Lo
Merged fix + follow-up for Retry-After parsing/jitter alignment: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1307-retry-after-parsing-and-backoff-jitter.json
Cut release v2.8.2.
Release notes include: “Fix: do not retry HTTP 400 when error body parsing fails; improved typed errors with request_id + retryable flag.”
2026-02-03 12:00 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Informed customer of v2.8.2 and provided upgrade guidance + confirmation steps:
- Upgrade @redwood-ai/sdk to 2.8.2.
- Run a controlled invalid request; verify only one request_id appears and retry_count remains 0.
- Keep maxRetries: 0 in prod until upgrade completes.

Re-answered billing question: token billing not incurred for these 400s; if they need an invoice-level confirmation, we can route to finance but logs indicate no successful generations on those request_ids.
2026-02-06 15:37 PT — Customer (Northwind AI)
Upgraded to 2.8.2 in staging. Confirmed no retries on 400 anymore. Their internal request counter is now consistent. Asked for a short written statement they can share internally that 4xx validation failures do not incur token charges.

No further issues.
2026-02-10 10:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Provided final billing statement and closed ticket. Customer confirmed resolved in production after rollout.

Follow-ups:
- Ensure conformance suite covers “400 + non-JSON body” across SDKs.
- Ensure docs/migration notes mention the retry classifier change and how to tune maxRetries.
2026-02-10 10:20 PT — Ibrahim Khan (internal)
Logged as an input to SDK parity effort: this bug is a concrete example of why error taxonomy must preserve status_code/request_id even on parse failures. Will reference in parity matrix and conformance fixtures.
Resolved in TypeScript SDK v2.8.2 by ensuring HTTP status/request_id are preserved even when error-body parsing fails, and by tightening retry classification so 400 is never retried by default. Customer mitigated by disabling retries until upgrade. Billing concern addressed: 4xx validation failures did not incur token charges.
Customer upgraded to TS SDK v2.8.2; confirmed 400 responses are not retried and internal metering no longer shows duplicate attempts. Provided written clarification that 4xx validation errors do not incur token billing.

title: Request exemption: higher burst limit for enterprise chat route (/v1/chat/completions) during market-open traffic spikes
content:
Request exemption: higher burst limit for enterprise chat route (/v1/chat/completions) during market-open traffic spikes

Issue summary
Proxima Bank is requesting a temporary increase to their burst allowance on the enterprise-protected chat route (/v1/chat/completions) in eu-west. They report predictable short spikes at market open (08:55–09:10 local) where they see elevated 429s despite overall sustained RPS being within their contracted baseline.

Customer request
- Increase burst capacity (token bucket burst) for /v1/chat/completions in eu-west.
- Keep sustained rate unchanged (they are not asking for a permanent throughput increase).
- They want the change to apply only to their tenant + route group (no broader tier default changes).

Impact observed (customer)
- During spikes, client sees 429 responses with reason=quota_exceeded and occasionally reason=overload_admission when the region is under pressure.
- Primary business impact is delayed responses for end-user chat assistant at market open; they can tolerate some throttling but want fewer hard 429s during the first 10–15 minutes.

Environment
- Hosted API (enterprise tier)
- Region: eu-west
- Route: /v1/chat/completions
- Model: rw-chat-large (pinned)
- Client uses streaming; retries are currently immediate (no jitter) per their current implementation.

Qualification notes (Support/CS)
- Customer is enterprise with explicit latency/availability SLO expectations.
- Pattern appears bursty and time-bounded; sustained usage is stable.
- Customer can implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter, but wants Redwood-side burst adjustment as primary mitigation.

Risk assessment (internal)
- Increasing burst allowance can shift pressure onto shared enterprise GPU pools during localized demand spikes.
- Must avoid degrading other protected enterprise tenants on the same route group.
- Exception must be scoped (tenant + route + region), time-boxed, and monitored.
- Must keep decision auditable and reversible (feature-flag/config driven; clear rollback criteria).

Requested outcome
- Approve a time-limited burst exemption with guardrails and monitoring, plus customer guidance to add retry backoff/jitter and concurrency caps.

Attachments/References
- Customer provided sample timestamps and request IDs in email to TAM; copied into internal comment thread below.
- Related to earlier burst event tracking in SUP-18433 (latency + shedding correlation).
2026-01-18 09:12 (Liam O'Rourke, Reporter)
Customer (Proxima Bank) asking for higher burst on /v1/chat/completions (eu-west). They can live with same sustained but want fewer 429s in first ~15 min of trading day. They shared a sample from today: 08:57–09:04 saw ~6–9% 429s. Request IDs: rwreq_9f2c… rwreq_aa31… (sent via email). Please advise if we can grant a scoped exception and how to message this alongside client-side backoff.

Priority requested: medium, but time-sensitive (next market open tomorrow).
2026-01-18 09:40 (Owen Phillips, Assignee)
Acknowledged. Moving to Triage. I’m pulling gateway metrics for tenant + route. Initial guess: they’re hitting burst bucket, not sustained. Will confirm reason code breakdown (quota_exceeded vs overload_admission). Also asking them to confirm their retry behavior (backoff+jitter) and max concurrency.
2026-01-18 10:05 (Aisha Bello)
From SRE perspective: OK to consider a time-boxed burst exemption if we keep it tenant-scoped and monitor shed/admission. Please ensure we don’t raise tier defaults. Provide rollback trigger: if enterprise p95 latency burn > 1.5x baseline for 10 min or overload_admission for other tenants increases.

Recommend we pair with customer guidance: exponential backoff with jitter + cap outstanding streams.
2026-01-18 10:22 (Cole Summers)
Quota config supports per-tenant overrides for burst tokens on route-group. We can raise burst without raising sustained rate. For eu-west chat route-group, default enterprise burst is currently 2x sustained. We can set Proxima to 3x for a limited window. Needs Product/SRE signoff.

Note: if region is in overload_admission mode, higher burst may still be shed (correct behavior).
2026-01-18 10:47 (Amara Diallo)
Confirming on gateway side: 429 headers differentiate quota vs overload. If they’re seeing quota_exceeded predominantly, burst change will help. If overload_admission dominates, this is capacity pressure and exemption won’t fix.

Also: please ensure customer parses Retry-After and uses jitter; immediate retries amplify the burst bucket depletion.
2026-01-18 11:10 (Owen Phillips)
Analysis summary (eu-west, last 3 market opens):
- 429 breakdown for Proxima on /v1/chat/completions: ~80–90% quota_exceeded in the 08:55–09:10 window; overload_admission appears intermittently (~1–2%) when regional pressure is elevated.
- Sustained RPS outside the window is within baseline; peak is ~2.6–2.9x baseline for 2–6 minutes.

Conclusion: a burst exception is likely to reduce the majority of their 429s during market open. It will not eliminate overload_admission when the region is under protection, but those events are rare in their traces.
2026-01-18 11:26 (Nikhil Sharma)
Product approval: OK with a temporary burst exemption for Proxima provided it is:
1) tenant + route + region scoped,
2) time-boxed (2 weeks) with renewal requiring review,
3) accompanied by customer action items (backoff/jitter, concurrency limits),
4) documented in ticket with explicit rollback criteria.

Please tag SRE lead for final go/no-go.
2026-01-18 11:44 (Rafael Mendes)
SRE approval with guardrails.

Proposed config:
- Route group: chat.completions.enterprise_protected
- Tenant: Proxima Bank
- Region: eu-west
- Change: burst multiplier 2.0x -> 3.0x (no sustained rate increase)
- Duration: 14 days (auto-expire), with review at day 10.

Rollback criteria:
- If enterprise route-group p95 latency increases >15% for >10 min attributable to admission pressure, or if shed/admission for other enterprise tenants increases materially during the same time window.

Please coordinate change window outside market open if possible and annotate dashboards.
2026-01-18 12:05 (Jordan Lee)
Policy engine note: add an audit log entry for this override (who approved, TTL, scope). If using the standard override mechanism, it will show in decision logs and the admin debug endpoint. Please include approval trail in this ticket (names + timestamp) and attach TTL.

No additional engineering required if we use existing override schema.
2026-01-18 14:20 (Owen Phillips)
Customer comms draft sent to TAM/CS (Rachel) for review:
- We can raise burst for eu-west chat route for 2 weeks.
- This addresses quota-based throttles; during regional overload you may still see overload_admission 429s.
- Action items: implement exponential backoff w/ jitter; honor Retry-After; cap concurrent streams; avoid immediate retries.

Pending: scheduling config change and confirming expiration mechanism.
2026-01-19 07:10 (Benji Okafor)
Override applied via config (tenant-scoped) and validated in staging. Rolled to eu-west prod at 07:05 UTC.

Details recorded:
- burst_multiplier=3.0
- scope: tenant=proxima-bank, route_group=chat.completions.enterprise_protected, region=eu-west
- TTL: expires 2026-02-02 07:00 UTC

Added dashboard annotation for change window and set reminder to review on 2026-01-29.
2026-01-19 10:18 (Rachel Kim)
Customer updated. They confirmed they will implement retry backoff + jitter by end of week. They appreciate the time-boxed approach and agree to share metrics after 3 market opens.

They asked whether this affects other regions (no) and whether it changes billing (no).
2026-01-21 09:32 (Owen Phillips)
Post-change check (2 market opens):
- Proxima 429 rate in 08:55–09:10 window dropped from ~6–9% to ~1–2%.
- Remaining 429s mostly correlate with client-side immediate retries (still visible in traces) and occasional overload_admission (~0.3–0.5% depending on regional pressure).
- No detectable negative impact to other enterprise tenants on route-group; p95 stable.

Next: keep exemption until TTL; review at day 10; follow up on their backoff rollout.
2026-01-23 16:40 (Owen Phillips)
Marking Resolved.
Resolution: Approved and applied a tenant/route/region-scoped burst multiplier increase (2.0x -> 3.0x) for Proxima Bank on /v1/chat/completions in eu-west for 14 days (auto-expiring 2026-02-02). Customer advised on proper retry/backoff and concurrency limits. Monitoring shows reduced quota-based 429s with no adverse impact to other enterprise traffic.
Temporary burst exemption approved and implemented. Burst allowance for Proxima Bank (enterprise) on /v1/chat/completions in eu-west increased from 2.0x to 3.0x sustained rate, with no sustained quota change. Scope is tenant + route group + region; TTL auto-expires 2026-02-02 07:00 UTC. Customer instructed to honor Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter + concurrency caps. No billing changes. Monitoring after rollout shows significant reduction in quota_exceeded 429s and no measurable degradation for other protected enterprise traffic.

title: Private install: Grafana loads but no Redwood dashboards (minimum observability pack)
content:
Private install: Grafana loads but no Redwood dashboards (minimum observability pack)

Issue summary
- Customer completed Redwood Private install (including the “observability minimum pack”). Grafana UI is reachable and Prometheus is scraping targets, but there are no Redwood dashboards visible under Browse/Dashboards.

Customer impact
- Customer platform team cannot validate runtime health post-install and is blocked on their internal acceptance checklist for go-live.
- No production outage, but reduces operational visibility and delays launch.

Customer environment (as provided)
- Deployment type: On-prem / air-gapped
- Installer version: redwood-private-installer v1.12.3 (offline bundle)
- Helm charts: redwood-helm-charts 1.12.3
- Observability pack: included in offline bundle (customer unsure which pack version)
- Namespace(s): redwood-system (control plane), redwood-runtime (data plane), monitoring (Grafana/Prometheus)
- Grafana: 10.4.x (from our bundled chart)
- Prometheus: kube-prometheus-stack (bundled)
- StorageClass: longhorn
- NetworkPolicies: enabled (customer baseline)

What’s expected
- Redwood-provisioned dashboards should appear automatically (Runtime Overview, Control Plane Health, GPU Fleet, etc.) in Grafana under a “Redwood” folder (or similarly named folder) after install.

What’s observed
- Grafana is up and login works.
- Datasource exists (“Prometheus”) and can query basic metrics (up, kube_pod_info).
- No dashboards in the Redwood folder; in some cases no Redwood folder at all.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Install Redwood Private with observability pack enabled using offline bundle.
2) Access Grafana -> Dashboards.
3) Observe no Redwood dashboards.

Initial hypotheses
- Dashboards ConfigMaps not present in cluster (missing from offline bundle or Helm values disabled).
- ConfigMaps present but not labeled for Grafana sidecar discovery.
- Grafana sidecar for dashboards disabled or misconfigured (watch namespace/label selector mismatch).
- Grafana provisioning path not mounted / permissions issue.
- RBAC preventing Grafana sidecar from listing ConfigMaps in target namespaces.

Key customer-provided snippets
1) kubectl get cm -n monitoring | grep -i redwood => (empty)
2) kubectl get pods -n monitoring => grafana-xxxxx Running
3) Grafana logs (excerpt):
   - "logger=provisioning.dashboard t=2025-07-18T16:02:11.913Z level=info msg=\"Starting Dashboard provisioning\""
   - No subsequent "Dashboard provisioned" entries

Support request
- Identify whether dashboards were packaged/applied.
- Provide a workaround to get dashboards installed in Grafana for air-gapped cluster.
- Confirm the correct Helm values/settings for the minimum pack and whether any known issue exists in v1.12.3 offline bundle.

Resolution summary (final)
- Root cause: Grafana dashboards were included in the cluster as ConfigMaps, but Grafana’s dashboard sidecar was watching only the monitoring namespace and a different label key than what the Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps used in 1.12.3 offline bundle. Additionally, RBAC was missing list/watch on ConfigMaps in redwood-system/redwood-runtime.
- Fix: Update Helm values to (a) align the sidecar label selector with the Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps and (b) allow cross-namespace discovery OR copy dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring. Applied RBAC fix and restarted Grafana.
- Outcome: Redwood dashboards appeared under folder “Redwood Private (Minimum Pack)” within 5 minutes; customer confirmed panels populated.

Workaround / customer steps (executed)
A) Confirm dashboards ConfigMaps exist:
- kubectl get cm -A | grep -E "redwood|observability|grafana-dashboard"

B) Update Grafana sidecar + RBAC (preferred) via values override:
- Set:
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.enabled=true
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.searchNamespace=ALL
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.label=grafana_dashboard
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.labelValue="1"
- Add RBAC for grafana sidecar service account to list/watch ConfigMaps in redwood-system and redwood-runtime.
- Helm upgrade kube-prometheus-stack / grafana release.

C) Restart Grafana:
- kubectl rollout restart deploy/grafana -n monitoring

D) Validate:
- Grafana -> Dashboards -> folder appears
- Prometheus datasource queries for redwood_* recording rules and runtime metrics return data

Notes
- If customer security policy blocks searchNamespace=ALL, alternative is copying the dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace with the expected label (documented below in comments).
2025-07-18 09:12 (Dev Patel - Support)
Created ticket from customer email + #support handoff. Requested environment details and installer/Helm versions. Asked for: `kubectl get cm -A | grep grafana` and Grafana pod logs around provisioning start.
2025-07-18 10:03 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
Install finished successfully and health checks passed. We can log into Grafana, Prometheus datasource works, but there are no Redwood dashboards. `kubectl get cm -n monitoring | grep -i redwood` returns nothing. We are air-gapped and used the offline bundle from Redwood. NetworkPolicies are enabled cluster-wide.
2025-07-18 10:26 (Bruno Silva - PS / Private Deployments)
Likely either (1) dashboards not applied because the pack values were off, or (2) dashboards are created in a different namespace than Grafana’s sidecar is watching. Can you run `kubectl get cm -A | grep -i grafana` and `kubectl describe deploy grafana -n monitoring` (look for sidecar args)?
2025-07-18 11:02 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
`kubectl get cm -A | grep -i grafana` shows:
- redwood-system/redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1
- redwood-runtime/redwood-runtime-dashboards-1
Both have labels:
- app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm
- redwood.ai/observability-pack=true
No label like grafana_dashboard=1.
`kubectl describe deploy grafana -n monitoring` shows sidecar enabled but label selector is `grafana_dashboard=1` and namespace is monitoring only.
2025-07-18 11:20 (Dylan Brooks - Dashboards/tooling)
That explains it: our dashboard ConfigMaps in 1.12.3 are labeled `redwood.ai/observability-pack=true` (not `grafana_dashboard=1`). Either update sidecar label selector to match our label, or (safer) add `grafana_dashboard=1` label to the existing ConfigMaps. Also, sidecar is only monitoring namespace; if ConfigMaps live in redwood-system/redwood-runtime you need searchNamespace=ALL or copy the ConfigMaps into monitoring.
Proposed immediate workaround:
1) Label ConfigMaps: `kubectl label cm -n redwood-system redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1 grafana_dashboard=1 --overwrite` and same for runtime.
2) Set sidecar searchNamespace=ALL (or copy CMs to monitoring if ALL is disallowed).
3) Restart Grafana deployment.
Longer-term we should align the Helm chart defaults/labels for private minimum pack.
2025-07-18 12:05 (Bruno Silva - PS / Private Deployments)
Customer prefers not to run sidecar across all namespaces due to security review. Suggested option: copy dashboards ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace.
Commands:
- `kubectl get cm -n redwood-system redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1 -o yaml | sed 's/namespace: redwood-system/namespace: monitoring/' | kubectl apply -n monitoring -f -`
- Repeat for `redwood-runtime/redwood-runtime-dashboards-1`
- Label the new CMs: `kubectl label cm -n monitoring <cm-name> grafana_dashboard=1 --overwrite`
Then restart Grafana.
Also asked customer to confirm Grafana SA has list/watch on ConfigMaps in monitoring (it does by default).
2025-07-18 14:18 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
We copied both ConfigMaps into monitoring and labeled `grafana_dashboard=1`. After restarting Grafana, we now see a “Redwood Private (Minimum Pack)” folder and dashboards are present. Panels were initially empty; after ~2 minutes they started populating. This unblocks us.
Question: is there an official supported fix so we don’t have to maintain copies after upgrades?
2025-07-18 15:01 (Dev Patel - Support)
Confirmed the workaround is acceptable short-term but we want a supported path. Looping in SRE/Telemetry to confirm recommended values for private minimum pack. Also linking runbook: private observability day-2 operations (Grafana provisioning section).
2025-07-19 09:42 (Rafael Mendes - SRE)
Recommendation for supported installs: either (A) keep dashboards in monitoring namespace to avoid cross-namespace watch, or (B) explicitly enable cross-namespace watch and add RBAC for grafana sidecar.
