For Private minimum pack we should default to (A) in air-gapped bundles to reduce security friction.
Also noted we’ve had a similar CI failure in INT-11804 where dashboards weren’t discovered due to label mismatch.
2025-07-19 11:10 (Connor O'Brien - Release/packaging)
Checked offline bundle manifest for 1.12.3: dashboards are included, but labels differ from kube-prometheus-stack defaults. This is tracked for backport in the private installer/helm wiring. Suggest we point customer to upgrading to 1.12.4 once released (will include corrected labels and/or chart values).
2025-07-21 16:30 (Dev Patel - Support)
Customer confirmed stable after 48h. No further action needed on their side until next upgrade. We provided guidance for keeping the copy step as part of their upgrade runbook if they remain on 1.12.3.
Closing ticket as resolved with workaround + upcoming product fix.
Internal follow-up: ensure minimum pack dashboards ship with `grafana_dashboard=1` (or chart default label is updated) and install places dashboards in monitoring namespace for air-gapped installs.
Resolved via workaround: copied Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace and labeled for Grafana sidecar discovery; restarted Grafana. Customer validated dashboards present and populated. Product follow-up identified to align labels/defaults in subsequent Private releases.
If you upgrade Redwood Private before the label/namespace fix is included, re-run the dashboard copy + label step (or opt into cross-namespace sidecar watch with RBAC). We will notify you once the supported default is available in a maintenance release.
Validate and backport dashboard label alignment for Private offline bundles (air-gapped) so kube-prometheus-stack Grafana sidecar discovers Redwood dashboards without manual copy.
Update Private day-2 runbook to include detection steps: where dashboards ConfigMaps live, required labels, and namespace watch settings.

title: Enterprise customer requests shadow evaluation metrics during upcoming model upgrade rollout (quality gates + dashboard/API)
content:
Enterprise customer requests shadow evaluation metrics during upcoming model upgrade rollout (quality gates + dashboard/API)

Issue summary
Northstar Customer Support AI (enterprise, Dedicated) is planning a production model upgrade within ~2 weeks and is requesting the ability to run shadow evaluations during rollout (mirror a sampled subset of production traffic to a candidate variant) and view quality deltas alongside latency/cost. They are asking for (a) a minimum set of quality metrics, (b) the ability to slice by route and workload segment, and (c) a "go/no-go" signal they can use as a rollout gate.

Customer context / timeline pressure
- Northstar has an internal change review on 2026-02-06 and wants evidence that the candidate model does not regress on: refusal/safety behavior, instruction-following, and output format compliance.
- They have had previous incidents during upgrades where average latency improved but answer quality degraded in subtle ways, which they did not catch until user tickets.
- They do not want any user-visible impact while collecting quality data.

Customer request (requirements)
1) Shadow traffic / mirroring
- Mirror 1–5% of production requests from Route: /v1/chat/completions (primary) to one or more candidate variants.
- Deterministic bucketing so repeated conversations are consistently assigned (so comparisons are meaningful over time).
- Fail-open guarantee: if shadow path errors, control response must still succeed and user latency must not change.

2) Quality metrics (minimum viable)
- Format adherence (JSON schema / tool-calling shape compliance) with a breakdown of failure reasons.
- Refusal rate / safety behavior: detect unexpected refusals and unexpected non-refusals for known sensitive intents.
- Instruction following (rubric score) and a "verbosity" / length drift indicator.
- Ability to export a small sample set of paired examples (control vs shadow output) for human review.

3) Visibility & gating
- Dashboard view with confidence intervals and time windows (1h/6h/24h).
- Alerting or at least a recommended threshold for "regression" (advisory is acceptable for first rollout).
- Attach results to a rollout / canary timeline so reviewers can see exactly what configuration/model was tested.

4) Data handling constraints
- Dedicated tenant with strict retention: prompts/responses retained for <= 7 days; prefer redaction and hashed identifiers.
- Ability to disable capture of raw prompts and store only scoring artifacts if needed.

Current limitations / notes
- The full "Shadow Experiments" feature is in progress. We may be able to enable a limited beta path for this tenant with guarded defaults (sampling cap, dimension cap) and provide a temporary dashboard + export.
- Need to confirm which scoring templates are production-ready for their workload and whether they require structured output evaluation.

Impact
- Customer states this is a blocker for approving the upgrade. Without a shadow quality signal, they will delay rollout or require a time-consuming manual offline evaluation.

Requested next steps
- Redwood to confirm feasibility and timeline for (1) shadow routing enablement on their tenant, (2) default metric bundle v1, and (3) dashboard access / export.
- If not feasible by 2026-02-06, provide an alternative: prompt-set eval-harness approach + guidance on sampling/power, plus a plan to run shadowing immediately after approval.

Owner notes (Support)
- This is aligned with the Shadow Traffic tool project scope. Need coordinated response across Rollouts (Paula), Evals (Jonas/Karthik), Telemetry (Logan/Nadia), and SRE (Sean/Allison) for guardrails + retention.

Attachments/refs
- HubSpot: sources/hubspot/company-northstar-customer-support-ai.json
- (Customer call notes) Fireflies: 2026-01-22 technical deep dive on shadow evals + rollouts
- Internal runbook draft: Shadow traffic rollout/rollback runbook (Confluence)

Open questions to resolve with customer
- Exact definition of "format adherence": strict JSON schema vs tool-call envelope compliance vs both.
- Whether they need per-intent segmentation (could increase cardinality risk).
- Whether shadowing should include streaming responses; if yes, what partial capture is acceptable.
- Which routes are in-scope for the first rollout (chat only vs embeddings/rerank).
2026-01-29 10:14 PT — Monica Patel (Support/Platform Enablement)
Acknowledged request from Northstar. Confirmed we can discuss limited beta access for shadow traffic + quality deltas. Asked for:
- target rollout date
- routes to include
- required metrics (must-have vs nice-to-have)
- data retention constraints (raw prompts allowed?)

Set expectation: likely advisory quality signals at launch; automatic rollback based on quality is not available yet.

Next: loop in Paula Mendes (Rollouts) + Jonas Weber (Evals) + Logan Wright (Telemetry) for feasibility and a proposed plan by EOW.
2026-01-30 09:02 PT — Customer (Northstar, Platform Eng lead)
Timeline: change review on 2026-02-06, rollout starts 2026-02-10 if approved.
Must-haves:
- shadow 2% production traffic
- format adherence + refusal drift + instruction-following rubric score
- dashboard with confidence bands (or at minimum: a daily summary with statistical significance)
- export 100–200 paired examples for audit
Constraints:
- retain prompts <= 7 days
- prefer hashed user identifiers; avoid storing full conversation histories if possible

They are OK with advisory gates but need a "recommended action" summary for reviewers (e.g., green/yellow/red).
2026-01-30 11:41 PT — Paula Mendes (Rollout policies)
We can support shadow sampling at the route level with deterministic bucketing (consistent hashing) and strict fail-open. For beta enablement we should:
- cap sampling at 2% (customer request fits)
- cap targets to 1–2 shadow variants
- ensure shadow request timeouts are < 150ms budget for routing path (async send)

Need SRE sign-off on guardrails and a kill switch plan. Also need to confirm that the Console view for quality deltas is available behind the feature flag for this tenant.
2026-01-31 14:10 PT — Jonas Weber (Evals/Scoring)
Metric feasibility:
- Format adherence: we can score tool-call envelope compliance + JSON parse success; strict schema validation requires customer-provided schema (not in v1). Proposed: v1 includes JSON parseable + required key presence.
- Refusal rate: can score via rubric template on shadow outputs; need to calibrate on their domain prompts (risk of false positives).
- Instruction-following: available as model-graded rubric; will pin rubric version for comparability.

Caveat: model-graded scoring adds compute cost; for 2% sampling we should be OK if we constrain max tokens captured/scored and use async queue with backpressure.
2026-02-01 10:55 PT — Allison Grant (Observability/Alerting)
Reminder on cardinality: no per-user or per-conversation IDs as metric labels. We can store hashed IDs in event payload for sampled examples only (separate store), but dashboards must aggregate by:
- tenant
- route
- model/control vs shadow
- region
- rubric_version

Proposed dashboards: quality delta overview (24h + rolling 6h) + scoring lag. Alerts: scoring lag and missing-data should page only if it impacts multiple tenants; for single tenant create ticket notifications.
2026-02-01 16:22 PT — Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Guardrails required before enabling on an enterprise tenant:
- circuit breaker if shadow target error rate > 10% for 5 min OR scoring queue lag > 30 min
- hard budget: user-path p99 latency delta <= 1% (shadowing must be strictly async/non-blocking)
- kill switch in control plane and documented rollback steps

If these are met, SRE OK with limited beta enablement for Northstar. Please ensure audit log entries are enabled for experiment creation/edits.
2026-02-02 09:18 PT — Monica Patel
Sent proposed plan to customer:
Option A (recommended): Enable limited beta shadow experiment for chat route at 2% sampling, 1 candidate variant, 7-day retention, redaction on by default. Provide Console dashboard access for quality deltas + export of paired examples.
Option B (fallback): If feature flag approval slips, run eval-harness prompt-set scoring using their provided prompt set and compare against candidate model offline; use this as change-review evidence.

Asked customer to confirm:
- whether streaming is enabled on their chat route (affects partial capture)
- whether they can provide a representative prompt set for calibration (for refusal/instruction-following rubrics).
2026-02-02 13:47 PT — Customer (Northstar)
Confirmed:
- Chat route is streaming-enabled for ~60% of traffic.
- They can provide a 300–500 prompt set for calibration by 2026-02-03.
- They want shadowing to cover streaming requests, but are OK if we only capture the final assembled output (not token-by-token).

They asked for written confirmation that user-path latency will not be impacted and that they can disable the experiment immediately if they see issues.
1) Paula Mendes to coordinate beta enablement + shadow policy config for Northstar tenant (target: 2026-02-03).
2) Jonas Weber to confirm rubric bundle v1 (format adherence JSON-parse + key checks, refusal drift rubric, instruction-following rubric) and provide rubric_version to pin.
3) Allison Grant to ensure dashboard access is enabled for tenant and dimensions are cardinality-safe.
4) Monica Patel to send customer a short enablement note including: fail-open behavior, retention defaults, and how to disable (kill switch) + expected time-to-see-metrics.
5) If any blockers by 2026-02-04: execute fallback Option B (eval-harness prompt set) for change review.
Coordinate with INT-912 for feature flag enablement workflow if needed. Ensure any prompt/response storage honors 7-day retention and redaction defaults. For streaming capture, align with current behavior: store final output only, mark partial=true when incomplete due to timeout.

title: Structured output: occasional invalid JSON returned (unterminated strings / trailing commas) leading to parse errors in customer app
content:
Structured output: occasional invalid JSON returned (unterminated strings / trailing commas) leading to parse errors in customer app

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent JSON parse failures when using Structured Output (schema-constrained responses). They are calling the Hosted API via TypeScript SDK and parsing the assistant message content as JSON. In ~1–3% of runs, the returned content is not valid JSON (examples include trailing commas, unterminated strings, and occasionally a partial object).

Impact:
- Production job failures in an agent workflow (their orchestrator expects valid JSON to drive downstream tool selection).
- Requires manual retries and/or fallback parsing.

Environment:
- Hosted API, prod
- Region: us-east
- Customer: AcmeAI (enterprise)
- SDK: TypeScript
- Models: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct (primary), redwood/qwen2.5-72b-instruct (A/B)

What the customer expected:
When requesting structured output with a JSON schema, assistant content should always be valid JSON that parses with JSON.parse, or the API should surface an explicit error.

What happened:
They occasionally receive a final assistant message that is close to JSON but fails parsing.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send chat request with response_format JSON schema.
2) Provide a prompt that asks for a list of objects with nested fields.
3) Run 100–200 times; observe a small number of invalid JSON responses.

Notes / suspicion:
- Customer uses streaming and attempts to parse incrementally on partial deltas (per their code snippet). They also observed failures in non-streaming mode but less frequently.
- They are not currently validating against schema; they only JSON.parse and then do ad-hoc field checks.

Example error (customer):
SyntaxError: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 842

Representative bad payload excerpt (redacted):
{"items":[{"id":"a1","confidence":0.83,}],"meta":{"source":"..."}}

Requested help:
- Confirmation of structured output guarantees per model.
- Recommended client-side handling: validation, retries, and streaming assembly.
- Whether this is a platform bug vs model behavior.
2025-02-11 09:18 PT — Priya Shah (Support): Ticket opened from support@ email. Assigned Sev2/P1 due to production impact but intermittent. Requested: request IDs, model, region, full request payload (minus secrets), and whether streaming is enabled.

Questions sent:
1) Are you parsing JSON on each stream chunk/delta or only after final event?
2) Can you share a single failing request_id so we can trace server-side logs?
3) Are you using response_format: { type: "json_schema" } or "json" mode equivalent?
2025-02-11 10:02 PT — Customer (AcmeAI): Provided two failing request_ids (rwreq_01HT…9K2 and rwreq_01HT…Q8V), confirmed streaming enabled. They parse as deltas arrive because they want early routing decisions. They send response_format with a JSON schema and set temperature=0.2. They confirmed the SDK example they started from was older and didn’t mention incremental parsing caveats.
2025-02-11 11:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalations): Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: invalid JSON likely caused by parsing before stream completion OR tool/assistant final assembly edge case. Asked for raw concatenated final content they receive (post-assembly) and whether they see any stream disconnect/reconnect events.
2025-02-11 13:55 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalations): Looked up traces for rwreq_01HT…9K2 in us-east. Server transcript shows multiple partial JSON deltas. Final message content (as stored) includes an extra trailing comma before closing bracket. No stream disconnect on server side.

Action: loop in SDK/DX for recommended handling and to confirm guarantee language (schema-constrained ≠ absolute guarantee for all models).
2025-02-12 09:07 PT — Wei Chen (Docs): Confirmed docs language needed tightening: structured output is “best-effort schema-constrained” depending on model family; examples should validate + retry. Working on adding a “Known pitfalls” section: (a) don’t parse during streaming, (b) validate against schema, (c) implement retry with corrective prompt.

Linked draft: structured-output-json-schema-guidance (Confluence).
2025-02-12 10:41 PT — Dana Lo (TS SDK): Noted our previous TS snippet encouraged JSON.parse on message.content without validation, and didn’t call out streaming incremental JSON. TS PR in flight to add runtime validation and a retry example (Ajv + zod-style checks), plus guidance to wait for final event when streaming.

Also: confirm we show response_format JSON schema in examples consistently across languages.
2025-02-12 12:20 PT — Brian Murphy (API/SDK semantics reviewer): Reminder: even with response_format=json_schema, some models can produce near-miss JSON under certain prompts (especially long nested lists). Recommended client behavior: strict assembly of the final assistant content, validate, then retry with a short “Fix to valid JSON only” instruction and set temperature=0.0 for the retry.

If streaming is needed, treat deltas as display-only until completion; do not route decisions on partial JSON.
2025-02-13 08:30 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalations): Sent guidance to customer:
- Do not JSON.parse on deltas; wait until stream completes and you have the final assembled assistant content.
- Validate against schema (Ajv) and reject outputs failing validation.
- Add a bounded retry (1–2 attempts) with temperature=0.0 and a repair instruction.
- Consider limiting output length / list sizes in the schema and prompt to reduce near-miss JSON.

Also requested they test non-streaming with the same schema to isolate any stream assembly issues.
2025-02-14 14:12 PT — Customer (AcmeAI): Tested with “parse only at end” and added Ajv validation. Fail rate improved but still saw ~0.5% invalid JSON (trailing comma). They asked whether Redwood can enforce stricter server-side validation or provide an API-level error instead of returning invalid JSON.
2025-02-14 16:05 PT — Ibrahim Khan (SDK parity TL): We don’t currently hard-fail server-side on schema noncompliance for all model families. For some models, we can detect invalid JSON late, but doing so universally can increase latency and/or cause false negatives.

Plan for docs/examples refresh:
- Make the guarantee language explicit per model (support matrix).
- Provide canonical retry/validation pattern (all SDKs).
- Add “repair” retry snippet and keep it consistent.

Resolution summary:
1) Root cause: combination of (a) customer parsing during streaming (incremental JSON) and (b) model-level near-miss JSON even under schema constraints for some prompts. Additionally, we identified a small streaming final-assembly corner case (fixed separately) that could exacerbate malformed output in rare sequences.

2) Workaround provided (now the recommended pattern):
- When streaming: treat deltas as partial text; do not JSON.parse until the final assistant message is fully assembled.
- Validate the final JSON against the provided JSON schema (e.g., Ajv in TypeScript).
- If JSON.parse or schema validation fails, retry 1–2 times with:
  - temperature=0.0
  - a short repair instruction (“Return ONLY valid JSON matching the schema. Do not include trailing commas.”)
  - optionally reduced max_output_tokens / smaller list sizes.

3) Documentation/examples updated:
- Added structured output guide with JSON schema + validation + retry pattern.
- Added runnable structured output sample app.

title: Variable accumulation window triggering intermittent p95/p99 inference latency spikes for dedicated tenant
content:
Variable accumulation window triggering intermittent p95/p99 inference latency spikes for dedicated tenant

Issue summary:
AtlasHealth reports intermittent p95/p99 inference latency spikes and occasional request timeouts for short streaming requests. Spikes started after a traffic pattern change on 2026-03-12 and correlate with increased short-lived stream volume (many < 200 token sessions).

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints experienced elevated p95/p99 latency (observed p99 from ~180ms baseline to 2.1s).
- A small fraction (~0.5%) of requests returned 504/timeouts during peak bursts.
- Affects production workloads for 3 AtlasHealth services (triage, summary, and alerts).

Environment:
- Tenant: AtlasHealth (dedicated pool)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Models: redwood/roberta-chat-13b-q4 pinned by customer
- Time window: first observed 2026-03-12 09:20 - recurring spikes 09:20-10:40 PST each day since.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Replay synthetic short streaming traffic that opens many concurrent short streams (median 80 tokens).
2) Sustain QPS of ~60 for 5-10 minutes with bursty arrival pattern (many short sessions).
3) Observe p95/p99 latency climb and intermittent 504s.

Observed behavior:
- The continuous batcher accumulation window appears to grow unpredictably when many short streams arrive in rapid succession.
- Batches sometimes hold open longer than configured linger thresholds, leading to increased tail latency and KV-cache warmup interactions.

Expected behavior:
- Batcher should flush according to configured linger and max_batch latencies, preventing sustained p99 spikes for short streams.

- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/atlashealth-tail-latency
- Support logs and request ids attached in 'logs' field below.

title: Tailback pressure causes 504 timeout for hyperlength single-turn generation with streaming
content:
Tailback pressure causes 504 timeout for hyperlength single-turn generation with streaming

Customer reports 504 Gateway Timeout when issuing a single-turn generation with an extremely long prompt (large context + large max_tokens) using streaming: connection closes before final chunks are emitted. Customer is on a Dedicated cluster in us-east. They reported this started after a spike in similar requests last week and is reproducible for one specific job id. The request uses the /v1/generate endpoint with streaming=true and max_tokens=150000. Impact: Podscribe's nightly ingestion job fails intermittently, causing downstream indexing delays and backfills.
1) Use customer API key on prod-us-east cluster. 2) POST to /v1/generate with model=redwood-open-6B-quant, streaming=true, max_tokens=150000, and a ~180k-token priming prompt (concatenated customer documents). 3) Keep TCP connection open and allow streaming chunks. 4) Observe 504 or connection reset after ~115-125s; occasional partial chunks delivered then finalizer error. Example curl provided to customer during triage: curl -i -N -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-open-6B-quant","stream":true,"max_tokens":150000,"prompt":"<very long priming text>"}'
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout or connection reset by peer. When a partial stream is returned, the final bytes are delayed then cut off. On successful-but-slow runs the finalizer queue length climbs and worker handoff latency spikes, then the connection is closed without finalization. No increased 5xx rate for other customers in the same cluster during most occurrences.
Streamed chunks continue until generation completes and finalizer emits final chunk; no client-visible 504 for requests that fit within resource quotas for Dedicated customers. If system must reject, return a clear 429 with a recommended fallback model/shorter max_tokens guidance.
Relevant logs for request_id=req_0a1b2c3d4e: 
[2026-03-12T03:18:57Z] api-gateway: accept request req_0a1b2c3d4e client_ip=54.210.12.34
[2026-03-12T03:19:00Z] scheduler: queued job job_99877 priority=normal queue_pos=17
[2026-03-12T03:19:12Z] scheduler: dispatch job job_99877 -> worker pool dedicated-eu? (chosen us-east)
[2026-03-12T03:19:48Z] serving-runtime: pool-alloc-delay=36s kernel-swap=true req=req_0a1b2c3d4e model=redwood-open-6B-quant sequence_len_est=180000
[2026-03-12T03:20:30Z] kv-cache: hit_ratio=0.18 resident=22% attempting-evict=true evict_rate=78%
[2026-03-12T03:20:50Z] finalizer: queue_length=12 headroom_tokens=0 backlog_ms=13450
[2026-03-12T03:21:57Z] finalizer: emit_chunk seq=last error=deadline_exceeded connection_closed=client_reset
[2026-03-12T03:21:57Z] api-gateway: 504 Gateway Timeout req=req_0a1b2c3d4e
Additional metrics: grafana panel: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/abc123/cluster-finalizer?var=cluster=prod-us-east
Initial hypothesis: finalizer queueing + pool allocation delay caused by resource headroom exhaustion under spike of hyperlength jobs. Data points: sustained high kv-cache eviction and large pool-alloc-delay for this job; finalizer queue length correlates with 504 events in the cluster. Further checking: autoscaler logs show burst_capacity_remaining=0 at time of request; node-provisioning latency of ~28s causing delay in new worker attach. No immediate OOMs on worker; CPU on router pods spiked but not saturated. We saw several concurrent jobs with similar token budgets from the same customer window (backfill). The serving runtime stalls around kernel-swap for very long sequences — older kernel path selection causes higher mem copies leading to slower throughput; this cluster is using an older runtime image (runtime v2.14) not yet updated to the optimized kernel selection introduced in v2.18.
Combination of (a) cluster exhausted burst headroom due to multiple hyperlength jobs from the same customer, (b) scheduler allocation delay + autoscaler cooldown preventing timely worker provisioning, and (c) older serving runtime kernel path that increases CPU-bound handoff latency for very long-sequence workloads, which created a finalizer backlog and ultimately triggered gateway-level 504s.
1) Temporarily scoped rate-limit: applied per-customer concurrency cap for Podscribe to 2 concurrent hyperlength jobs to prevent further backlog. 2) Manually increased cluster burst_capacity for prod-us-east and forced a scale-up (nodes added, new workers attached). 3) Enabled fallback policy on the customer's routes to route to redwood-open-6B-quant-smaller (token-window-limited) when headroom < 5%. 4) Restarted a subset of router pods to clear TCP stale connections. These actions reduced immediate 504s and allowed most queued jobs to finish within 90s after scale-up.
Recommend customers split monolithic priming into smaller chunks and use incremental generation + rerank instead of single hyperlength generation. For now we advised Podscribe to reduce max_tokens to <= 50k or switch to a dedicated private deployment with reserved capacity for their nightly backfills. Support provided a script to chunk prompts and stitch outputs client-side.
1) Backport kernel-selection and memory-copy optimizations from runtime v2.18 to v2.14 and roll to affected Dedicated clusters. 2) Improve autoscaler heuristics to detect hyperlength job spikes and pre-warm workers when queue length and estimated sequence length exceed thresholds. 3) Add explicit API-level guardrail: return 429 with explanatory body when estimated token+context cost exceeds dynamic headroom threshold rather than letting requests queue to finalizer. 4) Update docs + quickstart with best practices for large priming workloads. Timeline: hotfix (kernel backport) targeted within 2 weeks; autoscaler heuristics in 6 weeks.
Work in progress. Immediate mitigation reduced customer impact and suggested workaround accepted by customer. Engineering is tracking kernel backport PR and autoscaler changes. Customer asked to keep ticket open until backport is deployed to their dedicated cluster and they validate nightly success for one week.

2026-03-12 07:30 UTC - SRE (Liam Chen): Scaled cluster manually and observed worker attach completed at 2026-03-12T07:47Z; finalizer queue drained. Created temporary per-customer concurrency cap. Investigating autoscaler cooldown behavior.

2026-03-14 09:10 UTC - Customer (Samir Dogra, Podscribe): Confirmed that after temporary concurrency cap and reducing max_tokens to 40k their nightly runs completed successfully. They will trial the chunking script and report results next week.
1) Merge and deploy backport PR to prod-us-east dedicated clusters for Podscribe (owner: Priya). 2) Implement autoscaler heuristic change and test on staging with synthetic hyperlength workload (owner: SRE team). 3) Keep ticket open; validate one week of successful nightly backfills from Podscribe; schedule a check-in on 2026-03-21.

title: Streaming tool/function output tokens billed on final invoice despite console estimate showing zero
content:
Streaming tool/function output tokens billed on final invoice despite console estimate showing zero

Issue summary: Customer reports that streaming requests which include function/tool calls produced console estimates showing 0 tool-output tokens (console estimate column), but the finalized invoice contains token charges attributed to the tool outputs. Impact: LexiHealth reports a $9,200 unexpected charge on their monthly invoice tied to streamed sessions that used function calls for structured data retrieval. Environment: Production, us-east-1, enterprise account with reserved capacity and hosted fallback enabled. This affects streaming chat endpoints where the model returns tool invocations (function calls) and the tool outputs are streamed back as separate chunks.

Expected behavior: Console and estimate API should include a consistent token estimate for tool outputs (either zero if non-billable or the same token estimate used for invoice attribution). Final invoice should not introduce previously-unestimated token charges for tool outputs.

Actual behavior: Console estimate showed zero tool-output tokens for ~1.5M tokens across all tool invocations during the billing window. Final invoice shows ~1.45M billed tokens under a line labeled "tool-invoke-output" with reserved-rate fallback applied.

Customer impact: Revenue-impacting billing dispute, customer is holding renewal request pending resolution.

Attachments: Customer provided sample request IDs and screenshot of console estimate vs invoice lines.

2) Have the model return a function call and stream the tool output as separate chunks using the streaming protocol
3) Observe console estimate and /v1/estimates endpoint showing tool-output token count = 0 for these sessions
4) After billing cycle finalization, inspect invoice line items and see billed tokens attributed to 'tool-invoke-output' with nonzero count

title: Dashboard query optimizer injects noop filter causing empty resultset and missing trace links on embedded panels
content:
Dashboard query optimizer injects noop filter causing empty resultset and missing trace links on embedded panels

Issue summary: A customer-reported embedded dashboard panel started returning an empty visualization after a retention backfill. Investigation shows the query optimizer injected a redundant noop filter clause into the SQL-like query plan which caused the platform-side join to short-circuit. The panel therefore had zero rows and tracehook link generation skipped because no trace anchor was present.

Impact: Multiple embedded dashboards for BrightHealth Analytics (enterprise) in us-east show blank panels and missing trace links in their product when selecting 7d ranges that cross the retention backfill boundary. This affects internal customers embedding our console in a product-facing status page.

Environment: production, us-east region, console query-engine v3.7.1, retention backfill from 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-09 was running during the window.

Observed at: 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC when customer reported via #support-enterprise Slack.

Expected behavior: Embedded panel returns series and trace link anchors should be present for rows with sampling-enabled traces.

Actual behavior: Panel renders as "No data"; raw query returns empty resultset. Console does not attach trace_hook headers/links.

Workaround: Customer can toggle time-range to exclude the backfill window or disable "optimizer_trim" flag in advanced panel settings (temporary UI toggle we've exposed server-side) to force the legacy query path.
1) Login to console as org with embedded dashboard (BrightHealth Analytics)
2) Open embedded panel A (Usage heatmap) with time range that includes 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-09
3) Observe panel shows "No data" while surrounding panels show data
4) In developer tools capture the backend query and the planner output from /api/query/run
5) Toggle advanced setting 'optimizer_trim' to off and re-run the panel; panel repopulates data and trace links return

Hypothesis: optimizer path prunes partitions aggressively when backfill markers present, then adds noop guard to preserve semantics which interacts poorly with join ordering.

title: Post-repair provision: Wi-Fi profile collision prevents Intune enrollment on ThinkPad T15
content:
Post-repair provision: Wi-Fi profile collision prevents Intune enrollment on ThinkPad T15

Issue summary: After depot repair (Wi-Fi module + SSD replacement) the Lenovo ThinkPad T15 fails to finish corporate provisioning. Intune enrollment stalls at 'Applying Wi-Fi profile' and the provisioning agent exits with a network profile conflict error. Impact: Blocked check-in for two devices returned from depot in the last 48 hours; users cannot complete provisioning and join corp network without manual intervention.
Two devices from depot repair failed provisioning and required helpdesk manual cleanup. Affects internal provisioning SLA for depot returns and delays deskside returns to users.
1) Receive device from depot after Wi-Fi module replacement
2) Run standard depot imaging (autoprov-image-v2) with corporate packages and join steps
3) Boot out-of-the-box and let provisioning agent run (provisioner v1.8)
4) Observe provisioning stall at 'Applying Wi-Fi profile' and agent exit status with "NetworkProfileApplyError: duplicate-profile-id"
2026-03-10T08:32:12Z provisioner[3421]: INFO: Starting network configuration
2026-03-10T08:32:15Z network-manager: ERROR: apply_profile: failed, code=409, message='duplicate-profile-id'
2026-03-10T08:32:15Z intune-client[778]: WARN: Enrollment paused: network profile application failed
netsh wlan show profiles
Profiles on interface Wi-Fi:
Group policy profiles (read only)  : 0
User profiles
-----------------
All User Profile     : Corp-WiFi
All User Profile     : Corp-WiFi-OLD
Helpdesk reproduced failure and captured netsh/profile output showing two profiles for 'Corp-WiFi'.
Depot imaging logs indicate that the post-image script that imports Wi-Fi XML profiles (scripts/wifi-import.sh) ran twice due to an edge-case restart when the WLAN driver enumerated after image completion.
Hypothesis: Replaced Wi-Fi module caused interface name/NetCfgInstanceId to change, triggering the wifi-import script to re-apply an already-present profile under a slightly different identifier resulting in duplicate profile metadata in the Windows WLAN store.
We also observed that if a docking station is attached during first boot the system enumerates an additional virtual interface, and the current depot script does not de-duplicate profiles by SSID, only by GUID, so duplicates were created.
No evidence of DHCP MAC duplication or network-level collision; issue isolated to local WLAN profile store and provisioning agent's strict validation.
Reproduced locally by intentionally interrupting imaging after driver install to force a re-run of wifi-import.sh; observed duplicate profile GUIDs and provisioning failure match.
Related artifact: staging depot image had older wifi-import logic that used netsh wlan add profile filename=... without checking for existing SSID - this was the immediate trigger.

title: Unexpected egress affinity shift causing cold TLS handshakes and streaming cancels for BrightRetail
content:
Unexpected egress affinity shift causing cold TLS handshakes and streaming cancels for BrightRetail

Issue summary:
Customer BrightRetail observed repeated streaming cancellations and request timeouts starting 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC. Affected requests show unusually long TLS handshake durations (~2.5-6s) prior to application-level token exchange, causing client SDKs to cancel after 3s. The problem appears correlated with egress routing shifts where a small percentage of connections are routed across regions rather than to the account's pinned local egress pool.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints experiencing elevated p95/p99 latency for streaming API calls.
- Customer reports ~6% of requests for their production key are aborted by the client due to handshake/tcp timeout.
- Business impact: degraded chat experiences and user-visible timeouts for BrightRetail storefront search assistants.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightRetail Inc. (dedicated pool, us-west primary)
- Platform: hosted Redwood API (prod)
- Affected routes: /v1/streams/generate and /v1/chat/stream
- Time window: first observed 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC, ongoing as of update.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Issue occurs on first request after connection idle or session cache miss.
2) Client initiates streaming request to us-west endpoint; server logs show egress selection to us-east for ~6% of fresh connections.
3) TLS handshake duration recorded as 2500-6000ms in edge-proxy metrics.
4) Client SDK cancels at ~3000ms, generating client-side cancel and no downstream tokens returned.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Edge-proxy TLS handshake histogram: p50 ~45ms, p95 ~260ms, p99 ~3100ms during window.
- Routing logs: route decision for affected keys shows fallback to remote-pop due to transient affinity tag mismatch.
- Connection traces: new sessions include missing session-id header leading to allocation from warm pool in us-east.
- Error patterns: client-side cancel + server write timeout followed by a short-lived connection reset.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Session affinity tags occasionally not preserved by upstream gateway under burst conditions, causing a small fraction of fresh connections to be routed to a non-local egress pool (cross-region). Cold TLS handshakes on these remote pools are significantly slower due to lack of warm TLS session cache and additional network RTT.
- Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy warm pool eviction policy combined with NAT SNAT rotation results in different downstream 5-tuple, invalidating L4 affinity for a subset of connections.
- Metrics correlating egress-affinity flips with p99 handshake spikes: confirmed timestamps match customer reports.
- Captured packet-level pcap (redacted) shows TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello delay of ~2.8s for affected sessions.
- No config change recorded in the control plane for BrightRetail during incident window.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Engineering toggled strictly-local-egress routing rule for BrightRetail on 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC which reduced affected requests from 6% to ~0.3% in the following 6 hours.
- Increased edge-proxy TLS session cache TTL for the customer's egress pool to retain sessions across brief warm-pool churn (safe, short-term change).

Workaround for customer:
- Advise SDKs to increase client-side stream timeout to 6s during ongoing mitigation window to avoid client cancels (BrightRetail accepted temporary change).
- Recommend keepalive to reduce cold-connection rate.

Next steps / action items:
1) SRE: instrument detailed affinity tag propagation at the L4 proxy to capture missing headers and identify where tag removal occurs (assigned INT-7112).
2) Infra: audit warm-pool eviction thresholds; consider pre-warming remote egress for high-tier dedicated customers.
3) Networking: review SNAT churn and NAT table rotation that could be affecting L4 affinity.
4) Product: evaluate permanent local-egress enforcement option for dedicated customers to prevent cross-region cold-handshake regressions.
5) Postmortem: capture timeline and metric deltas; propose long-term fix and rolling deploy schedule.

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Local-egress enforcement and TTL increase applied as mitigations. Monitoring shows p99 handshake times returned to baseline for the majority of traffic. Longer-term fixes pending investigation.

2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - SRE (Ethan Morales): Confirmed handshake p99 spike in edge-proxy metrics for BrightRetail key. Suspect affinity misassignment; temporarily enabled local-egress enforcement for account to reduce impact.

title: snapshot-alignment-drift-causing-periodic-p99-pulses
content:
snapshot-alignment-drift-causing-periodic-p99-pulses

Issue summary:
Customers (LexiDocs, dedicated) began reporting recurring p99 latency pulses and occasional 504s on text-generation endpoints. The pattern is periodic (roughly every 7-12 minutes) and correlates with increases in request queue depth for short requests. Impact: production user-facing latency spikes and failed responses for interactive flows.

Impact:
- Intermittent p99 spikes from baseline ~220ms to 1.8-2.2s for generation endpoints.
- ~0.3% increase in 504s observed over a 3-hour window for LexiDocs traffic.
- Affects short-sequence use cases (chat/assistant).

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer LexiDocs) in prod us-east.
- Serving runtime v1.42.0 with continuous-batcher enabled and default alignment snapshotting enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Baseline low-latency traffic of small requests (~5-20 tokens) for 5-8 minutes.
2) System enters periodic alignment snapshot cycle tied to batcher metadata (every ~8 minutes).
3) During the snapshot window, multiple short requests queue while a larger snapshot I/O and KV alignment job runs, increasing per-request wait time and generating p99 pulses.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic p99 spikes aligned to snapshot window start times in metrics.
- Traces show requests waiting in the coalescer queue for 600-1800ms before entering a microbatch.
- Snapshot job logs show brief I/O stalls and a GC spike on the batcher worker during the same interval.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot/metadata maintenance should not cause request queuing that elevates tail latency beyond configured SLO. Maintenance should be staggered or performed off the hot path.

Initial logs/metrics references:
- Grafana dashboard: /d/serve/continuous-batcher?orgId=1&view=lexidocs-prod (p95/p99 panels)
- Traces: jaeger/trace/7f8b2e... (examples attached by customer)
- Batch worker logs: /var/log/redwood/serving/batcher-0.log lines 12430-12490 (I/O snapshot start/finish entries)

Temporary workaround offered:
- Switched LexiDocs traffic to a dedicated tenant routing policy with lower snapshot frequency (config override) which reduced the amplitude of pulses by ~60% for the short term.

Next steps requested:
- Engineering investigation to confirm root cause and provide a patch or recommended configuration.
2026-03-10 09:14 - Amina Patel (Support): Customer reported recurring tail latency every ~8 minutes resulting in visible delays for end-users. Provided initial traces and asked to escalate to batcher owners.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Jared Kim (SRE): Acknowledged ticket, started correlating batcher snapshot logs with customer traces. Assigned INT-4021 to track internal investigation for batcher worker GC/IO behavior.
2026-03-11 01:38 - LexiDocs (Customer): Confirmed rollback to previous routing config stabilized UX but wants permanent fix. Attached additional traces where p99 jumps to ~2.1s.
2026-03-12 16:24 - Jared Kim (SRE): Applied conservative config change to reduce snapshot frequency for LexiDocs tenant as a mitigation. Observed reduction in pulse magnitude; still seeing smaller periodic bumps. Captured heap/GC info from batcher process during a pulse and uploaded to shared drive.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Elena Rossi (Eng - batcher): Noted correlation between snapshot alignment windows and an opportunistic metadata compaction job introduced in serving-runtime v1.42.0. Drafting a targeted patch to run compaction asynchronously and add jitter to snapshot start times.
2026-03-13 15:30 - Jared Kim (SRE): Informed customer of planned fix and timeline; scheduled controlled rollout to dedicated fleets early next week. Marked ticket In Progress.
2026-03-13 16:02 - Amina Patel (Support): Customer acknowledged the plan and requested post-deploy monitoring and a follow-up summary.

Hypothesis 1: Snapshot/compaction job is running synchronously on batcher main loop, briefly blocking coalescer flush and increasing queue wait time.
Hypothesis 2: GC activity on batcher worker coincides with snapshot window due to increased allocation during compaction, amplifying pause time.
Evidence collected: Time-aligned logs show snapshot:start and p99 spike within <100ms. Heap profile sampled during pulse shows temporary retention increase and a STW GC mark phase lasting ~200-400ms on the batcher worker.
Experiment: Disabled compaction in a canary fleet; observed p99 pulses disappear in canary (0 instances) and persist in control group. This supports compaction as the main trigger.
Temporary mitigation applied: Reduced snapshot frequency and added tenant-scoped scheduling so LexiDocs snapshots are offset from global windows. Reduced but did not eliminate pulses.
Planned fix: Alter compaction to run off-thread (background worker) and add randomized jitter to snapshot start times per-tenant; add defensive backpressure so metadata maintenance yields to hot request path.
Related artifacts: INT-4021 (internal instrumenting of batcher compaction), PR #2843 implements background compaction and per-tenant jitter, Confluence runbook updated for postmortem.
Risk assessment: Low-risk change if compaction moved off hot path and controlled; however need canary validation on dedicated fleets to ensure no regression in memory stability.
Monitoring additions: Add an alert for 'batcher.snapshot_queue_wait' > 500ms for 5m on dedicated customers and create a dashboard tile showing alignment-phase overlap with p99.

Work in progress - patch authored to decouple compaction from main batcher loop and introduce per-tenant jitter. Patch under review (PR #2843). Plan: canary deploy to two dedicated fleets (including LexiDocs) 2026-03-17, monitor p99 for 48h, then schedule broader rollout if stable. Post-deploy summary and postmortem to be attached to this ticket.
We identified a periodic metadata compaction job in the continuous-batching subsystem that was running on the hot path and causing short bursts of queueing for small requests. We're moving that work off the hot path and adding jitter to snapshot timing; a canary rollout is planned and we'll follow up with results and recommended permanent configuration changes.

title: Cross-model embedding format incompatibility causing rerank queue buildup and degraded latency
content:
Cross-model embedding format incompatibility causing rerank queue buildup and degraded latency

Issue summary: Customer ClearSight reports that calls to the /v1/rerank endpoint started experiencing long tail latency and queueing beginning 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC. The rerank results also show quality regressions (unexpected ordering) when the customer mixes vectors produced by two different embedding variants in the same request.

Impact: Intermittent timeouts from the customer's service (503/504), increased 95th/99th percentile latency for rerank API in us-west, and customer-facing throughput drops. Several high-volume requests queued, causing rate-limit-like behavior and triggering their dedicated capacity autoscale.

Environment: Dedicated tenant (ClearSight) on prod:us-west using a mix of embed-lite-v2 (512 dims, L2-normalized) and embed-highdim-2025 (1024 dims, raw float) produced by their pipeline. Rerank service is expected to accept homogeneous vectors but did not validate dims in upstream request layer.

Steps to reproduce:
- Construct two embedding arrays: one from embed-lite-v2 (shape N x 512, l2-normalized) and one from embed-highdim-2025 (shape N x 1024, raw).
- Send a single /v1/rerank request containing a candidate list where some candidates include 512-d vectors and others include 1024-d vectors (no explicit embedding_version header).
- Observe immediate enqueuing and a sharp latency increase for that request ID (~>5s p99), occasionally resulting in 503 or rerank returning lower-quality ordering.

Observed logs: Trace IDs: rnk-20260310-8a4f, rnk-20260310-8b11. Error snippets show the rerank evaluator logging "embedding dim mismatch - implicit upcast" and downstream trace showing fallback to CPU quant path. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank/us-west?panelId=7&from=2026-03-10T08:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T09:00:00Z. Slack thread: #support (thread ts 1700003000.002200).
Generate 512-d L2-normalized embeddings (embed-lite-v2)
Generate 1024-d raw embeddings (embed-highdim-2025)
Combine both types in a single /v1/rerank request payload without embedding_version headers
Send to customer's dedicated endpoint in us-west and observe latency and ordering
2026-03-10T08:34:12Z rnk-20260310-8a4f rerank WARN embedding dim mismatch - implicit upcast
2026-03-10T08:34:13Z rnk-20260310-8a4f rerank INFO fallback to cpu-quant path, estimated token cost +1.9x
2026-03-10T08:34:14Z api-gateway 429 upstream queue depth exceeded for tenant clearsight
2026-03-10 09:02 - Ava Martinez (Support): Acknowledged customer report, requested sample payload and trace IDs. Asked for exact model variants and whether any normalization was applied client-side.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Customer (ClearSight - S. Patel): Provided sample payloads and confirmed the two models above; they said their ingestion pipeline accidentally stitched outputs during a rollout and didn't set embedding_version headers.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Ravi Shah (SRE): Observed sharp p99 increase aligned with trace IDs; rerank service allowed mixed-dim vectors and triggered a slow conversion in the scoring path. Filed INT-4012 to track an internal validation fix.
2026-03-11 07:18 - Eng (L. Chen): Root cause identified: upstream request validator omitted embedding dimension validation when a mixed candidate list is present. Implicit handling attempted to upcast 512->1024 and call into CPU fallback for several heavy kernels, causing latency spike. Created PR #1287 to add strict validation + syntactic hinting for embedding_version header.
2026-03-11 14:30 - Support (A. Martinez): Communicated temporary workaround to customer: ensure homogeneous embedding dims per request or include embedding_version header; If mixing is unavoidable, pad 512-d vectors with zeros to match 1024 length as a short-term mitigation.
2026-03-12 03:05 - Ravi Shah (SRE): Hotfix deployed to prod: validator now rejects mixed-dim requests with clear 400 response and guidance. Gradual rollout completed across us-west. Monitoring shows p99 latency back to baseline.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Customer (S. Patel): Confirmed issue resolved from their perspective; no further timeouts observed in last 24h and quality returned to expected ordering.
Checked Grafana: rerank queue depth spiked at 08:34 UTC, correlated with increase in cpu pathway calls (serving-runtime cpu_binder).
Heap/CPU profiles captured for one trace showed expensive memcpy and zero-padding steps executed under request lock while scoring ran on CPU vector kernels.
Hypothesis: absence of embedding_version header + mixing dims caused system to try compatibility conversion; conversion fallback path is not gated by timeout and increased latency drastically under concurrency.
Confirmed that prior safety check for vector length exists at model-serving layer but the rerank preprocessor path bypassed it during a historical refactor (see commit 6a2f8b3).
Related PR adding strict dims check and clear error messages: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/1287
Related internal ticket: INT-4012 for adding e2e tests and SDK validation helpers.
Deployed a validator that rejects mixed-dimension embedding lists with an informative 400 response explaining expected dims and embedding_version header format. Back-ported a short-circuit to avoid implicit upcast/conversion on hot paths. Created SDK guidance and sample code for ClearSight and added an integration test asserting consistent dims. Customer confirmed resolution. Action items: (1) Add automatic recommend-converter utility for customers who need cross-model compatibility; (2) Add telemetry to count mixed-dim attempts and trigger early alerts; (3) Update runbook with exact error messages and workaround steps.
Create conversion utility RFC (owner: L. Chen)
Add mixed-dim detector alert to PagerDuty playbook (owner: Ravi Shah)
Ship SDK helper that fails fast with clear error for mixed dims (owner: Developer Experience)
Customer-facing note provided: 'We temporarily observed elevated rerank latencies when mixing embeddings from different model families. The service now returns a clear error for mixed-dimension requests and we provided migration steps. We apologize for the disruption and are working on an automated converter for mixed workloads.'

title: Intermittent SSE disconnect behind AWS ALB strips 'end' event and duplicates trailing paragraph on resume
content:
Intermittent SSE disconnect behind AWS ALB strips 'end' event and duplicates trailing paragraph on resume

Issue summary: Customer reports that during intermittent network flaps through their ALB, SSE streams produced by our API sometimes arrive at the client missing the closing '</stream>' type end marker (we use a JSON control frame with event: "end"). Client reconnects, the resumed stream contains a duplicated trailing paragraph (the last sentence appears twice) and the response metadata envelope is repeated.

Impact: EditorFlow's editor integrations render partial HTML blobs and occasionally show duplicate concluding paragraphs. This leads to user confusion and corrupted saved drafts for a subset (~0.6%) of streaming sessions.

Environment: Production, routed through customer-managed AWS ALB that performs HTTP/2 fronting to our HTTP/1 edge. Customer uses server-sent events (SSE) streaming and a short client reconnect/backoff sequence.

Observed behavior: SSE stream terminates without emitting the standard '</stream>' type end marker (we use a JSON control frame with event: "end"). Client reconnect resumes with an earlier offset but the trailing paragraph is duplicated and trailing metadata block (conversation_id, timestamp) appears twice.

Expected behavior: On transient disconnects, stream resume should deliver a continuous output without duplicated sentences and should include a single, well-formed terminal control event indicating completion.
1) Create a long-running SSE generation request via the public API with chunked streaming enabled and a prompt that generates a 4+ paragraph response (example prompt attached).
2) Route traffic through an AWS ALB configured with HTTP/2 listener -> HTTP/1 target (same as customer config).
3) Induce a short connection flap by triggering an ALB target health probe during streaming (simulate by toggling backend target's socket for ~200-400ms).
4) Allow client to reconnect using normal resume logic (client sends last-received token index as resume_offset).
5) Observe the resumed stream: check for absence of 'end' control event and duplication of trailing paragraph and duplicate metadata envelope.
edge-proxy (2026-03-10T15:12:03Z) INFO connection reset by peer: client socket closed during write, session_id=abc123
service-runtime (2026-03-10T15:12:03Z) WARN chunker: emitted-final-marker but upstream connection terminated before flush, request_id=rf-7f4c
edge-proxy (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z) INFO reconnect attempt from client ip 54.83.21.9, resume_offset=298
upstream (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z) INFO resumed session rf-7f4c at offset 298 and re-emitted buffered suffix length=72
upstream (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z) INFO metadata-envelope emitted {conversation_id: 'cdf-99', ts: '2026-03-10T15:12:04Z'}
upstream (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z) INFO metadata-envelope emitted {conversation_id: 'cdf-99', ts: '2026-03-10T15:12:04Z'}
client-side capture (EditorFlow) - final console: '...and that concludes our summary.' appears twice in sequence
Initial hypothesis: ALB health probe / upgrade path may be causing partial TCP half-close that the edge-proxy interprets as a clean end, so the runtime flushes a final buffered suffix and then resume logic replays same suffix on reconnection.
Edge-proxy trace shows two metadata-envelope emits in quick succession during resume; need to determine whether duplication is from runtime replay or proxy retransmit logic.
Reproduced locally using a HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1 conversion proxy and a synthesized 300ms disconnect; observed missing 'end' control frame in 3/20 trials and duplicate trailing paragraph on 2/20 trials.
Binary tracing added: request_id rf-7f4c shows event sequence: CHUNK[n-1] -> CHUNK[n] (flushed) -> connection half-close -> client reconnect -> resume replay CHUNK[n] -> METADATA -> METADATA. The runtime's flush path writes CHUNK[n] and METADATA but does not mark session state as terminal when tcp half-close seen (race).
We suspect a race where the runtime's flush-on-half-close path emits the final chunk and metadata but fails to atomically set terminal flag; resume handler treats session as resumable and replays buffered suffix + metadata again.
Support (2026-03-10): Thanks for the report — capturing details and routing to streaming infra. Can you attach a HAR or client capture? — Daniel
Customer (EditorFlow - 2026-03-10): Attached a client-side capture and ALB access log for two sample sessions. We see the repeated paragraph in both client and application logs.
SRE (2026-03-11): Reproduced on staging with an ALB-like proxy. Adding an internal tracepoint to the runtime to log terminal flag transitions (PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4281). — Liam O'Connor
Infra (2026-03-12): Patch to runtime replay logic created to add an atomic terminal set before flush returns success. Patch in review; test matrix shows duplicates eliminated in our harness. — Aisha Patel
Race in runtime's flush-on-half-close path: final chunk and metadata could be emitted without atomically setting the session terminal flag. If a client reconnects quickly, resume handler replays buffered suffix and metadata producing duplicated trailing paragraph and duplicate metadata envelope.
Customer workaround: configure ALB idle timeout to be longer than typical keepalive (recommended 120s) and update client to use a brief exponential backoff (start at 200ms) before resuming to reduce resume/replay overlap. Also recommended: enable client-side de-duplication of immediate trailing sentences if present.
1) Merge runtime patch that sets terminal state atomically before flush (PR#4281).
2) Deploy patch to staging and run the ALB-proxy regression harness across 10k simulated stream sessions.
3) Coordinate a canary deploy to production for a subset of customers behind HTTP/2->HTTP/1 ALBs and monitor duplicate-trailer metric.
4) Follow up with EditorFlow to schedule a short maintenance window to test their ALB configuration and apply the recommended timeout change (if they accept).
5) Add a metric and alert for repeated metadata-envelope emits in a single session to catch regressions early.
In Progress - fix PR under review. Customer has applied the suggested ALB timeout and temporary client backoff; observed reduction in duplicates in their QA environment. Will update after production canary.
Consider adding a unit test that simulates TCP half-close during flush and asserts that terminal state is set before any resume unknowns.
Document guidance for customers using ALBs with HTTP/2 fronting and recommend default ALB idle timeout and client resume backoff settings in streaming best-practices page.
Instrument a lightweight 'resume-duplication' signal that increments when metadata envelope emitted more than once within 1s for same session_id.

title: Intermittent cross-region egress to us-east after enabling strict EU residency; TLS handshake and p95 latency spikes
content:
Intermittent cross-region egress to us-east after enabling strict EU residency; TLS handshake and p95 latency spikes

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent requests egressing to us-east after they enabled strict EU residency on 2026-03-09. The symptom is periodic p95/p99 latency and TLS handshake delays (~150-450ms extra) for traffic that should remain in eu-west-1. Impact:
- Customer production traffic for Finova Pay (payments flows) observed p95 latency spikes impacting user-facing flows.
- Occurs ~1-2 times per hour, lasting 30-90s windows.
Environment:
- Customer: Finova Pay (enterprise, private deployment with strict residency flag enabled)
- Platform: Redwood hosted control plane + private VPC egress in eu-west-1
- Affected model endpoints: rw-instruct-7b, gpt-4o-mini
Steps to reproduce (as customer observed):
1) Send a steady request stream pinned to eu-west-1 with strict residency enabled.
2) Watch p95 latency in their application metrics and our API logs.
3) When spike occurs, look at request egress metadata: some requests contain us-east-1 egress path.
Logs/snippets from customer:
- Example trace id: trace-20260310-11:06:03-fp1
- Client-side observed latency jump from 120ms p95 to 560ms p95 for 45s window.
- Customer-side TLS logs show additional handshake RTTs during window.

Requested:
- Why are a subset of requests leaving eu-west after strict residency is enabled?
- Are control-plane events (cert rotation, LB re-registration) causing temporary loss of residency stickiness?
- What mitigations can be applied to avoid user-facing latency spikes?
2026-03-10 12:05 - Asha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after customer alerted via #support-fintech. Customer provided traces and a short p95 time series. Marking P1 due to production impact.
2026-03-10 13:12 - Miguel Santos (SRE): I can reproduce an egress hop in the platform logs for the provided trace ID. Attaching control-plane event stream for that minute shows ALB re-registration event at 03:10:22 UTC. Investigating DNS TTL and healthcheck behavior.
2026-03-10 14:03 - Finova Pay (customer rep, Elena Kovacs): We saw this twice overnight; both times coincided with small bursts of failed payments. Happy to open a maintenance window if needed. We require strict EU residency for compliance.
2026-03-11 09:22 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Preliminary hypothesis: healthcheck/probe traffic and control-plane maintenance tasks use a separate probe subnet that incorrectly routes via us-east egress when backends are briefly deregistered. That can flip the residency lock when probes re-register. Correlating cert-rotation schedule with incident windows.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Priya Ramesh (Platform Eng): Found a related PR that changed probe registration behavior (PR#8123). The change introduced a fallback path for healthcheck probes when an AZ loses capacity; in rare cases this fallback picks cross-region egress. Rolling back that change in a canary to confirm.
2026-03-13 08:15 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Canary rollback completed in eu-west canary pool at 07:45 UTC. Customer confirmed no recurrence in the 12:00-08:00 test window. Next steps: schedule full rollback and patch to enforce probe egress alignment with residency lock.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Asha Patel (Support): Notified customer of the mitigation and asked for permission to coordinate a short maintenance window to apply the fix globally. Customer approved for 2026-03-14 02:00-03:00 UTC.
Observations and evidence:
- Control-plane logs (2026-03-10 03:10:22 UTC) show ALB target group re-registration for the customer's dedicated pool during cert rotation.
- DNS records TTL for residency lock are 30s; we observed a small window where control-plane healthchecks returned from fallback subnet IPs reported in us-east.
- Healthcheck probe workflow (post-PR#8123) attempts local AZ probe, then regional fallback. The fallback path incorrectly used a region-agnostic egress bucket which currently prefers us-east when local pool capacity is low.
- The residency lock state machine will re-evaluate egress candidate on successful healthcheck; if the first successful probe comes from a us-east egress IP, the lock flips to us-east for a short window until subsequent eu-west probes re-establish.
- TLS handshake timing: when egress hops to us-east, client TLS renegotiation and extra routing add ~180-400ms to p95 depending on customer proximity to eu-west.
- Incidence frequency correlates with our cert rotation schedule (every ~8 hours for canary targets) and with brief AZ capacity pressure.
Hypotheses considered and rejected:
- DNS cache on customer side alone: rejected because platform logs show outbound egress IPs from our side change during windows.
- Model runtime causing fallback: rejected; multiple models and endpoints affected simultaneously, pattern matches control-plane events.
Evidence links:
- Control-plane event stream: https://logs.redwood.internal/event/20260310/03:10:22
- Healthcheck trace for trace-20260310-11:06:03-fp1: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/trace-20260310-11:06:03-fp1

Workarounds and fixes applied:
- Short-term workaround: Coordinated with customer to disable strict residency (not ideal for compliance) or schedule maintenance windows during our cert rotation. Customer chose a maintenance window for full patch.
- Mitigation performed: Rolled back PR#8123 behavior in eu-west canary pool to prevent cross-region fallback egress for healthchecks. Observed no recurrence in canary for 24 hours.
- Planned permanent fix: Update probe routing logic to bind healthcheck/probe egress to the same residency lock as the customer pool (control-plane change). Add a guard that prevents the residency lock from flipping on a single probe success from a different egress region. Create INT ticket to change probe subnet allocation and cert rotation phasing.
Follow-ups and action items:
- INT-2410: Rework probe subnet assignment and enforce egress-region affinity for healthchecks (assigned to Platform Eng).
- Create rollout plan to apply rollback and patch to all EU pools outside peak windows (scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC with Finova Pay permission).
- Add automated alerting: detect probe-origin region mismatch events and emit residency-flip metrics to SLO dashboard.
- Postmortem to be authored in Confluence after full rollout; link will be added here.
Current status: In Progress (canary rollback successful; global rollback/patch scheduled).
Customer sensitive: do not include raw PCI data. Keep customer informed about maintenance window and compliance implications. Contact CS lead (Jordan Kim) for external communications.

title: Dock ACPI _DSM change reorders kernel modules and breaks encrypted-home mount during Linux provisioning
content:
Dock ACPI _DSM change reorders kernel modules and breaks encrypted-home mount during Linux provisioning

Issue summary:
During staging workstation provisioning, machines docked to the new TB4 dock (firmware v1.3.0) intermittently fail to mount the user's encrypted home (LUKS) during first-boot setup. The system stops at 'Waiting for encrypted partition' and drops into emergency mode.

Impact:
- Blocks automated imaging and enrollment for developers receiving docked laptops in staging.
- Affects both Dell XPS and Lenovo X1 hardware when docked during provisioning; undocked provisioning completes fine.
- Slows down depot turnaround and blocks a handful of on-call tasks.

Environment:
- Linux image: Ubuntu 22.04.5 + custom preseed (rd.luks.options set), kernel 6.1.47 (custom patches), initramfs generated by image-scripts v0.15.
- Dock firmware: TB4-dock v1.3.0 (rolled 2026-03-09).
- Provisioning server: staging provisioner behind NAT in us-west.
- Repro rate: ~40% of docked workflows, 0% when same device imaged undocked.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Attach laptop to TB4 dock (firmware v1.3.0).
2) Boot PXE to provisioning image, start automated installer (preseed).
3) Installer reaches disk partitioning and sets up LUKS for /home (automated).
4) Reboot into first-boot initramfs to unlock LUKS.
5) Observe initramfs fails to find underlying block device and drops to emergency shell.

Observed logs (key excerpts):
- journalctl (first-boot) shows: "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ..." then "udevd: failed to apply ACPI _DSM properties"
- initramfs debug: device nodes present (/dev/nvme0n1p3) but cryptsetup open fails with "Device or resource busy"
- dmesg: new ACPI _DSM object parsed, acpi_device_add changed ordering for USB/PCI hotplug events
- modprobe ordering: sometimes zram, then nvme, then a storage controller module; on successful boots nvme is probed earlier.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Dock firmware v1.3.0 exposes an ACPI _DSM method that triggers a late rebind of USB-attached NVMe bridges, altering the timing of block device availability during initramfs.
- Hypothesis B: The dock advertises an extra PSCI device and triggers kernel to probe a composite driver which delays nvme driver init order.
- Reproduced in lab with two different docks with v1.3.0; downgraded dock to v1.2.1 and provisioning succeeded for same machines.
- Captured early boot trace with initramfs + kmsg: shows module load order differs between good and bad runs.
- Tried forcing cryptsetup to wait for device (sleep 10s) as a workaround — reduces repro rate but not reliable.

Root cause (working theory):
Dock firmware change introduced an ACPI _DSM entry that causes the kernel to register an additional ACPI device late in early userspace. This shifts probe ordering so the NVMe controller module is loaded after initramfs attempts to open the encrypted partition, causing intermittent "device busy" or missing-device failures. The problem manifests only when the dock is attached because the device tree and ACPI namespace differ.

Temporary workaround implemented:
- Image-scripts: added a patch to initramfs that retries cryptsetup with exponential backoff up to 30s and explicitly triggers udev settle before unlocking. Deployed to staging (image-scripts v0.15.2).
- Procurement/Depot: advised to image undocked devices until dock firmware is rolled back.

Permanent remediation plan:
- Engineering (kernel/infra) to add a udev/kernel probe ordering fix: prefer NVMe controller binding earlier when block devices are expected during initramfs. (ENG ticket target: low-level module ordering patch).
- Work with Dock vendor to supply a firmware patch that removes or corrects the ACPI _DSM behavior (open vendor SR).
- Add an initramfs feature flag to wait for named block devices for critical partitions when docks are present; expose as a config in image-scripts.

Follow-up tasks:
- INT-884421: Create depot SOP to undock units before imaging (assigned to Depot Ops).
- ENG-PRIORITY: Kernel/module probe ordering engineering task (assigned to kernel team).
- Ops: Add automated boot-time diagnostic capture (kmsg + udevadm info) for next 50 failed boots.

Resolution notes (so far):
- Workaround (initramfs retry) reduced failures in staging from ~40% to ~6%.
- Vendor acknowledged a regression in the dock firmware and opened a ticket; vendor ETA for firmware patch: 2 weeks (awaiting confirmation).

Customer-facing impact: None (internal-only).

Next steps:
- Keep ticket In Progress until vendor firmware or kernel patch is deployed and we've validated 7 days of successful provisioning runs in staging (>99% success).
- Once validated, create a small Ops change to schedule dock firmware roll-forward in depots and update provisioning SOP.

title: Stuck model pin after canary throttle suppression causes routing to legacy variant
content:
Stuck model pin after canary throttle suppression causes routing to legacy variant

Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout of pf-3b-v2 for PathFinder Analytics (dedicated pool), a rate-adaptive canary throttle triggered 'suppression' mode which prevented the orchestrator from committing the per-tenant pin. The tenant traffic continued to be routed to the legacy pf-3b-v1 variant, causing inconsistent responses and elevated cost when some requests fell back to the hosted dequantized variant. Impact: customer reports mixed model outputs, degraded quality for ~12% of requests for a critical endpoint and a sudden spike in token usage due to fallback to a higher-cost variant.

Observed window: 2025-02-18 03:05 - 03:50 UTC.

Context: This customer is on a dedicated pool with explicit model version pin requested via API header X-Model-Pin, and a canary rollout (20% weight) was configured with adaptive-rate throttle enabled (adaptive-canary-throttle v2). The edge-proxy applied a transient rate-shed tag which the orchestrator interpreted as a health suppression and did not persist the pin commit in the cluster snapshot.
1) On a dedicated tenant with pinned header X-Model-Pin: pf-3b-v2, begin a weighted canary rollout (20%) via console rollout API.
2) Simulate a spike of short-lived concurrent requests to the canary slice to trigger adaptive-canary-throttle thresholds on the edge-proxy.
3) Observe orchestrator logs for pin commit path; confirm whether pin commit RPC returns 202 vs 200.
4) Inspect routing decisions returned by the edge (x-routing-variant header) and compare to requested pin.
5) Verify if snapshot store contains the committed pin entry for the tenant after rollout slice stabilizes.
edge-proxy logs (us-east-1) 2025-02-18T03:06:12Z: INFO rate-shed applied: tenant=pf-tenant-88 action=suppress reason=adaptive-throttle threshold=0.2
orchestrator logs 2025-02-18T03:06:15Z: WARN pin-commit-suppressed tenant=pf-tenant-88 snapshot_write_status=skipped reason=health-suppression
serving-runtime logs 2025-02-18T03:06:20Z: DEBUG route-eval tenant=pf-tenant-88 selected_variant=pf-3b-v1 (pin requested pf-3b-v2)
snapshot-store: last_written_epoch=8420 (pre-rollout), attempted_commit_epoch=8421 (skipped)
kvcache-metrics: prefix-hit-rate unchanged; no prewarm observed for pf-3b-v2 in tenant pool
2025-02-18 04:00 UTC - Triage: Confirmed customer reproduced discrepancy; initial hypothesis: edge suppression flag prevented snapshot commit path.
Checked rollout controller: commit flow returns 'skipped' when health suppression present (code path introduced in adaptive-throttle v2).
Reproduced in internal staging by enabling adaptive-canary-throttle and simulating 200rps spike; observed identical 'pin-commit-suppressed' logs.
Hypothesis refined: edge-proxy annotates requests with suppression metadata which the orchestrator treats as 'abort commit' instead of 'defer commit'. This leaves the tenant in a half-committed state where routing remains bound to previous snapshot epoch.
Temporary mitigation tested: manually forcing a snapshot write via admin endpoint produced a committed entry and restored pinned routing for the tenant.
Risk: If adaptive throttle suppression remains aggressive during low-latency window, automatic commit may never persist leading to rolling inconsistencies across tenants.
Support (Maya Chen) 2025-02-18T05:12Z: Reached out to PathFinder contact (ops@pathfinder.io) to request request IDs and sample traces. Customer confirms ~12% of calls returned different output shape.
Customer (Alex Rivera, PathFinder) 2025-02-18T05:40Z: Provided sample request IDs: req-9832, req-9841, req-9910. They noted risk to production analytics pipeline; asking for ETA on fix.
