title: incident-bot: PagerDuty P0 fired: private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat-loss for customer AcmeCorp (region: eu-west-1) — heartbeat missing from on-prem agent fleet for 3x polling intervals. PD: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/P12345
content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P0 fired: private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat-loss for customer AcmeCorp (region: eu-west-1) — heartbeat missing from on-prem agent fleet for 3x polling intervals. PD: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/P12345

pagerduty: Alert details: service=private-controlplane, urgency=high, impacted=AcmeCorp, symptom=agent-heartbeat-missing, last_heartbeat=2625000900, suggested_runbook=/runbooks/private-controlplane-heartbeat.md

maya_sre: ACK. I’m taking primary. joining bridge in 2m.

jamie_ops: I’m on-call too, joining bridge now. @maya_sre any known maintenance?

leah_support: CS notified AcmeCorp via email and Slack DM (ticket #INC-4123). Customer reporting increased 5xxs and model request timeouts since ~08:02 UTC.

alex_infra: quick triage: control plane pods appear healthy in cluster, but agent fleet for customer shows 'offline' in control-plane UI. hitting the agent host directly.

jamie_ops: running quick checks on one agent host:
```
$ ssh admin@10.11.12.33 
Last login: ...
$ sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
● redwood-agent.service - Redwood onprem agent
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/redwood-agent.service; enabled)
   Active: active (running) since ...
$ sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | tail -n 50
2026-03-14T08:00:45 AgentConnection - heartbeat timeout connecting to controlplane gateway 10.20.30.5:443
2026-03-14T08:01:46 AgentConnection - retrying, tls handshake failed: EOF
```

maya_sre: looks like agent -> control plane connectivity TLS/handshake failures. Could be customer network or local firewall/MTU. @tom_custeng can you confirm any recent network changes on your side?

tom_custeng: We haven't changed config, but we did see a maintenance window on our edge firewall earlier today. I'll check rule changes and MTU with our infra team now.

oncall-l2: I’m available to assist if we need host-level debugging or a config rollback.

jamie_ops: tried `curl -vk https://10.20.30.5:443/health` from agent host — TLS handshake fails with "alert handshake failure". Packet capture shows SYN/ACK then immediate RST from 10.20.30.1 (edge firewall).

alex_infra: escalating network suspicion. Short-term mitigation options: 1) restart agent (may restore session) 2) route traffic via fallback gateway in same region (requires control plane policy change) 3) request customer open firewall to allow controlplane IPs.

maya_sre: doing safety-first: will attempt agent restart on one host to see if re-registration works, then proceed one-by-one. Jamie's on it.

jamie_ops: running restart: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent`
```
$ sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 50 --no-pager | tail -n 40
2026-03-14T08:07:12 AgentConnection - attempting TLS handshake to 10.20.30.5:443
2026-03-14T08:07:13 AgentConnection - connected, registration successful, heartbeat established
```

incident-bot: Note: agent 10.11.12.33 heartbeat restored at 2625001632.

leah_support: Updated ticket INC-4123: "We restarted one agent which re-registered successfully; customer still seeing intermittent 504s for some routes. CS asked customer to check edge firewall logs for RSTs."

maya_sre: Verified control-plane metrics: agent heartbeats reappearing, control plane latency back within SLO for this host. However, 3/12 agent hosts still show flaky handshakes. Need network team & customer to confirm.

alex_infra: I can provision a fallback gateway and apply a routing override for AcmeCorp to bypass the suspected firewall hop. That will take ~8-12 minutes and a brief config push. We should get customer approval first.

tom_custeng: Please do not reroute without our change control signoff. We will run a rapid check on firewall rules and MTU, reporting back in 10m.

maya_sre: fair. we'll hold on bulk reroute. continuing rolling restarts on remaining hosts but throttled to avoid flapping. tagging oncall-l2 for net-level pcap help.

oncall-l2: attaching a pcap snippet from 10.11.12.34 -> 10.20.30.5:443, shows MSS/MTU mismatch and repeated ICMP fragmentation-needed messages. suspect MTU of 1400 on intermediate device while path requires 1500.

jamie_ops: confirming when we `curl --path-as-is` with +MTU tweak we can TLS handshake succeed. Temporary workaround is to set PMTU discovery or lower agent MTU to 1400.

leah_support: Communicated workaround to customer: "We identified a likely MTU mismatch. Temporary mitigation options: apply PMTU fixes on your edge or allow our fallback gateway (requires your approval). We can also lower agent MTU remotely if you approve." Customer acknowledged and requested us to attempt agent-side MTU change as quickest path.

maya_sre: proceeding with staged MTU adjustment on two remaining flapping hosts (with rollback plan). updating runbook steps in /runbooks/private-controlplane-heartbeat.md to include MTU troubleshooting notes.

jamie_ops: applied MTU=1400 on 10.11.12.34 and 10.11.12.35. Both re-registered and heartbeats stable.
```
$ sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400
$ sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
```

incident-bot: All known agents for AcmeCorp reported heartbeats restored at 2625003320. Alert status: resolved -> monitoring. PagerDuty: auto-resolve queued.

maya_sre: Post-mitigation status: control plane healthy, no new error spikes for 12m. Customer still performing validation on app traffic but reports reduction in 5xxs.

leah_support: Updated ticket INC-4123 and CC'd AcmeCorp network ops. Next action: CS to schedule a joint troubleshooting call to permanently fix MTU on their edge device.

oncall-l2: recommend follow-up action item: add MTU check to private agent onboarding checklist and add firewall/MTU verification to runbook.

maya_sre: Agreed. I'll create a short post-incident note and assign follow-ups: runbook update, onboarding checklist change, and a customer ops call. Tentatively closing incident in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:

jamie_ops: thanks everyone. monitoring channel for 30m.

leah_support: Customer ACK'd provisional resolution. Marking status as "mitigated" and waiting for customer confirmation before closure.

maya_sre: RESOLVED (mitigated). Root cause: likely MTU mismatch on customer edge firewall causing TLS handshake fragmentation failures. Permanent fix tracked in INC-4123 and follow-up ticket NET-789.

jamie_ops: closing thread, will reopen if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:

content:
eng-platform

Benji Okafor: pulling folks in for audit logging requirements for route experiments. need to lock fields + change-diff format this week so Console/backend can implement consistently. enterprise asks (Helio Finance esp) are: “who changed what, when, from where, and what exactly changed.” what’s the minimum set we MUST emit for create/update/start/stop/delete?

Marcus Lin: :eyes: Security POV: we should treat this like any other control-plane config mutation. Fields should be sufficient for: (1) incident response (2) compliance evidence (SOX-ish controls) (3) customer SIEM ingestion.

Kevin Osei: +1. Also: audit export expects stable schema and “diff” summary that doesn’t leak secrets. We’ll need to be explicit about redaction.

Benji Okafor: current experiment events we have in staging are basically `{event_type, actor, ts, experiment_id}` and some freeform message. not enough.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: from RBAC side: need to include what permissions/role allowed the action (or at least actor role + auth method). Some customers ask “was this break-glass?”

Ethan Park: we should align w/ existing audit event envelope used by model rollouts. do we have a canonical list?

Marcus Lin: yes-ish. But experiments add complexity b/c the “changed object” is a nested config (variants, allocations, eligibility, guardrails). We should define:
- envelope fields (who/when/where/request)
- target resource identifiers
- action
- diff representation
- policy/rbac context

Jada Williams: also note: updates can happen via Console UI *or* API. And we’ll likely have automated system actions soon (guardrail auto-stop). Need to distinguish human vs system actor.

Chloe Martin: +1. Console backend can pass `actor_type=user|service` and `actor_id`. For service, use service principal.

Benji Okafor: ok let’s enumerate. Here’s a strawman based on other systems:
- event_id (uuid)
- event_ts
- org_id / workspace_id
- environment (prod/staging)
- action (experiment.create/update/start/stop/delete)
- resource_type=route_experiment
- resource_id=exp_...
- resource_name (optional)
- route_id(s)
- actor_id
- actor_email (if user)
- actor_type
- actor_ip
- user_agent
- request_id / trace_id
- api_key_id or auth_method
- rbac_role or permission set
- diff (tbd)
- previous_version / new_version

Marcus Lin: add:
- “reason” / “comment” if provided (lots of customers require change ticket ID)
- “source” (console|api|system)
- “mfa_present” is nice but we probably don’t have it reliably
- “impersonated_by” / “delegated_actor” if support tooling does this (even if not GA now, keep a placeholder)

Kevin Osei: for export we need stable field names and consistent types. Also “actor_ip” might be null for server-to-server, but include anyway.

Rafael Mendes: SRE ask: include `config_propagation_state`? maybe not in audit event itself but in related status log. But for stop actions triggered by guardrails, audit should include the guardrail condition that triggered it.

Jada Williams: yes. we need “decision context” for system-triggered actions:
- trigger_type=guardrail
- trigger_metric=p99_latency
- trigger_threshold=…
- observed_value=…
- evaluation_window=…
(else the audit log looks spooky)

Marissa Cole: product: also want UI “Change history” to show a human-friendly summary (“Traffic split A: 50% -> 10%”, “Variant model v2 -> v3”, etc). But we can derive from diff if diff is usable.

Benji Okafor: diff format question. options:
1) store full before/after JSON blobs
2) JSON Patch (RFC6902)
3) our own list of changed fields with old/new
My worry w/ (1) is secrets + huge payload. (2) is precise but annoying to render in UI. (3) is easier for UI but less standard.

Kevin Osei: for SIEM export, JSON Patch is fine (customers don’t always parse deeply; they store raw). But *we* need to show in Console. We can convert patch to summary on the backend.

Marcus Lin: strongly prefer not full before/after. also redaction becomes hard. JSON Patch is acceptable IF:
- paths are stable
- values are redacted where required
- we include a human-readable `diff_summary` string (or multiple strings)

Chloe Martin: we can do both: store patch + a computed summary list (array of strings). But note: doc says no nested json in “slack doc”; sorry mixing. In our actual audit schema we can do nested. For now as requirement: patch + summary.

Benji Okafor: careful: audit export pipeline today expects flat-ish records. it can accept a `diff_json` string field though.

Kevin Osei: yep. In audit exports we typically serialize complex bits as strings:
- `diff_json`: stringified JSON patch
- `actor`: stringified object (or flatten actor fields)
But internal storage can be structured.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 flatten key fields so customers can filter in SIEM easily: action, actor_email, actor_id, org_id, resource_id, source, outcome.

Ethan Park: outcome! add `status=success|failure` + `error_code` and `error_message` for failed attempts (permission denied, validation rejected). Some enterprises want to see denied changes too.

Marcus Lin: yes, we should log *attempted* changes as well, but be cautious: don’t log full attempted payload if validation fails and contains sensitive strings. But for experiments, payload shouldn’t have secrets. still, guardrails may include prompt-set IDs etc.

Jada Williams: and we have the overlapping experiment validation edge cases; failed updates will happen. Logging them is useful.

Benji Okafor: ok so envelope includes:
- `outcome`
- `http_status` (if API)
- `error_type`

Marcus Lin: for compliance: include `performed_at` in RFC3339, not only unix seconds.

Kevin Osei: +1. In exports we do both `timestamp` (unix ms) and `timestamp_rfc3339`.

Chloe Martin: naming conventions: use `event_time_ms` and `event_time` (RFC3339). Also include `received_time_ms`? sometimes events are buffered.

Rafael Mendes: include `config_version` and `previous_config_version`. This is key for forensics when propagation lag is involved.

Benji Okafor: makes sense.

Marissa Cole: what about “what route(s)” and “what variants”? UI and customers will want it.

Marcus Lin: include identifiers, but be careful with cardinality/size. In audit log it’s ok to include list of route_ids and variant_ids. If it’s too big, we can include a count + truncated list.

Kevin Osei: for export, lists are fine as JSON strings. But we should at least include primary `route_id` if single-route experiments are our norm.

Jada Williams: initial GA is per-route experiment, but PRD allows multiple routes eventually. Let’s define:
- `route_ids`: string (json array)
- `primary_route_id`: string

Benji Okafor: ok. Proposed required fields (MUST):
1) Identifiers: event_id, org_id, resource_type, resource_id, action
2) Time: event_time_ms, event_time
3) Actor: actor_type, actor_id, actor_email (if user)
4) Source/request: source, request_id, trace_id, actor_ip (if available), user_agent (if available)
5) Authorization: rbac_role (or role_id), auth_method, api_key_id (if applicable)
6) Outcome: outcome, http_status, error_code
7) Change: diff_format, diff_json, diff_summary, previous_config_version, new_config_version
8) Target attrs: primary_route_id, route_ids, variant_ids
9) System-triggered: trigger_type, trigger_details_json
Does that match security?

Marcus Lin: mostly. One more: `region` (control plane region that processed request). Customers sometimes ask “changes must be made from us-east only” etc.

Kevin Osei: also `client_request_id` (if provided) so customers can correlate w/ their own logs.

Chloe Martin: we already accept `Idempotency-Key` for some endpoints; we can log that as `idempotency_key`.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: and `actor_session_id`? probably not.

Marcus Lin: optional.

Benji Okafor: diff_json example as JSON Patch. Something like:
```json
[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/allocations/variantA","value":0.1},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/allocations/variantB","value":0.9}
]
```
And diff_summary computed:
- "allocations.variantA: 0.50 -> 0.10"
- "allocations.variantB: 0.50 -> 0.90"

Marissa Cole: +1 that’s readable.

Jada Williams: important: diff_summary should use stable display names if available (variant name) not just IDs.

Kevin Osei: but for export we should include IDs anyway. If names change, audits still need stable reference.

Marcus Lin: redaction policy: diff_json MUST NOT include:
- any customer prompt text (if any)
- raw header values
- secrets
For experiments config we should be ok, but eligibility rules might include header matches? do we allow that?

Jada Williams: eligibility rules include “if header X exists” or “matches regex”. That regex might contain sensitive patterns.

Marcus Lin: then redact values for certain rule types. At minimum, allowlist what can appear in audit diff values.

Chloe Martin: for now we can do:
- include rule type + key name
- redact rule value with "[REDACTED]" if it’s not in allowlist

Benji Okafor: ok. I’ll capture this as requirements for ENG-9030/PR.

Kevin Osei: also need “change diff summary” for the audit export request from SUP-24944. They explicitly asked for “field changed” and “old/new” if available.

Marcus Lin: +1. But if redacted, summary should say “value changed (redacted)”.

Rafael Mendes: last thing: guardrail auto-stop events must be clearly labeled; customers will see a stop and think someone did it. So:
- action=experiment.stop
- source=system
- actor_type=service
- trigger_type=guardrail
- trigger_details_json includes metric/threshold/window

Benji Okafor: ack.

Marissa Cole: can we also include a linkable “change history” id so Console can deep link? like `console_url`?

Kevin Osei: don’t love putting URLs in audit export (env-specific). But internal event can include `ui_reference` string.

Marcus Lin: make it optional.

Benji Okafor: cool. I’ll send a summary to thread + convert into the confluence doc. if anyone objects to JSON Patch choice, speak now.

Marcus Lin: no objection. Please add note: RFC6902-ish and include `diff_format="json_patch_v1"` so we can evolve.

Kevin Osei: +1. And version the audit schema: `schema_version`.

Benji Okafor: good call. Adding `schema_version` required.

Chloe Martin: :thumbsup: once we have the field list finalized, I’ll sync w/ Felix on the UI rendering (diff_summary list) and w/ Kaitlyn on RBAC details.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: :thumbsup: I’ll confirm what we can reliably emit for auth_method + role. We may have to fill role from token claims.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll add requirements to runbook re: how to use audit logs during propagation lag incidents.

Benji Okafor: thanks all. I’ll post final list in 10.

Benji Okafor: Final proposed required fields for route experiment audit events (GA):
- schema_version
- event_id
- event_time_ms
- event_time (RFC3339)
- org_id
- environment
- region
- source (console|api|system)
- action (experiment.create|update|start|stop|delete)
- resource_type (route_experiment)
- resource_id
- resource_name (optional)
- primary_route_id
- route_ids (json string)
- variant_ids (json string)
- actor_type (user|service)
- actor_id
- actor_email (if user)
- actor_ip (if available)
- user_agent (if available)
- auth_method
- api_key_id (if applicable)
- rbac_role (or role_id)
- request_id
- trace_id
- client_request_id (if provided)
- idempotency_key (if provided)
- outcome (success|failure)
- http_status
- error_code / error_message (failure only, sanitized)
- previous_config_version
- new_config_version
- diff_format (json_patch_v1)
- diff_json (stringified JSON Patch, redacted)
- diff_summary (json string list)
- trigger_type + trigger_details_json (only for system-triggered actions)
Please react with :+1: if ok.

Marcus Lin: :+1:

Kevin Osei: :+1: (pls ensure export pipeline can handle diff_summary as json string)

Marissa Cole: :+1:

Jada Williams: :+1:

Kaitlyn Nguyen: :+1:

Rafael Mendes: :+1:

title: eng-security
content:
eng-security

nina: Hey folks — running into a flaky user-reported PII in logs for /api/v1/ingest. Need short-lived admin to fetch a few recent pod logs and run a grep. Not planning to export a full dataset, just 2h of logs. Any objections?

samir: What's the exact commands you need and why admin vs read-only?

nina: Need access to kubectl exec & logs in prod namespace to do `kubectl logs -n prod svc-ingest-*/ -c ingest --since=2h | grep -iP '\b(email|ssn|credit)\b'` — sometimes the mask/filter doesn't trigger on malformed payloads. Read-only cluster role doesn't let me run the container-side grep.

security-bot: Policy reminder: temporary elevation for debug requires ticket ID, business justification, duration (<=4h), and data handling plan. All elevated sessions are audited and flagged. See /policies/privileged-access.

olivia: @nina can you confirm no export/distribution of raw logs? If you find PII we need to follow the redaction playbook (mask in place, open incident if >1 user affected).

nina: Confirm — no export. If PII present I'll redact in-place and paste sanitized excerpts only. Ticket: INF-8042 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8042). Justification: investigate ingestion path that may bypass request-scrubber for malformed payloads. Duration requested: 2 hours.

security-bot: Received. Tagging: elev_request=INF-8042, requested_by=nina, ttl=2h. Automated check: user no outstanding compliance flags.

oncall-sre: I can grant a break-glass window for 2h starting now. Will scope kube role to `prod/namespace:svc-ingest-*` and only allow `logs, exec` for that period. I will attach `audit_tag: 1787654321-DBG` to all actions.

samir: Please include the exact rolebinding YAML in the thread so ops audit can verify. Also prefer `kubectl logs --since` and `grep` inside a debug container rather than `kubectl exec` into prod containers where possible.

oncall-sre: rolebinding YAML (applied):
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: temp-debug-nina-inf8042
  namespace: prod
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: temp-debug-logs-exec
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: nina
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

oncall-sre: Role grants `pods/log` and `pods/exec` for label selector `app=svc-ingest` only. TTL=2h. Audit tag attached.

olivia: Security note — before you grep, toggle redaction preview so any matches are flagged. Console path: Console -> Audit -> Redaction -> Preview mode. Make sure `redact_candidate=true` is set for your session.

nina: Got it. Starting now. Will post sanitized findings in this thread. If I find >10 user records with unmasked PII I will file an incident immediately. :shield:

oncall-sre: Session started and logged. If anyone needs to revoke earlier, ping me.

nina: Done. Found two malformed events with raw email fields. Redacted copies attached below (sanitized):
```
{"id":"xxxx","email":"redacted@example.com","payload":"..."}
```
No SSNs or CC numbers. Closing request after 30m. Thanks. :white_check_mark:

title: eng-ml
content:
eng-ml

maria: Bringing up cumulus15b-int4 on canary GPUs (a100). Hitting repeated OOMs on cold starts + memory fragmentation spikes. Default max_new_tokens=1024. Logs below, any quick ideas?

maria: Logs: ```OOM on alloc of 104857600, kv_cache reserve failed, memfrag: 78% used, available contiguous: 60MB```

sam: which kernel/runtime build? any recent kernel patches?

alex: saw similar on a different model — int4 pack layout + large max_new_tokens can frag GPU memory on cold start. temporarily fixed by setting batch_size=1 and max_new_tokens=256.

maria: tried batch_size=1 + max_new_tokens=256, still saw one cold-start OOM at first warmup, then stable. But throughput drop is large.

raj: two quick knobs: reduce reserve_slots (we default to 256 for 15b), try reserve_slots=96 or 64; and disable kv-prefetch on cold starts so we don't pre-allocate full prefix. Also try setting `gc_threshold=0.6` in runtime to force earlier compaction.

emma: (from infra-bot) deploy canary started for cumulus15b-int4 -> canary-3 on a100.

maria: I flipped reserve_slots=96 and disabled kv-prefetch for the canary. Reproduced OOM cleared, memfrag dipped to ~42%. Perf: tail latency increased ~12ms.

elaine: int4 quant layout sometimes increases allocator pressure because of alignment differences. Running quant-eval with warm snapshots helps. Can you run `python infra/evals/onboard_eval.py --model=cumulus15b --quant=int4 --warm_snap=1 --batch=1` and post the results?

maria: Ran eval, snippet: ```avg_latency: 182ms, p95: 412ms, mem_peak: 33.2GB, kv_frag_after_warm: 41%```. Quality checks passed (perplexity within expected).

sam: if int4 stable but latency penalty unacceptable, fallback plan: ship int8 canary for prod while we iterate int4 tunings. int8 seemed fine on our previous runs.

raj: also add a warmstart snapshot step to canary rollout pipeline: pre-warm kv cache with synthetic prefix to avoid cold allocation spikes. Example script: `./scripts/warm_cache.sh --model cumulus15b --tokens 1024` — this reduces cold OOMs in tests.

maria: Plan: rollback int4 canary for now, start int8 canary + add warmstart snapshot + set operator defaults: max_new_tokens=512, reserve_slots=96, batch_size_default=1 for canary traffic. Will create a follow-up PR with config. cc @oncall

sam: SGTM. opened ticket INC-7123 and assigned to eng-ml.

maria: executing rollback in 10m and will re-run quant-eval with warm snapshots after int8 canary is stable. Thanks for the quick input everyone :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for cumulus15b-int4 by maria (reason: cold-start OOMs).

title: partnerships
content:
partnerships

Ivy: Heads-up: PartnerCloud just raised a billing dispute. They say several customers got negative adjustments after we applied their compacted 'summary' payloads. Ticket: https://partnercloud.help/TK-771
Marcus: negative adjustments? like credits appearing suddenly?
Ivy: yep. For some accounts we applied a negative delta that exceeded the original usage for that window, ending up with a net negative billed quantity.
Diego: do we have a sample payload?
Ivy: pasted redacted example from partner: ```{"partner_id":"partnercloud","window":"2026-03-05T10:00:00Z","summaries":[{"customer":"pcust-19","delta":-120,"reason":"correction"}] ,"signature":"..."}```
Marcus: oof. they send deltas in summaries and expect us to apply them against prior raw events. We currently apply summaries eagerly as absolute adjustments without bounding, so negative deltas can over-correct when prior events are missing.
Diego: root cause guess: PartnerCloud compacts old raw lines into summaries and deletes the originals on their side. If our ingest missed the original (late delivery) we see a corrective delta without base usage.
Ivy: partner confirmed they do aggressive compaction after 48h to reduce S3 costs. they assume marketplace will store originals.
Marcus: quick mitigation: treat summary deltas as "provisional" if there is no matching prior window record. Don't mutate ledger; instead create a pending adjustment that requires reconciliation within 14 days.
Diego: agree. Technical plan: 1) Change summary handler so that if delta < 0 and no matching prior usage_id found -> insert pending_adjustment(row) and emit reconciliation alert. 2) If partner later replays raw events, auto-apply and clear pending.
billing-bot: Query queued: SELECT customer_id, SUM(delta) FROM marketplace_summaries WHERE partner='partnercloud' AND delta < 0 AND received_at >= '2026-02-01' GROUP BY customer_id; estimated rows: ~32 customers with non-zero negative totals
Ivy: for affected customers we'll need to open invoices with "pending credit" flag and not auto-issue refunds until manual review.
Marcus: policy decision: do we expose a SLA requiring partners to retain raw events for 30 days or accept liability for over-crediting? We should push for retention requirement in marketplace onboarding.
Diego: enforcement idea: extend the ingestion contract to require either (a) retain raw events 30d OR (b) include full snapshot (absolute usage) in any corrective summary. That way we can reconcile without originals.
Ivy: partner relations: I'll draft amendment language and present to PartnerCloud. Also need to surface these impacted customers and propose temporary suspend of auto-refunds.
partner-relations-bot: Note logged: partnercloud-contact@partnercloud.com CC: marketplace-ops@redwood.com
Marcus: operational tasks: Diego implement provisional flag + pending_adjustment table; billing team to show "pending credits" in invoices UI; Ivy coordinate with partner on retention clause and timeline; billing-bot generate affected customer list and mark invoices as review_needed.
billing-bot: Action items recorded: ["Diego: provisional summary flow PR","Ivy: partner amendment + comms","Billing: show pending credits in UI","billing-bot: affected customer list"]
Diego: I'll aim to open PR today that prevents auto-application of negative deltas when no anchor exists; includes unit tests for replay path.
Ivy: PartnerCloud asked for a replay API to push originals for up to 21 days. They can do 21d for enterprise customers, 7d for all others. Can we accept 21d for enterprise?
Marcus: yes but require signed manifests when >7d. Also enforce HMAC signatures on replays and throttle replays to avoid DOS.
Ivy: next sync: internal triage at 11:00, and I'll send partner note with proposed 21d enterprise / 7d standard and draft retention clause. Thanks all.

content:
support

Alex H: FYI customer ThermaTech (acct: thrm-402) reports a wire was RETURNED by the receiving bank. They called out a SWIFT/IBAN mismatch and a returned fee. Can payments look?
Raj P: Can you drop the tx id + raw request/response? quick check: was this routed through an intermediary bank?
Alex H: tx id tx_01G7YK2Z5A9
Alex H: request payload snippet:
```json
{
  "amount": 5200.00,
  "currency": "EUR",
  "beneficiary_name": "ThermaTech GmbH",
  "beneficiary_iban": "DE89370400440532013000",
  "beneficiary_bic": "BOFAUS3N",        // customer-provided (looks US BIC)
  "beneficiary_address": "",
  "routing_type": "wire",
  "intermediary_bank_bic": "CHASGB2L"
}
```
Alex H: bank response (sanitized): `RETURNED - INCOMPLETE_DETAILS - beneficiary address required / SWIFT mismatch`
payments-bot: Detected bank return code 0191 / reason: INCOMPLETE_PAYEE_DETAILS
Linda S: quick read: BIC `BOFAUS3N` is a US clearing BIC, IBAN is German. Receiving bank likely did an automated mismatch check and flagged it. Also beneficiary_address is empty — non-SEPA wires often need full address.
Raj P: repro steps for engineering ops: 1) fetch event logs `GET /v1/payments/tx_01G7YK2Z5A9/events` 2) inspect route chosen `route_id` 3) check our validation: `validate_iban_vs_bic(iban,bic)` returned false?
Raj P: cb run: I pulled logs, route used partner `europe-pay-03`, intermediary CHASGB2L forwarded. Bank returned after intermediary review.
Alex H: customer says they copied BIC from their ERP; they want us to re-send immediately and reimburse $35 wire fee. They attached PO #98765.
billing-bot: Customer billed wire fee: $35.00 on 2025-10-03. Refund requires manager approval or auto-refund policy match.
Linda S: For immediate workaround: we can either (A) reissue with corrected BIC (look up BIC from IBAN), and include full beneficiary address, or (B) switch to an ACH/EU SEPA route if customer bank supports it. But we need explicit confirmation from the payer on corrected details.
Raj P: Long-term fix: add server-side validation that flags IBAN/BIC country mismatch and require beneficiary_address for non-SEPA currency+route combos. Also add a rule to block user-supplied BICs that clearly conflict with IBAN country without explicit override.
Alex H: Customer asked for steps we already ran so they can do internal change too. Can we provide a minimal repro for them? e.g. commands to pull the returned wire payload and recommended corrected values.
Raj P: Provide this to customer: 
1) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments/tx_01G7YK2Z5A9`
2) Corrected fields suggestion: `beneficiary_bic: DEUTDEFF` (example) and `beneficiary_address: "Musterstrasse 12, 10115 Berlin, Germany"`
3) If they prefer we resend, customer must confirm new BIC + full address and accept potential bank charges.
Alex H: I'll ask Maria to get confirmation. Maria, can you call ThermaTech and get updated BIC/address and confirm they want us to retry? Also ask if they'd like refund of the wire fee.
Maria G: On it, pinging now. ETA 20m. I'll collect updated payee info and share here. :phone: 
Linda S: Ops note: I'll create a short incident: `payments-validation-mismatch` and assign to infra + payments for a small validation patch. We'll aim for a rollback-safe rule: flag vs block.
Raj P: Also logging enhancement: include `iban_country` and `bic_country` in the routed event to make hunts easier.
Alex H: thanks. tagging for visibility: @Raj P @Linda S @Maria G. I'll mark this thread as escalation -> finance-sr.
billing-bot: Logged refund request rfd_7782, status: pending-approval.
Alex H: Customer reply (after call): "We confirm new BIC DEUTDEFF and address Musterstrasse 12, retry please. We approve reimbursement of the $35 fee."
Maria G: confirmed details & PO attached. Customer wants retry now.
Raj P: Ok - two action items: (1) Payments ops to reissue wire with corrected BIC/address via partner route (note: might incur another intermediary fee) (2) Finance to process $35 refund once manager signs off. I'll kick off the resend and post logs when done.
Linda S: assigning to myself to run the resend and monitor. Will paste event ids here. :white_check_mark:
Alex H: Great — keep this thread updated. Add a short postmortem once resolved so we can surface validation change to product.
Maria G: will collect customer sign-off email and upload to ticket.
Alex H: thx all.

title: eng-ml
content:
eng-ml

zoe: FYI I'm trying to bring up customer 'Astraeus' LoRA merge on int4 for a fast pilot. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/astraeus-lora/pull/7  Quick smoke shows amount extraction weirdness in invoices. Can someone kick the eval pack (invoices-mini + long-context samples)? :wave:
tom: I can run it. Will spin up runtime-intel64 int4 and run invoices-mini + qa_short. Posting results when done.
eval-bot: Queued eval for thread 1765570011 on runner-02. Estimates 5-7m.
tom: Quick numbers: token-perp delta +0.9% vs int8 baseline, amount extraction recall down 12% (units parsing fails), amount normalization off for negative/parentheses formats. Date fields OK. Artifact: s3://redwood-evals/astraeus/1765570011/artifact.json
ravi: +0.9% perp and amounts are classic sign of tokenization splits changing numeric subpieces. Was the LoRA trained with the same tokenizer merge table?
zoe: PR notes say trained from a customer checkpoint using tokenizer v1.8. Our serving runtime currently loads v1.9 (changed merges for punctuation and parentheses).
carmen: Customer is on production pilot with strict expected accuracy. I recommend we gate Astraeus route on int8 until we validate. Rolling out int4 with this drop isn't acceptable.
ravi: Agreed. Two options: 1) a token-alias map on model load that remaps embedding rows and KV indices, 2) ship a small wrapper tokenizer that reproduces the training splits. Alias map idea (sketch):```python
# sketch
if model.tokenizer_id != runtime.tokenizer_id:
    alias = compute_alias(model.tokens, runtime.tokens)
    model.embeddings = model.embeddings[alias.map_to_runtime]
    patch_kv_indexing(alias)
```
Need to watch attention cache layout and ensure remap is deterministic for long context.

title: architecture
content:
architecture

tom: Heads-up: we still see ambiguous handoffs between runtime and control-plane for dedicated customers. Observed symptom: two runners briefly accept traffic during node failover. Need a lightweight handback protocol.

nina: Agreed. My draft idea: a two-step "intent -> ack" flow instead of a long-lived lease. Sequence: runtime asks for IntentToServe, CP responds with IntentToken + grace_window. Runtime serves, then CP may request Handback; runtime replies HandbackAck within grace_window and drains or accepts redirect.

carl: Flow sketch:
```
POST /intents { tenant, runtime } -> { intent_id, grace_sec }
POST /handbacks { intent_id } -> { status: queued | acked }
GET /intents/{id} -> { holder, expires_at, state }
```
Make grace_sec small (10-60s) and require runtime to expose a drain endpoint.

maria: This differs from leases because intent is reversible quickly and CP can return 409 if another runtime already has intent. If CP cannot reach both, it returns 202 + "continue-serving" to avoid double-stop.

nina: Important: include a "quiesce" flag on handback to indicate whether in-flight requests must finish or be redirected immediately. Example: { handback_ack: true, quiesce: true, drain_deadline: 12 }

carl: For dedicated we probably want CP to prefer issuing intent to the runtime with highest residency score, but allow the runtime to renew intent if it has recent activity. Renewal windows should be jittered to avoid stampede.

maria: Ops concerns: need audit events for intent_granted, intent_revoked, handback_requested, handback_acked, handback_timeout. Also surface a metric: double-serve-seconds for billing reconciliation.

nina: Security: use short-lived signed intent tokens. Validation is local; token contains tenant, runtime, issued_at, expires_at, signature. Private mode: customer CP signs their own intents with their key. Hosted/dedicated: our CP signs.

carl: Edge case: split-brain when both sides think they have intent due to clock skew. Mitigation: require monotonic sequence number in token and CP to prefer higher sequence. Also prefer wall-clock expiry with small drift tolerance.

maria: Ops playbook idea: if double-serve detected, auto-trigger handback with quiesce=true to minimize user impact, then run postmortem on the metric.

ops-bot: incident-check: no active incidents matching "double-serve". Canary job queued: infra/intent-proto -> staging started 1765020100

tom: Action items:
- nina: write RFC for Intent/Handback proto + token format + sample SDK behavior.
- carl: simulate failure modes and measure double-serve-seconds; propose safe defaults for grace_sec.
- maria: define audit events and billing reconciliation hooks.
We should sync next Tue. :calendar:

elena: Heads-up — customer CS-4821 sees tool outputs getting swapped when they invoke multiple tools in parallel. The payload returns tool_result for the wrong tool (confidentiality risk). Repro steps below.
frank: yikes. any request ids or logs we can look at?
elena: gave them req id `req_0a7c2b9f` and two correlation ids `corr-6112` / `corr-6113`. Logs show both tool pipelines executed on same host but final response maps tool_result IDs incorrectly.
sam: can you paste the minimal request they used? are they using function-calling or our legacy tool endpoint?
elena: function-calling wrapper. here's a redacted minimal payload they used (they said parallel=true):
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-redwood-2",
  "input": "Check price and inventory for SKU X1",
  "tools": [
    {"name": "price_lookup", "args": {"sku": "X1"}},
    {"name": "inventory_check", "args": {"sku": "X1"}}
  ],
  "tool_options": {"invoke_mode": "parallel"}
}
```
elena: curl they used: `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/function_call -d @payload.json`
tariq: I took a quick look at the runtime code path. There's a race in the tool_result association map: we keyed by `parent_request_ts` instead of a per-tool invocation uuid when tools are spawned concurrently. If two tool calls finish close enough, one write can overwrite the other's entry. That matches the symptom.
maria: which runtime version was this on? can we get worker logs around `req_0a7c2b9f`?
elena: customer on runtime `v2.14.1`. Redacted worker log snippet they provided:
```
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=price_lookup invoc=0x9f2 start
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=inventory_check invoc=0x9f3 start
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=inventory_check invoc=0x9f3 result=result_88a
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=price_lookup invoc=0x9f2 result=result_88b
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f assoc_map_write key=1678458724 value=result_88a
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f assoc_map_write key=1678458724 value=result_88b
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f final_response tool_results=[result_88b, result_88b]
```
elena: note the assoc_map_write uses epoch key `1678458724` — that's the root of the bug.
frank: quick patch idea: switch assoc key to `request_id + invocation_uuid` and guard writes with a mutex or atomic map ops. I can prototype a fix + unit test.
sam: can we get a small repro test in our infra so we don't have to repro on customer's data? I can run a harness that spawns N parallel tool calls under same parent request.
maria: also need to know if any customers saw PII leak; if tool results are swapped between different parent requests that’s higher severity. For CS-4821 looks like only within same parent request but still bad.
support-bot: Ticket CS-4821 updated and assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P1 (customer-facing). https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4821 :white_check_mark:
elena: temporary mitigation suggested to customer: set `tool_options.invoke_mode = "sequential"` or serialize calls client-side until we ship fix. They confirmed workaround works.
tariq: I'll own the codefix. Plan: add per-invocation UUID, replace epoch key, add unit+concurrency tests, and deploy in canary. Expect patch PR today, canary tomorrow.
maria: please post PR link and ETA for rollback/patch notes so CS can update KB.

Diego R.: Hey finance team — received invoice CFDI-2026-09 from CDMX Cloud Services for platform usage (MXN 146,300). Vendor marked themselves as 'nonresident' on the PDF and didn't include an RFC for tax withholding. They also attached a nota fiscal that looks odd. Should we apply Mexico withholding or ask for RFC / CFDI 4.0 XML?

Marcela V.: Can you paste the lines they filled? For Mexican suppliers we need RFC and a valid CFDI XML to validate the 'comprobante' and tax regimes. If they claim nonresident status we need a RFC or a foreigner tax ID plus evidence.

Diego R.: Here's the text from the invoice: 
"Proveedor: CDMX Cloud Services
RFC: - (nonresident)
Concepto: Servicios de software
Total: MXN 146,300

Attached: invoice.pdf (no CFDI XML), note: 'Supplier is foreign entity, tax withheld at source should be applied by payer'"

Anita P.: If vendor is a foreign entity providing services in Mexico, withholding rules can apply (ISR and IVA treatment depends on place of supply). But vendor cannot simply ask us to withhold without documentation. We need either: (A) a validated CFDI issued in Mexico with their RFC, or (B) if truly foreign, a declaration and their fiscal ID plus statement of where services were performed. Also check if they meant "no RFC" because they are a foreign branch of a Mexican entity.

Leo H.: Operationally: hold payment until we get the CFDI XML or a formal tax residency declaration. If vendor insists on withholding and we apply it incorrectly, we could misreport. AP-bot, flag invoice and set hold.

AP-bot: Hold flag applied on invoice CFDI-2026-09 — reason: missing RFC/CFDI validation. AP queue notified.

Marcela V.: I'll reach out to our Mexico tax advisor to confirm the exact withholding rates if services were rendered in Mexico by a foreign supplier. Typical ISR withholding on foreign services is around 10% but depends on treaty. IVA (16%) may or may not apply. Do not gross-up.

Diego R.: Drafting vendor message, posting now: 
"Hi CDMX Cloud Services — thanks for the invoice. To process payment we need a valid CFDI XML (CFDI 4.0) including your RFC. If you are a foreign entity, please provide your tax ID, a declaration of tax residency, and confirmation of the country where the services were performed. Please clarify whether you expect Redwood to withhold taxes and provide supporting documentation. Payment will remain on hold until we receive the requested documentation. If you charge Mexican VAT (IVA), please reissue the invoice showing IVA line and RFC.

Best, Diego on behalf of Redwood AP"

Anita P.: Also ask them to confirm bank details and whether they want payment in MXN or USD. If they push for immediate payment, escalate to Legal.
